optionExplanations: ✓ Enabling versioning preserves previous versions of objects so that accidental deletions or overwrites can be recovered, protecting against accidental deletion.
✓ Enabling MFA Delete requires multi-factor authentication to permanently delete object versions or disable versioning, adding strong protection against accidental or malicious deletion.
✗ A bucket policy controls access permissions but is not the primary mechanism for protecting against accidental deletion compared to versioning and MFA Delete.
✗ Default encryption protects data confidentiality at rest but does nothing to prevent or recover from accidental deletion.
✗ A lifecycle policy automates transitions and expirations of objects and could actually cause deletions, so it does not protect against accidental deletion.

text: A company has a data ingestion workfiow that consists of the following: • An Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for notifications about new data deliveries • An AWS Lambda function to process the data and record metadata The company observes that the ingestion workfiow fails occasionally because of network connectivity issues. When such a failure occurs, the Lambda function does not ingest the corresponding data unless the company manually reruns the job. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to ensure that the Lambda function ingests all data in the future? (Choose two.)
options: A. Deploy the Lambda function in multiple Availability Zones.
B. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue, and subscribe it to the SNS topic.
C. Increase the CPU and memory that are allocated to the Lambda function.
D. Increase provisioned throughput for the Lambda function.
E. Modify the Lambda function to read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.
optionExplanations: ✗ Deploying Lambda in multiple Availability Zones is handled automatically by AWS and does not address lost messages caused by transient network/processing failures.
✓ Creating an SQS queue subscribed to the SNS topic durably buffers notifications so that messages are retained and retried, preventing data loss during failures.
✗ Increasing CPU and memory improves performance but does not provide durability or retry for failed ingestion events.
✗ Increasing provisioned throughput (concurrency) affects scaling, not the durability or retry of messages lost during network failures.
✓ Modifying the Lambda function to read from the SQS queue enables reliable polling with automatic retries and visibility timeouts, ensuring all buffered data is eventually ingested.

text: A company has an application that provides marketing services to stores. The services are based on previous purchases by store customers. The stores upload transaction data to the company through SFTP, and the data is processed and analyzed to generate new marketing offers. Some of the files can exceed 200 GB in size. Recently, the company discovered that some of the stores have uploaded files that contain personally identifiable information (PII) that should not have been included. The company wants administrators to be alerted if PII is shared again. The company also wants to automate remediation. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Inspector to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, trigger an S3 Lifecycle policy to remove the objects that contain PII.

B. Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Macie to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.

C. Implement custom scanning algorithms in an AWS Lambda function. Trigger the function when objects are loaded into the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.

D. Implement custom scanning algorithms in an AWS Lambda function. Trigger the function when objects are loaded into the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to trigger a notification to the administrators and trigger an S3 Lifecycle policy to remove the meats that contain PII.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Inspector assesses EC2/container vulnerabilities and network exposure; it does not scan S3 objects for PII, so it cannot meet the requirement.
✓ Amazon Macie uses managed machine learning to automatically discover and classify PII in S3 objects, and SNS can alert administrators, meeting the requirement with the least development effort.
✗ Implementing custom scanning algorithms in Lambda requires significant development effort to detect PII, which the company wants to avoid.

✗ Implementing custom scanning algorithms in Lambda again requires building PII detection logic, contradicting the least-development-effort requirement, and SES adds no advantage over a managed PII detection service.

text: A company needs guaranteed Amazon EC2 capacity in three specific Availability Zones in a specific AWS Region for an upcoming event that will last 1 week. What should the company do to guarantee the EC2 capacity?
options: A. Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region needed.
B. Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region needed.
C. Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
D. Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
optionExplanations: ✗ Regional Reserved Instances provide a billing discount and regional capacity benefit but do not guarantee capacity in specific Availability Zones.
✗ An On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies only the Region does not reserve capacity in the three specific Availability Zones required; capacity reservations are zonal.
✗ Reserved Instances are a billing/pricing construct for long-term cost savings and are not the right mechanism to guarantee short-term capacity for a one-week event.

✓ An On-Demand Capacity Reservation specifying the Region and the three specific Availability Zones reserves EC2 capacity in those exact zones for as long as needed, guaranteeing capacity for the event.

text: A company's website uses an Amazon EC2 instance store for its catalog of items. The company wants to make sure that the catalog is highly available and that the catalog is stored in a durable location. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Move the catalog to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
B. Deploy a larger EC2 instance with a larger instance store.
C. Move the catalog from the instance store to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
D. Move the catalog to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
optionExplanations: ✗ ElastiCache for Redis is an in-memory cache that is not intended as a durable primary store for a catalog and data can be lost, so it does not meet the durability requirement.
✗ A larger EC2 instance store is still ephemeral storage tied to the instance lifecycle; data is lost if the instance stops or fails, so it is neither durable nor highly available.
✗ S3 Glacier Deep Archive is durable but designed for cold archival with retrieval times of hours, making it unsuitable for a frequently accessed, highly available catalog.
✓ Amazon EFS provides durable, highly available shared file storage across multiple Availability Zones, making the catalog both durable and highly available.

text: A company stores call transcript files on a monthly basis. Users access the files randomly within 1 year of the call, but users access the files infrequently after 1 year. The company wants to optimize its solution by giving users the ability to query and retrieve files that are less than 1-year- old as quickly as possible. A delay in retrieving older files is acceptable. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Query the tags to retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.

B. Store individual files in Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files that are in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena. Query and retrieve the files that are in S3 Glacier by using S3 Glacier Select.

C. Store individual files with tags in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Store search metadata for each archive in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year. Query and retrieve the files by searching for metadata from Amazon S3.

D. Store individual files in Amazon S3 Standard storage. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Store search metadata in Amazon RDS. Query the files from Amazon RDS. Retrieve the files from S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is for rarely accessed archive data, not data accessed randomly within the first year; using it for the active first-year data costs more per access and is not optimized for frequent random access. Glacier also does not support tag-based querying of file contents.

✗ B. S3 Intelligent-Tiering adds monitoring/automation overhead and cost, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is slower (minutes to hours) which is fine for old data, but Athena queries object data in S3, not arbitrary call transcripts, and S3 Glacier Select only works on objects already in Glacier with limited query support. This is more complex and not the most cost-effective fit.

✓ C. Storing recent files in S3 Standard gives fast access during the first year, keeping searchable metadata in S3 lets users find files, and an S3 Lifecycle policy moving them to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year reduces cost while still allowing millisecond retrieval for the acceptable-delay older files. This is the most cost-effective design that meets all requirements.

✗ D. S3 Glacier Deep Archive has retrieval times of up to 12 hours which exceeds 'a delay is acceptable' reasonableness for query-and-retrieve, and running Amazon RDS just to hold search metadata adds unnecessary ongoing cost and operational overhead compared to storing metadata in S3.

text: A company has a production workload that runs on 1,000 Amazon EC2 Linux instances. The workload is powered by third-party software. The company needs to patch the third-party software on all EC2 instances as quickly as possible to remediate a critical security vulnerability. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS Lambda function to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
B. Configure AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
C. Schedule an AWS Systems Manager maintenance window to apply the patch to all EC2 instances.
D. Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run a custom command that applies the patch to all EC2 instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. AWS Lambda is not designed to patch software on EC2 instances; it has no native mechanism to execute commands across 1,000 instances and would require building custom agent integration, which is slow and complex.

✗ B. Systems Manager Patch Manager patches the OS (and supported software via baselines) but is oriented around patch baselines and scheduled scans/installs; it is not the immediate ad-hoc way to push a specific third-party patch as quickly as possible.
✗ C. A Systems Manager maintenance window runs tasks on a defined schedule, which introduces delay; the requirement is to remediate as quickly as possible, not at a scheduled future time.

✓ D. Systems Manager Run Command lets you immediately execute a custom command (such as installing the third-party patch) across all 1,000 managed EC2 instances at once, providing the fastest remediation with no scheduling delay.

text: A company is developing an application that provides order shipping statistics for retrieval by a REST API. The company wants to extract the shipping statistics, organize the data into an easy-to-read HTML format, and send the report to several email addresses at the same time every morning. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Configure the application to send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
B. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to format the data and to send the report by email.
C. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Glue job to query the application's API for the data.
D. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Lambda function to query the application's API for the data.
E. Store the application data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as an S3 event destination to send the report by email.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is for streaming/delivering data to destinations like S3 or Redshift; it does not query a REST API on a schedule or format/email reports, so it does not fit this batch reporting requirement.
✓ B. Amazon SES can send the formatted HTML report by email to multiple recipients at once, directly meeting the email delivery and formatting requirement.

✗ C. An EventBridge scheduled event could trigger work daily, but AWS Glue is an ETL service for large-scale data transformation, which is overkill and not suited to simply calling a REST API for shipping statistics.
✓ D. An EventBridge scheduled event invoking an AWS Lambda function every morning is the right way to query the application's REST API and assemble the data on a fixed daily schedule.

✗ E. An S3 event with an SNS topic only sends notifications on object events and cannot produce a formatted HTML report emailed at a scheduled time; SNS does not format HTML reports and is event-driven, not schedule-driven.

text: A company wants to migrate its on-premises application to AWS. The application produces output files that vary in size from tens of gigabytes to hundreds of terabytes. The application data must be stored in a standard file system structure. The company wants a solution that scales automatically. is highly available, and requires minimum operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Migrate the application to run as containers on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use Amazon S3 for storage.
B. Migrate the application to run as containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for storage.
C. Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for storage.
D. Migrate the application to Amazon EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for storage.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Amazon S3 is object storage, not a standard (POSIX) file system structure, so it does not satisfy the requirement for a standard file system, even though ECS could host the app.
✗ B. Amazon EBS volumes are attached to single instances and do not provide a shared, automatically scaling file system across a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group, and EKS adds cluster management overhead.

✓ C. EC2 instances in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group with Amazon EFS provide a standard POSIX file system that automatically scales to petabytes, is highly available across AZs, and requires minimal operational overhead, matching all requirements.

✗ D. Amazon EBS is block storage tied to a single AZ/instance and does not scale automatically as a shared file system, so it cannot store hundreds of terabytes in a shared standard file system with high availability.

text: A company needs to store its accounting records in Amazon S3. The records must be immediately accessible for 1 year and then must be archived for an additional 9 years. No one at the company, including administrative users and root users, can be able to delete the records during the entire 10-year period. The records must be stored with maximum resiliency. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Store the records in S3 Glacier for the entire 10-year period. Use an access control policy to deny deletion of the records for a period of 10 years.
B. Store the records by using S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use an IAM policy to deny deletion of the records. After 10 years, change the IAM policy to allow deletion.
C. Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.

D. Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode for a period of 10 years.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. An access control policy can be modified or removed by privileged/root users, so it cannot guarantee that no one can delete the records, and storing everything in S3 Glacier for the full period does not provide immediate access during year one.
✗ B. An IAM policy can be changed by administrators or root, so it does not provide the WORM guarantee that prevents deletion by all users including root.

✓ C. An S3 Lifecycle policy transitions records to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after the first year for low-cost long-term archival, and S3 Object Lock in compliance mode enforces immutability that even the root user cannot override for the 10-year retention, with S3 providing maximum resiliency across multiple AZs.

✗ D. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, reducing resiliency rather than maximizing it, and Object Lock in governance mode can be bypassed by users with special permissions, so it does not prevent all deletions.

text: A company runs multiple Windows workloads on AWS. The company's employees use Windows file shares that are hosted on two Amazon EC2 instances. The file shares synchronize data between themselves and maintain duplicate copies. The company wants a highly available and durable storage solution that preserves how users currently access the files. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Migrate all the data to Amazon S3. Set up IAM authentication for users to access files.
B. Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Mount the S3 File Gateway on the existing EC2 instances.
C. Extend the file share environment to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to FSx for Windows File Server.
D. Extend the file share environment to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to Amazon EFS.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Migrating to Amazon S3 with IAM authentication changes how users access files (object API instead of Windows file shares) and does not preserve the existing SMB file share access pattern.

✗ B. An S3 File Gateway presents files over SMB/NFS but is a hybrid gateway backed by S3 objects and is intended for on-premises access; it does not natively replace native Windows file shares with a fully managed highly available service in the way required here.

✓ C. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed native Windows (SMB) file shares with a Multi-AZ configuration for high availability and durability, preserving exactly how users currently access the files.
✗ D. Amazon EFS uses the NFS protocol and is for Linux workloads; it does not support the native Windows SMB shares the employees currently use.

text: A solutions architect is developing a VPC architecture that includes multiple subnets. The architecture will host applications that use Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances. The architecture consists of six subnets in two Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone includes a public subnet, a private subnet, and a dedicated subnet for databases. Only EC2 instances that run in the private subnets can have access to the RDS databases. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a new route table that excludes the route to the public subnets' CIDR blocks. Associate the route table with the database subnets.
B. Create a security group that denies inbound trafic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the public subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
C. Create a security group that allows inbound trafic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the private subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
D. Create a new peering connection between the public subnets and the private subnets. Create a different peering connection between the private subnets and the database subnets.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Route tables control routing between subnets but do not by themselves restrict which instances can connect to the RDS databases; subnets in the same VPC remain reachable, so this does not enforce the access requirement.
✗ B. Security groups are stateful allow-lists and do not support deny rules, so you cannot create a security group that 'denies' inbound traffic from the public subnets' group.

✓ C. Creating a security group that allows inbound traffic only from the security group assigned to the private-subnet EC2 instances, and attaching it to the DB instances, precisely permits only those instances to reach RDS while implicitly denying everything else.
✗ D. VPC peering connects separate VPCs, not subnets within the same VPC; you cannot create peering connections between subnets, so this option is invalid.

text: A company has registered its domain name with Amazon Route 53. The company uses Amazon API Gateway in the ca-central-1 Region as a public interface for its backend microservice APIs. Third-party services consume the APIs securely. The company wants to design its API Gateway URL with the company's domain name and corresponding certificate so that the third-party services can use HTTPS. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create stage variables in API Gateway with Name="Endpoint-URL" and Value="Company Domain Name" to overwrite the default URL. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).

B. Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point the alias record to the Regional API Gateway stage endpoint. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.

C. Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway endpoint. Configure Route 53 to route trafic to the API Gateway endpoint.

D. Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway APIs. Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point an A record to the company's domain name.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. API Gateway stage variables do not override the public endpoint URL with a custom domain, and a Regional custom domain requires the ACM certificate to be in the same Region as the API, not addressed correctly here.

✗ B. Pointing a Route 53 alias to the Regional endpoint is part of the answer, but for a Regional API Gateway custom domain the ACM certificate must be imported in the same Region (ca-central-1), not us-east-1, so this is incorrect.

✓ C. Creating a Regional API Gateway endpoint, associating it with the company's custom domain name, importing the public ACM certificate in the same Region as the API, attaching it to the custom domain, and configuring Route 53 to route traffic to that endpoint correctly enables HTTPS with the company's domain.

✗ D. For a Regional API Gateway custom domain the certificate must be in the same Region as the API (ca-central-1); us-east-1 is only required for edge-optimized endpoints, so importing the certificate in us-east-1 here is incorrect.

text: A company is running a popular social media website. The website gives users the ability to upload images to share with other users. The company wants to make sure that the images do not contain inappropriate content. The company needs a solution that minimizes development effort. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon Comprehend to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
B. Use Amazon Rekognition to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
C. Use Amazon SageMaker to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
D. Use AWS Fargate to deploy a custom machine learning model to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service for text, not images, so it cannot detect inappropriate visual content in uploaded images.

✓ B. Amazon Rekognition provides built-in content moderation that detects inappropriate or unsafe images and returns confidence scores, and it integrates with Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) for human review of low-confidence predictions, minimizing development effort.
✗ C. Amazon SageMaker requires building, training, and managing a custom model, which is significant development effort and does not minimize work as required.

✗ D. Deploying a custom machine learning model on AWS Fargate requires building, training, and operating the model and infrastructure, which is the most development-intensive option and contrary to the minimal-effort requirement.

text: A company wants to run its critical applications in containers to meet requirements for scalability and availability. The company prefers to focus on maintenance of the critical applications. The company does not want to be responsible for provisioning and managing the underlying infrastructure that runs the containerized workload. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon EC2 instances, and install Docker on the instances.
B. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
C. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
D. Use Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)-optimized Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Installing Docker on self-managed EC2 instances still requires the company to provision, patch, and manage the underlying servers, which the company explicitly wants to avoid.
✗ B. Amazon ECS on EC2 worker nodes still requires the company to manage the EC2 instances/cluster capacity, so it does not remove responsibility for the underlying infrastructure.

✓ C. Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate runs containers serverlessly without the company provisioning or managing any EC2 infrastructure, while providing scalability and availability, exactly meeting the requirements.
✗ D. Using EC2 instances from an ECS-optimized AMI still leaves the company responsible for provisioning and managing those EC2 instances, which is what they want to avoid.

text: A company hosts more than 300 global websites and applications. The company requires a platform to analyze more than 30 TB of clickstream data each day. What should a solutions architect do to transmit and process the clickstream data?
options: A. Design an AWS Data Pipeline to archive the data to an Amazon S3 bucket and run an Amazon EMR cluster with the data to generate analytics.
B. Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to process the data and send it to an Amazon S3 data lake for Amazon Redshift to use for analysis.
C. Cache the data to Amazon CloudFront. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. When an object is added to the S3 bucket. run an AWS Lambda function to process the data for analysis.
D. Collect the data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to transmit the data to an Amazon S3 data lake. Load the data in Amazon Redshift for analysis.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. AWS Data Pipeline with EMR can run analytics but is a batch-oriented, higher-overhead approach that is not designed for continuously transmitting high-volume real-time clickstream data and is largely a legacy service.
✗ B. Building and managing an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances to ingest clickstream data adds significant operational overhead and is not a purpose-built streaming ingestion solution.

✗ C. Amazon CloudFront is a CDN for content delivery, not a clickstream ingestion pipeline; triggering Lambda per S3 object is not an appropriate or scalable way to transmit and process 30 TB/day of streaming clickstream data.

✓ D. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams collects the high-volume real-time clickstream data, Kinesis Data Firehose reliably delivers it to an Amazon S3 data lake, and loading it into Amazon Redshift enables analysis, which is the purpose-built, scalable pipeline for this use case.

text: A company has a website hosted on AWS. The website is behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that is configured to handle HTTP and HTTPS separately. The company wants to forward all requests to the website so that the requests will use HTTPS. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?
options: A. Update the ALB's network ACL to accept only HTTPS trafic.
B. Create a rule that replaces the HTTP in the URL with HTTPS.
C. Create a listener rule on the ALB to redirect HTTP trafic to HTTPS.
D. Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer configured to use Server Name Indication (SNI).
optionExplanations: ✗ A. A network ACL operates at Layer 3/4 and accepting only HTTPS would simply block HTTP requests rather than redirecting them to HTTPS, so users on HTTP would fail instead of being forwarded.
✗ B. There is no generic ALB feature that 'replaces HTTP in the URL with HTTPS' as a string rewrite; redirection must be done via a listener rule, making this option imprecise/incorrect.
✓ C. An ALB HTTP listener rule can be configured to redirect HTTP (port 80) traffic to HTTPS (port 443), forwarding all requests to use HTTPS exactly as required.
✗ D. A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and cannot perform HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects; SNI relates to TLS certificate selection, not protocol redirection.

text: A company is developing a two-tier web application on AWS. The company's developers have deployed the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that connects directly to a backend Amazon RDS database. The company must not hardcode database credentials in the application. The company must also implement a solution to automatically rotate the database credentials on a regular basis. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Store the database credentials in the instance metadata. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and instance metadata at the same time.

B. Store the database credentials in a configuration file in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and the credentials in the configuration file at the same time. Use S3 Versioning to ensure the ability to fall back to previous values.
C. Store the database credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation for the secret. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the secret.

D. Store the database credentials as encrypted parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation for the encrypted parameters. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the encrypted parameters.
optionExplanations: ✗ Instance metadata is not a secure credential store and cannot natively rotate RDS credentials; building a Lambda to sync metadata is high operational overhead and insecure.
✗ Storing credentials in an S3 config file and building a Lambda to rotate them is custom, high-overhead, and less secure than a managed secrets service.

✓ AWS Secrets Manager natively integrates with RDS, supports built-in automatic credential rotation via managed Lambda, and the EC2 role can be granted least-privilege access, giving the least operational overhead.
✗ SSM Parameter Store can store encrypted parameters but does not provide built-in automatic rotation for database credentials; rotation would require custom Lambda code, adding overhead.

text: A company is deploying a new public web application to AWS. The application will run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application needs to be encrypted at the edge with an SSL/TLS certificate that is issued by an external certificate authority (CA). The certificate must be rotated each year before the certificate expires. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.

B. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an SSL/TLS certificate. Import the key material from the certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALUse the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.

C. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private Certificate Authority to issue an SSL/TLS certificate from the root CA. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.

D. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to import an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send a notification when the certificate is nearing expiration. Rotate the certificate manually.
optionExplanations: ✗ ACM can issue and auto-renew public certificates, but ACM-issued public certs are signed by Amazon's CA, not by the required external CA, so this does not meet the requirement.
✗ ACM does not let you export or import key material from an ACM-issued certificate, and managed renewal does not apply to externally issued certs; this option is technically invalid.
✗ ACM Private CA issues certificates from a private root CA, which are not trusted by public clients and are not from the specified external CA, so it is unsuitable for a public web application.
✓ For a certificate from an external CA, you import it into ACM and apply it to the ALB; ACM cannot auto-renew imported certs, so EventBridge can notify on expiration and you rotate manually.

text: A company runs its infrastructure on AWS and has a registered base of 700,000 users for its document management application. The company intends to create a product that converts large .pdf files to .jpg image files. The .pdf files average 5 MB in size. The company needs to store the original files and the converted files. A solutions architect must design a scalable solution to accommodate demand that will grow rapidly over time. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Save the .pdf files to Amazon S3. Configure an S3 PUT event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in Amazon S3.
B. Save the .pdf files to Amazon DynamoDUse the DynamoDB Streams feature to invoke an AWS Lambda function to convert the files to .jpg format and store them back in DynamoDB.

C. Upload the .pdf files to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application that includes Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage, and an Auto Scaling group. Use a program in the EC2 instances to convert the files to .jpg format. Save the .pdf files and the .jpg files in the EBS store.

D. Upload the .pdf files to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application that includes Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) storage, and an Auto Scaling group. Use a program in the EC2 instances to convert the file to .jpg format. Save the .pdf files and the .jpg files in the EBS store.
optionExplanations: ✓ Storing PDFs in S3 and using an S3 PUT event to trigger a Lambda for conversion is serverless, fully scalable, and most cost-effective since you pay only per request and for durable S3 storage.
✗ DynamoDB is a key-value database not designed to store 5 MB binary files (400 KB item limit) and is not appropriate for image/document storage, making this unworkable and not cost-effective.

✗ Running Elastic Beanstalk EC2 instances with EBS for conversion incurs continuous compute and per-instance EBS costs, and EBS volumes cannot be shared across instances, making it less scalable and more expensive than serverless.
✗ This option mixes EFS and EBS inconsistently and still requires always-on EC2 instances, which is more costly and operationally heavier than the serverless S3-plus-Lambda approach.

text: A company has more than 5 TB of file data on Windows file servers that run on premises. Users and applications interact with the data each day. The company is moving its Windows workloads to AWS. As the company continues this process, the company requires access to AWS and on- premises file storage with minimum latency. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead and requires no significant changes to the existing file access patterns. The company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection for connectivity to AWS. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Move the on-premises file data to FSx for Windows File Server. Reconfigure the workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS.

B. Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the S3 File Gateway. Reconfigure the on- premises workloads and the cloud workloads to use the S3 File Gateway.

C. Deploy and configure an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to Amazon S3. Reconfigure the workloads to use either Amazon S3 directly or the S3 File Gateway. depending on each workload's location.

D. Deploy and configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Deploy and configure an Amazon FSx File Gateway on premises. Move the on-premises file data to the FSx File Gateway. Configure the cloud workloads to use FSx for Windows File Server on AWS. Configure the on- premises workloads to use the FSx File Gateway.
optionExplanations: ✗ Moving all data to FSx for Windows File Server in AWS and reconfiguring on-premises workloads to access it over the VPN introduces high latency for on-premises users, failing the minimum-latency requirement.

✗ S3 File Gateway exposes data via NFS/SMB to S3 objects but is not a native Windows file system and changes file access patterns; it is not ideal for Windows workloads needing SMB with full fidelity.

✗ S3 File Gateway storing data as S3 objects changes the existing Windows file access patterns and does not provide a native Windows file system, so it does not meet the no-significant-changes requirement.

✓ FSx for Windows File Server provides native Windows file shares in AWS, while the Amazon FSx File Gateway caches files on premises for low-latency local access, preserving existing SMB access patterns with minimal overhead.

text: A hospital recently deployed a RESTful API with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The hospital uses API Gateway and Lambda to upload reports that are in PDF format and JPEG format. The hospital needs to modify the Lambda code to identify protected health information (PHI) in the reports. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use existing Python libraries to extract the text from the reports and to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
B. Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon SageMaker to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
C. Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
D. Use Amazon Rekognition to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
optionExplanations: ✗ Building custom Python libraries to extract text and identify PHI requires developing and maintaining PHI-detection logic, which is high operational overhead and error-prone.
✗ Textract correctly extracts text, but using SageMaker requires building, training, and maintaining a custom ML model to detect PHI, which is significant operational overhead.
✓ Amazon Textract extracts text from PDF and JPEG documents, and Amazon Comprehend Medical is a purpose-built managed service that detects PHI automatically, giving the least operational overhead.
✗ Amazon Rekognition is for image/video analysis and only does limited text-in-image detection, not full document text extraction from PDFs, so it is the wrong service for extracting report text.

text: A company has an application that generates a large number of files, each approximately 5 MB in size. The files are stored in Amazon S3. Company policy requires the files to be stored for 4 years before they can be deleted. Immediate accessibility is always required as the files contain critical business data that is not easy to reproduce. The files are frequently accessed in the first 30 days of the object creation but are rarely accessed after the first 30 days. Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?
options: A. Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
B. Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
C. Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.

D. Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Move the files to S3 Glacier 4 years after object creation.
optionExplanations: ✗ S3 Glacier does not provide immediate accessibility (retrievals take minutes to hours), violating the always-immediately-accessible requirement.
✗ S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, reducing durability/availability; for critical data that is hard to reproduce, the single-AZ risk makes it unsuitable despite lower cost.

✓ S3 Standard-IA gives immediate access at lower storage cost for infrequently accessed data while retaining multi-AZ durability, and a lifecycle rule deletes the files after 4 years, making it the most cost-effective fit.
✗ Moving to Glacier at 4 years coincides with deletion, so it adds no benefit; the files should simply be deleted at 4 years, making this option illogical.

text: A company hosts an application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes messages from an Amazon SQS queue, writes to an Amazon RDS table, and deletes the message from the queue. Occasional duplicate records are found in the RDS table. The SQS queue does not contain any duplicate messages. What should a solutions architect do to ensure messages are being processed once only?
options: A. Use the CreateQueue API call to create a new queue.
B. Use the AddPermission API call to add appropriate permissions.
C. Use the ReceiveMessage API call to set an appropriate wait time.
D. Use the ChangeMessageVisibility API call to increase the visibility timeout.
optionExplanations: ✗ Creating a new queue does not address duplicate processing caused by messages becoming visible again before processing completes.
✗ Adding permissions via AddPermission controls access policy and has nothing to do with preventing duplicate record processing.
✗ Setting a wait time on ReceiveMessage enables long polling to reduce empty responses, but it does not prevent duplicates caused by visibility timeout expiring during processing.

✓ Duplicates occur because processing takes longer than the visibility timeout, so the message reappears and is processed again; increasing the visibility timeout with ChangeMessageVisibility prevents reprocessing before deletion.

text: A solutions architect is designing a new hybrid architecture to extend a company's on-premises infrastructure to AWS. The company requires a highly available connection with consistent low latency to an AWS Region. The company needs to minimize costs and is willing to accept slower trafic if the primary connection fails. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a VPN connection as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
B. Provision a VPN tunnel connection to a Region for private connectivity. Provision a second VPN tunnel for private connectivity and as a backup if the primary VPN connection fails.
C. Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a second Direct Connect connection to the same Region as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.

D. Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Use the Direct Connect failover attribute from the AWS CLI to automatically create a backup connection if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
optionExplanations: ✓ A Direct Connect connection provides consistent low latency for the primary path, and a lower-cost VPN backup accepts slower traffic on failover, meeting high availability at minimum cost.
✗ Two VPN tunnels rely on the public internet and cannot guarantee the consistent low latency the company requires for the primary connection.
✗ A second Direct Connect connection provides high availability but is far more expensive than a VPN backup, conflicting with the requirement to minimize costs.
✗ There is no Direct Connect failover attribute in the AWS CLI that automatically provisions a backup connection; this option is fabricated and not a valid AWS capability.

text: A company is running a business-critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database that is deployed in a single Availability Zone. The company wants the application to be highly available with minimum downtime and minimum loss of data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Place the EC2 instances in different AWS Regions. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks to redirect trafic. Use Aurora PostgreSQL Cross- Region Replication.
B. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the database as Multi-AZ. Configure an Amazon RDS Proxy instance for the database.
C. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use one Availability Zone. Generate hourly snapshots of the database. Recover the database from the snapshots in the event of a failure.

D. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple AWS Regions. Write the data from the application to Amazon S3. Use S3 Event Notifications to launch an AWS Lambda function to write the data to the database.
optionExplanations: ✗ Multi-Region EC2 with Route 53 and Aurora cross-Region replication is far more complex and operationally heavy than needed for AZ-level high availability.

✓ Spreading the Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs and converting Aurora to Multi-AZ provides high availability with minimal data loss and low effort, and RDS Proxy improves connection resilience during failover.
✗ Using a single AZ with hourly snapshots leaves a single point of failure and risks up to an hour of data loss, failing the minimum-downtime and minimum-data-loss requirements.
✗ Auto Scaling groups do not span multiple AWS Regions, and routing writes through S3 and Lambda is an overly complex, fragile design that is not appropriate.

text: A company's HTTP application is behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The NLB's target group is configured to use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with multiple EC2 instances that run the web service. The company notices that the NLB is not detecting HTTP errors for the application. These errors require a manual restart of the EC2 instances that run the web service. The company needs to improve the application's availability without writing custom scripts or code. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Enable HTTP health checks on the NLB, supplying the URL of the company's application.
B. Add a cron job to the EC2 instances to check the local application's logs once each minute. If HTTP errors are detected. the application will restart.
C. Replace the NLB with an Application Load Balancer. Enable HTTP health checks by supplying the URL of the company's application. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances.
D. Create an Amazon Cloud Watch alarm that monitors the UnhealthyHostCount metric for the NLB. Configure an Auto Scaling action to replace unhealthy instances when the alarm is in the ALARM state.
optionExplanations: ✗ Network Load Balancers do not support application-layer HTTP health checks (they support TCP/HTTP at the listener level limitedly but classic NLB health checks are not HTTP path-based in the way required); relying on the NLB here will not reliably detect HTTP application errors as needed.
✗ Adding a cron job to check logs and restart is custom scripting/code, which the requirement explicitly prohibits.

✓ An Application Load Balancer supports HTTP health checks against an application URL to detect HTTP errors, and Auto Scaling can automatically replace instances that fail those health checks, with no custom code.
✗ UnhealthyHostCount depends on the NLB's health checks, which do not detect application-layer HTTP errors here, so the alarm would not trigger on the HTTP failures the company needs to catch.

text: A company runs a shopping application that uses Amazon DynamoDB to store customer information. In case of data corruption, a solutions architect needs to design a solution that meets a recovery point objective (RPO) of 15 minutes and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 1 hour. What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure DynamoDB global tables. For RPO recovery, point the application to a different AWS Region.
B. Configure DynamoDB point-in-time recovery. For RPO recovery, restore to the desired point in time.
C. Export the DynamoDB data to Amazon S3 Glacier on a daily basis. For RPO recovery, import the data from S3 Glacier to DynamoDB.
D. Schedule Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots for the DynamoDB table every 15 minutes. For RPO recovery, restore the DynamoDB table by using the EBS snapshot.
optionExplanations: ✗ DynamoDB global tables provide multi-Region replication for availability, but they replicate corrupted data too, so they do not protect against data corruption recovery.
✓ DynamoDB point-in-time recovery allows restoring the table to any second in the last 35 days, easily meeting the 15-minute RPO and 1-hour RTO and protecting against data corruption.
✗ Daily exports to S3 Glacier yield an RPO of up to 24 hours and slow Glacier retrievals, failing the 15-minute RPO and 1-hour RTO.
✗ EBS snapshots cannot be taken of a DynamoDB table because DynamoDB is a fully managed service with no EBS volumes, making this option technically invalid.

text: A company runs a photo processing application that needs to frequently upload and download pictures from Amazon S3 buckets that are located in the same AWS Region. A solutions architect has noticed an increased cost in data transfer fees and needs to implement a solution to reduce these costs. How can the solutions architect meet this requirement?
options: A. Deploy Amazon API Gateway into a public subnet and adjust the route table to route S3 calls through it.
B. Deploy a NAT gateway into a public subnet and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
C. Deploy the application into a public subnet and allow it to route through an internet gateway to access the S3 buckets.
D. Deploy an S3 VPC gateway endpoint into the VPC and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
optionExplanations: ✗ API Gateway is for managing APIs and does not reduce S3 data transfer costs; routing S3 calls through it is not a valid cost-reduction mechanism.
✗ A NAT gateway routes traffic to S3 over the internet and incurs additional NAT data processing charges, increasing rather than reducing costs.
✗ Routing through an internet gateway sends S3 traffic over the public path and does not eliminate data transfer charges that an in-Region VPC endpoint would avoid.
✓ An S3 gateway VPC endpoint routes S3 traffic privately within the AWS network at no additional charge, eliminating the data transfer costs incurred when accessing S3 over the internet.

text: A company recently launched Linux-based application instances on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet and launched a Linux-based bastion host on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet of a VPC. A solutions architect needs to connect from the on-premises network, through the company's internet connection, to the bastion host, and to the application servers. The solutions architect must make sure that the security groups of all the EC2 instances will allow that access. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the application instances.
B. Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the internal IP range for the company.
C. Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the external IP range for the company.
D. Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the private IP address of the bastion host.
E. Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the public IP address of the bastion host.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: allowing inbound only from the application instances would block the on-premises users from reaching the bastion host at all.
✗ Wrong: the company's internal/private IP range is not what arrives at the bastion; traffic traverses the internet via the company's NAT/firewall, so it presents the company's external public IP.
✓ the bastion is in a public subnet and on-premises traffic reaches it over the internet, so its security group must allow inbound SSH from the company's external (public) IP range.
✓ the application instances are in the private subnet and are reached from the bastion within the VPC, so they should allow inbound SSH only from the bastion's private IP address.
✗ Wrong: traffic from the bastion to the private application instances is routed internally using the bastion's private IP, not its public IP, so referencing the public IP would not match.

text: A solutions architect is designing a two-tier web application. The application consists of a public-facing web tier hosted on Amazon EC2 in public subnets. The database tier consists of Microsoft SQL Server running on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet. Security is a high priority for the company. How should security groups be configured in this situation? (Choose two.)
options: A. Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound trafic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
B. Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound trafic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
C. Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound trafic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
D. Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound trafic on ports 443 and 1433 to the security group for the web tier.
E. Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound trafic on ports 443 and 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
optionExplanations: ✓ the public-facing web tier must accept inbound HTTPS on port 443 from any client on the internet (0.0.0.0/0).
✗ Wrong: security groups are stateful, so outbound rules for return traffic are not required; this also misconfigures HTTPS serving (outbound on 443 to all is for the tier acting as a client).
✓ the SQL Server database tier should allow inbound on port 1433 only from the web tier's security group, restricting access to that tier.
✗ Wrong: security groups are stateful and there is no need to add an explicit outbound rule, and port 443 is not relevant to the database accepting connections.
✗ Wrong: the database does not need inbound on port 443; only port 1433 (SQL Server) from the web tier security group is required, so adding 443 is unnecessary exposure.

text: A company wants to move a multi-tiered application from on premises to the AWS Cloud to improve the application's performance. The application consists of application tiers that communicate with each other by way of RESTful services. Transactions are dropped when one tier becomes overloaded. A solutions architect must design a solution that resolves these issues and modernizes the application. Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally eficient?
options: A. Use Amazon API Gateway and direct transactions to the AWS Lambda functions as the application layer. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) as the communication layer between application services.

B. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze the application performance history to determine the servers' peak utilization during the performance failures. Increase the size of the application server's Amazon EC2 instances to meet the peak requirements.

C. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SNS queue length and scale up and down as required.

D. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SQS queue length and scale up when communication failures are detected.
optionExplanations: ✓ API Gateway with Lambda is a serverless, modernized application layer, and SQS decouples the tiers with a durable buffer so transactions are not dropped when a tier is overloaded; this is the most operationally efficient choice.
✗ Wrong: vertically scaling EC2 instances does not modernize the application and does not prevent dropped transactions during spikes; it adds operational burden and a fixed ceiling.
✗ Wrong: SNS is a pub/sub notification service, not a queue with a length to buffer overload; it cannot reliably hold and replay dropped transactions, and there is no SNS queue length metric.
✗ Wrong: while SQS correctly decouples the tiers, keeping the app on EC2 in an Auto Scaling group is not the modernized, most operationally efficient design compared to API Gateway plus Lambda.

text: A company receives 10 TB of instrumentation data each day from several machines located at a single factory. The data consists of JSON files stored on a storage area network (SAN) in an on-premises data center located within the factory. The company wants to send this data to Amazon S3 where it can be accessed by several additional systems that provide critical near-real-time analytics. A secure transfer is important because the data is considered sensitive. Which solution offers the MOST reliable data transfer?
options: A. AWS DataSync over public internet
B. AWS DataSync over AWS Direct Connect
C. AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) over public internet
D. AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) over AWS Direct Connect
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: DataSync is the right transfer tool, but the public internet is less reliable and consistent than a dedicated connection for sensitive 10 TB/day transfers.

✓ AWS DataSync is purpose-built for fast, secure, reliable transfer of large file/object datasets to S3, and running it over Direct Connect provides a dedicated, consistent, private connection for the most reliable transfer.
✗ Wrong: AWS DMS is for migrating databases, not transferring JSON files from a SAN to S3, so it is the wrong tool regardless of the network path.
✗ Wrong: AWS DMS is a database migration service and is not suited to moving JSON files to S3, even over Direct Connect.

text: A company needs to configure a real-time data ingestion architecture for its application. The company needs an API, a process that transforms data as the data is streamed, and a storage solution for the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance to host an API that sends data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.

B. Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance to host an API that sends data to AWS Glue. Stop source/destination checking on the EC2 instance. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to send the data to Amazon S3.

C. Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that uses the Kinesis data stream as a data source. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to send the data to Amazon S3.
D. Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to send data to AWS Glue. Use AWS Lambda functions to transform the data. Use AWS Glue to send the data to Amazon S3.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: hosting the API on a self-managed EC2 instance adds operational overhead compared to a fully managed API Gateway endpoint.
✗ Wrong: Glue is a batch ETL service, not a real-time streaming transform; running an EC2-hosted API and disabling source/destination checks is irrelevant and not real-time.

✓ API Gateway provides the managed API, Kinesis Data Streams ingests in real time, Kinesis Data Firehose with Lambda transforms the streaming data, and Firehose delivers it to S3, all fully managed with the least operational overhead.
✗ Wrong: Glue is not designed for real-time streaming ingestion and delivery, so this combination does not meet the real-time requirement with the least overhead.

text: A company needs to keep user transaction data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company must retain the data for 7 years. What is the MOST operationally eficient solution that meets these requirements?
options: A. Use DynamoDB point-in-time recovery to back up the table continuously.
B. Use AWS Backup to create backup schedules and retention policies for the table.
C. Create an on-demand backup of the table by using the DynamoDB console. Store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.

D. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to back up the table and to store the backup in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set an S3 Lifecycle configuration for the S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery only retains a rolling 35-day window, so it cannot meet a 7-year retention requirement.
✓ AWS Backup natively supports DynamoDB with centralized backup schedules and retention policies, making it the most operationally efficient way to retain data for 7 years.
✗ Wrong: manual on-demand console backups with custom S3 lifecycle management is a manual, error-prone process and adds significant operational overhead.
✗ Wrong: building a custom EventBridge plus Lambda backup pipeline is far more operationally complex than using the managed AWS Backup service.

text: A company is planning to use an Amazon DynamoDB table for data storage. The company is concerned about cost optimization. The table will not be used on most mornings. In the evenings, the read and write trafic will often be unpredictable. When trafic spikes occur, they will happen very quickly. What should a solutions architect recommend?
options: A. Create a DynamoDB table in on-demand capacity mode.
B. Create a DynamoDB table with a global secondary index.
C. Create a DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity and auto scaling.
D. Create a DynamoDB table in provisioned capacity mode, and configure it as a global table.
optionExplanations: ✓ on-demand capacity mode automatically accommodates unpredictable traffic that can spike very quickly and charges nothing for idle periods, making it ideal and cost-effective for this workload.
✗ Wrong: a global secondary index addresses query access patterns, not capacity cost optimization for unpredictable spiky traffic.
✗ Wrong: provisioned with auto scaling reacts gradually and can be throttled by very fast, sudden spikes, and it still incurs cost during idle mornings.
✗ Wrong: provisioned capacity does not handle sudden unpredictable spikes well, and a global table adds multi-Region cost and complexity that is unnecessary here.

text: A company recently signed a contract with an AWS Managed Service Provider (MSP) Partner for help with an application migration initiative. A solutions architect needs ta share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from an existing AWS account with the MSP Partner's AWS account. The AMI is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) and uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt EBS volume snapshots. What is the MOST secure way for the solutions architect to share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account?
options: A. Make the encrypted AMI and snapshots publicly available. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
B. Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.

C. Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to trust a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner for encryption.

D. Export the AMI from the source account to an Amazon S3 bucket in the MSP Partner's AWS account, Encrypt the S3 bucket with a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner. Copy and launch the AMI in the MSP Partner's AWS account.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: making the encrypted AMI and snapshots publicly available is highly insecure and violates the requirement to share only with the MSP Partner.

✓ modifying the AMI launchPermission to share only with the MSP Partner's account, combined with updating the customer managed KMS key policy to grant that account permission to use the key, securely shares the encrypted AMI.
✗ Wrong: a KMS key cannot be decrypted by trusting a different key owned by the partner; the encrypted snapshots require access to the original key, so this would not allow the AMI to launch.
✗ Wrong: AMIs cannot simply be exported to an S3 bucket and re-launched this way, and this convoluted approach is unnecessary and not the secure intended sharing mechanism.

text: A solutions architect is designing the cloud architecture for a new application being deployed on AWS. The process should run in parallel while adding and removing application nodes as needed based on the number of jobs to be processed. The processor application is stateless. The solutions architect must ensure that the application is loosely coupled and the job items are durably stored. Which design should the solutions architect use?
options: A. Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on CPU usage.

B. Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on network usage.

C. Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of items in the SQS queue.

D. Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of messages published to the SNS topic.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: SNS is pub/sub and does not durably store job items for later processing, and scaling on CPU usage does not reflect the number of pending jobs; launch configurations are also legacy.
✗ Wrong: although SQS provides durable decoupling, scaling on network usage does not accurately track the number of jobs to process, and launch configurations are the legacy approach.

✓ SQS durably stores job items and loosely couples the tiers, a launch template plus Auto Scaling group runs the stateless processor, and scaling on the number of items in the SQS queue matches capacity to the actual job backlog.
✗ Wrong: SNS does not durably store jobs for pull-based processing, and there is no native ASG scaling metric for messages published to an SNS topic.

text: A company hosts its web applications in the AWS Cloud. The company configures Elastic Load Balancers to use certificates that are imported into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). The company's security team must be notified 30 days before the expiration of each certificate. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?
options: A. Add a rule in ACM to publish a custom message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic every day, beginning 30 days before any certificate will expire.

B. Create an AWS Config rule that checks for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when AWS Config reports a noncompliant resource.

C. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on Trusted Advisor metrics for check status changes. Configure the alarm to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

D. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to detect any certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: ACM does not have a built-in rule feature to publish daily custom SNS messages starting 30 days before expiration.

✓ the AWS Config managed rule acm-certificate-expiration-check flags certificates expiring within a configurable window, and EventBridge can react to the noncompliant finding to send an SNS alert, meeting the 30-day notification requirement.

✗ Wrong: Trusted Advisor's certificate expiration check covers ELB-associated ACM certificates but this CloudWatch-on-Trusted-Advisor-metrics approach is less reliable and not the recommended pattern compared to the AWS Config rule.

✗ Wrong: EventBridge cannot directly detect certificates expiring within 30 days on its own; it has no native scheduled query of ACM expiry, so a Lambda function would have to implement the check, making it more complex than the AWS Config managed rule.

text: A company's dynamic website is hosted using on-premises servers in the United States. The company is launching its product in Europe, and it wants to optimize site loading times for new European users. The site's backend must remain in the United States. The product is being launched in a few days, and an immediate solution is needed. What should the solutions architect recommend?
options: A. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in us-east-1 and migrate the site to it.
B. Move the website to Amazon S3. Use Cross-Region Replication between Regions.
C. Use Amazon CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the on-premises servers.
D. Use an Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing policy pointing to on-premises servers.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: launching an EC2 instance in us-east-1 keeps the content in the United States and does nothing to reduce loading times for European users.
✗ Wrong: the site is dynamic, so it cannot simply be served as static objects from S3, and Cross-Region Replication would not handle dynamic backend processing.

✓ CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the existing on-premises servers caches and accelerates content at edge locations near European users while keeping the backend in the United States, and it can be deployed immediately.
✗ Wrong: Route 53 geoproximity routing only directs DNS to endpoints; with a single on-premises backend it does not reduce latency or accelerate delivery for European users.

text: A company wants to reduce the cost of its existing three-tier web architecture. The web, application, and database servers are running on Amazon EC2 instances for the development, test, and production environments. The EC2 instances average 30% CPU utilization during peak hours and 10% CPU utilization during non-peak hours. The production EC2 instances run 24 hours a day. The development and test EC2 instances run for at least 8 hours each day. The company plans to implement automation to stop the development and test EC2 instances when they are not in use. Which EC2 instance purchasing solution will meet the company's requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use Spot Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
B. Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
C. Use Spot blocks for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
D. Use On-Demand Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Spot blocks for the development and test EC2 instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: production runs 24/7 and must be reliable, so Spot Instances (which can be interrupted) are inappropriate for production, and Reserved Instances for intermittently stopped dev/test wastes the upfront commitment.

✓ Reserved Instances are most cost-effective for the always-on production instances, while On-Demand Instances suit the dev/test instances that run only part-time and are stopped when not in use (you pay only while running).
✗ Wrong: Spot blocks for production risk interruption of the 24/7 workload and are deprecated, and Reserved Instances for stopped dev/test instances waste the commitment.
✗ Wrong: On-Demand for always-on production is more expensive than Reserved Instances, and Spot blocks are a poor and deprecated fit for dev/test.

text: A company has a production web application in which users upload documents through a web interface or a mobile app. According to a new regulatory requirement. new documents cannot be modified or deleted after they are stored. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?
options: A. Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning and S3 Object Lock enabled.
B. Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to archive the documents periodically.
C. Store the uploaded documents in an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an ACL to restrict all access to read-only.
D. Store the uploaded documents on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Access the data by mounting the volume in read- only mode.
optionExplanations: ✓ S3 Object Lock provides WORM (write-once-read-many) protection so objects cannot be modified or deleted, and it requires S3 Versioning to be enabled, satisfying the regulatory immutability requirement.
✗ Wrong. An S3 Lifecycle policy that archives documents only changes their storage class (e.g., to Glacier); it does not prevent the objects from being modified or deleted.
✗ Wrong. Versioning alone preserves old versions but does not block deletion or overwrites, and ACLs control access permissions rather than enforcing immutability; objects could still be deleted.

✗ Wrong. EFS mounted read-only only restricts the client that mounts it that way; the underlying file system data can still be modified or deleted by other clients, so it does not enforce true immutability.

text: A company has several web servers that need to frequently access a common Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. The company wants a secure method for the web servers to connect to the database while meeting a security requirement to rotate user credentials frequently. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Store the database user credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access AWS Secrets Manager.
B. Store the database user credentials in AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to access OpsCenter.
C. Store the database user credentials in a secure Amazon S3 bucket. Grant the necessary IAM permissions to allow the web servers to retrieve credentials and access the database.

D. Store the database user credentials in files encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) on the web server file system. The web server should be able to decrypt the files and access the database.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Secrets Manager securely stores database credentials and provides built-in automatic rotation for RDS, and EC2 web servers can retrieve them using IAM permissions, meeting the secure storage and frequent rotation requirements.
