The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Users are starting to experience long delays and interruptions that are caused by database read performance. The company wants to improve the user experience while minimizing changes to the application’s architecture. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon ElastiCache in front of the database.
B. Use RDS Proxy between the application and the database.
C. Migrate the application from EC2 instances to AWS Lambda.
D. Migrate the database from Amazon RDS for MySQL to Amazon DynamoDB.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon ElastiCache placed in front of the database caches frequent read query results in memory, dramatically improving read performance with minimal architectural changes.
✗ RDS Proxy pools and manages database connections to improve scalability and failover but does not cache query results, so it does not directly fix read-performance bottlenecks.
✗ Migrating from EC2 to Lambda re-architects the compute tier and does nothing to address the database read performance problem.
✗ Migrating from RDS MySQL to DynamoDB is a major re-architecture requiring data-model and application rewrites, contradicting the goal of minimizing changes.

text: An ecommerce company has noticed performance degradation of its Amazon RDS based web application. The performance degradation is attributed to an increase in the number of read-only SQL queries triggered by business analysts. A solutions architect needs to solve the problem with minimal changes to the existing web application. What should the solutions architect recommend?
options: A. Export the data to Amazon DynamoDB and have the business analysts run their queries.
B. Load the data into Amazon ElastiCache and have the business analysts run their queries.
C. Create a read replica of the primary database and have the business analysts run their queries.
D. Copy the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster and have the business analysts run their queries.
optionExplanations: ✗ Exporting to DynamoDB requires a data model change and rewriting the analysts' relational SQL queries, which is not minimal change.
✗ ElastiCache is an in-memory key/value cache and is not suited for ad hoc analytical SQL queries from business analysts.
✓ Creating an RDS read replica offloads the read-only analyst queries from the primary, relieving the performance degradation with minimal changes to the existing application.
✗ Copying data into a Redshift cluster requires building an ETL pipeline and a separate data warehouse, which is more change than needed for this read-offload problem.

text: A company is using a centralized AWS account to store log data in various Amazon S3 buckets. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the data is encrypted at rest before the data is uploaded to the S3 buckets. The data also must be encrypted in transit. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use client-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
B. Use server-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
C. Create bucket policies that require the use of server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for S3 uploads.
D. Enable the security option to encrypt the S3 buckets through the use of a default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.
optionExplanations: ✓ Client-side encryption encrypts the data on the client before it is uploaded, satisfying the explicit requirement that data be encrypted at rest before upload; combined with the default HTTPS/TLS S3 endpoints, the data is also encrypted in transit. Correct.
✗ Server-side encryption (SSE) encrypts data only after S3 receives it, so the data is NOT encrypted before being uploaded; this fails the stated 'before upload' requirement. Incorrect.
✗ A bucket policy requiring SSE-S3 still encrypts only after S3 receives the data (server-side), not before upload, so it does not meet the pre-upload encryption requirement. Incorrect.
✗ Enabling default SSE-KMS encryption on the bucket also encrypts data only server-side after it arrives at S3, not before upload, so it fails the requirement. Incorrect.

text: A solutions architect observes that a nightly batch processing job is automatically scaled up for 1 hour before the desired Amazon EC2 capacity is reached. The peak capacity is the ‘same every night and the batch jobs always start at 1 AM. The solutions architect needs to find a cost-effective solution that will allow for the desired EC2 capacity to be reached quickly and allow the Auto Scaling group to scale down after the batch jobs are complete. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Increase the minimum capacity for the Auto Scaling group.
B. Increase the maximum capacity for the Auto Scaling group.
C. Configure scheduled scaling to scale up to the desired compute level.
D. Change the scaling policy to add more EC2 instances during each scaling operation.
optionExplanations: ✗ Increasing the minimum capacity would keep instances running all day, wasting cost since the peak is only needed at 1 AM.
✗ Increasing the maximum capacity does not make instances launch faster; the group still scales up reactively over an hour.
✓ Scheduled scaling proactively scales the group to the known peak capacity right before the 1 AM job, reaching desired capacity quickly, then scales down afterward cost-effectively.

✗ Adding more instances per scaling step still relies on reactive metric-based scaling and may overshoot or still lag, and does not deterministically meet the fixed 1 AM start time as well as scheduled scaling.

text: A company serves a dynamic website from a fieet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website needs to support multiple languages to serve customers around the world. The website’s architecture is running in the us-west-1 Region and is exhibiting high request latency for users that are located in other parts of the world. The website needs to serve requests quickly and eficiently regardless of a user’s location. However, the company does not want to recreate the existing architecture across multiple Regions. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Replace the existing architecture with a website that is served from an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
B. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the ALB as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept- Language request header.

C. Create an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with the ALB. Configure the API to use the HTTP integration type. Set up an API Gateway stage to enable the API cache based on the Accept-Language request header.

D. Launch an EC2 instance in each additional Region and configure NGINX to act as a cache server for that Region. Put all the EC2 instances and the ALB behind an Amazon Route 53 record set with a geolocation routing policy.
optionExplanations: ✗ Replacing the dynamic site with a static S3-hosted site is a major re-architecture and S3 cannot serve the existing dynamic application.

✓ A CloudFront distribution with the existing ALB as origin caches and accelerates content globally over the edge network, and caching on the Accept-Language header serves correct localized content quickly without recreating the architecture in other Regions.
✗ API Gateway with HTTP integration adds an unnecessary layer and is not designed to globally accelerate a full dynamic website the way CloudFront does.

✗ Launching NGINX cache EC2 instances in each Region with Route 53 geolocation recreates infrastructure across Regions, which the company explicitly wants to avoid, and adds high operational overhead.

text: A rapidly growing ecommerce company is running its workloads in a single AWS Region. A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) strategy that includes a different AWS Region. The company wants its database to be up to date in the DR Region with the least possible latency. The remaining infrastructure in the DR Region needs to run at reduced capacity and must be able to scale up if necessary. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LOWEST recovery time objective (RTO)?
options: A. Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a pilot light deployment.
B. Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a warm standby deployment.
C. Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a pilot light deployment.
D. Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a warm standby deployment.
optionExplanations: ✗ Aurora global database does give low-latency cross-Region replication, but a pilot light deployment keeps the DR infrastructure minimal/off, requiring it to be provisioned and scaled at failover, yielding a higher RTO than warm standby.

✓ Aurora global database provides cross-Region replication with typically sub-second lag (least latency, database up to date), and a warm standby keeps a scaled-down but running copy of the infrastructure that can scale up, delivering the lowest RTO of these options.

✗ RDS Multi-AZ provides high availability within a single Region only (synchronous standby in another AZ), not cross-Region DR, so it does not satisfy the different-Region requirement; pilot light also adds startup time.
✗ RDS Multi-AZ is confined to a single Region and does not replicate to a separate DR Region as required, so even with a warm standby it fails the cross-Region database requirement.

text: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to implement a disaster recovery (DR) solution for the application. The DR solution needs to have a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 4 hours. The DR solution also needs to use the fewest possible AWS resources during normal operations. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally eficient way?
options: A. Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS Lambda and custom scripts.
B. Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS CloudFormation.
C. Launch EC2 instances in a secondary AWS Region. Keep the EC2 instances in the secondary Region active at all times.
D. Launch EC2 instances in a secondary Availability Zone. Keep the EC2 instances in the secondary Availability Zone active at all times.
optionExplanations: ✗ Backing up with AMIs copied to a secondary Region is a valid low-resource (backup-and-restore) approach, but using AWS Lambda and custom scripts to deploy infrastructure is less operationally efficient and harder to maintain than CloudFormation.

✓ AMIs copied to a secondary Region use minimal resources during normal operations, and AWS CloudFormation automates the full infrastructure deployment quickly to meet an under-4-hour RTO in the most operationally efficient way.
✗ Keeping EC2 instances always active in a secondary Region uses many resources during normal operations, violating the fewest-resources requirement.
✗ Keeping instances active in a secondary Availability Zone is not a cross-Region DR solution and also consumes resources continuously, failing the requirements.

text: A company runs an internal browser-based application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales up to 20 instances during work hours, but scales down to 2 instances overnight. Staff are complaining that the application is very slow when the day begins, although it runs well by mid-morning. How should the scaling be changed to address the staff complaints and keep costs to a minimum?
options: A. Implement a scheduled action that sets the desired capacity to 20 shortly before the ofice opens.
B. Implement a step scaling action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
C. Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
D. Implement a scheduled action that sets the minimum and maximum capacity to 20 shortly before the ofice opens.
optionExplanations: ✓ A scheduled action that sets desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens proactively pre-warms the fleet for the predictable, time-based morning surge, eliminating the reactive scaling lag; because it only sets the starting desired capacity, normal dynamic scaling can still reduce instances later in the day, keeping costs minimal. Correct.

✗ Step scaling triggered at a lower CPU threshold with a shorter cooldown is still reactive: it only responds after CPU rises, so the morning spike still hits the small 2-instance fleet before scaling completes, leaving staff with the same initial slowness. Wrong.

✗ Target tracking with a lower CPU threshold and shorter cooldown remains reactive and cannot pre-empt a predictable scheduled load; the fleet would still start at 2 instances and lag behind the morning demand spike. Wrong.

✗ A scheduled action that sets both minimum and maximum capacity to 20 forces and pins all 20 instances running until the values are changed, preventing any scale-down and incurring unnecessary cost, which violates the keep-costs-to-a-minimum requirement. Wrong.

text: A company has a multi-tier application deployed on several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. An Amazon RDS for Oracle instance is the application’ s data layer that uses Oracle-specific PL/SQL functions. Trafic to the application has been steadily increasing. This is causing the EC2 instances to become overloaded and the RDS instance to run out of storage. The Auto Scaling group does not have any scaling metrics and defines the minimum healthy instance count only. The company predicts that trafic will continue to increase at a steady but unpredictable rate before leveling off. What should a solutions architect do to ensure the system can automatically scale for the increased trafic? (Choose two.)
options: A. Configure storage Auto Scaling on the RDS for Oracle instance.
B. Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora to use Auto Scaling storage.
C. Configure an alarm on the RDS for Oracle instance for low free storage space.
D. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average CPU as the scaling metric.
E. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the average free memory as the scaling metric.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon RDS for Oracle supports storage Auto Scaling, which automatically increases allocated storage when free space runs low, directly solving the database running out of storage without manual intervention.

✗ Migrating to Amazon Aurora would break the application because Aurora (MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible) does not support Oracle-specific PL/SQL functions; this is unnecessary effort when RDS for Oracle already offers storage Auto Scaling.

✗ A CloudWatch alarm on low free storage only notifies or triggers an action manually-configured response; by itself it does not automatically add storage, so it fails the automatic-scaling requirement.

✓ Configuring the Auto Scaling group to scale on average CPU utilization adds/removes EC2 instances as load rises, which addresses the overloaded compute tier for steady, unpredictable traffic growth.

✗ Average free memory is not a native EC2/CloudWatch metric (it requires the CloudWatch agent) and CPU utilization is the more direct and standard indicator of the described overload, making this the weaker choice.

text: A company provides an online service for posting video content and transcoding it for use by any mobile platform. The application architecture uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard to collect and store the videos so that multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances can access the video content for processing. As the popularity of the service has grown over time, the storage costs have become too expensive. Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?
options: A. Use AWS Storage Gateway for files to store and process the video content.
B. Use AWS Storage Gateway for volumes to store and process the video content.
C. Use Amazon EFS for storing the video content. Once processing is complete, transfer the files to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).
D. Use Amazon S3 for storing the video content. Move the files temporarily over to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to the server for processing.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Storage Gateway file gateway is for hybrid on-premises access to S3 via NFS/SMB; it adds an unnecessary gateway layer for a fully cloud-native EC2 workload and is not the most cost-effective approach.
✗ AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway presents iSCSI block volumes backed by S3 for hybrid use; it is not designed for shared cloud-native video processing and does not minimize storage cost here.

✗ Continuing to use Amazon EFS for primary storage keeps the same expensive per-GB file storage that caused the cost problem; EBS is also not a shared multi-instance store, so this does not reduce cost.

✓ Amazon S3 is far cheaper per GB than EFS for storing large volumes of video, and copying files to an attached EBS volume only during processing gives the EC2 instance fast local access while keeping the bulk of data in low-cost S3, making it the most cost-effective solution.

text: A company wants to create an application to store employee data in a hierarchical structured relationship. The company needs a minimum-latency response to high-trafic queries for the employee data and must protect any sensitive data. The company also needs to receive monthly email messages if any financial information is present in the employee data. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Use Amazon Redshift to store the employee data in hierarchies. Unload the data to Amazon S3 every month.
B. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the employee data in hierarchies. Export the data to Amazon S3 every month.
C. Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly events to AWS Lambda.
D. Use Amazon Athena to analyze the employee data in Amazon S3. Integrate Athena with Amazon QuickSight to publish analysis dashboards and share the dashboards with users.
E. Configure Amazon Macie for the AWS account. Integrate Macie with Amazon EventBridge to send monthly notifications through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) subscription.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Redshift is a columnar data warehouse for analytical queries, not optimized for low-latency high-traffic key-based lookups, and it is not designed to natively store hierarchical relationships; this does not meet the minimum-latency hierarchical-data requirement.

✓ Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value/document store that delivers single-digit-millisecond latency at high request volume and supports hierarchical data via composite keys/adjacency-list patterns; exporting to S3 monthly enables downstream scanning for sensitive data, satisfying the latency and hierarchy requirements.

✗ Configuring Amazon Macie correctly detects sensitive/financial data, and integrating with EventBridge is valid, but routing events to AWS Lambda does not by itself deliver the required monthly email notifications, so this option is incomplete compared to using SNS for email.

✗ Amazon Athena queries data in S3 and QuickSight builds dashboards, but this provides analytics/visualization, not low-latency transactional queries, sensitive-data protection, or email alerting; it does not address the stated requirements.

✓ Configuring Amazon Macie discovers sensitive financial data in the S3 export, and integrating Macie findings with EventBridge to publish to an Amazon SNS subscription delivers the required monthly email notifications, satisfying the sensitive-data and email requirements.

text: A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company’s compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.

B. Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.

C. Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month. Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.

D. Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression. Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.
optionExplanations: ✓ A. AWS Backup natively supports DynamoDB, can schedule a backup on the first of each month, transition backups to cold storage after the warm period, and set a 7-year retention, fully managed without custom code.
✗ B. DynamoDB on-demand backups cannot be moved into S3 Glacier with an S3 Lifecycle policy; you do not manage DynamoDB backups as S3 objects, so this approach is not supported.
✗ C. Writing and maintaining custom SDK scripts adds unnecessary operational overhead, and DynamoDB on-demand backups cannot simply be transitioned to cold storage by a script the way described.
✗ D. The AWS CLI on-demand backup command has no parameters to transition backups to cold storage after 6 months or auto-delete after 7 years, so this does not work as stated.

text: A company is using Amazon CloudFront with its website. The company has enabled logging on the CloudFront distribution, and logs are saved in one of the company’s Amazon S3 buckets. The company needs to perform advanced analyses on the logs and build visualizations. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
B. Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
C. Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
D. Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Athena correctly queries CloudFront logs in S3 with SQL, but AWS Glue is an ETL/catalog service and is not a visualization tool.
✓ B. Athena runs standard SQL directly against CloudFront logs in S3, and QuickSight connects to Athena to build the required visualizations and dashboards.
✗ C. DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store and cannot run SQL queries against logs stored in an S3 bucket.
✗ D. DynamoDB cannot query S3-based CloudFront logs with SQL, even though QuickSight is a valid visualization tool.

text: A company runs a fieet of web servers using an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. After a routine compliance check, the company sets a standard that requires a recovery point objective (RPO) of less than 1 second for all its production databases. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
B. Enable auto scaling for the DB instance in one Availability Zone.
C. Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and create multiple read replicas in a separate Availability Zone.
D. Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) tasks.
optionExplanations: ✓ A. A Multi-AZ RDS deployment synchronously replicates to a standby in another AZ, providing an RPO of effectively zero (well under 1 second) with automatic failover.
✗ B. RDS storage auto scaling only grows storage capacity and provides no replication or recovery-point protection.
✗ C. Read replicas use asynchronous replication, which can lag and does not guarantee a sub-1-second RPO.
✗ D. AWS DMS CDC is for ongoing data migration/replication between databases and is not the appropriate or guaranteed mechanism for a sub-1-second production-database RPO.

text: A company runs a web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet of a VPC. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across the public subnets directs web trafic to the EC2 instances. The company wants to implement new security measures to restrict inbound trafic from the ALB to the EC2 instances while preventing access from any other source inside or outside the private subnet of the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure a route in a route table to direct trafic from the internet to the private IP addresses of the EC2 instances.
B. Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to only allow trafic that comes from the security group for the ALB.
C. Move the EC2 instances into the public subnet. Give the EC2 instances a set of Elastic IP addresses.
D. Configure the security group for the ALB to allow any TCP trafic on any port.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Routing internet traffic directly to private EC2 instances exposes them publicly, the opposite of the restriction required, and private instances have no public route anyway.
✓ B. Referencing the ALB's security group as the source in the EC2 security group allows only the ALB to reach the instances and blocks all other sources, exactly meeting the requirement.
✗ C. Moving instances to a public subnet with Elastic IPs increases exposure and does not restrict access to only the ALB.
✗ D. Allowing any TCP traffic on any port to the ALB broadens access rather than restricting it and does not control traffic to the EC2 instances.

text: A research company runs experiments that are powered by a simulation application and a visualization application. The simulation application runs on Linux and outputs intermediate data to an NFS share every 5 minutes. The visualization application is a Windows desktop application that displays the simulation output and requires an SMB file system. The company maintains two synchronized file systems. This strategy is causing data duplication and ineficient resource usage. The company needs to migrate the applications to AWS without making code changes to either application. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Migrate both applications to AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to exchange data between the applications.
B. Migrate both applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon FSx File Gateway for storage.

C. Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to exchange data between the applications.
D. Migrate the simulation application to Linux Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the visualization application to Windows EC2 instances. Configure Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for storage.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Lambda is not suited to running a long-running simulation outputting every 5 minutes or a Windows desktop GUI application, and would require code changes.
✗ B. FSx File Gateway is for on-premises hybrid access to FSx and does not provide simultaneous native NFS and SMB access for cloud EC2 applications without changes.
✗ C. SQS exchanges messages, not a shared file system, so it cannot serve the NFS and SMB file-access needs without rewriting both applications.
✓ D. FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a single file system accessible over both NFS (Linux) and SMB (Windows), eliminating duplication and requiring no application code changes.

text: As part of budget planning, management wants a report of AWS billed items listed by user. The data will be used to create department budgets. A solutions architect needs to determine the most eficient way to obtain this report information. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Run a query with Amazon Athena to generate the report.
B. Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
C. Access the bill details from the billing dashboard and download the bill.
D. Modify a cost budget in AWS Budgets to alert with Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Athena could query Cost and Usage Reports in S3 but requires setup and SQL, which is far less efficient than a built-in cost-reporting tool for this need.
✓ B. Cost Explorer can group and report billed costs (including by linked account/tag/user dimension) and the report can be downloaded directly, making it the most efficient option.
✗ C. The billing dashboard bill download gives a summary invoice but is not an efficient, flexible way to break billed items out by user for budgeting.
✗ D. AWS Budgets sends threshold alerts, not detailed per-user billing reports, so it does not produce the required report.

text: A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage. The contact form will have dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company anticipates that there will be fewer than 100 site visits each month. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.
B. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
C. Convert the static webpage to dynamic by deploying Amazon Lightsail. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

D. Create a t2.micro Amazon EC2 instance. Deploy a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP/Perl/Python) stack to host the webpage. Use client- side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Running the form on ECS keeps containers/infrastructure provisioned and is overkill and costly for fewer than 100 visits per month.
✓ B. API Gateway plus a Lambda backend calling SES is fully serverless and pay-per-use, costing essentially nothing at fewer than 100 requests per month, the most cost-effective fit.
✗ C. Lightsail runs an always-on instance with a fixed monthly charge, which is unnecessary cost for such low traffic, and WorkMail adds per-mailbox fees.
✗ D. A continuously running t2.micro EC2 LAMP stack incurs ongoing compute cost and management overhead, far more expensive than serverless for minimal traffic.

text: A company has a static website that is hosted on Amazon CloudFront in front of Amazon S3. The static website uses a database backend. The company notices that the website does not refiect updates that have been made in the website’s Git repository. The company checks the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the webhooks are configured properly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Add an Application Load Balancer.
B. Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached to the database layer of the web application.
C. Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
D. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to validate the website’s SSL certificate.
optionExplanations: ✗ An Application Load Balancer distributes traffic across compute targets like EC2/ECS; it does nothing for a CloudFront-fronted S3 static site that is serving stale cached objects, so it does not address the problem.

✗ Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached caches database query results; the symptom is stale static website content from edge caching, not slow database reads, so this is irrelevant to the missing updates.

✓ Since the CI/CD pipeline successfully deploys new files to S3 but the site shows old content, CloudFront is serving cached objects past their TTL; invalidating the CloudFront cache forces edge locations to fetch the updated objects from the S3 origin and immediately reflects the updates.

✗ AWS Certificate Manager provisions and validates SSL/TLS certificates for HTTPS; this affects encryption and trust, not whether updated content is displayed, so it does not resolve the caching issue.

text: A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers. How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?
options: A. Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
B. Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
C. Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.

D. Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Hosting SQL Server on EC2 supports native backups and Data Quality Services, but FSx File Gateway is a hybrid on-premises service rather than the right cloud SMB file share for the tiers.

✓ B. Running all tiers on EC2 lets SQL Server use native backups and Data Quality Services (which RDS does not fully support), and FSx for Windows File Server provides the SMB shared file storage for the Windows tiers.
✗ C. Amazon RDS for SQL Server does not support native backups to your control or Data Quality Services, so it fails the SQL Server feature requirement.
✗ D. RDS for SQL Server lacks the required native backup and Data Quality Services support, and an EBS volume cannot be shared across multiple instances for file sharing.

text: A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
B. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.
C. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
D. Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. An S3 bucket is object storage accessed via API, not a POSIX file system mount, so the application would need changes to use it.
✗ B. CloudFront with an S3 origin is a content delivery setup, not a mountable shared file system for the web servers.
✓ C. Amazon EFS provides a POSIX-compliant NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently on all Linux web servers, giving shared file access with no application changes.
✗ D. An EBS gp3 volume can attach to only a limited set of instances and is not a general shared file store for an entire fleet without changes.

text: A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?
options: A. Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
B. Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
C. Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function’s code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
D. Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.
optionExplanations: ✗ An S3 bucket policy can grant access, but it does not give the Lambda function an identity to assume and is not the recommended way to grant a Lambda function permissions; the role-based approach with least privilege is more secure.

✓ Attaching an IAM execution role to the Lambda function with a least-privilege IAM policy scoped to read only the specific S3 bucket is the most secure approach using temporary credentials automatically rotated by AWS.
✗ Embedding long-lived access keys and secret keys in code is the least secure option because the static credentials can be exposed and do not rotate.
✗ Granting read access to all S3 buckets in the account violates least privilege; scoping to only the required bucket is more secure.

text: A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to user demand. The company wants to optimize cost savings without making a long-term commitment. Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Dedicated Instances only
B. On-Demand Instances only
C. A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances
D. A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances
optionExplanations: ✗ Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to a single customer and are the most expensive option, not cost-optimized.
✗ On-Demand Instances only avoid commitment but do not optimize cost savings as much as adding Spot Instances for the scalable portion.
✓ A mix of On-Demand Instances (for baseline reliability) and Spot Instances (for cheap scaling capacity) optimizes cost without a long-term commitment, which suits an Auto Scaling web tier.
✗ Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment, which the company explicitly wants to avoid.

text: A media company uses Amazon CloudFront for its publicly available streaming video content. The company wants to secure the video content that is hosted in Amazon S3 by controlling who has access. Some of the company’s users are using a custom HTTP client that does not support cookies. Some of the company’s users are unable to change the hardcoded URLs that they are using for access. Which services or methods will meet these requirements with the LEAST impact to the users? (Choose two.)
options: A. Signed cookies
B. Signed URLs
C. AWS AppSync
D. JSON Web Token (JWT)
E. AWS Secrets Manager
optionExplanations: ✓ Signed cookies let CloudFront restrict access without changing the URL, so they serve the users whose hardcoded URLs cannot be modified; access is controlled via the Cookie header.
✓ Signed URLs embed access policy in the URL query string, which works for the custom HTTP client that does not support cookies; this covers that user group with minimal impact.
✗ AWS AppSync is a managed GraphQL API service and has nothing to do with restricting access to CloudFront/S3 streaming content.
✗ JWT is a token format used for authentication/authorization in apps; CloudFront content access control uses signed URLs/cookies, not raw JWTs, so it does not meet the requirement.
✗ AWS Secrets Manager stores and rotates secrets such as credentials; it does not control viewer access to CloudFront-distributed S3 content.

text: A company is preparing a new data platform that will ingest real-time streaming data from multiple sources. The company needs to transform the data before writing the data to Amazon S3. The company needs the ability to use SQL to query the transformed data. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

B. Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

C. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data. Use Amazon EMR to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

D. Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to stream the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to transform the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.

E. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the data. Use AWS Glue to transform the data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to write the data to Amazon S3. Use the Amazon RDS query editor to query the transformed data from Amazon S3.
optionExplanations: ✓ Kinesis Data Streams ingests real-time streaming data, Kinesis Data Analytics transforms it with SQL/Flink, Firehose delivers it to S3, and Athena provides SQL queries over the S3 data, fully meeting all requirements.

✓ Amazon MSK ingests real-time streaming data, AWS Glue (Spark-based ETL with streaming jobs) transforms the data and writes it to S3, and Athena provides SQL querying over S3, satisfying all requirements.
✗ AWS DMS is for database migration/replication, not for ingesting arbitrary real-time streaming data from multiple sources, making it a poor fit for this streaming ingestion requirement.

✗ While MSK and Kinesis Data Analytics can stream and transform, the Amazon RDS query editor only queries RDS relational databases, not transformed data stored in Amazon S3, so the query requirement is not met.

✗ Although Kinesis Data Streams, Glue, and Firehose handle ingestion/transformation/delivery to S3, the Amazon RDS query editor cannot query data in S3, so this option fails the SQL-query-of-S3-data requirement.

text: A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
B. Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on- premises systems with local access to the data.

C. Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

D. Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Snowball is a one-time bulk data transfer appliance; it does not provide an ongoing, automatically transferred backup solution, and there is no Snowball S3 endpoint to mount for continuous local access to data.

✗ AWS Snowball Edge is also a physical migration/edge appliance for one-time transfers; its file interface offers only temporary local access during the transfer, not a persistent backup solution with ongoing local access to all data.

✗ A cached volume gateway stores the full dataset in Amazon S3 and retains only frequently accessed (recently used) data locally as a cache, so it does not keep ALL data available locally, failing the requirement to maintain local access to all the data.

✓ A stored volume gateway keeps the entire primary dataset on premises (mapped to local storage) for low-latency local access to all data, while asynchronously and securely backing it up to AWS as EBS snapshots in S3, exactly meeting the requirement for full local access plus automatic secure cloud backup.

text: An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Trafic must not traverse the internet. How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.
B. Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
C. Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
D. Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✗ A Route 53 private hosted zone provides DNS resolution within a VPC; it does not create a private network path to S3.
✓ A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 routes traffic to S3 privately over the AWS network so it never traverses the internet, at no additional cost.
✗ A NAT gateway sends traffic to S3 over the public internet (via the public S3 endpoint), which violates the requirement.
✗ A Site-to-Site VPN connects a VPC to an on-premises network, not to an S3 bucket, so this is not applicable.

text: An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants to use the data in three applications. Only one of the applications needs to process the PII. The PII must be removed before the other two applications process the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a proxy application layer to intercept and process the data that each application requests.
B. Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.
C. Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon S3 buckets so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective S3 bucket.

D. Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon DynamoDB tables so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective DynamoDB table.
optionExplanations: ✗ Using DynamoDB with a custom proxy application layer requires building and maintaining the proxy, adding significant operational overhead.

✓ S3 Object Lambda lets you attach a Lambda function to a GET request to remove PII on the fly for the two applications while the third reads the original data, all from a single stored copy with the least operational overhead.
✗ Maintaining three separate S3 buckets with pre-transformed datasets duplicates data and requires extra ETL pipelines, increasing operational overhead.
✗ Maintaining three separate DynamoDB tables with custom datasets duplicates data and requires additional processing pipelines, increasing operational overhead.

text: A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC. What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?
optionExplanations: ✗ A /32 CIDR represents a single IP address, which is not a valid VPC CIDR block (VPCs require /16 to /28).
✗ 192.168.0.0/24 is identical to the development VPC CIDR; overlapping CIDR blocks are not allowed for a VPC peering connection.
✗ A /32 is a single IP address and is not a valid VPC CIDR block size.

✓ 10.0.1.0/24 is a valid VPC CIDR (within the /16-/28 range) and does not overlap with the development VPC's 192.168.0.0/24, so peering is allowed; among the valid options it is the smallest acceptable block.

text: A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes trafic to the instances by using a target group. The average CPU usage on each of the instances is below 10% most of the time, with occasional surges to 65%. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that enters the ALARM state when the CPUUtilization metric is less than 20%. Create an AWS Lambda function that the CloudWatch alarm invokes to terminate one of the EC2 instances in the ALB target group.

B. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

C. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, and the maximum instances to 6. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.

D. Create two Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Configure the first CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is below 20%. Configure the second CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization matric is above 50%. Configure the alarms to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an email message. After receiving the message, log in to decrease or increase the number of EC2 instances that are running.
optionExplanations: ✗ A CloudWatch alarm invoking a Lambda to terminate instances only scales in; it provides no automatic scale-out when surges to 65% occur, so the application could be starved of CPU. It is also fragile custom automation, not the intended scaling mechanism.

✓ An EC2 Auto Scaling group with a target tracking policy on ASGAverageCPUUtilization at 50% automatically adds capacity during surges and removes it when load is low, fully automating scalability while optimizing cost. The min 2 / desired 3 / max 6 range plus the existing ALB and target group correctly meets all requirements.

✗ An Auto Scaling group with only static min/desired/max settings and no scaling policy will not respond to CPU surges automatically; it just maintains a fixed desired count, failing the requirement to ensure CPU resources during surges.

✗ Using two CloudWatch alarms that publish to SNS for email and then requiring a human to manually log in and change instance counts is not automated and introduces high operational overhead and delay, so it does not meet the automation or timely-surge requirements.

text: A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance. The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone. Which solution will make the application highly available?
options: A. Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.

B. Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
C. Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

D. Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
optionExplanations: ✗ A subnet correctly resides in one AZ, but configuring the RDS DB instance 'with connections to each network' is not a real RDS feature; RDS high availability is achieved via Multi-AZ deployment, not by attaching the DB to multiple subnets.
✗ a VPC subnet always exists within a single Availability Zone and cannot extend across two AZs, and 'connections to each network' is not how RDS provides HA.

✓ provisioning one subnet per AZ lets the Auto Scaling group spread EC2 instances across both AZs, and RDS Multi-AZ deployment maintains a synchronous standby replica in the second AZ with automatic failover, making both tiers highly available.
✗ a single subnet cannot extend across both Availability Zones (a subnet is bound to one AZ), so this design is technically invalid even though RDS Multi-AZ is the right database choice.

text: A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data. Which solution will meet the performance requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Sat each volume’ tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the fila system on the EC2 instances.

B. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
D. Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume’s tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ FSx for NetApp ONTAP is a general-purpose NAS that does not deliver the sub-millisecond, 6 GBps HPC-scale parallel throughput this workload needs; an ALL tiering policy also moves data to slower capacity storage, hurting latency.

✓ FSx for Lustre is a high-performance parallel file system built for HPC, providing sub-millisecond latencies and hundreds of GBps of throughput when scaled; persistent SSD storage delivers the lowest latency, and S3 import/export integrates the raw data, fully meeting the 6 GBps requirement across hundreds of EC2 instances.
✗ FSx for Lustre with persistent HDD storage is optimized for throughput-heavy but latency-tolerant workloads and cannot meet sub-millisecond latency; SSD is required here.

✗ FSx for NetApp ONTAP (even with NONE tiering keeping data on SSD) is a general-purpose multi-protocol NAS and is not designed to deliver the sustained 6 GBps parallel HPC throughput that FSx for Lustre provides.

text: A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application’s database storage continues to grow over time. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
B. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
C. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
D. Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ EC2 Spot Instances can be interrupted at any time, which is unsuitable for an application that must run 24/7, and S3 is object storage, not a relational database for a legacy application.
✗ EC2 Reserved Instances suit the 24/7 workload, but RDS On-Demand Instances are more expensive than Reserved Instances for an always-on database, so this is not the most cost-effective.

✓ For an application running 24/7 with steadily growing database storage, EC2 Reserved Instances cover the constant application load most cheaply, and Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances provide a managed relational database with auto-scaling storage at the lowest steady-state cost.

✗ EC2 On-Demand Instances are more expensive than Reserved Instances for a constant 24/7 workload, so this is not the most cost-effective for the application layer even though RDS Reserved is appropriate.

text: A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The laboratory has a 1 Gbps network link that many other departments in the university share. The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer. However, the laboratory needs to be able to control the amount of bandwidth that the service uses to minimize the impact on other departments. The data migration must take place within the next 5 days. Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. AWS Snowcone
B. Amazon FSx File Gateway
C. AWS DataSync
D. AWS Transfer Family
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Snowcone is a small physical device shipped offline; with 30 TB and a 5-day deadline plus an existing 1 Gbps link, online transfer is feasible, and Snowcone's 8 TB capacity is too small and slow to ship.
✗ Amazon FSx File Gateway provides on-premises cached access to an FSx for Windows file system; it is not a bulk migration service and does not provide bandwidth-throttled data transfer.

✓ AWS DataSync maximizes transfer performance over the network, integrates natively with FSx for Windows File Server, and supports built-in bandwidth throttling to limit impact on other departments, completing 30 TB well within 5 days on a 1 Gbps link.
✗ AWS Transfer Family provides managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP endpoints for S3 and EFS, not for FSx for Windows, and it is not designed for high-performance bulk file migration with bandwidth control.

text: A company wants to create a mobile app that allows users to stream slow-motion video clips on their mobile devices. Currently, the app captures video clips and uploads the video clips in raw format into an Amazon S3 bucket. The app retrieves these video clips directly from the S3 bucket. However, the videos are large in their raw format. Users are experiencing issues with buffering and playback on mobile devices. The company wants to implement solutions to maximize the performance and scalability of the app while minimizing operational overhead. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching.
B. Use AWS DataSync to replicate the video files across AW'S Regions in other S3 buckets.
C. Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
D. Deploy an Auto Sealing group of Amazon EC2 instances in Local Zones for content delivery and caching.
E. Deploy an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to convert the video files to more appropriate formats.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon CloudFront caches and delivers video content from edge locations close to users, reducing latency and buffering while scaling automatically with minimal operational overhead.
✗ AWS DataSync replicating files to other Regions does not solve the buffering problem caused by large raw video and adds cost and operational complexity without improving playback.
✓ Amazon Elastic Transcoder is a fully managed service that converts raw video into mobile-optimized adaptive formats, reducing file size and buffering with minimal operational overhead.
✗ Deploying EC2 in Local Zones for content delivery adds significant operational overhead and is not the managed, scalable approach that CloudFront provides for caching/distribution.
✗ Running a self-managed EC2 Auto Scaling group to transcode video adds substantial operational overhead compared to the fully managed Elastic Transcoder service.

text: A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it is expecting high trafic to the application upon its launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases. What should a solutions architect recommend?
options: A. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous trafic patterns.
B. Use an AWS Lambda function to scale Amazon ECS based on metric breaches that trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
C. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
D. Use AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies to scale when ECS metric breaches trigger an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
optionExplanations: ✗ EC2 Auto Scaling on previous traffic patterns (scheduled/predictive) does not react dynamically to actual CPU/memory utilization and applies to EC2 instances, not Fargate tasks which have no managed EC2 fleet.
✗ Using a custom Lambda function to scale ECS is unnecessary custom plumbing; Application Auto Scaling natively integrates with ECS and CloudWatch alarms.
✗ EC2 Auto Scaling with simple scaling policies scales the EC2 fleet, but Fargate has no EC2 instances to scale, and simple scaling is less responsive than target tracking.

✓ AWS Application Auto Scaling with target tracking policies is the native way to scale ECS Fargate service desired task count up on high utilization and back down when utilization decreases, reducing cost automatically.

text: A company recently created a disaster recovery site in a different AWS Region. The company needs to transfer large amounts of data back and forth between NFS file systems in the two Regions on a periodic basis. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use AWS DataSync.
B. Use AWS Snowball devices.
C. Set up an SFTP server on Amazon EC2.
D. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS DataSync natively transfers data between NFS file systems (including EFS) and supports scheduled periodic, bidirectional transfers across Regions with the least operational overhead.
✗ AWS Snowball devices are physical, offline, and ship by mail, which is impractical for periodic recurring transfers between two AWS Regions.
✗ Setting up an SFTP server on EC2 requires building and maintaining custom infrastructure and scripting, adding significant operational overhead.
✗ AWS DMS migrates databases, not NFS file systems, so it does not fit file-based data transfer.

text: A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed. Which AWS solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
B. Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
C. Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
D. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS DataSync is a data transfer service, not a mountable shared file system, so it cannot provide SMB shared storage for the application.
✗ A self-managed EC2 Windows instance with a file share role is not fully managed and requires ongoing patching, scaling, and availability management.
✓ Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed file system that natively supports the SMB protocol for Windows clients, meeting the shared storage and fully managed requirements.
✗ Amazon S3 is object storage accessed via API and does not natively support SMB clients; mounting it as a file share requires extra tooling and is not the intended SMB solution.

text: A company wants to run an in-memory database for a latency-sensitive application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes more than 100,000 transactions each minute and requires high network throughput. A solutions architect needs to provide a cost- effective network design that minimizes data transfer charges. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.
B. Launch all EC2 instances in different Availability Zones within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with partition strategy when launching EC2 instances.
C. Deploy an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones based on a network utilization target.
D. Deploy an Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones.
optionExplanations: ✓ Launching all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone with a cluster placement group provides the highest network throughput and lowest latency, and keeping traffic within one AZ avoids inter-AZ data transfer charges.
✗ Placing instances in different AZs with a partition strategy incurs inter-AZ data transfer charges and does not deliver the low-latency, high-throughput single-AZ networking the workload needs.
✗ Spreading instances across AZs via Auto Scaling on network utilization adds cross-AZ data transfer costs and does not address the in-memory, low-latency network requirement.
✗ An Auto Scaling group with step scaling across AZs likewise incurs inter-AZ transfer charges and does not optimize for the low-latency high-throughput in-memory workload.

text: A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises. The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally. Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?
options: A. Amazon S3 File Gateway
B. AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
C. AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes
D. AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon S3 File Gateway presents an NFS/SMB file interface backed by S3 objects, not the iSCSI block volumes the company uses for its on-premises storage.
✗ Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library (iSCSI VTL) for backup/archive to S3/Glacier, not primary recently-accessed block storage.
✗ Volume Gateway stored volumes keep the entire dataset on premises and only asynchronously back up to AWS, so they do not reduce the need to scale local iSCSI storage.
✓ Volume Gateway cached volumes store the primary data in S3 while keeping only recently accessed data cached locally over iSCSI, minimizing on-premises storage growth as required.

text: A company has multiple AWS accounts that use consolidated billing. The company runs several active high performance Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances for 90 days. The company’s finance team has access to AWS Trusted Advisor in the consolidated billing account and all other AWS accounts. The finance team needs to use the appropriate AWS account to access the Trusted Advisor check recommendations for RDS. The finance team must review the appropriate Trusted Advisor check to reduce RDS costs. Which combination of steps should the finance team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running.
B. Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the consolidated billing account to see all RDS instance checks at the same time.
C. Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
D. Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
E. Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon Redshift Reserved Node Optimization.
optionExplanations: ✗ Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks like Reserved Instance Optimization are based on consolidated billing data and are best viewed from the payer (consolidated billing) account; reviewing per member account does not aggregate billing-based recommendations across the organization.

✓ the consolidated billing (management/payer) account is where Trusted Advisor aggregates billing-derived checks across all linked accounts, so the finance team can see all RDS instance recommendations together.

✓ the instances are active, high-performance, and have been running continuously for 90 days, making them ideal candidates for Reserved Instances; this check identifies potential savings from purchasing RDS Reserved Instances versus On-Demand.
✗ the RDS Idle DB Instances check flags instances with little or no activity, but these are described as active high-performance instances, so this check would not surface relevant cost savings.
✗ this check applies to Amazon Redshift reserved nodes, not Amazon RDS for Oracle, so it is irrelevant to reducing RDS costs.

text: A solutions architect needs to optimize storage costs. The solutions architect must identify any Amazon S3 buckets that are no longer being accessed or are rarely accessed. Which solution will accomplish this goal with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.
B. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 dashboard in the AWS Management Console.
C. Turn on the Amazon CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes metric for buckets. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the metrics data with Amazon Athena.
D. Turn on AWS CloudTrail for S3 object monitoring. Analyze bucket access patterns by using CloudTrail logs that are integrated with Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
optionExplanations: ✓ S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide and bucket-level activity metrics (including access patterns) in a built-in dashboard, identifying rarely or never-accessed buckets with the least operational overhead.
✗ The basic S3 dashboard in the console does not surface advanced access-pattern/activity analytics needed to identify rarely accessed buckets.
✗ The CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes metric only reports storage size, not access frequency, and analyzing it with Athena adds setup overhead without revealing access patterns.

✗ Enabling CloudTrail S3 object-level logging and analyzing logs via CloudWatch Logs is functional but requires significant configuration and analysis effort, far more operational overhead than Storage Lens.

text: A company sells datasets to customers who do research in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML). The datasets are large, formatted files that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company hosts a web application that the customers use to purchase access to a given dataset. The web application is deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. After a purchase is made, customers receive an S3 signed URL that allows access to the files. The customers are distributed across North America and Europe. The company wants to reduce the cost that is associated with data transfers and wants to maintain or improve performance. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the existing S3 bucket. Direct customer requests to the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.
B. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.

C. Set up a second S3 bucket in the eu-central-1 Region with S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Direct customer requests to the closest Region. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.

D. Modify the web application to enable streaming of the datasets to end users. Configure the web application to read the data from the existing S3 bucket. Implement access control directly in the application.
optionExplanations: ✗ S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads/downloads over long distances but adds a per-GB acceleration fee, so it increases rather than reduces data transfer cost.

✓ A CloudFront distribution caches the datasets at edge locations close to North American and European users, reducing data transfer-out costs (lower CloudFront egress pricing and caching) while improving performance, and CloudFront signed URLs provide equivalent access control.
✗ Cross-Region Replication to eu-central-1 doubles storage cost, adds replication transfer cost, and requires custom routing logic, without the caching benefits of a CDN.
✗ Modifying the app to stream datasets through the EC2 fleet routes all traffic through the application and S3, increasing data transfer cost and load rather than reducing it.

text: A company is using AWS to design a web application that will process insurance quotes. Users will request quotes from the application. Quotes must be separated by quote type, must be responded to within 24 hours, and must not get lost. The solution must maximize operational eficiency and must minimize maintenance. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create multiple Amazon Kinesis data streams based on the quote type. Configure the web application to send messages to the proper data stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to use the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to pool messages from its own data stream.

B. Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for each quote type. Subscribe the Lambda function to its associated SNS topic. Configure the application to publish requests for quotes to the appropriate SNS topic.

C. Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure SNS message filtering to publish messages to the proper SQS queue based on the quote type. Configure each backend application server to use its own SQS queue.

D. Create multiple Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams based on the quote type to deliver data streams to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster. Configure the application to send messages to the proper delivery stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to search for the messages from OpenSearch Service and process them accordingly.
optionExplanations: ✗ Multiple Kinesis data streams with the KCL require managing shards, consumers, and client libraries, which is far more maintenance than a managed pub/sub-plus-queue pattern and is geared to streaming analytics rather than durable per-type request queues.

✗ SNS-to-Lambda per quote type delivers notifications but SNS does not persistently retain undelivered messages, risking message loss and lacking the durable buffering needed for a 24-hour response window.

✓ A single SNS topic with message filtering fanning out to per-quote-type SQS queues separates quotes by type, durably retains messages so none are lost, and lets each backend process its own queue within 24 hours, maximizing operational efficiency with minimal maintenance.

✗ Multiple Kinesis Data Firehose streams into OpenSearch is a logging/analytics pipeline, not a durable work-queue pattern, and adds significant complexity unsuitable for reliable per-type request processing.

text: A company has an application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances. Each EC2 instance has multiple Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) data volumes attached to it. The application’s EC2 instance configuration and data need to be backed up nightly. The application also needs to be recoverable in a different AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally eficient way?
options: A. Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application’s EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Region.
B. Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EC2 instances as resources.
C. Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EBS volumes as resources.
D. Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application's EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Availability Zone.
optionExplanations: ✗ A custom Lambda snapshotting only EBS volumes captures data but not the EC2 instance configuration, and building/maintaining the scheduling and cross-Region copy logic adds operational overhead compared to a managed service.

✓ AWS Backup with EC2 instances as resources backs up the full instance configuration plus all attached EBS data volumes as an AMI/recovery point, supports scheduled nightly plans and cross-Region copy natively, and is the most operationally efficient managed solution meeting all requirements.
