✗ AWS Backup adding only EBS volumes as resources backs up the data but not the EC2 instance configuration, so it fails the requirement to back up the instance configuration for recovery.
✗ A custom Lambda copying snapshots only to a different Availability Zone does not meet the cross-Region recoverability requirement and also omits the EC2 instance configuration.

text: A company is building a mobile app on AWS. The company wants to expand its reach to millions of users. The company needs to build a platform so that authorized users can watch the company’s content on their mobile devices. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Publish content to a public Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stream content.
B. Set up IPsec VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
C. Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
D. Set up AWS Client VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
optionExplanations: ✗ A public S3 bucket exposes content to everyone and KMS keys do not stream content to authorized users; this fails the access-control and scale requirements.
✗ An IPsec VPN is a point-to-point network tunnel that does not scale to millions of mobile users and is not how content is delivered to a mobile app.

✓ Amazon CloudFront distributes content globally with low latency to millions of users, and signed URLs (or signed cookies) restrict access to authorized users only, meeting both scale and authorization requirements.
✗ AWS Client VPN provides individual remote VPN access into a VPC and does not scale to millions of public mobile users for content streaming.

text: A company has an on-premises MySQL database used by the global sales team with infrequent access patterns. The sales team requires the database to have minimal downtime. A database administrator wants to migrate this database to AWS without selecting a particular instance type in anticipation of more users in the future. Which service should a solutions architect recommend?
options: A. Amazon Aurora MySQL
B. Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL
C. Amazon Redshift Spectrum
D. Amazon RDS for MySQL
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Aurora MySQL requires you to select a provisioned instance type/class, so it does not match the requirement to avoid choosing an instance type.

✓ Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL automatically scales capacity up and down (and can pause) without selecting an instance type, which suits an infrequently accessed database that may grow in the future.
✗ Amazon Redshift Spectrum queries data in S3 from a Redshift data warehouse and is not a MySQL migration target.
✗ Amazon RDS for MySQL requires choosing a specific DB instance type/class, which the requirement explicitly wants to avoid.

text: A company experienced a breach that affected several applications in its on-premises data center. The attacker took advantage of vulnerabilities in the custom applications that were running on the servers. The company is now migrating its applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement a solution that actively scans for vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances and sends a report that details the findings. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy AWS Shield to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Create an AWS Lambda function to log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
B. Deploy Amazon Macie and AWS Lambda functions to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
C. Turn on Amazon GuardDuty. Deploy the GuardDuty agents to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
D. Turn on Amazon Inspector. Deploy the Amazon Inspector agent to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks and does not scan EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities.
✗ Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data in S3; it does not scan EC2 instances for vulnerabilities.

✗ Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service that analyzes logs and behavior for malicious activity; it does not perform host vulnerability scanning of installed software/CVEs (and the scenario specifically wants vulnerability scanning).
✓ Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances (via the SSM agent) for software vulnerabilities and CVEs and produces findings that can be reported, directly meeting the requirement.

text: A company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run a script to poll for and process messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining its ability to process a growing number of messages that are added to the queue. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Increase the size of the EC2 instance to process messages faster.
B. Use Amazon EventBridge to turn off the EC2 instance when the instance is underutilized.
C. Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
D. Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the script on demand.
optionExplanations: ✗ Increasing the EC2 instance size still leaves an always-on instance incurring cost and does not elastically scale with the message volume.
✗ Using EventBridge to stop the instance when underutilized risks losing message-processing capacity and does not provide reliable, scalable processing.
✓ Migrating the script to AWS Lambda lets SQS trigger functions on demand, automatically scaling with the number of messages and charging only for execution time, reducing operational cost.
✗ Systems Manager Run Command runs scripts on demand on managed instances but still requires running EC2 instances and manual/triggered invocation, so it does not reduce cost or scale automatically.

text: A company uses a legacy application to produce data in CSV format. The legacy application stores the output data in Amazon S3. The company is deploying a new commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) application that can perform complex SQL queries to analyze data that is stored in Amazon Redshift and Amazon S3 only. However, the COTS application cannot process the .csv files that the legacy application produces. The company cannot update the legacy application to produce data in another format. The company needs to implement a solution so that the COTS application can use the data that the legacy application produces. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.
B. Develop a Python script that runs on Amazon EC2 instances to convert the .csv files to .sql files. Invoke the Python script on a cron schedule to store the output files in Amazon S3.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use an S3 event to invoke the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in the DynamoDB table.

D. Use Amazon EventBridge to launch an Amazon EMR cluster on a weekly schedule. Configure the EMR cluster to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in an Amazon Redshift table.
optionExplanations: ✓ An AWS Glue scheduled ETL job is a fully managed, serverless way to convert the CSV files and load the data into Amazon Redshift, which the COTS application can query, with the least operational overhead.

✗ Building a custom Python script on EC2 with cron requires managing instances and code, adding significant operational overhead, and converting CSV to .sql files does not make data queryable by the COTS app.
✗ DynamoDB is not a supported source for the COTS application (which queries only Redshift and S3), so loading data into DynamoDB does not meet the requirement.
✗ Launching an EMR cluster weekly involves managing big-data clusters, far more operational overhead than a managed Glue job for simple CSV-to-Redshift transformation.

text: A company recently migrated its entire IT environment to the AWS Cloud. The company discovers that users are provisioning oversized Amazon EC2 instances and modifying security group rules without using the appropriate change control process. A solutions architect must devise a strategy to track and audit these inventory and configuration changes. Which actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing.
B. Use data lifecycle policies for the Amazon EC2 instances.
C. Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and reference the security dashboard.
D. Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.
E. Restore previous resource configurations with an AWS CloudFormation template.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS CloudTrail records API activity, providing an audit trail of who provisioned instances and modified security groups, meeting the auditing requirement.
✗ Data lifecycle policies automate EBS snapshot management and have nothing to do with tracking configuration or inventory changes.
✗ Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks and recommendations but does not track or audit per-change configuration and inventory history.
✓ AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes over time and can evaluate rules for compliance, directly meeting the inventory and configuration-change auditing requirement.
✗ Restoring configurations with a CloudFormation template is a remediation action, not a method to track or audit changes.

text: A company has hundreds of Amazon EC2 Linux-based instances in the AWS Cloud. Systems administrators have used shared SSH keys to manage the instances. After a recent audit, the company’s security team is mandating the removal of all shared keys. A solutions architect must design a solution that provides secure access to the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of administrative overhead?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
B. Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate one-time SSH keys on demand.
C. Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.
D. Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secure, auditable shell access through the SSM agent and IAM without any SSH keys or open inbound ports, meeting the requirement with the least administrative overhead.
✗ AWS STS issues temporary AWS credentials, not SSH keys, so it does not natively generate one-time SSH keys and would require significant custom tooling.
✗ Bastion hosts still rely on SSH keys and require managing and hardening additional instances, which does not remove shared keys with minimal overhead.
✗ Using Cognito and a Lambda function to generate temporary SSH keys is a complex custom solution with high administrative overhead.

text: A company is using a fieet of Amazon EC2 instances to ingest data from on-premises data sources. The data is in JSON format and ingestion rates can be as high as 1 MB/s. When an EC2 instance is rebooted, the data in-fiight is lost. The company’s data science team wants to query ingested data in near-real time. Which solution provides near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss?
options: A. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.
B. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon Redshift as the destination. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data.
C. Store ingested data in an EC2 instance store. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon S3 as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
D. Store ingested data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Publish data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Subscribe to the Redis channel to query the data.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon Kinesis Data Streams durably buffers streaming data across shards (scaling with throughput) and persists records, so reboots of producers do not lose in-flight data; Kinesis Data Analytics queries the stream in near-real time. This best meets scalable, near-real-time, minimal-loss querying.

✗ Kinesis Data Firehose to Redshift buffers and batches data before loading, introducing minutes of latency rather than near-real-time querying, so it does not satisfy the near-real-time requirement as well as streaming directly.

✗ Storing data in an EC2 instance store does not solve data loss because instance store is ephemeral and lost on reboot/stop; Firehose to S3 with Athena also adds buffering delay, making it not truly near-real-time.

✗ An EBS volume plus ElastiCache for Redis pub/sub is not durable for streaming ingestion (Redis pub/sub messages are not persisted and are lost if no subscriber is connected), so this risks data loss and does not scale as a managed ingestion pipeline.

text: What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?
options: A. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set.
B. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set to private.
C. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an aws:SecureTransport header set to true.
D. Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.
optionExplanations: ✗ The s3:x-amz-acl header controls the object ACL/permissions, not encryption, so denying based on it does not enforce encryption.
✗ Setting s3:x-amz-acl to private controls access permissions, not encryption of the object.
✗ aws:SecureTransport enforces encryption in transit (HTTPS/TLS), not server-side encryption of stored objects.
✓ Denying PutObject when the x-amz-server-side-encryption header is absent forces uploads to specify server-side encryption, ensuring all stored objects are encrypted at rest.

text: A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier application for a company. The application's users upload images from a mobile device. The application generates a thumbnail of each image and returns a message to the user to confirm that the image was uploaded successfully. The thumbnail generation can take up to 60 seconds, but the company wants to provide a faster response time to its users to notify them that the original image was received. The solutions architect must design the application to asynchronously dispatch requests to the different application tiers. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Write a custom AWS Lambda function to generate the thumbnail and alert the user. Use the image upload process as an event source to invoke the Lambda function.
B. Create an AWS Step Functions workfiow. Configure Step Functions to handle the orchestration between the application tiers and alert the user when thumbnail generation is complete.

C. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.

D. Create Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification topics and subscriptions. Use one subscription with the application to generate the thumbnail after the image upload is complete. Use a second subscription to message the user's mobile app by way of a push notification after thumbnail generation is complete.
optionExplanations: ✗ A single Lambda invoked synchronously on upload would have the user wait for the up-to-60-second thumbnail generation, contradicting the need for a fast acknowledgment and asynchronous dispatch.

✗ Step Functions can orchestrate tiers but is more than required, and the design still centers on tracking completion rather than simply acknowledging receipt quickly; SQS is the simpler asynchronous decoupling fit.

✓ Placing a message on an SQS queue decouples the slow thumbnail-generation tier from the upload tier, so the application can immediately confirm receipt to the user while processing happens asynchronously, meeting the fast-response requirement.

✗ Using SNS subscriptions to generate the thumbnail still couples the user notification to thumbnail completion and pushes the final notification only after the 60-second generation, not providing the desired immediate received confirmation through simple decoupling.

text: A company’s facility has badge readers at every entrance throughout the building. When badges are scanned, the readers send a message over HTTPS to indicate who attempted to access that particular entrance. A solutions architect must design a system to process these messages from the sensors. The solution must be highly available, and the results must be made available for the company’s security team to analyze. Which system architecture should the solutions architect recommend?
options: A. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance to serve as the HTTPS endpoint and to process the messages. Configure the EC2 instance to save the results to an Amazon S3 bucket.
B. Create an HTTPS endpoint in Amazon API Gateway. Configure the API Gateway endpoint to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
C. Use Amazon Route 53 to direct incoming sensor messages to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to process the messages and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

D. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Configure a Site-to-Site VPN connection from the facility network to the VPC so that sensor data can be written directly to an S3 bucket by way of the VPC endpoint.
optionExplanations: ✗ A single EC2 instance as the HTTPS endpoint is a single point of failure and is not highly available without additional architecture.

✓ Amazon API Gateway provides a highly available, managed HTTPS endpoint that invokes Lambda to process each message and store results in DynamoDB for the security team to analyze, meeting availability and accessibility requirements.
✗ Route 53 is a DNS service and cannot directly receive HTTPS messages or route them to a Lambda function for processing.
✗ A gateway VPC endpoint and Site-to-Site VPN writing directly to S3 does not provide an HTTPS message-processing endpoint for the badge readers and does not fit the described HTTPS sensor messages.

text: A company wants to implement a disaster recovery plan for its primary on-premises file storage volume. The file storage volume is mounted from an Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) device on a local storage server. The file storage volume holds hundreds of terabytes (TB) of data. The company wants to ensure that end users retain immediate access to all file types from the on-premises systems without experiencing latency. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the company's existing infrastructure?
options: A. Provision an Amazon S3 File Gateway as a virtual machine (VM) that is hosted on premises. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Modify existing applications to access the files through the NFS protocol. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and mount the S3 bucket that contains the files.

B. Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway. Use a data backup solution to back up all existing data to a virtual tape library. Configure the data backup solution to run nightly after the initial backup is complete. To recover from a disaster, provision an Amazon EC2 instance and restore the data to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume from the volumes in the virtual tape library.

C. Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volume. Set the local cache to 10 TB. Mount the Volume Gateway cached volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.

D. Provision an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volume with the same amount of disk space as the existing file storage volume. Mount the Volume Gateway stored volume to the existing file server by using iSCSI, and copy all files to the storage volume. Configure scheduled snapshots of the storage volume. To recover from a disaster, restore a snapshot to an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and attach the EBS volume to an Amazon EC2 instance.
optionExplanations: ✗ An S3 File Gateway uses NFS/SMB file protocols and requires modifying applications away from iSCSI, plus a 10 TB cache cannot keep hundreds of TB locally, so it changes the infrastructure and risks latency for uncached files.
✗ A tape gateway is for backup/archival to virtual tape and does not provide immediate low-latency access to all files for end users.

✗ A Volume Gateway cached volume keeps only frequently accessed data in the local 10 TB cache while primary data lives in AWS, so accessing the hundreds of TB of all file types can incur retrieval latency, not immediate local access.

✓ A Volume Gateway stored volume keeps the entire dataset on local disk (giving immediate, low-latency access to all files) while asynchronously backing up to AWS as EBS snapshots, preserving the existing iSCSI mount with the least change and enabling DR by restoring snapshots to EBS on EC2.

text: A company is hosting a web application from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses Amazon Cognito as an identity provider to authenticate users and return a JSON Web Token (JWT) that provides access to protected resources that are stored in another S3 bucket. Upon deployment of the application, users report errors and are unable to access the protected content. A solutions architect must resolve this issue by providing proper permissions so that users can access the protected content. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Update the Amazon Cognito identity pool to assume the proper IAM role for access to the protected content.
B. Update the S3 ACL to allow the application to access the protected content.
C. Redeploy the application to Amazon S3 to prevent eventually consistent reads in the S3 bucket from affecting the ability of users to access the protected content.
D. Update the Amazon Cognito pool to use custom attribute mappings within the identity pool and grant users the proper permissions to access the protected content.
optionExplanations: ✓ Cognito identity pools provide temporary AWS credentials by having authenticated users assume an IAM role; the role's policy must grant access to the protected S3 bucket, which resolves the permission errors.
✗ S3 ACLs are a legacy object/bucket access mechanism and are not how Cognito-authenticated users obtain scoped access; updating ACLs does not map the JWT to the correct IAM permissions.
✗ The errors are an authorization/permissions problem, not a consistency issue; S3 is strongly consistent and redeployment would not grant access to the protected content.
✗ Custom attribute mappings affect how token claims map to user attributes and do not by themselves grant IAM permissions to access protected S3 content; an IAM role assumption is required.

text: An image hosting company uploads its large assets to Amazon S3 Standard buckets. The company uses multipart upload in parallel by using S3 APIs and overwrites if the same object is uploaded again. For the first 30 days after upload, the objects will be accessed frequently. The objects will be used less frequently after 30 days, but the access patterns for each object will be inconsistent. The company must optimize its S3 storage costs while maintaining high availability and resiliency of stored assets. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Move assets to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days.
B. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up incomplete multipart uploads.
C. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to clean up expired object delete markers.
D. Move assets to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
E. Move assets to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
optionExplanations: ✗ S3 Intelligent-Tiering suits unpredictable access patterns, but it adds a per-object monitoring charge and is less cost-effective here than Standard-IA when you simply want to move objects after a known 30-day frequent period; the better lifecycle answer pairs with cleanup of multipart uploads.

✓ Because the company uses parallel multipart uploads and overwrites objects, incomplete multipart upload parts can accumulate and incur storage charges; a lifecycle rule to abort/clean them up optimizes cost.

✗ Cleaning up expired object delete markers applies to versioned buckets to remove orphaned delete markers; there is no indication versioning is used, so it does not address this cost optimization scenario.
✓ Moving objects to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days reduces storage cost for infrequently accessed data while maintaining multi-AZ high availability and resiliency required by the company.
✗ S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, which reduces resiliency and availability and violates the requirement to maintain high availability and resiliency.

text: A solutions architect must secure a VPC network that hosts Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances contain highly sensitive data and run in a private subnet. According to company policy, the EC2 instances that run in the VPC can access only approved third-party software repositories on the internet for software product updates that use the third party’s URL. Other internet trafic must be blocked. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Update the route table for the private subnet to route the outbound trafic to an AWS Network Firewall firewall. Configure domain list rule groups.
B. Set up an AWS WAF web ACL. Create a custom set of rules that filter trafic requests based on source and destination IP address range sets.
C. Implement strict inbound security group rules. Configure an outbound rule that allows trafic only to the authorized software repositories on the internet by specifying the URLs.

D. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances. Direct all outbound trafic to the ALB. Use a URL-based rule listener in the ALB’s target group for outbound access to the internet.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Network Firewall supports domain-list (FQDN) filtering via stateful rule groups; routing the private subnet's outbound traffic through it lets you allow only approved third-party repository URLs and block all other internet traffic.

✗ AWS WAF protects HTTP/HTTPS requests at the application layer for resources like ALB/CloudFront and filters inbound web requests; it cannot control arbitrary outbound EC2 internet traffic by domain.
✗ Security groups allow rules based on IP/CIDR, ports, and protocols only; they cannot filter outbound traffic by URL or domain name, so they cannot enforce the URL-based allowlist.
✗ An ALB handles inbound load balancing of client requests to targets and has no mechanism to proxy or URL-filter outbound traffic from EC2 instances to the internet.

text: A company is hosting a three-tier ecommerce application in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the website on Amazon S3 and integrates the website with an API that handles sales requests. The company hosts the API on three Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The API consists of static and dynamic front-end content along with backend workers that process sales requests asynchronously. The company is expecting a significant and sudden increase in the number of sales requests during events for the launch of new products. What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure that all the requests are processed successfully?
options: A. Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Increase the number of EC2 instances to handle the increase in trafic.
B. Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on network trafic.
C. Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the dynamic content. Add an Amazon ElastiCache instance in front of the ALB to reduce trafic for the API to handle.
D. Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the static content. Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to receive requests from the website for later processing by the EC2 instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ CloudFront caches static content, not dynamic content, so distributing the dynamic content is the wrong cache target; merely increasing EC2 instances does not buffer a sudden spike and risks dropping requests if capacity is exceeded.

✗ CloudFront for static content is correct, but Auto Scaling reactively based on network traffic cannot absorb a sudden burst fast enough and provides no durable buffer, so requests can still be lost during the spike.
✗ ElastiCache is an in-memory cache for read-heavy data and cannot be placed in front of an ALB to buffer incoming sales (write) requests; CloudFront should also cache static, not dynamic, content.

✓ CloudFront offloads static content while an SQS queue durably buffers the sudden surge of sales requests, letting the asynchronous EC2 workers process every request without loss, which directly satisfies the requirement that all requests are processed successfully.

text: A security audit reveals that Amazon EC2 instances are not being patched regularly. A solutions architect needs to provide a solution that will run regular security scans across a large fieet of EC2 instances. The solution should also patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule and provide a report of each instance’s patch status. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Set up Amazon Macie to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up a cron job on each EC2 instance to patch the instance on a regular schedule.

B. Turn on Amazon GuardDuty in the account. Configure GuardDuty to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
C. Set up Amazon Detective to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.

D. Turn on Amazon Inspector in the account. Configure Amazon Inspector to scan the EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities. Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to patch the EC2 instances on a regular schedule.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data in S3; it does not scan EC2 for software vulnerabilities, and per-instance cron jobs are high-overhead and not centrally reportable.

✗ GuardDuty is a threat-detection service analyzing logs and (with the agent) some runtime threats, but it is not the patch/vulnerability-scan service, and Session Manager provides shell access, not scheduled patching.
✗ Amazon Detective analyzes and visualizes security findings for investigation; it does not scan EC2 for vulnerabilities, and an EventBridge rule alone does not apply OS patches.

✓ Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances for software vulnerabilities, and Systems Manager Patch Manager patches them on a defined maintenance schedule and reports each instance's patch compliance status.

text: A company is planning to store data on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must encrypt the data at rest. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?
options: A. Create a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable encryption for the DB instances.
B. Create an encryption key. Store the key in AWS Secrets Manager. Use the key to encrypt the DB instances.
C. Generate a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
D. Generate a certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
optionExplanations: ✓ RDS encryption at rest uses AWS KMS keys; you create/select a KMS key and enable encryption when launching the DB instance to encrypt storage, backups, and snapshots.
✗ Secrets Manager stores and rotates credentials/secrets, not encryption keys used for RDS storage encryption; RDS at-rest encryption is configured with KMS, not Secrets Manager.
✗ ACM certificates enable SSL/TLS for data in transit (e.g., on load balancers), not encryption at rest for RDS storage volumes.
✗ IAM does not generate TLS server certificates for RDS encryption at rest; encryption at rest is provided by KMS, and TLS only protects data in transit.

text: A company must migrate 20 TB of data from a data center to the AWS Cloud within 30 days. The company’s network bandwidth is limited to 15 Mbps and cannot exceed 70% utilization. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Snowball.
B. Use AWS DataSync.
C. Use a secure VPN connection.
D. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Snowball is a physical data transport appliance. With usable bandwidth of only 10.5 Mbps (70% of 15 Mbps), 20 TB would take roughly 176 days to transfer online, far exceeding the 30-day window, so shipping data via Snowball is the only viable option.
✗ AWS DataSync transfers data over the network, so it is still constrained by the 10.5 Mbps usable bandwidth and cannot move 20 TB within 30 days.
✗ A secure VPN connection runs over the same limited internet link (10.5 Mbps usable), which cannot complete a 20 TB transfer in 30 days.

✗ Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes uploads over the network via CloudFront edge locations, but it cannot overcome the fundamental 10.5 Mbps usable bandwidth ceiling and so cannot meet the 30-day deadline.

text: A company needs to provide its employees with secure access to confidential and sensitive files. The company wants to ensure that the files can be accessed only by authorized users. The files must be downloaded securely to the employees’ devices. The files are stored in an on-premises Windows file server. However, due to an increase in remote usage, the file server is running out of capacity. . Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Migrate the file server to an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet. Configure the security group to limit inbound trafic to the employees’ IP addresses.
B. Migrate the files to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Integrate the Amazon FSx file system with the on-premises Active Directory. Configure AWS Client VPN.
C. Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a private VPC endpoint. Create a signed URL to allow download.
D. Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a public VPC endpoint. Allow employees to sign on with AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).
optionExplanations: ✗ Placing a file server on a public-subnet EC2 instance increases exposure and operational burden, and IP-based security group rules are brittle for remote employees with changing IPs; it does not cleanly meet secure, authorized access requirements.

✓ FSx for Windows File Server replaces the capacity-limited Windows file server, integrates with the existing Active Directory for authorized user access, and AWS Client VPN provides secure remote download to employee devices.

✗ Migrating to S3 with a private VPC endpoint and presigned URLs changes the access model away from the Windows file-share workflow and does not integrate with Active Directory for user-level authorization as required.
✗ There is no public VPC endpoint for S3 (endpoints are private), and this approach abandons the Windows file-server model; it does not properly meet the secure file-share requirements.

text: A company’s application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. On the first day of every month at midnight, the application becomes much slower when the month-end financial calculation batch runs. This causes the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances to immediately peak to 100%, which disrupts the application. What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure the application is able to handle the workload and avoid downtime?
options: A. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB.
B. Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling simple scaling policy based on CPU utilization.
C. Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling policy based on the monthly schedule.
D. Configure Amazon ElastiCache to remove some of the workload from the EC2 instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon CloudFront caches and accelerates content delivery but does not add compute capacity; it would not help an internal CPU-bound batch calculation that immediately spikes the instances to 100%.
✗ A simple scaling policy reacts only after CPU utilization rises, and because the spike is immediate to 100% the scale-out would lag the demand, causing the disruption the company wants to avoid.

✓ the load is fully predictable (first day of every month at midnight), so a scheduled scaling policy can pre-provision additional EC2 capacity before the batch runs, preventing the CPU spike and downtime.
✗ ElastiCache offloads repeated database read latency, but the bottleneck here is a CPU-intensive monthly batch calculation, not cacheable read traffic, so it would not address the root cause.

text: A company wants to give a customer the ability to use on-premises Microsoft Active Directory to download files that are stored in Amazon S3. The customer’s application uses an SFTP client to download the files. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead and no changes to the customer’s application?
options: A. Set up AWS Transfer Family with SFTP for Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
B. Set up AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to synchronize the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Configure integrated Active Directory authentication.
C. Set up AWS DataSync to synchronize between the on-premises location and the S3 location by using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).
D. Set up a Windows Amazon EC2 instance with SFTP to connect the on-premises client with Amazon S3. Integrate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP endpoint backed by S3 and supports integrated Active Directory authentication, so the customer's existing SFTP client downloads files unchanged with the least operational overhead.
✗ AWS DMS migrates and replicates databases, not file downloads over SFTP from S3, and does not provide an SFTP endpoint or AD-authenticated file access for the client application.

✗ DataSync moves data between on-premises storage and AWS in bulk and does not expose an SFTP endpoint for an application's SFTP client; it also does not authenticate end users via Active Directory for downloads.
✗ Running a self-managed Windows EC2 SFTP server adds significant operational overhead (patching, scaling, availability) compared to the fully managed Transfer Family service.

text: A company is experiencing sudden increases in demand. The company needs to provision large Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Machine Image (AMI). The instances will run in an Auto Scaling group. The company needs a solution that provides minimum initialization latency to meet the demand. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use the aws ec2 register-image command to create an AMI from a snapshot. Use AWS Step Functions to replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.
B. Enable Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) fast snapshot restore on a snapshot. Provision an AMI by using the snapshot. Replace the AMI in the Auto Scaling group with the new AMI.
C. Enable AMI creation and define lifecycle rules in Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM). Create an AWS Lambda function that modifies the AMI in the Auto Scaling group.
D. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke AWS Backup lifecycle policies that provision AMIs. Configure Auto Scaling group capacity limits as an event source in EventBridge.
optionExplanations: ✗ register-image simply creates an AMI from a snapshot without pre-warming EBS blocks, so first-launch instances still suffer lazy-loading latency from S3; Step Functions adds orchestration but not faster initialization.

✓ EBS fast snapshot restore fully initializes volumes created from the snapshot so instances launched from the resulting AMI deliver full performance immediately, minimizing initialization latency for the Auto Scaling group.
✗ Amazon DLM automates AMI/snapshot creation and retention but does not eliminate the lazy block-loading latency on first use, so it does not minimize instance initialization latency.

✗ AWS Backup with EventBridge automates backup/AMI lifecycle but does not pre-warm volumes, so launched instances still experience initialization latency; it does not address the performance requirement.

text: A company hosts a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances. The company’s IT security guidelines mandate that the database credentials be encrypted and rotated every 14 days. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.

B. Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.

C. Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier. Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.

D. Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Secrets Manager natively stores the Aurora credentials encrypted with a KMS key and provides built-in managed rotation (configurable to 14 days) for RDS/Aurora with no custom code, giving the least operational effort.

✗ SSM Parameter Store SecureString can encrypt the password but has no built-in rotation, requiring you to build and maintain a custom Lambda rotation function, which is more operational effort than Secrets Manager.
✗ Storing credentials in an encrypted EFS file and writing a custom Lambda to rotate them is complex and high-maintenance compared to Secrets Manager's managed rotation.
✗ Storing credentials in an encrypted S3 file with custom download logic and a custom rotation Lambda is unnecessarily complex and operationally heavy versus Secrets Manager's native rotation.

text: A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The company hosts the backend database on Amazon RDS for MySQL with a primary DB instance and five read replicas to support scaling needs. The read replicas must lag no more than 1 second behind the primary DB instance. The database routinely runs scheduled stored procedures. As trafic on the website increases, the replicas experience additional lag during periods of peak load. A solutions architect must reduce the replication lag as much as possible. The solutions architect must minimize changes to the application code and must minimize ongoing operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.

B. Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database. Modify the application to check the cache before the application queries the database. Replace the stored procedures with AWS Lambda functions.

C. Migrate the database to a MySQL database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Choose large, compute optimized EC2 instances for all replica nodes. Maintain the stored procedures on the EC2 instances.

D. Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a large number of read capacity units (RCUs) to support the required throughput, and configure on-demand capacity scaling. Replace the stored procedures with DynamoDB streams.
optionExplanations: ✓ Aurora MySQL uses a shared storage layer so Aurora Replicas have replication lag typically well under 1 second (single-digit milliseconds), Aurora Auto Scaling handles read scaling during peak load, and Aurora native functions reduce the burden of stored procedures, all with minimal code change and low operational overhead.

✗ Wrong. ElastiCache for Redis fronting the database requires significant application code changes to implement cache-checking logic, and replacing stored procedures with Lambda functions is a major re-architecture; it does not directly address RDS read replica lag.

✗ Wrong. Self-managing MySQL on EC2 increases operational overhead substantially (patching, replication, failover) and does not inherently reduce replication lag below the asynchronous lag MySQL already exhibits.

✗ Wrong. Migrating to DynamoDB is a full rewrite of the data model and application code, DynamoDB Streams are change-capture features not a replacement for stored procedures, and this violates the requirement to minimize code changes.

text: A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) plan for a high-volume software as a service (SaaS) platform. All data for the platform is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The DR plan must replicate data to a secondary AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use MySQL binary log replication to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Provision one DB instance for the Aurora cluster in the secondary Region.
B. Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. When setup is complete, remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
C. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to continuously replicate data to an Aurora cluster in the secondary Region. Remove the DB instance from the secondary Region.
D. Set up an Aurora global database for the DB cluster. Specify a minimum of one DB instance in the secondary Region.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. Manually configuring MySQL binary log replication to a separate Aurora cluster adds operational overhead and is not the purpose-built, cost-effective DR mechanism for Aurora.

✗ Wrong. An Aurora global database requires at least one DB instance in the secondary Region (headless secondary clusters with zero instances were not supported historically); you cannot fully remove the instance and still have a writable failover target in standard exam scope.
✗ Wrong. AWS DMS for continuous replication adds ongoing operational overhead and cost compared to the native Aurora global database, and removing the secondary instance breaks the target.

✓ An Aurora global database provides low-latency, storage-level cross-Region replication for DR with a minimum of one DB instance in the secondary Region, which is the most cost-effective managed solution.

text: A company has a custom application with embedded credentials that retrieves information from an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. Management says the application must be made more secure with the least amount of programming effort. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create keys. Configure the application to load the database credentials from AWS KMS. Enable automatic key rotation.

B. Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function that rotates the credentials in Secret Manager.

C. Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Secrets Manager. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Secrets Manager.

D. Create credentials on the RDS for MySQL database for the application user and store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the application to load the database credentials from Parameter Store. Set up a credentials rotation schedule for the application user in the RDS for MySQL database using Parameter Store.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. AWS KMS manages encryption keys, not database credentials; it cannot store or rotate RDS username/password secrets, so it does not solve the embedded credentials problem.

✗ Wrong. Storing credentials in Secrets Manager is correct, but writing a custom Lambda rotation function adds programming effort; Secrets Manager provides built-in managed rotation for RDS, so a custom function is unnecessary.

✓ Storing the credentials in Secrets Manager and using its built-in managed rotation schedule for RDS for MySQL secures the application with the least programming effort, since rotation is handled natively without custom code.

✗ Wrong. Systems Manager Parameter Store does not provide automatic rotation of RDS credentials, so setting up a rotation schedule through Parameter Store is not supported and would require custom development.

text: A media company hosts its website on AWS. The website application’s architecture includes a fieet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a database that is hosted on Amazon Aurora. The company’s cybersecurity team reports that the application is vulnerable to SQL injection. How should the company resolve this issue?
options: A. Use AWS WAF in front of the ALB. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
B. Create an ALB listener rule to reply to SQL injections with a fixed response.
C. Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
D. Set up Amazon Inspector to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS WAF placed in front of the Application Load Balancer with a web ACL containing SQL injection rules (including the AWS managed SQLi rule group) inspects and blocks malicious requests, directly mitigating SQL injection.
✗ Wrong. An ALB listener rule with a fixed-response action cannot reliably detect SQL injection payloads in request content; ALB rules route based on host/path/headers, not deep content inspection.
✗ Wrong. AWS Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks, not application-layer SQL injection, and does not inspect request payloads for SQLi.
✗ Wrong. Amazon Inspector performs vulnerability assessment and security scanning of workloads; it does not sit inline to block live SQL injection requests.

text: A company has an Amazon S3 data lake that is governed by AWS Lake Formation. The company wants to create a visualization in Amazon QuickSight by joining the data in the data lake with operational data that is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The company wants to enforce column-level authorization so that the company’s marketing team can access only a subset of columns in the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon EMR to ingest the data directly from the database to the QuickSight SPICE engine. Include only the required columns.

B. Use AWS Glue Studio to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Attach an IAM policy to the QuickSight users to enforce column-level access control. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.

C. Use AWS Glue Elastic Views to create a materialized view for the database in Amazon S3. Create an S3 bucket policy to enforce column- level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.

D. Use a Lake Formation blueprint to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Use Lake Formation to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon Athena as the data source in QuickSight.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. Amazon EMR ingesting directly into SPICE adds significant operational overhead and does not provide centralized column-level authorization through Lake Formation.

✗ Wrong. AWS Glue Studio ingestion combined with IAM policies on QuickSight users does not provide native column-level access control; IAM does not enforce per-column data filtering, increasing complexity.
✗ Wrong. AWS Glue Elastic Views (deprecated/preview) plus S3 bucket policies cannot enforce column-level access control, since bucket policies operate at the object level, not the column level.

✓ A Lake Formation blueprint ingests the Aurora data into the S3 data lake, Lake Formation natively enforces column-level access control for QuickSight users, and Athena serves as the QuickSight data source with the least operational overhead.

text: A transaction processing company has weekly scripted batch jobs that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The number of transactions can vary, but the baseline CPU utilization that is noted on each run is at least 60%. The company needs to provision the capacity 30 minutes before the jobs run. Currently, engineers complete this task by manually modifying the Auto Scaling group parameters. The company does not have the resources to analyze the required capacity trends for the Auto Scaling group counts. The company needs an automated way to modify the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on the CPU utilization metric. Set the target value for the metric to 60%.

B. Create a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Set the appropriate desired capacity, minimum capacity, and maximum capacity. Set the recurrence to weekly. Set the start time to 30 minutes before the batch jobs run.

C. Create a predictive scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group. Configure the policy to scale based on forecast. Set the scaling metric to CPU utilization. Set the target value for the metric to 60%. In the policy, set the instances to pre-launch 30 minutes before the jobs run.

D. Create an Amazon EventBridge event to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the CPU utilization metric value for the Auto Scaling group reaches 60%. Configure the Lambda function to increase the Auto Scaling group’s desired capacity and maximum capacity by 20%.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. A dynamic (target tracking) scaling policy reacts to CPU after load increases, so it cannot provision capacity 30 minutes ahead of a scheduled job, causing initial lag.

✓ A scheduled scaling policy with the appropriate desired/min/max capacity, weekly recurrence, and a start time 30 minutes before the batch jobs run pre-provisions capacity exactly as needed with the least operational overhead, since the schedule is known.

✗ Wrong. Predictive scaling requires historical data and forecast analysis, but the company explicitly lacks resources to analyze capacity trends; it is more complex than needed for a known weekly schedule.
✗ Wrong. An EventBridge plus Lambda solution that reacts when CPU reaches 60% is reactive and adds custom code/operational overhead, and it cannot pre-provision 30 minutes before the jobs run.

text: A solutions architect is designing a company’s disaster recovery (DR) architecture. The company has a MySQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet with scheduled backup. The DR design needs to include multiple AWS Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Migrate the MySQL database to multiple EC2 instances. Configure a standby EC2 instance in the DR Region. Turn on replication.
B. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS. Use a Multi-AZ deployment. Turn on read replication for the primary DB instance in the different Availability Zones.
C. Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon Aurora global database. Host the primary DB cluster in the primary Region. Host the secondary DB cluster in the DR Region.
D. Store the scheduled backup of the MySQL database in an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR). Use the data backup to restore the database in the DR Region.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. Migrating to multiple self-managed EC2 instances with manual replication to a standby in the DR Region carries high operational overhead for patching, replication, and failover.
✗ Wrong. RDS Multi-AZ and read replicas across Availability Zones provide high availability within a single Region; this does not satisfy the multi-Region DR requirement.

✓ An Amazon Aurora global database with the primary cluster in the primary Region and a secondary cluster in the DR Region provides managed, low-latency cross-Region replication and fast failover with the least operational overhead.

✗ Wrong. Storing scheduled backups in an S3 bucket with Cross-Region Replication and manually restoring in the DR Region is a backup-and-restore approach with higher RTO and more manual operational effort than a managed global database.

text: A company has a Java application that uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to parse messages. The application cannot parse messages that are larger than 256 KB in size. The company wants to implement a solution to give the application the ability to parse messages as large as 50 MB. Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the code?
options: A. Use the Amazon SQS Extended Client Library for Java to host messages that are larger than 256 KB in Amazon S3.
B. Use Amazon EventBridge to post large messages from the application instead of Amazon SQS.
C. Change the limit in Amazon SQS to handle messages that are larger than 256 KB.
D. Store messages that are larger than 256 KB in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Configure Amazon SQS to reference this location in the messages.
optionExplanations: ✓ The Amazon SQS Extended Client Library for Java transparently stores message payloads larger than 256 KB in Amazon S3 and passes a reference through SQS, enabling payloads up to 2 GB with the fewest code changes.
✗ Wrong. Amazon EventBridge has its own payload size limit (256 KB) and switching messaging services would require substantial application rework, not the fewest changes.
✗ Wrong. The 256 KB maximum message size in Amazon SQS is a hard service limit that cannot be increased by changing a setting.
✗ Wrong. Amazon EFS is not natively integrated with SQS message handling; manually storing payloads in EFS and referencing them would require significant custom code and infrastructure changes.

text: A company wants to restrict access to the content of one of its main web applications and to protect the content by using authorization techniques available on AWS. The company wants to implement a serverless architecture and an authentication solution for fewer than 100 users. The solution needs to integrate with the main web application and serve web content globally. The solution must also scale as the company's user base grows while providing the lowest login latency possible. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use Amazon Cognito for authentication. Use Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
B. Use AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Use AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
C. Use Amazon Cognito for authentication. Use AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
D. Use AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Use Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon Cognito provides serverless, scalable, low-cost authentication for a small user base, Lambda@Edge runs authorization at edge locations for the lowest login latency, and CloudFront serves the web content globally, meeting all requirements cost-effectively.

✗ Wrong. AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory is not serverless and incurs significant hourly cost, which is not cost-effective for fewer than 100 users; an ALB also does not serve content globally with low edge latency.

✗ Wrong. While Cognito and Lambda are appropriate, S3 Transfer Acceleration is designed to speed up uploads/downloads to S3, not to serve and globally distribute a web application with low login latency like CloudFront does.

✗ Wrong. AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory is not serverless and is costly for a small user base, and Elastic Beanstalk provisions managed servers rather than serving content globally at the edge.

text: A company has an aging network-attached storage (NAS) array in its data center. The NAS array presents SMB shares and NFS shares to client workstations. The company does not want to purchase a new NAS array. The company also does not want to incur the cost of renewing the NAS array’s support contract. Some of the data is accessed frequently, but much of the data is inactive. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that migrates the data to Amazon S3, uses S3 Lifecycle policies, and maintains the same look and feel for the client workstations. The solutions architect has identified AWS Storage Gateway as part of the solution. Which type of storage gateway should the solutions architect provision to meet these requirements?
options: A. Volume Gateway
B. Tape Gateway
C. Amazon FSx File Gateway
D. Amazon S3 File Gateway
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. Volume Gateway presents iSCSI block volumes, not SMB/NFS file shares, so it does not maintain the same file-based look and feel for client workstations.
✗ Wrong. Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library (VTL interface) for backup applications, not SMB/NFS shares for client workstations.
✗ Wrong. Amazon FSx File Gateway provides on-premises access to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server (SMB only) and stores data in FSx, not in Amazon S3 with S3 Lifecycle policies as required.

✓ Amazon S3 File Gateway presents both SMB and NFS shares to clients while storing files as objects in Amazon S3, supporting S3 Lifecycle policies and preserving the same file-share look and feel for workstations.

text: A company has an application that is running on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect has standardized the company on a particular instance family and various instance sizes based on the current needs of the company. The company wants to maximize cost savings for the application over the next 3 years. The company needs to be able to change the instance family and sizes in the next 6 months based on application popularity and usage. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Compute Savings Plan
B. EC2 Instance Savings Plan
C. Zonal Reserved Instances
D. Standard Reserved Instances
optionExplanations: ✓ A Compute Savings Plan provides up to 3-year cost savings with maximum flexibility, automatically applying across any instance family, size, Region, OS, and tenancy, so the company can change instance families and sizes in 6 months without losing the discount.

✗ Wrong. An EC2 Instance Savings Plan locks the discount to a specific instance family in a Region; changing to a different instance family would forfeit the savings, so it does not meet the flexibility requirement.
✗ Wrong. Zonal Reserved Instances are tied to a specific Availability Zone and instance type with no size flexibility across families, so they cannot accommodate changing instance families.
✗ Wrong. Standard Reserved Instances offer the highest discount but limited flexibility (no family change), so switching instance families later would not be covered without selling/modifying RIs.

text: A company collects data from a large number of participants who use wearable devices. The company stores the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table and uses applications to analyze the data. The data workload is constant and predictable. The company wants to stay at or below its forecasted budget for DynamoDB. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use provisioned mode and DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA). Reserve capacity for the forecasted workload.
B. Use provisioned mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs).
C. Use on-demand mode. Set the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) high enough to accommodate changes in the workload.
D. Use on-demand mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) with reserved capacity.
optionExplanations: ✗ Provisioned mode suits the constant, predictable workload, but the DynamoDB Standard-IA table class is designed for infrequently accessed data with cheaper storage and higher per-request costs; since this data is actively and continuously analyzed, Standard-IA raises request costs and is the wrong table class here.

✓ Provisioned mode lets you specify RCUs and WCUs for a steady, predictable workload, which is the most cost-effective fit; capacity can be fixed to the forecasted budget (and optionally enhanced with reserved capacity), making this the correct choice for a constant, predictable workload.

✗ On-demand mode bills per request with no need to set RCUs/WCUs (and you cannot actually 'set' them in on-demand), and it is more expensive than provisioned for steady, predictable traffic; overprovisioning to handle variability also contradicts staying within budget.
✗ On-demand mode does not use RCUs/WCUs and does not support reserved capacity; reserved capacity applies only to provisioned mode, so this option is technically invalid and not cost-effective.

text: A company stores confidential data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database in the ap-southeast-3 Region. The database is encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. The company was recently acquired and must securely share a backup of the database with the acquiring company’s AWS account in ap-southeast-3. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a database snapshot. Copy the snapshot to a new unencrypted snapshot. Share the new snapshot with the acquiring company’s AWS account.
B. Create a database snapshot. Add the acquiring company’s AWS account to the KMS key policy. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company’s AWS account.
C. Create a database snapshot that uses a different AWS managed KMS key. Add the acquiring company’s AWS account to the KMS key alias. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.

D. Create a database snapshot. Download the database snapshot. Upload the database snapshot to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the acquiring company’s AWS account.
optionExplanations: ✗ Copying an encrypted snapshot to an unencrypted snapshot is not allowed for KMS-encrypted RDS/Aurora snapshots, and it would expose confidential data, so this fails the security requirement.

✓ To share an encrypted Aurora snapshot cross-account you must share the snapshot and add the target account as a key user/grantee in the customer managed KMS key policy so the acquiring account can decrypt it.
✗ You cannot re-encrypt with an AWS managed key by simply taking a snapshot, and key aliases do not control cross-account access; access is granted via the KMS key policy, so this is invalid.
✗ Aurora snapshots cannot be downloaded to local disk and uploaded to S3; this is not a supported export path and is unnecessarily complex and insecure.

text: A company uses a 100 GB Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server Single-AZ DB instance in the us-east-1 Region to store customer transactions. The company needs high availability and automatic recovery for the DB instance. The company must also run reports on the RDS database several times a year. The report process causes transactions to take longer than usual to post to the customers’ accounts. The company needs a solution that will improve the performance of the report process. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Modify the DB instance from a Single-AZ DB instance to a Multi-AZ deployment.
B. Take a snapshot of the current DB instance. Restore the snapshot to a new RDS deployment in another Availability Zone.
C. Create a read replica of the DB instance in a different Availability Zone. Point all requests for reports to the read replica.
D. Migrate the database to RDS Custom.
E. Use RDS Proxy to limit reporting requests to the maintenance window.
optionExplanations: ✓ Converting the Single-AZ instance to a Multi-AZ deployment provisions a synchronous standby in another AZ and provides automatic failover and recovery, directly meeting the high availability and automatic recovery requirement.

✗ Restoring a snapshot to a new instance creates a one-time static copy that does not stay in sync, provides no automatic failover, and does not offload live reporting workloads, so it meets neither requirement.

✓ A read replica asynchronously replicates the primary and lets all report queries be directed to it, offloading the heavy read workload so transactions on the primary post without the slowdown caused by reporting.

✗ RDS Custom is for workloads needing OS/database access for legacy or custom configurations; it neither provides built-in HA nor improves report performance, so it does not address these requirements.

✗ RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections to improve scalability and failover handling; it cannot restrict report queries to a maintenance window and does not offload reporting load to improve performance.

text: A company is moving its data management application to AWS. The company wants to transition to an event-driven architecture. The architecture needs to be more distributed and to use serverless concepts while performing the different aspects of the workfiow. The company also wants to minimize operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Build out the workfiow in AWS Glue. Use AWS Glue to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workfiow steps.
B. Build out the workfiow in AWS Step Functions. Deploy the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Step Functions to invoke the workfiow steps on the EC2 instances.
C. Build out the workfiow in Amazon EventBridge. Use EventBridge to invoke AWS Lambda functions on a schedule to process the workfiow steps.
D. Build out the workfiow in AWS Step Functions. Use Step Functions to create a state machine. Use the state machine to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workfiow steps.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Glue is an ETL service for data integration, not a general event-driven workflow orchestrator, and it is not the right fit for orchestrating distributed serverless application steps.
✗ Deploying on EC2 instances introduces server management and is not serverless, conflicting with the serverless and minimal operational overhead requirements.
✗ EventBridge on a schedule is time-driven rather than truly event-driven workflow orchestration, and it lacks the state management of a workflow engine.
✓ AWS Step Functions state machines orchestrate distributed, event-driven serverless workflows by invoking Lambda functions, with minimal operational overhead.

text: A company is designing the network for an online multi-player game. The game uses the UDP networking protocol and will be deployed in eight AWS Regions. The network architecture needs to minimize latency and packet loss to give end users a high-quality gaming experience. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Setup a transit gateway in each Region. Create inter-Region peering attachments between each transit gateway.
B. Set up AWS Global Accelerator with UDP listeners and endpoint groups in each Region.
C. Set up Amazon CloudFront with UDP turned on. Configure an origin in each Region.
D. Set up a VPC peering mesh between each Region. Turn on UDP for each VPC.
optionExplanations: ✗ Transit gateways with inter-Region peering route VPC traffic over the AWS network but do not optimize end-user internet ingress latency or provide UDP-aware global routing for end users.
✓ AWS Global Accelerator supports UDP listeners and endpoint groups per Region, routing users over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy endpoint, minimizing latency and packet loss.
✗ CloudFront is a CDN optimized for HTTP/HTTPS content delivery and does not support generic UDP gaming traffic.
✗ VPC peering connects VPCs privately but does not improve end-user internet latency, and there is no per-VPC 'turn on UDP' setting for this purpose.

text: A company hosts a three-tier web application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone. The web application uses a self-managed MySQL database that is hosted on an EC2 instance to store data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. The MySQL database currently uses a 1 TB Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volume. The company expects trafic of 1,000 IOPS for both reads and writes at peak trafic. The company wants to minimize any disruptions, stabilize performance, and reduce costs while retaining the capacity for double the IOPS. The company wants to move the database tier to a fully managed solution that is highly available and fault tolerant. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with an io2 Block Express EBS volume.
B. Use a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with a General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume.
C. Use Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering access tiers.
D. Use two large EC2 instances to host the database in active-passive mode.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ is fully managed, highly available, and fault tolerant, but io2 Block Express is provisioned high-performance storage priced far above what is needed for only 2,000 IOPS, so it is not the most cost-effective choice.

✓ Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ is fully managed, highly available, and fault tolerant. A 1 TB gp2 volume delivers a 3,000 IOPS baseline (3 IOPS/GB), which comfortably exceeds the 2,000 IOPS (double the 1,000 peak) requirement at a much lower cost than provisioned IOPS volumes, making it the most cost-effective option.
✗ Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering is object storage for cost-optimized data access tiers; it is not a relational database and cannot host a MySQL database tier.

✗ Two large EC2 instances in active-passive mode is still a self-managed solution requiring manual database administration and failover, which fails the explicit requirement for a fully managed solution and adds operational overhead.

text: A company hosts a serverless application on AWS. The application uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The company notices an increase in application errors that result from database connection timeouts during times of peak trafic or unpredictable trafic. The company needs a solution that reduces the application failures with the least amount of change to the code. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Reduce the Lambda concurrency rate.
B. Enable RDS Proxy on the RDS DB instance.
C. Resize the RDS DB instance class to accept more connections.
D. Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand scaling.
optionExplanations: ✗ Reducing Lambda concurrency throttles the application and degrades performance rather than solving connection exhaustion during traffic spikes.
✓ RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections, preventing connection timeouts from Lambda concurrency spikes with minimal code change.
✗ Resizing the DB instance is a temporary, costlier fix that still does not efficiently manage the rapid connection churn from Lambda during unpredictable traffic.
✗ Migrating to DynamoDB is a major architectural and code change, contradicting the requirement for the least amount of code change.

text: A company is migrating an old application to AWS. The application runs a batch job every hour and is CPU intensive. The batch job takes 15 minutes on average with an on-premises server. The server has 64 virtual CPU (vCPU) and 512 GiB of memory. Which solution will run the batch job within 15 minutes with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use AWS Lambda with functional scaling.
B. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate.
C. Use Amazon Lightsail with AWS Auto Scaling.
D. Use AWS Batch on Amazon EC2.
optionExplanations: ✗ Lambda is limited to a 15-minute maximum runtime and roughly 6 vCPU/10 GB memory, which cannot match the 64 vCPU/512 GiB CPU-intensive workload reliably.
✗ ECS with Fargate could run the job but requires defining and managing container images and task definitions, more setup than a managed batch service for a scheduled CPU job.
✗ Lightsail with Auto Scaling is not a standard pairing and is intended for simple workloads, not large CPU-intensive batch processing with this much vCPU/memory.
