The application recently experienced data loss after a database server crashed because of an unexpected power outage. The company needs a solution that avoids any single points of failure. The solution must give the application the ability to scale to meet user demand. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ configuration.
B. Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone. Deploy the database on an EC2 instance. Enable EC2 Auto Recovery.

C. Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance with a read replica in a single Availability Zone. Promote the read replica to replace the primary DB instance if the primary DB instance fails.

D. Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Deploy the primary and secondary database servers on EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach to create shared storage between the instances.
optionExplanations: ✓ EC2 Auto Scaling across multiple AZs removes the application-tier single point of failure and provides demand-based scaling, while RDS Multi-AZ keeps a synchronously replicated standby in another AZ for automatic failover and durable, highly available data. This meets every requirement.

✗ Placing the Auto Scaling group in a single AZ leaves an AZ-level single point of failure, and a self-managed database on one EC2 instance with only Auto Recovery still has no replica, so it remains a single point of failure and risks data loss. Incorrect.

✗ RDS multi-AZ deployment is missing; a read replica in a single AZ provides only asynchronous replication (risking data loss) and requires manual promotion, so it is not automatic failover and the single-AZ replica is a single point of failure. Incorrect.

✗ Self-managing primary/secondary databases on EC2 adds high operational overhead, and EBS Multi-Attach is not supported across Availability Zones (it is single-AZ only) and is unsuitable for standard RDBMS shared storage, so this fails the multi-AZ resilience requirement. Incorrect.

text: A company needs to ingest and handle large amounts of streaming data that its application generates. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and sends data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, which is configured with default settings. Every other day, the application consumes the data and writes the data to an Amazon S3 bucket for business intelligence (BI) processing. The company observes that Amazon S3 is not receiving all the data that the application sends to Kinesis Data Streams. What should a solutions architect do to resolve this issue?
options: A. Update the Kinesis Data Streams default settings by modifying the data retention period.
B. Update the application to use the Kinesis Producer Library (KPL) to send the data to Kinesis Data Streams.
C. Update the number of Kinesis shards to handle the throughput of the data that is sent to Kinesis Data Streams.
D. Turn on S3 Versioning within the S3 bucket to preserve every version of every object that is ingested in the S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✓ Kinesis Data Streams default retention is 24 hours, but the application consumes data every other day (48 hours); records expire before consumption, so increasing the retention period (up to 7 days, or longer with extended retention) ensures all data is available when read. This directly resolves the data loss.
✗ The Kinesis Producer Library improves write efficiency, batching, and reliability when sending data, but the problem is data expiring before it is consumed, not a producer-side write failure.

✗ Adding shards increases write/read throughput and prevents throttling, but the scenario describes loss due to the 48-hour consumption gap exceeding the 24-hour default retention, not throughput limits.
✗ S3 Versioning preserves multiple versions of objects already written to S3; it cannot recover data that never reached S3 because it expired in Kinesis.

text: A developer has an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to upload files to Amazon S3 and needs the required permissions to perform the task. The developer already has an IAM user with valid IAM credentials required for Amazon S3. What should a solutions architect do to grant the permissions?
options: A. Add required IAM permissions in the resource policy of the Lambda function.
B. Create a signed request using the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
C. Create a new IAM user and use the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
D. Create an IAM execution role with the required permissions and attach the IAM role to the Lambda function.
optionExplanations: ✗ A Lambda resource policy controls who can invoke the function, not the permissions the function uses to access other AWS services like S3.
✗ Embedding IAM credentials to create signed requests inside the function is an insecure anti-pattern and is not the recommended way to grant a Lambda function permissions.
✗ Creating a new IAM user and hardcoding its credentials in the function is insecure and not the best practice for granting Lambda permissions.
✓ Creating an IAM execution role with the required S3 permissions and attaching it to the Lambda function is the correct, secure way to grant the function permission to upload files to S3.

text: A company has deployed a serverless application that invokes an AWS Lambda function when new documents are uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. The application uses the Lambda function to process the documents. After a recent marketing campaign, the company noticed that the application did not process many of the documents. What should a solutions architect do to improve the architecture of this application?
options: A. Set the Lambda function's runtime timeout value to 15 minutes.
B. Configure an S3 bucket replication policy. Stage the documents in the S3 bucket for later processing.
C. Deploy an additional Lambda function. Load balance the processing of the documents across the two Lambda functions.
D. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Send the requests to the queue. Configure the queue as an event source for Lambda.
optionExplanations: ✗ Increasing the Lambda timeout to 15 minutes does not help when the problem is a burst of invocations exceeding concurrency limits, causing dropped documents.
✗ An S3 replication policy copies objects to another bucket and does not buffer or guarantee processing of the document workload.
✗ Adding a second Lambda function and manually load balancing is complex and does not reliably buffer bursts; Lambda already scales concurrently.
✓ Placing an SQS queue between S3 and Lambda buffers the burst of requests, retries failed processing, and lets Lambda consume at a controlled rate so documents are not dropped during traffic spikes.

text: A solutions architect is designing the architecture for a software demonstration environment. The environment will run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The system will experience significant increases in trafic during working hours but is not required to operate on weekends. Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to ensure that the system can scale to meet demand? (Choose two.)
options: A. Use AWS Auto Scaling to adjust the ALB capacity based on request rate.
B. Use AWS Auto Scaling to scale the capacity of the VPC internet gateway.
C. Launch the EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions to distribute the load across Regions.
D. Use a target tracking scaling policy to scale the Auto Scaling group based on instance CPU utilization.
E. Use scheduled scaling to change the Auto Scaling group minimum, maximum, and desired capacity to zero for weekends. Revert to the default values at the start of the week.
optionExplanations: ✗ Application Load Balancers scale automatically and are not capacity-managed by AWS Auto Scaling, so this option is not valid.
✗ Internet gateways are fully managed by AWS, scale automatically, and cannot be scaled by Auto Scaling.
✗ Launching instances in multiple Regions adds significant complexity and is unnecessary for a demonstration environment that simply needs to scale with daily demand.
✓ A target tracking scaling policy based on instance CPU utilization automatically scales the Auto Scaling group up during high-traffic working hours and down when load drops.

✓ Scheduled scaling that sets the group capacity to zero on weekends and reverts to default values at the start of the week eliminates cost when the system is not needed and ensures capacity returns for the work week.

text: A solutions architect is designing a two-tiered architecture that includes a public subnet and a database subnet. The web servers in the public subnet must be open to the internet on port 443. The Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in the database subnet must be accessible only to the web servers on port 3306. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Create a network ACL for the public subnet. Add a rule to deny outbound trafic to 0.0.0.0/0 on port 3306.
B. Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to allow trafic from the public subnet CIDR block on port 3306.
C. Create a security group for the web servers in the public subnet. Add a rule to allow trafic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443.
D. Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to allow trafic from the web servers’ security group on port 3306.
E. Create a security group for the DB instance. Add a rule to deny all trafic except trafic from the web servers’ security group on port 3306.
optionExplanations: ✗ Network ACLs control subnet-level traffic but adding an outbound deny on port 3306 from the public subnet would block the web servers from reaching the RDS DB instance, defeating the requirement.

✗ A DB security group allowing the public subnet CIDR block on port 3306 would work, but it is less precise and less secure than referencing the web servers' security group; AWS best practice prefers SG referencing over CIDR.
✓ A security group for the web servers allowing inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443 correctly exposes the web tier to the internet on HTTPS, satisfying the public-facing requirement.

✓ A DB security group that allows inbound traffic from the web servers' security group on port 3306 is the AWS best-practice way to restrict database access to only the web servers, automatically covering all web server instances.
✗ Security groups are stateful and support only allow rules; they cannot contain explicit deny rules, so this option is invalid for security groups (deny semantics belong to network ACLs).

text: A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use Lustre clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
B. Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
C. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
D. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS DataSync is a data transfer service, not a Lustre-compatible shared file system, so it does not meet the requirement.
✗ AWS Storage Gateway file gateway provides NFS/SMB access, not the Lustre protocol clients need.
✗ Amazon EFS uses the NFS protocol and cannot be configured to support Lustre, so this option is technically inaccurate.
✓ Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed, Lustre-compatible high-performance file system ideal for compute-intensive workloads like gaming, meeting all requirements.

text: A company runs an application that receives data from thousands of geographically dispersed remote devices that use UDP. The application processes the data immediately and sends a message back to the device if necessary. No data is stored. The company needs a solution that minimizes latency for the data transmission from the devices. The solution also must provide rapid failover to another AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the two Regions. Configure the NLB to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the data.

B. Use AWS Global Accelerator. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the two Regions as an endpoint. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the NLProcess the data in Amazon ECS.

C. Use AWS Global Accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each of the two Regions as an endpoint. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.

D. Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each of the two Regions. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.
optionExplanations: ✗ Route 53 failover relies on DNS, which fails over slowly due to TTL caching and does not provide the rapid failover or anycast latency optimization that Global Accelerator does.

✓ AWS Global Accelerator routes traffic over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint with near-instant failover, and Network Load Balancers support the UDP protocol required by the devices, with ECS Fargate processing the data.
✗ Application Load Balancers operate at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and do not support UDP, so they cannot handle the device traffic.
✗ Route 53 failover is DNS-based with slow failover, and Application Load Balancers do not support UDP, so this option fails both requirements.

text: A solutions architect must migrate a Windows Internet Information Services (IIS) web application to AWS. The application currently relies on a file share hosted in the user's on-premises network-attached storage (NAS). The solutions architect has proposed migrating the IIS web servers to Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones that are connected to the storage solution, and configuring an Elastic Load Balancer attached to the instances. Which replacement to the on-premises file share is MOST resilient and durable?
options: A. Migrate the file share to Amazon RDS.
B. Migrate the file share to AWS Storage Gateway.
C. Migrate the file share to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
D. Migrate the file share to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon RDS is a relational database service, not a file share, and cannot serve the SMB/Windows file share that the IIS application relies on.

✗ AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid service for bridging on-premises environments to AWS storage; it is not the resilient, durable native file share replacement for EC2 instances already running in AWS.

✓ Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed native Windows (SMB) file share with Multi-AZ deployment for high availability and durable storage, making it the ideal resilient replacement for a Windows IIS application's NAS file share.
✗ Amazon EFS only supports NFS (Linux) protocol and does not support the SMB protocol required by Windows IIS applications, so it cannot replace the Windows file share.

text: A company is deploying a new application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application writes data to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company needs to ensure that all data that is written to the EBS volumes is encrypted at rest. Which solution will meet this requirement?
options: A. Create an IAM role that specifies EBS encryption. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.
B. Create the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes. Attach the EBS volumes to the EC2 instances.
C. Create an EC2 instance tag that has a key of Encrypt and a value of True. Tag all instances that require encryption at the EBS level.
D. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key policy that enforces EBS encryption in the account. Ensure that the key policy is active.
optionExplanations: ✗ An IAM role grants permissions but does not itself encrypt EBS volumes; there is no IAM role attribute that turns on EBS encryption for attached volumes.
✓ Creating the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes and attaching them ensures all data written to those volumes is encrypted at rest using AWS KMS keys.
✗ EC2 instance tags are metadata labels and have no effect on whether the attached EBS volumes are encrypted.
✗ A KMS key policy controls access to a KMS key; it cannot enforce that EBS volumes are created as encrypted in an account.

text: A company has a web application with sporadic usage patterns. There is heavy usage at the beginning of each month, moderate usage at the start of each week, and unpredictable usage during the week. The application consists of a web server and a MySQL database server running inside the data center. The company would like to move the application to the AWS Cloud, and needs to select a cost-effective database platform that will not require database modifications. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Amazon DynamoDB
B. Amazon RDS for MySQL
C. MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora Serverless
D. MySQL deployed on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and would require significant application/database modifications to migrate a MySQL workload, which the requirement prohibits.
✗ Amazon RDS for MySQL requires a provisioned instance running continuously, which is not cost-effective for sporadic, unpredictable usage where capacity should scale to demand.

✓ MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora Serverless automatically scales capacity up and down to match the sporadic, unpredictable usage, is cost-effective (paying only for capacity used), and is MySQL-compatible so it requires no database modifications.
✗ MySQL on EC2 in an Auto Scaling group is not a standard way to run a stateful relational database and introduces significant operational complexity, making it neither cost-effective nor low-effort.

text: An image-hosting company stores its objects in Amazon S3 buckets. The company wants to avoid accidental exposure of the objects in the S3 buckets to the public. All S3 objects in the entire AWS account need to remain private. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon GuardDuty to monitor S3 bucket policies. Create an automatic remediation action rule that uses an AWS Lambda function to remediate any change that makes the objects public.

B. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to find publicly accessible S3 buckets. Configure email notifications in Trusted Advisor when a change is detected. Manually change the S3 bucket policy if it allows public access.

C. Use AWS Resource Access Manager to find publicly accessible S3 buckets. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a change is detected. Deploy a Lambda function that programmatically remediates the change.

D. Use the S3 Block Public Access feature on the account level. Use AWS Organizations to create a service control policy (SCP) that prevents IAM users from changing the setting. Apply the SCP to the account.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service and does not monitor or remediate S3 bucket policies for public access; this approach is reactive and complex rather than preventive.
✗ AWS Trusted Advisor can identify public buckets but relies on manual remediation, which does not reliably prevent accidental exposure and is reactive.
✗ AWS Resource Access Manager is used to share resources across accounts, not to find publicly accessible S3 buckets; this option misuses the service.

✓ Enabling S3 Block Public Access at the account level prevents all public access, and using an AWS Organizations SCP to prevent users from changing the setting enforces that objects remain private account-wide.

text: An ecommerce company is experiencing an increase in user trafic. The company’s store is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances as a two-tier web application consisting of a web tier and a separate database tier. As trafic increases, the company notices that the architecture is causing significant delays in sending timely marketing and order confirmation email to users. The company wants to reduce the time it spends resolving complex email delivery issues and minimize operational overhead. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a separate application tier using EC2 instances dedicated to email processing.
B. Configure the web instance to send email through Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
C. Configure the web instance to send email through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
D. Create a separate application tier using EC2 instances dedicated to email processing. Place the instances in an Auto Scaling group.
optionExplanations: ✗ Building a dedicated EC2 email-processing tier increases operational overhead and does not solve complex email-delivery issues like deliverability, bounces, and reputation management.
✓ Amazon SES is a managed email service that handles the complex email-delivery issues and offloads sending marketing and order confirmation emails with minimal operational overhead.
✗ Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service for messages to subscribers/endpoints, not a service for sending standard transactional or marketing email to end users.
✗ Adding an Auto Scaling group to a dedicated EC2 email tier still requires managing email infrastructure and does not address complex deliverability issues, increasing operational overhead.

text: A company has a business system that generates hundreds of reports each day. The business system saves the reports to a network share in CSV format. The company needs to store this data in the AWS Cloud in near-real time for analysis. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
options: A. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create a scheduled task that runs at the end of each day.
B. Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Update the business system to use a new network share from the S3 File Gateway.
C. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create an application that uses the DataSync API in the automation workfiow.
D. Deploy an AWS Transfer for SFTP endpoint. Create a script that checks for new files on the network share and uploads the new files by using SFTP.
optionExplanations: ✗ A DataSync scheduled task that runs once at the end of each day does not meet the near-real-time requirement.

✓ An Amazon S3 File Gateway presents an NFS/SMB network share that automatically and continuously uploads files written to it into Amazon S3, providing near-real-time storage with the least administrative overhead.
✗ Building a custom application around the DataSync API adds development and maintenance overhead, which is more administrative effort than needed.
✗ Deploying an AWS Transfer for SFTP endpoint plus a custom file-watching upload script adds scripting and maintenance overhead, more than the managed file gateway approach.

text: A company is storing petabytes of data in Amazon S3 Standard. The data is stored in multiple S3 buckets and is accessed with varying frequency. The company does not know access patterns for all the data. The company needs to implement a solution for each S3 bucket to optimize the cost of S3 usage. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational eficiency?
options: A. Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
B. Use the S3 storage class analysis tool to determine the correct tier for each object in the S3 bucket. Move each object to the identified storage tier.
C. Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
D. Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone- IA).
optionExplanations: ✓ S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on changing access patterns, which is ideal when access patterns are unknown and varying. A Lifecycle rule transitioning objects to Intelligent-Tiering delivers automatic cost optimization with the least operational overhead.

✗ S3 storage class analysis only provides recommendations; it requires manual evaluation and manual movement of objects to the identified tier, which is high operational overhead and impractical at petabyte scale across many buckets.

✗ S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is for long-lived, rarely accessed data with millisecond retrieval. Blindly transitioning all objects to it when access patterns are unknown risks higher retrieval costs and latency for frequently accessed data, and it does not adapt automatically.

✗ S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, reducing durability/availability, and is meant for infrequently accessed, re-creatable data. It is unsuitable for data with unknown/varying access patterns and does not auto-adapt.

text: A rapidly growing global ecommerce company is hosting its web application on AWS. The web application includes static content and dynamic content. The website stores online transaction processing (OLTP) data in an Amazon RDS database The website’s users are experiencing slow page loads. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)
options: A. Configure an Amazon Redshift cluster.
B. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution.
C. Host the dynamic web content in Amazon S3.
D. Create a read replica for the RDS DB instance.
E. Configure a Multi-AZ deployment for the RDS DB instance.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics/OLAP workloads and would not improve page load speed for an OLTP web application.
✓ An Amazon CloudFront distribution caches static (and dynamic) content at edge locations close to global users, reducing latency and speeding up page loads.
✗ Amazon S3 hosts static content, not dynamic content; dynamic content requires compute, so this option is incorrect.
✓ Creating a read replica for the RDS DB instance offloads read traffic from the primary, reducing database load and improving page response times.
✗ A Multi-AZ deployment provides high availability and failover but does not improve read performance or page load speed, since the standby does not serve read traffic.

text: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions to run its application. The company has VPCs with public subnets and private subnets in its AWS account. The EC2 instances run in a private subnet in one of the VPCs. The Lambda functions need direct network access to the EC2 instances for the application to work. The application will run for at least 1 year. The company expects the number of Lambda functions that the application uses to increase during that time. The company wants to maximize its savings on all application resources and to keep network latency between the services low. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage and the number of invocations. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances.

B. Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan Optimize the Lambda functions' duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Connect the Lambda functions to a public subnet in the same VPC where the EC2 instances run.

C. Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Connect the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances.

D. Purchase a Compute Savings Plan. Optimize the Lambda functions’ duration and memory usage, the number of invocations, and the amount of data that is transferred. Keep the Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC.
optionExplanations: ✗ An EC2 Instance Savings Plan does not cover Lambda costs, and the company wants to maximize savings on all resources including the growing number of Lambda functions, so this is suboptimal.

✗ An EC2 Instance Savings Plan does not cover Lambda, and connecting Lambda to a public subnet does not provide a route to the EC2 instances in the private subnet, so it fails to give direct network access.

✓ A Compute Savings Plan covers both EC2 and Lambda for maximum savings, and connecting the Lambda functions to the private subnet containing the EC2 instances gives direct, low-latency network access.
✗ Keeping the Lambda functions in the Lambda service VPC means they cannot reach the EC2 instances in the private subnet, so the application would not work.

text: A solutions architect needs to allow team members to access Amazon S3 buckets in two different AWS accounts: a development account and a production account. The team currently has access to S3 buckets in the development account by using unique IAM users that are assigned to an IAM group that has appropriate permissions in the account. The solutions architect has created an IAM role in the production account. The role has a policy that grants access to an S3 bucket in the production account. Which solution will meet these requirements while complying with the principle of least privilege?
options: A. Attach the Administrator Access policy to the development account users.
B. Add the development account as a principal in the trust policy of the role in the production account.
C. Turn off the S3 Block Public Access feature on the S3 bucket in the production account.
D. Create a user in the production account with unique credentials for each team member.
optionExplanations: ✗ Attaching the Administrator Access policy grants far more permission than needed, violating the principle of least privilege.

✓ Adding the development account as a principal in the production role's trust policy allows the existing development IAM users to assume the role and access only the specific S3 bucket, satisfying least privilege via cross-account role assumption.
✗ Turning off S3 Block Public Access would expose the bucket publicly and does not grant the team scoped access; it is a security risk and does not address the requirement.
✗ Creating separate users in the production account duplicates credential management and is not least-privilege friendly compared to assuming a scoped role.

text: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and runs multiple Amazon EC2 workloads in the ap-southeast-2 Region. The company has a service control policy (SCP) that prevents any resources from being created in any other Region. A security policy requires the company to encrypt all data at rest. An audit discovers that employees have created Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes for EC2 instances without encrypting the volumes. The company wants any new EC2 instances that any IAM user or root user launches in ap-southeast-2 to use encrypted EBS volumes. The company wants a solution that will have minimal effect on employees who create EBS volumes. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. In the Amazon EC2 console, select the EBS encryption account attribute and define a default encryption key.

B. Create an IAM permission boundary. Attach the permission boundary to the root organizational unit (OU). Define the boundary to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
C. Create an SCP. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU). Define the SCP to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action whenthe ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
D. Update the IAM policies for each account to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
E. In the Organizations management account, specify the Default EBS volume encryption setting.
optionExplanations: ✓ Enabling the EBS encryption-by-default account attribute with a default key in the EC2 console (in the ap-southeast-2 Region) ensures new EBS volumes are automatically encrypted with minimal effect on employees.
✗ IAM permission boundaries cannot be attached to an organizational unit; they apply to IAM users/roles, so this option is technically invalid.

✓ An SCP attached to the root OU that denies ec2:CreateVolume when ec2:Encrypted is false enforces encryption across all accounts and applies even to root users, preventing unencrypted volume creation.
✗ Updating IAM policies in each account individually is high-effort, error-prone, and does not reliably cover the root user, making it less suitable than an SCP.

✗ There is no Organizations management-account setting that specifies a default EBS volume encryption for member accounts; EBS encryption-by-default is a per-account, per-Region EC2 setting, so this option is invalid.

text: A company wants to use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB cluster to simplify time-consuming database administrative tasks for production database workloads. The company wants to ensure that its database is highly available and will provide automatic failover support in most scenarios in less than 40 seconds. The company wants to ofioad reads off of the primary instance and keep costs as low as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Create one read replica and point the read workload to the read replica.
B. Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB duster deployment Create two read replicas and point the read workload to the read replicas.
C. Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Point the read workload to the secondary instances in the Multi-AZ pair.
D. Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment Point the read workload to the reader endpoint.
optionExplanations: ✗ An RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment with one read replica works but is more costly and the standard Multi-AZ instance failover typically takes longer (often 60+ seconds), not reliably under 40 seconds.

✗ An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster has exactly two readable standby instances by default; you do not create separate read replicas, and pointing reads to them rather than the reader endpoint is not the intended low-cost design.
✗ An RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment does not allow reading from the secondary standby instance, so this option is technically impossible.

✓ An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment provides two readable standby instances with failover typically under 35 seconds and a reader endpoint to offload reads, meeting the high-availability, fast-failover, read-offload, and low-cost requirements.

text: A company runs a highly available SFTP service. The SFTP service uses two Amazon EC2 Linux instances that run with elastic IP addresses to accept trafic from trusted IP sources on the internet. The SFTP service is backed by shared storage that is attached to the instances. User accounts are created and managed as Linux users in the SFTP servers. The company wants a serverless option that provides high IOPS performance and highly configurable security. The company also wants to maintain control over user permissions. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a public endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the EBS volume to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.

B. Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with elastic IP addresses and a VPC endpoint that has internet-facing access. Attach a security group to the endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the EFS volume to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.

C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a public endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the S3 bucket to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.

D. Create an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a VPC endpoint that has internal access in a private subnet. Attach a security group that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the S3 bucket to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Transfer Family SFTP cannot use an Amazon EBS volume as backing storage; EBS is block storage attached to EC2, not a supported Transfer Family backend (only S3 and EFS are), so this is invalid.

✓ AWS Transfer Family is the serverless SFTP option; backing it with encrypted Amazon EFS provides POSIX/Linux-style user semantics and high IOPS, and a VPC endpoint with internet-facing access plus a security group restricting trusted source IPs delivers the configurable security and user-permission control required.

✗ An S3-backed Transfer Family service is serverless but S3 is object storage that does not deliver the high block-level IOPS performance or the Linux POSIX user/permission model the company wants to preserve, making it a weaker fit.

✗ An internal-only VPC endpoint in a private subnet would not be reachable from trusted internet IP sources without additional networking, and S3 still does not provide the high IOPS/POSIX permission model required, so this fails the access and storage requirements.

text: A company is developing a new machine learning (ML) model solution on AWS. The models are developed as independent microservices that fetch approximately 1 GB of model data from Amazon S3 at startup and load the data into memory. Users access the models through an asynchronous API. Users can send a request or a batch of requests and specify where the results should be sent. The company provides models to hundreds of users. The usage patterns for the models are irregular. Some models could be unused for days or weeks. Other models could receive batches of thousands of requests at a time. Which design should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Direct the requests from the API to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy the models as AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by the NLB.

B. Direct the requests from the API to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use AWS App Mesh to scale the instances of the ECS cluster based on the SQS queue size.

C. Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by SQS events. Use AWS Auto Scaling to increase the number of vCPUs for the Lambda functions based on the SQS queue size.

D. Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from the queue. Enable AWS Auto Scaling on Amazon ECS for both the cluster and copies of the service based on the queue size.
optionExplanations: ✗ An NLB cannot directly invoke AWS Lambda functions (only ALB can), and the asynchronous batch pattern with where-to-send-results fits a queue, not a synchronous load balancer; Lambda also struggles with loading 1 GB of model data and large batches.

✗ An ALB fronting ECS does not match the asynchronous queue-driven request pattern, and AWS App Mesh is a service mesh for traffic routing/observability, not an autoscaling mechanism based on SQS queue depth, so this design is wrong.

✗ AWS Lambda is invoked by SQS events, but you cannot use AWS Auto Scaling to increase vCPUs of a Lambda based on queue size, and Lambda's 15-minute limit, memory ceiling, and 1 GB model load per cold start make it a poor fit for thousands of requests and large model data.

✓ Decoupling requests through SQS and running models as ECS services that scale both the service tasks and the cluster based on queue depth correctly handles irregular usage (scale to zero/low when idle, scale out for thousands of requests) while keeping the 1 GB model loaded in long-lived containers.

text: A solutions architect wants to use the following JSON text as an identity-based policy to grant specific permissions: Which IAM principals can the solutions architect attach this policy to? (Choose two.)
options: A. Role
B. Group
C. Organization
D. Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) resource
E. Amazon EC2 resource
optionExplanations: ✓ An IAM role is a principal to which an identity-based policy can be attached.
✓ An IAM group is a principal to which an identity-based policy can be attached (applying to all users in the group).
✗ An AWS Organization is not an IAM principal; identity-based policies cannot be attached to it (organizations use service control policies, which are a different mechanism).
✗ An Amazon ECS resource is not an IAM identity principal; identity-based policies attach to users, groups, and roles, not to ECS resources.
✗ An Amazon EC2 resource is not an IAM identity principal; identity-based policies attach to users, groups, and roles, not to EC2 resources.

text: A company is running a custom application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. The application has frontend nodes that need to run 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and backend nodes that need to run only for a short time based on workload. The number of backend nodes varies during the day. The company needs to scale out and scale in more instances based on workload. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.
B. Use Reserved Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Spot Instances for the backend nodes.
C. Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use Reserved Instances for the backend nodes.
D. Use Spot Instances for the frontend nodes. Use AWS Fargate for the backend nodes.
optionExplanations: ✗ Reserved Instances correctly cover the steady 24/7 frontend, but AWS Fargate for short, variable backend tasks is more expensive than Spot Instances and is not the most cost-effective choice for fault-tolerant, interruptible backend work.

✓ Reserved Instances give the largest discount for the always-on frontend nodes, and Spot Instances are the cheapest option for the short-lived, variable, interruption-tolerant backend nodes, minimizing total cost.

✗ Spot Instances are inappropriate for frontend nodes that must run 24/7 because they can be interrupted at any time, and Reserved Instances are wasteful for backend nodes that run only briefly and variably.

✗ Spot Instances are unsuitable for always-on frontend nodes due to possible interruptions, and Fargate for the bursty backend is costlier than Spot, so this is not the most cost-effective combination.

text: A company uses high block storage capacity to runs its workloads on premises. The company's daily peak input and output transactions per second are not more than 15,000 IOPS. The company wants to migrate the workloads to Amazon EC2 and to provision disk performance independent of storage capacity. Which Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume type will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. GP2 volume type
B. io2 volume type
C. GP3 volume type
D. io1 volume type
optionExplanations: ✗ GP2 IOPS scale with volume size (3 IOPS/GB) rather than being provisioned independently of capacity, so achieving up to 15,000 IOPS forces a large, more expensive volume.
✗ io2 lets you provision IOPS independently of size but is a high-end, higher-cost Provisioned IOPS SSD; for a workload capped at 15,000 IOPS it is not the most cost-effective choice.
✓ GP3 lets you provision IOPS (up to 16,000) independently of storage capacity at a lower price point than io1/io2, fully covering the 15,000 IOPS peak most cost-effectively.
✗ io1 provisions IOPS independently of size but is a premium Provisioned IOPS SSD priced higher than GP3, so it is not the most cost-effective option for a 15,000 IOPS requirement.

text: A company needs to store data from its healthcare application. The application’s data frequently changes. A new regulation requires audit access at all levels of the stored data. The company hosts the application on an on-premises infrastructure that is running out of storage capacity. A solutions architect must securely migrate the existing data to AWS while satisfying the new regulation. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS DataSync to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log data events.
B. Use AWS Snowcone to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log management events.
C. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log data events.
D. Use AWS Storage Gateway to move the existing data to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to log management events.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS DataSync efficiently and securely migrates the frequently changing on-premises data to Amazon S3, and enabling AWS CloudTrail data events logs object-level (data-level) access required to satisfy the audit-at-all-levels regulation.

✗ AWS Snowcone is an offline edge transfer device that is impractical for frequently changing data needing fast migration, and CloudTrail management events only log control-plane actions, not the object-level data access the regulation requires.

✗ S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads but is not a managed migration tool for existing on-premises datasets, and although it pairs with CloudTrail data events, DataSync is the appropriate migration mechanism here.

✗ AWS Storage Gateway is for ongoing hybrid storage access rather than a one-time secure migration of existing data, and CloudTrail management events do not capture the object-level data access the audit requirement demands.

text: A solutions architect is implementing a complex Java application with a MySQL database. The Java application must be deployed on Apache Tomcat and must be highly available. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy the application in AWS Lambda. Configure an Amazon API Gateway API to connect with the Lambda functions.
B. Deploy the application by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Configure a load-balanced environment and a rolling deployment policy.
C. Migrate the database to Amazon ElastiCache. Configure the ElastiCache security group to allow access from the application.

D. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Install a MySQL server on the EC2 instance. Configure the application on the server. Create an AMI. Use the AMI to create a launch template with an Auto Scaling group.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Lambda with API Gateway does not run a complex Java application on Apache Tomcat (a long-running servlet container) and would require a major re-architecture, so it does not meet the requirement.

✓ AWS Elastic Beanstalk natively supports Tomcat for Java applications, and configuring a load-balanced (multi-instance, multi-AZ) environment with a rolling deployment policy delivers the required high availability with minimal effort.
✗ Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, not a relational database, so it cannot replace the MySQL database, and this option does nothing to deploy the Tomcat application with high availability.

✗ A single EC2 instance with a locally installed MySQL server is not highly available for the database, and baking everything into one AMI behind an Auto Scaling group creates inconsistent, non-shared databases across instances.

text: A serverless application uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. The Lambda function needs permissions to read and write to the DynamoDB table. Which solution will give the Lambda function access to the DynamoDB table MOST securely?
options: A. Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters as part of the Lambda environment variables. Ensure that other AWS users do not have read and write access to the Lambda function configuration.

B. Create an IAM role that includes Lambda as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Update the configuration of the Lambda function to use the new role as the execution role.

C. Create an IAM user with programmatic access to the Lambda function. Attach a policy to the user that allows read and write access to the DynamoDB table. Store the access_key_id and secret_access_key parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as secure string parameters. Update the Lambda function code to retrieve the secure string parameters before connecting to the DynamoDB table.

D. Create an IAM role that includes DynamoDB as a trusted service. Attach a policy to the role that allows read and write access from the Lambda function. Update the code of the Lambda function to attach to the new role as an execution role.
optionExplanations: ✗ Storing long-lived IAM user access keys in Lambda environment variables embeds static credentials that can leak and must be rotated manually, which is far less secure than role-based access.

✓ Creating an IAM role that trusts the Lambda service and granting it DynamoDB read/write, then using it as the function's execution role, provides temporary auto-rotated credentials with no stored secrets, the most secure AWS-recommended pattern.
✗ Using IAM user access keys even when stored in Parameter Store still relies on long-lived static credentials and adds retrieval complexity, making it less secure than a Lambda execution role.
✗ An IAM role's trust policy must trust the Lambda service (not DynamoDB) for Lambda to assume it; trusting DynamoDB is incorrect, so this role could not be assumed as the function's execution role.

text: The following IAM policy is attached to an IAM group. This is the only policy applied to the group. What are the effective IAM permissions of this policy for group members?
options: A. Group members are permitted any Amazon EC2 action within the us-east-1 Region. Statements after the Allow permission are not applied.
B. Group members are denied any Amazon EC2 permissions in the us-east-1 Region unless they are logged in with multi-factor authentication (MFA).

C. Group members are allowed the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances permissions for all Regions when logged in with multi- factor authentication (MFA). Group members are permitted any other Amazon EC2 action.

D. Group members are allowed the ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances permissions for the us-east-1 Region only when logged in with multi-factor authentication (MFA). Group members are permitted any other Amazon EC2 action within the us-east-1 Region.
optionExplanations: ✗ IAM evaluates all statements and an explicit Deny always overrides an Allow, so statements after the Allow are still applied; this description of evaluation order is wrong.
✗ The policy does not deny all EC2 actions without MFA; the Allow grants general EC2 access in the Region, and only the conditional Deny restricts specific actions, so this overstates the denial.
✗ The Allow is scoped to the us-east-1 Region, not all Regions, so the permissions are not granted across all Regions as stated.

✓ The policy allows EC2 actions within us-east-1, but the MFA-conditioned explicit Deny removes ec2:StopInstances and ec2:TerminateInstances unless the user is MFA-authenticated, so those two actions require MFA while any other EC2 action in us-east-1 remains permitted.

text: A manufacturing company has machine sensors that upload .csv files to an Amazon S3 bucket. These .csv files must be converted into images and must be made available as soon as possible for the automatic generation of graphical reports. The images become irrelevant after 1 month, but the .csv files must be kept to train machine learning (ML) models twice a year. The ML trainings and audits are planned weeks in advance. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
options: A. Launch an Amazon EC2 Spot Instance that downloads the .csv files every hour, generates the image files, and uploads the images to the S3 bucket.
B. Design an AWS Lambda function that converts the .csv files into images and stores the images in the S3 bucket. Invoke the Lambda function when a .csv file is uploaded.

C. Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 1 day after they are uploaded. Expire the image files after 30 days.

D. Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 1 day after they are uploaded. Expire the image files after 30 days.

E. Create S3 Lifecycle rules for .csv files and image files in the S3 bucket. Transition the .csv files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 1 day after they are uploaded. Keep the image files in Reduced Redundancy Storage (RRS).
optionExplanations: ✗ Launching an EC2 Spot Instance that polls hourly adds operational overhead, cannot guarantee 'as soon as possible' availability (up to an hour delay), and Spot interruptions risk failed conversions; it is less cost-effective and slower than event-driven processing.

✓ AWS Lambda triggered by an S3 upload event converts each .csv to an image immediately with no idle compute cost and no servers to manage, meeting the 'as soon as possible' and most cost-effective requirements.

✓ S3 Lifecycle transitions .csv files to S3 Glacier 1 day after upload (cheapest durable storage, and ML trainings/audits are planned weeks in advance so Glacier retrieval times are acceptable) and expires the now-irrelevant image files after 30 days.

✗ S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ and is more expensive than Glacier for files that must be kept long-term and are only accessed twice a year; with weeks of advance notice Glacier is cheaper and durable across multiple AZs, so this is not the MOST cost-effective.
✗ S3 Standard-IA still costs more than Glacier for rarely-accessed archival .csv files, and Reduced Redundancy Storage is deprecated and not cost-effective; this combination is suboptimal.

text: A company has developed a new video game as a web application. The application is in a three-tier architecture in a VPC with Amazon RDS for MySQL in the database layer. Several players will compete concurrently online. The game’s developers want to display a top-10 scoreboard in near- real time and offer the ability to stop and restore the game while preserving the current scores. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Set up an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to cache the scores for the web application to display.
B. Set up an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to compute and cache the scores for the web application to display.
C. Place an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the web application to cache the scoreboard in a section of the application.
D. Create a read replica on Amazon RDS for MySQL to run queries to compute the scoreboard and serve the read trafic to the web application.
optionExplanations: ✗ ElastiCache for Memcached is a simple cache without sorted-set ranking or data persistence, so it cannot efficiently compute a top-10 leaderboard or preserve scores across stop/restore.
✓ ElastiCache for Redis supports sorted sets ideal for computing a near-real-time top-10 scoreboard and offers persistence/snapshots so scores can be preserved when the game is stopped and restored.
✗ Amazon CloudFront caches content at the edge and would serve stale scoreboard data, which is incompatible with near-real-time score updates and does not preserve or compute scores.
✗ An RDS for MySQL read replica adds replication lag and relational query overhead, making it poorly suited for near-real-time leaderboard computation compared to an in-memory Redis sorted set.

text: An ecommerce company wants to use machine learning (ML) algorithms to build and train models. The company will use the models to visualize complex scenarios and to detect trends in customer data. The architecture team wants to integrate its ML models with a reporting platform to analyze the augmented data and use the data directly in its business intelligence dashboards. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use AWS Glue to create an ML transform to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
B. Use Amazon SageMaker to build and train models. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
C. Use a pre-built ML Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the AWS Marketplace to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
D. Use Amazon QuickSight to build and train models by using calculated fields. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Glue ML transforms are limited mainly to record matching/deduplication rather than general model building and trend visualization, and OpenSearch Service is a search/analytics engine that adds operational overhead and is not a native BI dashboard for augmented data.

✓ Amazon SageMaker is the managed service for building and training ML models with minimal operational overhead, and Amazon QuickSight integrates ML insights directly into business intelligence dashboards, giving the lowest-overhead end-to-end solution.
✗ Using a pre-built ML AMI from the Marketplace requires managing and patching EC2 infrastructure yourself, increasing operational overhead, and OpenSearch is not the targeted BI dashboard platform.
✗ Amazon QuickSight is a BI/visualization tool and cannot build or train ML models via calculated fields, so it cannot satisfy the model-building requirement.

text: A company is running its production and nonproduction environment workloads in multiple AWS accounts. The accounts are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to design a solution that will prevent the modification of cost usage tags. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a custom AWS Config rule to prevent tag modification except by authorized principals.
B. Create a custom trail in AWS CloudTrail to prevent tag modification.
C. Create a service control policy (SCP) to prevent tag modification except by authorized principals.
D. Create custom Amazon CloudWatch logs to prevent tag modification.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Config detects and evaluates resource configurations and can flag non-compliant tags, but it is reactive and cannot prevent (block) the modification of tags in real time.
✗ AWS CloudTrail only records API activity for auditing; it logs tag modifications after the fact but cannot prevent them.

✓ A service control policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations can explicitly deny tag-modification API actions for everyone except authorized principals, proactively preventing the modification of cost usage tags across member accounts.
✗ Amazon CloudWatch Logs only ingest and store log data for monitoring; they cannot enforce or block tag modifications.

text: A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group and with an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to ensure the application can be made available in anotherAWS Region with minimal downtime. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of downtime?
options: A. Create an Auto Scaling group and a load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.

B. Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, load balancers, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when needed Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.

C. Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and a load balancer to be launched when needed. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.

D. Create an Auto Scaling group and load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to trigger an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 pointing to the disaster recovery load balancer.
optionExplanations: ✓ Pre-provisioning the Auto Scaling group and load balancer in the DR Region (warm standby), using a DynamoDB global table for continuous active-active replication, and configuring Route 53 DNS failover gives the least downtime because the standby infrastructure already exists and failover is near-instant. Correct.

✗ Using CloudFormation to create EC2, ELB, and DynamoDB only when needed means the infrastructure is launched at failover time, adding significant provisioning delay; this also does not replicate existing DynamoDB data. More downtime, so wrong.

✗ CloudFormation launches EC2 and the load balancer on demand, so compute and the ALB are not ready in advance, adding stack-creation startup time before traffic can be served. The global table is good for data, but the on-demand compute increases downtime, so wrong.

✗ Pre-provisioning ASG/ELB and a global table is good, but using a CloudWatch alarm to trigger a Lambda that manually rewrites Route 53 records adds operational complexity and latency compared with Route 53's native health-check failover, making it inferior to option A for least downtime/overhead. Wrong.

text: A company needs to migrate a MySQL database from its on-premises data center to AWS within 2 weeks. The database is 20 TB in size. The company wants to complete the migration with minimal downtime. Which solution will migrate the database MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes. Send the Snowball Edge device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.

B. Order an AWS Snowmobile vehicle. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowmobile vehicle back to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.

C. Order an AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized with GPU device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowball device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication

D. Order a 1 GB dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection to establish a connection with the data center. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes.
optionExplanations: ✓ A Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device efficiently ships the 20 TB bulk load offline while DMS with SCT replicates ongoing changes for minimal downtime, which is the most cost-effective approach within the 2-week window.
✗ AWS Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale (up to 100 PB) truck intended for massive datacenter migrations; it is vastly oversized and far too costly for only 20 TB.
✗ The Snowball Edge Compute Optimized with GPU device is designed for edge compute/ML workloads, not bulk data transfer, and is more expensive than the Storage Optimized device for this migration.
✗ A 1 Gbps Direct Connect link takes weeks to provision and would transfer 20 TB slowly; it cannot reliably meet the 2-week deadline and adds recurring connection cost, making it less cost-effective.

text: A company moved its on-premises PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company successfully launched a new product. The workload on the database has increased. The company wants to accommodate the larger workload without adding infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Buy reserved DB instances for the total workload. Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance larger.
B. Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance a Multi-AZ DB instance.
C. Buy reserved DB instances for the total workload. Add another Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance.
D. Make the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance an on-demand DB instance.
optionExplanations: ✓ Buying Reserved DB Instances for the steady workload and scaling up to a larger instance class accommodates the increased load on the existing single instance without adding infrastructure, at the lowest cost via the RI discount.

✗ Converting to Multi-AZ adds a standby replica for high availability but the standby does not serve read/write traffic, so it does not increase capacity for the larger workload and roughly doubles cost.
✗ Adding another RDS PostgreSQL DB instance adds infrastructure, which the requirement explicitly prohibits.
✗ Switching to on-demand pricing increases cost compared to reserved instances and by itself adds no capacity to handle the larger workload.

text: A company operates an ecommerce website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in an Auto Scaling group. The site is experiencing performance issues related to a high request rate from illegitimate external systems with changing IP addresses. The security team is worried about potential DDoS attacks against the website. The company must block the illegitimate incoming requests in a way that has a minimal impact on legitimate users. What should a solutions architect recommend?
options: A. Deploy Amazon Inspector and associate it with the ALB.
B. Deploy AWS WAF, associate it with the ALB, and configure a rate-limiting rule.
C. Deploy rules to the network ACLs associated with the ALB to block the incomingtrafic.
D. Deploy Amazon GuardDuty and enable rate-limiting protection when configuring GuardDuty.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Inspector assesses EC2/workload vulnerabilities and cannot be associated with an ALB to block incoming requests.

✓ AWS WAF associated with the ALB with a rate-based (rate-limiting) rule blocks high-rate illegitimate requests from changing IPs while allowing normal legitimate traffic, providing layer-7 DDoS mitigation with minimal user impact.
✗ Network ACLs are stateless IP/CIDR filters and cannot effectively block attackers whose source IP addresses constantly change, and manually managing them does not scale.
✗ Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service that generates findings; it has no rate-limiting protection feature and cannot block requests at the ALB.

text: A company wants to share accounting data with an external auditor. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS DB instance that resides in a private subnet. The auditor has its own AWS account and requires its own copy of the database. What is the MOST secure way for the company to share the database with the auditor?
options: A. Create a read replica of the database. Configure IAM standard database authentication to grant the auditor access.
B. Export the database contents to text files. Store the files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create a new IAM user for the auditor. Grant the user access to the S3 bucket.
C. Copy a snapshot of the database to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an IAM user. Share the user's keys with the auditor to grant access to the object in the S3 bucket.
D. Create an encrypted snapshot of the database. Share the snapshot with the auditor. Allow access to the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key.
optionExplanations: ✗ A read replica stays within the company's environment and cannot be handed to a separate AWS account as the auditor's own copy; standard database authentication also does not grant cross-account ownership securely.
✗ Exporting to plain text files in S3 and granting an IAM user access exposes the data in unencrypted, ad hoc form and is far less secure than sharing an encrypted snapshot directly.
✗ Sharing an IAM user's access keys with an external party is a major security anti-pattern and the snapshot would need a proper export; this is the least secure option.
✓ Creating an encrypted RDS snapshot, sharing it with the auditor's account, and granting access to the KMS key lets the auditor create their own copy securely with encryption preserved end to end.

text: A solutions architect configured a VPC that has a small range of IP addresses. The number of Amazon EC2 instances that are in the VPC is increasing, and there is an insuficient number of IP addresses for future workloads. Which solution resolves this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Add an additional IPv4 CIDR block to increase the number of IP addresses and create additional subnets in the VPC. Create new resources in the new subnets by using the new CIDR.
B. Create a second VPC with additional subnets. Use a peering connection to connect the second VPC with the first VPC Update the routes and create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
C. Use AWS Transit Gateway to add a transit gateway and connect a second VPC with the first VPUpdate the routes of the transit gateway and VPCs. Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.

D. Create a second VPC. Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the first VPC and the second VPC by using a VPN-hosted solution on Amazon EC2 and a virtual private gateway. Update the route between VPCs to the trafic through the VPN. Create new resources in the subnets of the second VPC.
optionExplanations: ✓ Adding a secondary IPv4 CIDR block to the existing VPC and creating new subnets immediately expands the available IP space and lets new resources launch in the same VPC with the least operational overhead.
✗ Creating a second VPC with peering solves the address shortage but adds another VPC, peering connection, and route management, which is more operational overhead than simply extending the CIDR.
✗ Using Transit Gateway to connect a second VPC introduces an additional managed networking component and ongoing cost, far more overhead than adding a CIDR block.
✗ Building a self-managed EC2-based Site-to-Site VPN between two VPCs is highly complex, adds maintenance and a single point of failure, and is the most operationally burdensome option.

text: A company used an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance during application testing. Before terminating the DB instance at the end of the test cycle, a solutions architect created two backups. The solutions architect created the first backup by using the mysqldump utility to create a database dump. The solutions architect created the second backup by enabling the final DB snapshot option on RDS termination. The company is now planning for a new test cycle and wants to create a new DB instance from the most recent backup. The company has chosen a MySQL-compatible edition ofAmazon Aurora to host the DB instance. Which solutions will create the new DB instance? (Choose two.)
options: A. Import the RDS snapshot directly into Aurora.
B. Upload the RDS snapshot to Amazon S3. Then import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
C. Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then import the database dump into Aurora.
D. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
E. Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the database dump into Aurora.
optionExplanations: ✓ An RDS for MySQL DB snapshot can be migrated/restored directly to an Aurora MySQL-compatible DB cluster; Aurora natively supports creating a new cluster from an existing RDS MySQL snapshot without intermediate steps.

✗ Restoring an RDS snapshot to Aurora does not require uploading the snapshot to S3 first; RDS snapshots are managed objects you cannot manually upload to S3, and the direct snapshot-to-Aurora migration path makes this unnecessary.
✓ A mysqldump output file can be uploaded to Amazon S3 and imported into Aurora MySQL using the supported S3-based bulk import (LOAD/migration) process to create the new cluster's data.
✗ AWS DMS migrates data between live source and target databases; it does not consume an RDS snapshot as an input. A snapshot is restored, not imported via DMS.
✗ AWS DMS migrates data from a live database endpoint, not from a static mysqldump file sitting in S3; DMS cannot use an S3 SQL dump file as a MySQL source for this import.

text: A company hosts a multi-tier web application on Amazon Linux Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The company observes that the Auto Scaling group launches more On-Demand Instances when the application's end users access high volumes of static web content. The company wants to optimize cost. What should a solutions architect do to redesign the application MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Update the Auto Scaling group to use Reserved Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
B. Update the Auto Scaling group to scale by launching Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
C. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to host the static web contents from an Amazon S3 bucket.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function behind an Amazon API Gateway API to host the static website contents.
optionExplanations: ✗ Switching the Auto Scaling group to Reserved Instances reduces per-instance price but still scales out EC2 capacity to serve static content, which is far less cost-effective than offloading static delivery.
✗ Using Spot Instances lowers compute cost but the instances can be interrupted and you still serve static content from EC2 rather than eliminating the unnecessary scaling.

✓ Serving the static web content from an Amazon S3 bucket fronted by Amazon CloudFront offloads that traffic from EC2, stops the Auto Scaling group from launching extra instances, and caches content near users at the lowest cost.
✗ Rebuilding static content delivery on Lambda behind API Gateway is unnecessary and not designed for serving static assets; it adds complexity and per-request cost rather than caching static files.

text: A company stores several petabytes of data across multiple AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Lake Formation to manage its data lake. The company's data science team wants to securely share selective data from its accounts with the company's engineering team for analytical purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Copy the required data to a common account. Create an IAM access role in that account. Grant access by specifying a permission policy that includes users from the engineering team accounts as trusted entities.
B. Use the Lake Formation permissions Grant command in each account where the data is stored to allow the required engineering team users to access the data.
C. Use AWS Data Exchange to privately publish the required data to the required engineering team accounts.
D. Use Lake Formation tag-based access control to authorize and grant cross-account permissions for the required data to the engineering team accounts.
optionExplanations: ✗ Copying petabytes of data into a common account duplicates massive amounts of storage and requires ongoing sync, which is high cost and operational overhead.
✗ Running individual Lake Formation Grant commands in each account for each user is manual and does not scale across many accounts and datasets, increasing operational overhead.
✗ AWS Data Exchange is designed for publishing/subscribing to third-party data products, not for internal cross-team Lake Formation sharing, and adds unnecessary overhead.

✓ Lake Formation tag-based access control (LF-TBAC) lets you define attribute-based policies and grant cross-account permissions to the engineering team accounts in place, providing scalable, selective sharing with the least operational overhead.

text: A company wants to host a scalable web application on AWS. The application will be accessed by users from different geographic regions of the world. Application users will be able to download and upload unique data up to gigabytes in size. The development team wants a cost-effective solution to minimize upload and download latency and maximize performance. What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?
options: A. Use Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration to host the application.
B. Use Amazon S3 with CacheControl headers to host the application.
C. Use Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling and Amazon CloudFront to host the application.
D. Use Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling and Amazon ElastiCache to host the application.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration routes uploads and downloads through CloudFront edge locations over AWS's optimized backbone, minimizing latency for geographically dispersed users transferring large (gigabyte-scale) unique files. This is the correct, cost-effective, fully managed choice.

✗ S3 with Cache-Control headers only governs how cached objects expire; it does nothing to accelerate cross-region uploads or large-file transfers, and unique data is not cacheable, so it does not meet the latency requirement.

✗ EC2 with Auto Scaling and CloudFront can serve cached content fast, but CloudFront primarily accelerates downloads of cacheable content; uploading unique gigabyte files to EC2-backed storage adds significant operational overhead and cost compared to S3 Transfer Acceleration.

✗ EC2 with Auto Scaling and ElastiCache caches in-memory data within a single region and provides no global edge acceleration for uploading or downloading large unique files, failing the worldwide low-latency requirement.
