text: A company has hired a solutions architect to design a reliable architecture for its application. The application consists of one Amazon RDS DB instance and two manually provisioned Amazon EC2 instances that run web servers. The EC2 instances are located in a single Availability Zone. An employee recently deleted the DB instance, and the application was unavailable for 24 hours as a result. The company is concerned with the overall reliability of its environment. What should the solutions architect do to maximize reliability of the application's infrastructure?
options: A. Delete one EC2 instance and enable termination protection on the other EC2 instance. Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.

B. Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection. Place the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer, and run them in an EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones.

C. Create an additional DB instance along with an Amazon API Gateway and an AWS Lambda function. Configure the application to invoke the Lambda function through API Gateway. Have the Lambda function write the data to the two DB instances.

D. Place the EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group that has multiple subnets located in multiple Availability Zones. Use Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the health of the instances Update the DB instance to be Multi-AZ, and enable deletion protection.
optionExplanations: ✗ Deleting one instance and protecting the other still leaves a single EC2 instance in one AZ with no redundancy or scaling, so it does not maximize reliability.

✓ Making the DB instance Multi-AZ with deletion protection prevents accidental deletion and adds DB failover, while placing the EC2 instances behind an ALB in an Auto Scaling group across multiple AZs provides full multi-AZ redundancy and self-healing for the web tier.

✗ Adding a second DB and a Lambda/API Gateway layer that dual-writes introduces a fragile, non-standard replication pattern and does not address EC2 single-AZ risk, reducing rather than improving reliability.

✗ Using Spot Instances for the web tier risks interruptions that harm availability, and although Multi-AZ DB with deletion protection helps, Spot is inappropriate for a reliability-focused production tier compared to the ALB + standard Auto Scaling design.

text: A company is storing 700 terabytes of data on a large network-attached storage (NAS) system in its corporate data center. The company has a hybrid environment with a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. After an audit from a regulator, the company has 90 days to move the data to the cloud. The company needs to move the data eficiently and without disruption. The company still needs to be able to access and update the data during the transfer window. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS DataSync agent in the corporate data center. Create a data transfer task Start the transfer to an Amazon S3 bucket.
B. Back up the data to AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices. Ship the devices to an AWS data center. Mount a target Amazon S3 bucket on the on-premises file system.
C. Use rsync to copy the data directly from local storage to a designated Amazon S3 bucket over the Direct Connect connection.
D. Back up the data on tapes. Ship the tapes to an AWS data center. Mount a target Amazon S3 bucket on the on-premises file system.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS DataSync with an on-premises agent transfers data efficiently over the 10 Gbps Direct Connect link to S3, supports incremental syncs so the source remains accessible/updatable, and easily completes 700 TB within 90 days.

✗ Wrong: Snowball Edge could move the data offline, but the step 'mount a target S3 bucket on the on-premises file system' is invalid (S3 is not mountable that way) and shipping disrupts/complicates ongoing access and updates.
✗ Wrong: rsync cannot copy directly to an S3 bucket because S3 is object storage, not a POSIX filesystem; this is not a supported native operation.
✗ Wrong: Physical tape shipment is slow, error-prone, and the 'mount an S3 bucket on the file system' step is invalid; it does not support continued access/updates during transfer.

text: A company stores data in PDF format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must follow a legal requirement to retain all new and existing data in Amazon S3 for 7 years. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Turn on the S3 Versioning feature for the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Lifecycle to delete the data after 7 years. Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete for all S3 objects.
B. Turn on S3 Object Lock with governance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
C. Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Recopy all existing objects to bring the existing data into compliance.
D. Turn on S3 Object Lock with compliance retention mode for the S3 bucket. Set the retention period to expire after 7 years. Use S3 Batch Operations to bring the existing data into compliance.
optionExplanations: ✗ S3 Versioning plus Lifecycle deletion plus MFA delete does not enforce a legal retention guarantee; data could still be deleted, and managing MFA delete adds operational overhead. It does not satisfy a compliance retention requirement.

✗ S3 Object Lock in governance mode lets privileged users (with special permissions) override or remove the lock, so it does not meet a strict legal 7-year retention requirement. Also, recopying all existing objects manually is high operational overhead.

✗ Compliance mode correctly enforces immutable retention that no one, including the root account, can override, satisfying the legal requirement. However, manually recopying all existing objects is high operational overhead, making this not the LEAST-overhead choice.

✓ Compliance mode enforces a non-overridable 7-year retention lock meeting the legal requirement, and S3 Batch Operations applies the lock to existing objects at scale automatically, giving the least operational overhead.

text: A company has a stateless web application that runs on AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by Amazon API Gateway. The company wants to deploy the application across multiple AWS Regions to provide Regional failover capabilities. What should a solutions architect do to route trafic to multiple Regions?
options: A. Create Amazon Route 53 health checks for each Region. Use an active-active failover configuration.
B. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin for each Region. Use CloudFront health checks to route trafic.
C. Create a transit gateway. Attach the transit gateway to the API Gateway endpoint in each Region. Configure the transit gateway to route requests.
D. Create an Application Load Balancer in the primary Region. Set the target group to point to the API Gateway endpoint hostnames in each Region.
optionExplanations: ✓ Route 53 health checks per Region with a failover (or active-active) routing policy detect Regional health and route traffic to healthy Regional API Gateway endpoints, providing the desired Regional failover.

✗ Wrong: CloudFront supports origin failover via origin groups but does not perform 'CloudFront health checks' to route across Regional origins in the manner described; Route 53 is the standard DNS-level multi-Region failover mechanism.
✗ Wrong: Transit Gateway connects VPCs/on-premises networks within routing domains; it does not attach to API Gateway endpoints or perform internet-facing request routing/failover.

✗ Wrong: An ALB cannot use cross-Region API Gateway hostnames as targets in a way that provides Regional failover; ALB targets are instances/IPs/Lambda within supported scopes, and this is a single-Region resource.

text: A company has two VPCs named Management and Production. The Management VPC uses VPNs through a customer gateway to connect to a single device in the data center. The Production VPC uses a virtual private gateway with two attached AWS Direct Connect connections. The Management and Production VPCs both use a single VPC peering connection to allow communication between the applications. What should a solutions architect do to mitigate any single point of failure in this architecture?
options: A. Add a set of VPNs between the Management and Production VPCs.
B. Add a second virtual private gateway and attach it to the Management VPC.
C. Add a second set of VPNs to the Management VPC from a second customer gateway device.
D. Add a second VPC peering connection between the Management VPC and the Production VPC.
optionExplanations: ✗ Adding VPNs between the Management and Production VPCs does not address the actual single point of failure, which is the single customer gateway device connecting the Management VPC to the data center; inter-VPC traffic already flows over the peering connection.

✗ A virtual private gateway is the AWS-side endpoint for VPN/Direct Connect; the Management VPC's weakness is the single on-premises customer gateway device, not the AWS-side gateway, and a VPC can have only one VGW, so this does not remove the SPOF.

✓ the Management VPC connects to the data center through VPNs terminating on a single customer gateway device, which is the single point of failure; adding a second set of VPNs from a second customer gateway device provides redundant tunnels and removes that SPOF.

✗ AWS does not permit a second VPC peering connection between the same pair of VPCs, and VPC peering is built on redundant, highly available AWS infrastructure, so this neither is possible nor addresses the customer gateway SPOF.

text: A company runs its application on an Oracle database. The company plans to quickly migrate to AWS because of limited resources for the database, backup administration, and data center maintenance. The application uses third-party database features that require privileged access. Which solution will help the company migrate the database to AWS MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Replace third-party features with cloud services.
B. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
C. Migrate the database to an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) for Oracle. Customize the database settings to support third-party features.
D. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL by rewriting the application code to remove dependency on Oracle APEX.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: RDS for Oracle does not grant the privileged/OS-level access required by the third-party features, and replacing those features adds significant effort, conflicting with the quick, low-effort migration goal.

✓ RDS Custom for Oracle provides managed backups and maintenance while granting privileged access to the OS and database, allowing the third-party features that require elevated access to keep working with minimal rework.
✗ Wrong: Self-managing Oracle on an EC2 AMI gives full access but reverts backup, patching, and maintenance burden back to the company, which is the opposite of reducing administrative resources.
✗ Wrong: Migrating to RDS for PostgreSQL requires rewriting application code and removing Oracle dependencies, which is a slow, high-effort path, not a quick cost-effective migration.

text: A company has a three-tier web application that is in a single server. The company wants to migrate the application to the AWS Cloud. The company also wants the application to align with the AWS Well-Architected Framework and to be consistent with AWS recommended best practices for security, scalability, and resiliency. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)
options: A. Create a VPC across two Availability Zones with the application's existing architecture. Host the application with existing architecture on an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet in each Availability Zone with EC2 Auto Scaling groups. Secure the EC2 instance with security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs).
B. Set up security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs) to control access to the database layer. Set up a single Amazon RDS database in a private subnet.

C. Create a VPC across two Availability Zones. Refactor the application to host the web tier, application tier, and database tier. Host each tier on its own private subnet with Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and application tier.
D. Use a single Amazon RDS database. Allow database access only from the application tier security group.
E. Use Elastic Load Balancers in front of the web tier. Control access by using security groups containing references to each layer's security groups.
F. Use an Amazon RDS database Multi-AZ cluster deployment in private subnets. Allow database access only from application tier security groups.
optionExplanations: ✗ Hosting the application with its existing (monolithic single-server) architecture on EC2 does not refactor it into proper separated tiers, conflicting with the three-tier best-practice and Well-Architected design; incorrect.
✗ A single Amazon RDS database in a private subnet provides no resiliency because it is not Multi-AZ; a single-instance database fails the availability/resiliency goal; incorrect.

✓ Refactoring into separate web, application, and database tiers, each in its own private subnet across two AZs with Auto Scaling on the web and app tiers, properly separates concerns and provides scalability, security, and resiliency; correct.
✗ A single Amazon RDS database, even when scoped to the application tier security group, lacks Multi-AZ resiliency and is inferior to the Multi-AZ option; incorrect.
✓ Placing Elastic Load Balancers in front of the web tier and using security groups that reference each layer's security groups gives scalable, secure layered access control; correct.

✓ An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ cluster deployment in private subnets with access restricted to the application tier security groups delivers the required resiliency and security for the database layer; correct.

text: A company is migrating its applications and databases to the AWS Cloud. The company will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), AWS Direct Connect, and Amazon RDS. Which activities will be managed by the company's operational team? (Choose three.)
options: A. Management of the Amazon RDS infrastructure layer, operating system, and platforms
B. Creation of an Amazon RDS DB instance and configuring the scheduled maintenance window
C. Configuration of additional software components on Amazon ECS for monitoring, patch management, log management, and host intrusion detection
D. Installation of patches for all minor and major database versions for Amazon RDS
E. Ensure the physical security of the Amazon RDS infrastructure in the data center
F. Encryption of the data that moves in transit through Direct Connect
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. For Amazon RDS, AWS (not the customer) manages the underlying infrastructure layer, the host operating system, and the database platform under the shared responsibility model.
✓ Creating an RDS DB instance and configuring its scheduled maintenance window are customer-controlled actions performed via the AWS console/API.
✓ On Amazon ECS the customer is responsible for the guest-level software they add, such as monitoring agents, patch/log management, and host intrusion detection on tasks/instances they control.
✗ Wrong. AWS performs minor and major RDS database engine patching as the managed-service provider; the customer only schedules/approves it, not installs it.
✗ Wrong. Physical security of the data centers hosting RDS infrastructure is AWS's responsibility (security 'of' the cloud).
✓ AWS Direct Connect traffic is not encrypted by default, so the customer is responsible for encrypting data in transit (e.g., via a VPN/IPsec or application-layer encryption over the DX link).

text: A company runs a Java-based job on an Amazon EC2 instance. The job runs every hour and takes 10 seconds to run. The job runs on a scheduled interval and consumes 1 GB of memory. The CPU utilization of the instance is low except for short surges during which the job uses the maximum CPU available. The company wants to optimize the costs to run the job. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to containerize the job. Run the job as an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task on AWS Fargate with 0.5 virtual CPU (vCPU) and 1 GB of memory.
B. Copy the code into an AWS Lambda function that has 1 GB of memory. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to run the code each hour.
C. Use AWS App2Container (A2C) to containerize the job. Install the container in the existing Amazon Machine Image (AMI). Ensure that the schedule stops the container when the task finishes.
D. Configure the existing schedule to stop the EC2 instance at the completion of the job and restart the EC2 instance when the next job starts.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS App2Container with an ECS task on Fargate works, but Fargate bills for the full provisioned task duration and has minimum per-task overhead; for a 10-second hourly job this leaves resources/cost far higher than a true pay-per-invocation model.

✓ Migrating the Java code to an AWS Lambda function with 1 GB memory and triggering it via an EventBridge scheduled rule is the most cost-optimal: Lambda bills only for the ~10 seconds of execution per hour, requires no idle EC2/instance cost, and easily handles the short CPU surge and 1 GB memory need within the 15-minute limit.

✗ Containerizing with A2C and baking the container into the existing AMI still requires a running EC2 instance to host it, so you keep paying for EC2 (and management overhead) rather than optimizing cost.

✗ Stopping and restarting the EC2 instance around the job avoids some compute cost but still incurs EBS storage charges while stopped, start/stop latency, and operational overhead; it is far less cost-effective than serverless Lambda for a 10-second job.

text: A company wants to implement a backup strategy for Amazon EC2 data and multiple Amazon S3 buckets. Because of regulatory requirements, the company must retain backup files for a specific time period. The company must not alter the files for the duration of the retention period. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in governance mode. Create the required backup plan.
B. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create the required automated snapshot policy.
C. Use Amazon S3 File Gateway to create the backup. Configure the appropriate S3 Lifecycle management.
D. Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault that has a vault lock in compliance mode. Create the required backup plan.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: AWS Backup with a vault lock in governance mode allows privileged users to alter or delete recovery points, so it does not guarantee the files remain unaltered for the regulatory retention period.
✗ Wrong: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager automates EBS snapshots but does not cover S3 buckets and does not provide immutable, regulatory-grade retention locking.
✗ Wrong: S3 File Gateway with lifecycle policies is for hybrid file storage and does not provide immutable, write-once backup retention for EC2 and S3 backups.

✓ AWS Backup with a vault lock in compliance mode makes recovery points immutable for the retention period (no user, including root, can shorten retention or delete them), covering both EC2 and S3 backups.

text: A company has resources across multiple AWS Regions and accounts. A newly hired solutions architect discovers a previous employee did not provide details about the resources inventory. The solutions architect needs to build and map the relationship details of the various workloads across all accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally eficient way?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager Inventory to generate a map view from the detailed view report.
B. Use AWS Step Functions to collect workload details. Build architecture diagrams of the workloads manually.
C. Use Workload Discovery on AWS to generate architecture diagrams of the workloads.
D. Use AWS X-Ray to view the workload details. Build architecture diagrams with relationships.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: Systems Manager Inventory collects metadata about managed instances/software but does not automatically build relationship maps/architecture diagrams across multiple accounts and Regions.
✗ Wrong: Step Functions orchestrates workflows but building architecture diagrams manually is highly operationally inefficient and not its purpose.

✓ Workload Discovery on AWS automatically discovers resources across accounts and Regions and generates architecture diagrams that map workload relationships, meeting the requirement most efficiently.
✗ Wrong: AWS X-Ray traces application request flows for distributed tracing/debugging; it does not inventory and map all resource relationships across accounts and Regions.

text: A company uses AWS Organizations. The company wants to operate some of its AWS accounts with different budgets. The company wants to receive alerts and automatically prevent provisioning of additional resources on AWS accounts when the allocated budget threshold is met during a specific period. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)
options: A. Use AWS Budgets to create a budget. Set the budget amount under the Cost and Usage Reports section of the required AWS accounts.
B. Use AWS Budgets to create a budget. Set the budget amount under the Billing dashboards of the required AWS accounts.
C. Create an IAM user for AWS Budgets to run budget actions with the required permissions.
D. Create an IAM role for AWS Budgets to run budget actions with the required permissions.

E. Add an alert to notify the company when each account meets its budget threshold. Add a budget action that selects the IAM identity created with the appropriate config rule to prevent provisioning of additional resources.

F. Add an alert to notify the company when each account meets its budget threshold. Add a budget action that selects the IAM identity created with the appropriate service control policy (SCP) to prevent provisioning of additional resources.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Budgets is the correct service, but you do not set a budget amount under the Cost and Usage Reports section; Cost and Usage Reports deliver detailed billing data files and are not where budgets are defined.
✓ AWS Budgets is created and the budget amount is set from the Billing/Budgets dashboard for the required accounts, which is the proper place to define spend thresholds.
✗ AWS Budgets actions are executed by an IAM role that Budgets assumes, not by an IAM user; a user is not the right identity for automated budget actions.
✓ AWS Budgets requires an IAM role with the necessary permissions so Budgets can assume it and run budget actions when a threshold is reached.
✗ an AWS Config rule evaluates and reports compliance but cannot block resource provisioning when a budget threshold is met, so this does not satisfy the prevention requirement.
✓ a budget action can attach a service control policy (SCP) via AWS Organizations to deny further resource provisioning, combined with an alert to notify the company when the threshold is met.

text: A company runs applications on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The company wants to back up the EC2 instances to a second Region. The company also wants to provision EC2 resources in the second Region and manage the EC2 instances centrally from one AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Create a disaster recovery (DR) plan that has a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Configure data replication.
B. Create point-in-time Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the EC2 instances. Copy the snapshots to the second Region periodically.
C. Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup. Configure cross-Region backup to the second Region for the EC2 instances.
D. Deploy a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data from the source Region to the second Region.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong: Standing up a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region with data replication is a full DR (warm/pilot) setup that incurs ongoing compute costs, far more expensive than just backing up.
✗ Wrong: Manually creating and copying EBS snapshots cross-Region is more operationally intensive and does not provide the centralized, policy-driven management that AWS Backup offers.

✓ AWS Backup with a cross-Region backup plan backs up the EC2 instances to the second Region and provides centralized, policy-based management from one account most cost-effectively (no idle running instances).
✗ Wrong: Deploying duplicate running EC2 instances and using DataSync incurs ongoing compute costs and extra complexity, which is not the most cost-effective backup approach.

text: A company that uses AWS is building an application to transfer data to a product manufacturer. The company has its own identity provider (IdP). The company wants the IdP to authenticate application users while the users use the application to transfer data. The company must use Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) protocol. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
B. Use Amazon AppFlow fiows to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task for IdP authentication.
C. Use AWS Transfer Family to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
D. Use AWS Storage Gateway to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool for IdP authentication.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS DataSync moves data between storage systems but does not support the AS2 protocol, so it cannot meet the AS2 requirement.
✗ Amazon AppFlow integrates SaaS applications, not AS2 file transfers; it does not support the AS2 protocol.
✓ AWS Transfer Family natively supports the AS2 protocol for B2B data exchange and can use a Lambda function as a custom identity provider to authenticate users against the company's own IdP.
✗ AWS Storage Gateway provides hybrid storage access (file/volume/tape), not AS2-based application data transfer, so it does not meet the requirement.

text: A solutions architect is designing a RESTAPI in Amazon API Gateway for a cash payback service. The application requires 1 GB of memory and 2 GB of storage for its computation resources. The application will require that the data is in a relational format. Which additional combination ofAWS services will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort? (Choose two.)
options: A. Amazon EC2
B. AWS Lambda
C. Amazon RDS
D. Amazon DynamoDB
E. Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Services (Amazon EKS)
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon EC2 provides virtual servers but requires you to manage the OS, patching, scaling, and capacity, which is far more administrative effort than a serverless option for these modest compute needs.

✓ AWS Lambda is serverless and can be configured with up to 10 GB of memory and up to 10 GB of ephemeral storage, easily satisfying the 1 GB memory / 2 GB storage requirement with no servers to manage, making it the least-effort compute choice for an API Gateway backend.
✓ Amazon RDS is a fully managed relational database service (handling patching, backups, and failover), satisfying the relational data format requirement with minimal administrative effort.
✗ Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL key-value/document database and does not provide a relational data format, so it fails the requirement.
✗ Amazon EKS is a managed Kubernetes service that still requires significant operational effort to manage clusters, nodes, and containers, far more than the serverless Lambda option.

text: A company uses AWS Organizations to run workloads within multiple AWS accounts. A tagging policy adds department tags to AWS resources when the company creates tags. An accounting team needs to determine spending on Amazon EC2 consumption. The accounting team must determine which departments are responsible for the costs regardless ofAWS account. The accounting team has access to AWS Cost Explorer for all AWS accounts within the organization and needs to access all reports from Cost Explorer. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally eficient way?
options: A. From the Organizations management account billing console, activate a user-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.

B. From the Organizations management account billing console, activate an AWS-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.

C. From the Organizations member account billing console, activate a user-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by the tag name, and filter by EC2.

D. From the Organizations member account billing console, activate an AWS-defined cost allocation tag named department. Create one cost report in Cost Explorer grouping by tag name, and filter by EC2.
optionExplanations: ✓ Cost allocation tags must be activated from the Organizations management (payer) account, and the custom 'department' tag created by the tagging policy is a user-defined tag; grouping by it and filtering by EC2 gives the required cross-account view most efficiently.
✗ The 'department' tag was created by the company, making it a user-defined cost allocation tag, not an AWS-defined tag, so this option mislabels the tag type.
✗ Cost allocation tags cannot be activated from a member account; only the management account can activate them.
✗ Member accounts cannot activate cost allocation tags, and the tag is user-defined rather than AWS-defined, so this option is wrong on both counts.

text: A company wants to securely exchange data between its software as a service (SaaS) application Salesforce account and Amazon S3. The company must encrypt the data at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys (CMKs). The company must also encrypt the data in transit. The company has enabled API access for the Salesforce account.
options: A. Create AWS Lambda functions to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
B. Create an AWS Step Functions workfiow. Define the task to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
C. Create Amazon AppFlow fiows to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
D. Create a custom connector for Salesforce to transfer the data securely from Salesforce to Amazon S3.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Lambda could be coded to transfer the data but requires custom development and maintenance, which is unnecessary given a managed option exists.
✗ AWS Step Functions orchestrates workflows but still requires building custom integration logic to move Salesforce data to S3.

✓ Amazon AppFlow provides a managed, no-code integration with Salesforce, encrypts data in transit, and supports writing to S3 with encryption at rest using KMS customer managed keys, meeting all requirements with the least effort.
✗ Building a custom connector requires significant development and maintenance effort when AppFlow already provides a native Salesforce connector.

text: A company is developing a mobile gaming app in a single AWS Region. The app runs on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The company stores the app data in Amazon DynamoDB. The app communicates by using TCP trafic and UDP trafic between the users and the servers. The application will be used globally. The company wants to ensure the lowest possible latency for all users. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB.

B. Use AWS Global Accelerator to create an accelerator. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind an accelerator endpoint that uses Global Accelerator integration and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB.

C. Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the NLB. Update CloudFront to use the NLB as the origin.

D. Create an Amazon CloudFront content delivery network (CDN) endpoint. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) behind the endpoint and listening on the TCP and UDP ports. Update the Auto Scaling group to register instances on the ALB. Update CloudFront to use the ALB as the origin.
optionExplanations: ✗ An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and does not support UDP or raw TCP traffic, so it cannot handle the app's TCP and UDP requirements.

✓ AWS Global Accelerator routes traffic over the AWS global network for lowest latency to globally distributed users, and a Network Load Balancer supports both TCP and UDP listeners, satisfying all requirements.
✗ CloudFront is a CDN optimized for HTTP/HTTPS content delivery and does not proxy arbitrary TCP/UDP gaming traffic, making it unsuitable here.
✗ CloudFront cannot serve UDP/TCP gaming traffic, and an ALB also lacks UDP support, so this combination fails the requirements.

text: A company has an application that processes customer orders. The company hosts the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that saves the orders to an Amazon Aurora database. Occasionally when trafic is high the workload does not process orders fast enough. What should a solutions architect do to write the orders reliably to the database as quickly as possible?
options: A. Increase the instance size of the EC2 instance when trafic is high. Write orders to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Subscribe the database endpoint to the SNS topic.

B. Write orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SQS queue and process orders into the database.

C. Write orders to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Subscribe the database endpoint to the SNS topic. Use EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SNS topic.

D. Write orders to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue when the EC2 instance reaches CPU threshold limits. Use scheduled scaling of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer to read from the SQS queue and process orders into the database.
optionExplanations: ✗ SNS is a pub/sub notification service and a database endpoint cannot subscribe to an SNS topic, so orders would not reliably reach Aurora.

✓ Writing orders to an SQS queue buffers them durably during traffic spikes, and an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances consuming the queue processes orders into the database reliably as fast as capacity allows.
✗ A database endpoint cannot be an SNS subscriber, so this approach cannot deliver orders to Aurora.
✗ Scheduled scaling reacts on a fixed schedule rather than to actual queue depth, and only queuing on CPU threshold can lose orders, so this is less reliable than dynamic scaling on the queue.

text: An IoT company is releasing a mattress that has sensors to collect data about a user’s sleep. The sensors will send data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The sensors collect approximately 2 MB of data every night for each mattress. The company must process and summarize the data for each mattress. The results need to be available as soon as possible. Data processing will require 1 GB of memory and will finish within 30 seconds. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use AWS Glue with a Scala job
B. Use Amazon EMR with an Apache Spark script
C. Use AWS Lambda with a Python script
D. Use AWS Glue with a PySpark job
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Glue with a Scala job is a serverless Spark ETL service billed per DPU-hour with a 1-minute minimum and Spark cluster startup latency; it is overkill and not cost-effective for a 2 MB, 1 GB, 30-second job.

✗ Amazon EMR with an Apache Spark script requires provisioning and running a cluster, which carries significant cost and operational overhead and is far too heavy for processing only 2 MB of data per mattress.

✓ AWS Lambda with a Python script can be triggered by S3 event notifications for near-real-time processing, supports up to 1 GB+ memory, runs well within the 15-minute (here 30-second) limit, and bills only for the short execution time, making it the most cost-effective and fastest option.

✗ AWS Glue with a PySpark job is the same serverless Spark engine as the Scala option, incurring DPU-hour billing, minimum billing duration, and Spark startup overhead that is not cost-effective for such tiny, short workloads.

text: A company hosts an online shopping application that stores all orders in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instance. Management wants to eliminate single points of failure and has asked a solutions architect to recommend an approach to minimize database downtime without requiring any changes to the application code. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Convert the existing database instance to a Multi-AZ deployment by modifying the database instance and specifying the Multi-AZ option.
B. Create a new RDS Multi-AZ deployment. Take a snapshot of the current RDS instance and restore the new Multi-AZ deployment with the snapshot.
C. Create a read-only replica of the PostgreSQL database in another Availability Zone. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across the databases.
D. Place the RDS for PostgreSQL database in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum group size of two. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted record sets to distribute requests across instances.
optionExplanations: ✓ Modifying the existing RDS instance to enable Multi-AZ adds a synchronous standby in another AZ for automatic failover, eliminating the single point of failure with no application code changes and no manual migration.
✗ Creating a new Multi-AZ deployment and restoring from a snapshot achieves Multi-AZ but is unnecessarily disruptive and would change the endpoint, requiring more effort than a simple modify.
✗ A read replica is for read scaling and is asynchronous; using Route 53 weighted routing does not provide automatic failover and would require application changes to direct writes.
✗ RDS managed instances cannot be placed in an EC2 Auto Scaling group, so this option is technically invalid.

text: A company is developing an application to support customer demands. The company wants to deploy the application on multiple Amazon EC2 Nitro-based instances within the same Availability Zone. The company also wants to give the application the ability to write to multiple block storage volumes in multiple EC2 Nitro-based instances simultaneously to achieve higher application availability. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
B. Use Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
C. Use Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
D. Use General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volumes with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach
optionExplanations: ✗ gp3 volumes do not support EBS Multi-Attach; Multi-Attach is only available on Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) volumes.
✗ Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) volumes do not support EBS Multi-Attach.
✓ Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volumes support EBS Multi-Attach, allowing multiple Nitro-based instances in the same AZ to concurrently read and write to the same volume for higher availability.
✗ gp2 volumes do not support EBS Multi-Attach, so they cannot be attached to multiple instances simultaneously.

text: A company designed a stateless two-tier application that uses Amazon EC2 in a single Availability Zone and an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. New company management wants to ensure the application is highly available. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?
options: A. Configure the application to use Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling and create an Application Load Balancer
B. Configure the application to take snapshots of the EC2 instances and send them to a different AWS Region
C. Configure the application to use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to feed requests to the application
D. Configure Amazon Route 53 rules to handle incoming requests and create a Multi-AZ Application Load Balancer
optionExplanations: ✓ Spreading EC2 instances across multiple AZs with Auto Scaling and fronting them with an Application Load Balancer makes the stateless web tier highly available, complementing the existing Multi-AZ RDS.
✗ Sending EC2 snapshots to another Region is a backup/DR measure and does not provide high availability for a single-AZ application.
✗ Route 53 latency-based routing distributes across Regions or endpoints but does nothing to remove the single-AZ single point of failure for the EC2 tier.
✗ Route 53 rules plus a Multi-AZ ALB do not add multiple EC2 instances across AZs; a load balancer alone without multi-AZ instances behind it does not make the compute tier highly available.

text: A company uses AWS Organizations. A member account has purchased a Compute Savings Plan. Because of changes in the workloads inside the member account, the account no longer receives the full benefit of the Compute Savings Plan commitment. The company uses less than 50% of its purchased compute power.
options: A. Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the member account that purchased the Compute Savings Plan.
B. Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the company's Organizations management account.
C. Migrate additional compute workloads from another AWS account to the account that has the Compute Savings Plan.
D. Sell the excess Savings Plan commitment in the Reserved Instance Marketplace.
optionExplanations: ✗ Discount (RI and Savings Plans) sharing is a billing setting controlled only by the management/payer account, not by a member account. A member account cannot enable organization-wide sharing from its own Billing Preferences, so this does not work.

✓ In AWS Organizations, RI and Savings Plans discount sharing is toggled in the Billing Preferences of the management (payer) account. Enabling it lets the member account's unused Compute Savings Plan benefit be applied to eligible usage in other accounts across the organization, recovering the otherwise-wasted commitment with no migration effort.

✗ Migrating workloads into the account would consume the commitment but is high operational effort, may not be feasible, and is unnecessary because discount sharing already spreads the benefit org-wide automatically.
✗ Savings Plans cannot be sold on the Reserved Instance Marketplace; only Standard Reserved Instances are sellable there. This option is technically impossible for a Compute Savings Plan.

text: A company is developing a microservices application that will provide a search catalog for customers. The company must use REST APIs to present the frontend of the application to users. The REST APIs must access the backend services that the company hosts in containers in private VPC subnets. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.

B. Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a private VPC link for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.

C. Design a WebSocket API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.

D. Design a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway. Host the application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) in a private subnet. Create a security group for API Gateway to access Amazon ECS.
optionExplanations: ✗ WebSocket API is for bidirectional real-time communication, not the REST APIs explicitly required; a private VPC link is correct but the API type is wrong.

✓ A REST API in API Gateway matches the explicit REST requirement, and a private VPC link (with a Network Load Balancer) lets API Gateway securely reach ECS containers in private subnets without exposing them publicly. Correct.
✗ WebSocket API does not satisfy the REST requirement, and API Gateway cannot reach private-subnet ECS via a security group alone; it needs a VPC link. Wrong on both counts.

✗ REST API is correct, but API Gateway cannot connect to ECS in private subnets using just a security group; it requires a private VPC link to integrate with resources in a private VPC. Wrong integration mechanism.

text: A company stores raw collected data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data is used for several types of analytics on behalf of the company's customers. The type of analytics requested determines the access pattern on the S3 objects. The company cannot predict or control the access pattern. The company wants to reduce its S3 costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use S3 replication to transition infrequently accessed objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
B. Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
C. Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
D. Use S3 Inventory to identify and transition objects that have not been accessed from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
optionExplanations: ✗ S3 replication copies objects to another bucket; it is not a mechanism to transition objects to S3 Standard-IA and does not address unpredictable access patterns or cost reduction.

✗ Lifecycle rules to Standard-IA move objects on a fixed schedule, but if an IA object is accessed frequently you incur retrieval fees; this fails when the access pattern is unpredictable and could increase cost.
✓ S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on changing access patterns with no retrieval fees, which is ideal when access is unpredictable and minimizes cost.

✗ S3 Inventory only reports on objects and does not itself transition them; it adds operational overhead and still relies on a manual/scheduled transition rather than automatic adaptation to unpredictable access.

text: A company has applications hosted on Amazon EC2 instances with IPv6 addresses. The applications must initiate communications with other external applications using the internet. However the company’s security policy states that any external service cannot initiate a connection to the EC2 instances. What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?
options: A. Create a NAT gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
B. Create an internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
C. Create a virtual private gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
D. Create an egress-only internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
optionExplanations: ✗ A NAT gateway provides outbound internet access for IPv4 private addresses; it does not support IPv6 traffic, so it cannot serve IPv6-addressed instances.
✗ An internet gateway allows bidirectional traffic, so external services could initiate inbound connections to the instances, violating the security policy.
✗ A virtual private gateway is for connecting a VPC to an on-premises network over VPN/Direct Connect, not for outbound IPv6 internet access.
✓ An egress-only internet gateway allows outbound IPv6 communication from instances while preventing the internet from initiating inbound connections, exactly meeting the requirement.

text: A company is creating an application that runs on containers in a VPC. The application stores and accesses data in an Amazon S3 bucket. During the development phase, the application will store and access 1 TB of data in Amazon S3 each day. The company wants to minimize costs and wants to prevent trafic from traversing the internet whenever possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering for the S3 bucket
B. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for the S3 bucket
C. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC
D. Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC
optionExplanations: ✗ S3 Intelligent-Tiering manages storage tier costs but does nothing to keep traffic off the internet or reduce data transfer routing.
✗ S3 Transfer Acceleration routes traffic over the public internet/CloudFront edge to speed long-distance transfers and adds cost, the opposite of the requirement.
✓ A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 routes traffic to S3 privately over the AWS network at no additional cost, keeping traffic off the internet and minimizing cost.

✗ S3 supports a gateway endpoint, not an interface endpoint associated with route tables for the standard use case; interface endpoints incur hourly and data processing charges, making this both incorrect and more costly.

text: A company has a mobile chat application with a data store based in Amazon DynamoDB. Users would like new messages to be read with as little latency as possible. A solutions architect needs to design an optimal solution that requires minimal application changes. Which method should the solutions architect select?
options: A. Configure Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the new messages table. Update the code to use the DAX endpoint.
B. Add DynamoDB read replicas to handle the increased read load. Update the application to point to the read endpoint for the read replicas.
C. Double the number of read capacity units for the new messages table in DynamoDB. Continue to use the existing DynamoDB endpoint.
D. Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache to the application stack. Update the application to point to the Redis cache endpoint instead of DynamoDB.
optionExplanations: ✓ DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed in-memory cache purpose-built for DynamoDB, delivering microsecond read latency with minimal code changes (point to the DAX endpoint).
✗ DynamoDB does not have a separate read-replica concept with a read endpoint; this is not a valid DynamoDB feature.
✗ Doubling read capacity units increases throughput but does not reduce per-read latency, so it does not meet the low-latency goal.
✗ ElastiCache for Redis could cache reads but requires significant application changes to manage cache population and invalidation, more than the minimal-change DAX solution.

text: A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content. Website trafic is increasing, and the company is concerned about a potential increase in cost.
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache state files at edge locations
B. Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Connect the ALB to the ElastiCache cluster to serve cached files
C. Create an AWS WAF web ACL and associate it with the ALB. Add a rule to the web ACL to cache static files
D. Create a second ALB in an alternative AWS Region. Route user trafic to the closest Region to minimize data transfer costs
optionExplanations: ✓ CloudFront caches static content at edge locations, reducing requests and data transfer from the origin EC2/ALB and lowering cost while improving performance.
✗ ElastiCache is an in-memory database cache for application data; it does not serve cached static web files and an ALB cannot connect to it to serve files.
✗ AWS WAF filters and protects against malicious web traffic; it does not cache static files, so it does not reduce cost from serving content.
✗ A second ALB in another Region adds cost and complexity and does not cache static content, so it does not address the cost concern for static delivery.

text: A company has multiple VPCs across AWS Regions to support and run workloads that are isolated from workloads in other Regions. Because of a recent application launch requirement, the company’s VPCs must communicate with all other VPCs across all Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?
options: A. Use VPC peering to manage VPC communication in a single Region. Use VPC peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
B. Use AWS Direct Connect gateways across all Regions to connect VPCs across regions and manage VPC communications.
C. Use AWS Transit Gateway to manage VPC communication in a single Region and Transit Gateway peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
D. Use AWS PrivateLink across all Regions to connect VPCs across Regions and manage VPC communications
optionExplanations: ✗ VPC peering is non-transitive and requires a full mesh of connections; managing many peerings within and across Regions is high administrative effort.
✗ Direct Connect gateways are for connecting on-premises networks to VPCs over dedicated connections, not for inter-VPC mesh communication across Regions.
✓ Transit Gateway provides hub-and-spoke connectivity within a Region and inter-Region Transit Gateway peering, greatly reducing the number of connections to manage with the least effort.
✗ AWS PrivateLink exposes individual services via endpoints rather than providing full VPC-to-VPC network connectivity, making it unsuitable for general all-to-all VPC communication.

text: A company is designing a containerized application that will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application needs to access a shared file system that is highly durable and can recover data to another AWS Region with a recovery point objective (RPO) of 8 hours. The file system needs to provide a mount target m each Availability Zone within a Region. A solutions architect wants to use AWS Backup to manage the replication to another Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ deployment
B. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with a Multi-AZ deployment
C. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with the Standard storage class
D. Amazon FSx for OpenZFS
optionExplanations: ✗ FSx for Windows File Server is designed for Windows/SMB workloads and is not the standard Linux-container shared file system; AWS Backup cross-Region replication for this scenario points to EFS.

✗ FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports cross-Region replication but typically via SnapMirror/NetApp tooling, and it is more than required; the question specifically calls for AWS Backup managing replication, which fits EFS.
✓ Amazon EFS provides a highly durable shared POSIX file system with a mount target in each AZ, integrates with ECS, and supports AWS Backup with cross-Region copy to meet an 8-hour RPO.
✗ FSx for OpenZFS is single-AZ for its standard deployment and does not provide the multi-AZ mount-target model with AWS Backup cross-Region replication required here.

text: A company is expecting rapid growth in the near future. A solutions architect needs to configure existing users and grant permissions to new users on AWS. The solutions architect has decided to create IAM groups. The solutions architect will add the new users to IAM groups based on department. Which additional action is the MOST secure way to grant permissions to the new users?
options: A. Apply service control policies (SCPs) to manage access permissions
B. Create IAM roles that have least privilege permission. Attach the roles to the IAM groups
C. Create an IAM policy that grants least privilege permission. Attach the policy to the IAM groups
D. Create IAM roles. Associate the roles with a permissions boundary that defines the maximum permissions
optionExplanations: ✗ Service control policies are an AWS Organizations guardrail that sets the maximum allowable permissions across accounts; they do not grant permissions to users and cannot be attached to IAM groups, so they do not solve this requirement.

✗ IAM roles cannot be attached to IAM groups. Roles are assumed by trusted entities (users, services) and are not a mechanism for granting persistent group-based permissions, so this is technically invalid.

✓ You attach an IAM identity-based policy directly to an IAM group, and all members inherit it. Authoring the policy with least privilege is the most secure standard way to grant the new department users their permissions.

✗ IAM roles cannot be associated with IAM groups, and permissions boundaries cap the maximum permissions of an identity rather than granting permissions. This does not fulfill the goal of granting group-based permissions to users.

text: A group requires permissions to list an Amazon S3 bucket and delete objects from that bucket. An administrator has created the following IAM policy to provide access to the bucket and applied that policy to the group. The group is not able to delete objects in the bucket. The company follows least-privilege access rules. Which statement should a solutions architect add to the policy to correct bucket access?
options: A.
B.
C.
D.
optionExplanations: ✓ Assuming this option supplies the s3:DeleteObject action scoped to the bucket's objects (arn .../bucket/*), it grants the missing delete permission while preserving least privilege; selected as the most likely intended correct statement.
✗ Option content is not provided; if it grants overly broad actions like s3:* it would violate least-privilege and would not be the correct minimal fix.
✗ Option content is not provided; if it omits the object-level resource ARN (/*) the DeleteObject permission would not apply to objects, so it would not fix the issue.
✗ Option content is not provided; if it adds permissions unrelated to deleting objects (e.g., bucket-level only) it would not resolve the inability to delete objects.

text: A law firm needs to share information with the public. The information includes hundreds of files that must be publicly readable. Modifications or deletions of the files by anyone before a designated future date are prohibited. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?
options: A. Upload all files to an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for static website hosting. Grant read-only IAM permissions to any AWS principals that access the S3 bucket until the designated date.

B. Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Use S3 Object Lock with a retention period in accordance with the designated date. Configure the S3 bucket for static website hosting. Set an S3 bucket policy to allow read-only access to the objects.

C. Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an event trigger to run an AWS Lambda function in case of object modification or deletion. Configure the Lambda function to replace the objects with the original versions from a private S3 bucket.

D. Upload all files to an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for static website hosting. Select the folder that contains the files. Use S3 Object Lock with a retention period in accordance with the designated date. Grant read-only IAM permissions to any AWS principals that access the S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✗ Upload all files to an S3 bucket configured for static website hosting with read-only IAM permissions provides no immutability; nothing prevents authorized principals from modifying or deleting files before the designated date, so it fails the WORM requirement.

✓ Creating an S3 bucket with Versioning enabled and S3 Object Lock with a retention period (in compliance/governance mode) enforces true WORM immutability, preventing modification or deletion by anyone (including root) until the designated date; static website hosting plus a bucket policy delivers public read access. This is the most secure solution.

✗ S3 Versioning with a Lambda function that restores original versions on modification/deletion is reactive remediation, not prevention; files can still be changed or deleted (even temporarily), and it does not satisfy the requirement to prohibit modifications. It is also more operationally complex.

✗ S3 Object Lock cannot be enabled on an existing bucket or applied to a selected folder after upload; it must be enabled at bucket creation and applies per object. Granting read-only IAM permissions also does not provide public read access to anonymous users, so this fails both the immutability and public-access requirements.

text: A company is making a prototype of the infrastructure for its new website by manually provisioning the necessary infrastructure. This infrastructure includes an Auto Scaling group, an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon RDS database. After the configuration has been thoroughly validated, the company wants the capability to immediately deploy the infrastructure for development and production use in two Availability Zones in an automated fashion. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager to replicate and provision the prototype infrastructure in two Availability Zones
B. Define the infrastructure as a template by using the prototype infrastructure as a guide. Deploy the infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation.
C. Use AWS Config to record the inventory of resources that are used in the prototype infrastructure. Use AWS Config to deploy the prototype infrastructure into two Availability Zones.
D. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk and configure it to use an automated reference to the prototype infrastructure to automatically deploy new environments in two Availability Zones.
optionExplanations: ✗ Systems Manager is for operational management and automation of existing resources, not for defining and repeatably provisioning a full infrastructure stack from a prototype.

✓ Defining the infrastructure as a CloudFormation template lets the company repeatably and automatically deploy the validated stack (ASG, ALB, RDS) across environments and AZs, meeting the requirement.
✗ AWS Config records resource configuration and compliance; it cannot deploy or provision infrastructure.

✗ Elastic Beanstalk deploys and manages applications on standardized environments and cannot directly replicate an arbitrary manually built stack including a specific RDS topology as a reference; CloudFormation is the proper IaC tool.

text: A business application is hosted on Amazon EC2 and uses Amazon S3 for encrypted object storage. The chief information security oficer has directed that no application trafic between the two services should traverse the public internet. Which capability should the solutions architect use to meet the compliance requirements?
options: A. AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
B. VPC endpoint
C. Private subnet
D. Virtual private gateway
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS KMS manages encryption keys but does not control the network path between EC2 and S3, so it cannot keep traffic off the public internet.
✓ A VPC endpoint (gateway endpoint for S3) routes traffic between EC2 and S3 privately over the AWS network, ensuring it never traverses the public internet.
✗ A private subnet alone restricts inbound internet access but instances still reach S3 over the internet via NAT unless an endpoint is used, so it does not by itself meet the requirement.
✗ A virtual private gateway connects a VPC to an on-premises network over VPN/Direct Connect and does not provide private connectivity to S3.

text: A company hosts a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud. A Multi-AZAmazon RDS for MySQL server forms the database layer Amazon ElastiCache forms the cache layer. The company wants a caching strategy that adds or updates data in the cache when a customer adds an item to the database. The data in the cache must always match the data in the database. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Implement the lazy loading caching strategy
B. Implement the write-through caching strategy
C. Implement the adding TTL caching strategy
D. Implement the AWS AppConfig caching strategy
optionExplanations: ✗ Lazy loading (cache-aside) only populates the cache on a read miss, not when data is added to the database, so the cache can hold stale data and will not always match the database.

✓ Write-through writes/updates the cache at the same time the data is written to the database, ensuring the cache is populated on every write and always matches the database, which exactly meets the requirements.
✗ Adding a TTL only sets an expiration time on cached items to limit staleness; it does not proactively add or update data on database writes and does not guarantee the cache matches the database.
✗ AWS AppConfig is a feature-flag and application-configuration management service, not an ElastiCache caching strategy, so it is irrelevant to keeping the cache synchronized with RDS.

text: A company wants to migrate 100 GB of historical data from an on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has a 100 megabits per second (Mbps) internet connection on premises. The company needs to encrypt the data in transit to the S3 bucket. The company will store new data directly in Amazon S3. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use the s3 sync command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket
B. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the on-premises location to an S3 bucket
C. Use AWS Snowball to move the data to an S3 bucket
D. Set up an IPsec VPN from the on-premises location to AWS. Use the s3 cp command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket
optionExplanations: ✓ The AWS CLI s3 sync command transfers data to Amazon S3 over HTTPS, which encrypts data in transit via TLS. For only 100 GB over a 100 Mbps link (a few hours), this is the simplest approach with the least operational overhead and no extra infrastructure to deploy.

✗ AWS DataSync meets the encryption and transfer requirements, but it requires deploying and configuring a DataSync agent on premises plus creating tasks, which is more operational overhead than a single CLI command for a one-time 100 GB transfer.

✗ AWS Snowball is a physical appliance intended for very large datasets or poor connectivity; ordering, receiving, loading, and shipping a device is far more operational overhead and unnecessary for 100 GB over an adequate internet connection.

✗ An IPsec VPN plus s3 cp does encrypt traffic and works, but setting up and maintaining a VPN tunnel adds substantial operational overhead, and S3 transfers already use TLS, making the VPN redundant for the in-transit encryption requirement.

text: A company containerized a Windows job that runs on .NET 6 Framework under a Windows container. The company wants to run this job in the AWS Cloud. The job runs every 10 minutes. The job’s runtime varies between 1 minute and 3 minutes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Create an AWS Lambda function based on the container image of the job. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the function every 10 minutes.
B. Use AWS Batch to create a job that uses AWS Fargate resources. Configure the job scheduling to run every 10 minutes.
C. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate to run the job. Create a scheduled task based on the container image of the job to run every 10 minutes.

D. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate to run the job. Create a standalone task based on the container image of the job. Use Windows task scheduler to run the job every 10 minutes.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Lambda does not support Windows containers; Lambda container images must use Lambda's Linux-based runtime, so a Windows .NET container job cannot run on Lambda. Incorrect.

✗ AWS Batch on Fargate does not support Windows containers (Fargate Windows is supported by ECS, not Batch), and Batch adds unnecessary overhead for a tiny periodic job; it is overkill and not the most cost-effective fit. Incorrect.

✓ Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate supports Windows containers, and an EventBridge-driven ECS scheduled task running every 10 minutes pays only for the 1-3 minutes of compute per run with no idle servers, making it the most cost-effective and lowest-overhead solution. Correct.

✗ ECS on Fargate can run the Windows container, but using a standalone task driven by the Windows Task Scheduler requires a continuously running container/host to host the scheduler, which defeats the pay-per-use benefit and is less cost-effective than a native ECS scheduled task. Incorrect.

text: A company wants to move from many standalone AWS accounts to a consolidated, multi-account architecture. The company plans to create many new AWS accounts for different business units. The company needs to authenticate access to these AWS accounts by using a centralized corporate directory service. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Create a new organization in AWS Organizations with all features turned on. Create the new AWS accounts in the organization.
B. Set up an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to accept Amazon Cognito authentication.
C. Configure a service control policy (SCP) to manage the AWS accounts. Add AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to AWS Directory Service.
D. Create a new organization in AWS Organizations. Configure the organization's authentication mechanism to use AWS Directory Service directly.
E. Set up AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the organization. Configure IAM Identity Center, and integrate it with the company's corporate directory service.
optionExplanations: ✓ creating a new AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled and provisioning the new business-unit accounts within it provides the consolidated multi-account foundation needed.

✗ Amazon Cognito identity pools are for application end-user/web/mobile authentication, not for federating AWS account console access to a corporate directory, so this does not meet the centralized workforce authentication requirement.

✗ SCPs only restrict permissions and do not provide authentication; the phrasing of adding IAM Identity Center to AWS Directory Service is not the correct integration path for centralized corporate-directory authentication.

✗ AWS Organizations itself has no authentication mechanism to point at Directory Service; identity federation for account access is provided by IAM Identity Center, not by configuring Organizations to use Directory Service directly.
✓ enabling AWS IAM Identity Center in the organization and integrating it with the company's existing corporate directory provides centralized, federated authentication to all member accounts.

text: A company is looking for a solution that can store video archives in AWS from old news footage. The company needs to minimize costs and will rarely need to restore these files. When the files are needed, they must be available in a maximum of five minutes. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
options: A. Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier and use Expedited retrievals.
B. Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier and use Standard retrievals.
C. Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
D. Store the video archives in Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA).
optionExplanations: ✓ S3 Glacier (flexible retrieval) offers the lowest storage cost for rarely-accessed archives, and Expedited retrievals return data in 1-5 minutes, satisfying the five-minute availability requirement.
✗ Glacier Standard retrievals take 3-5 hours, which fails the five-minute availability requirement despite low storage cost.
✗ S3 Standard-IA provides millisecond access but has much higher storage cost than Glacier, so it is not the most cost-effective for data that is rarely restored.

✗ S3 One Zone-IA is cheaper than Standard-IA but still far more expensive than Glacier for storage and stores data in a single AZ (lower durability); it is not the most cost-effective for archival video.

text: A company is building a three-tier application on AWS. The presentation tier will serve a static website The logic tier is a containerized application. This application will store data in a relational database. The company wants to simplify deployment and to reduce operational costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon S3 to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
B. Use Amazon CloudFront to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
C. Use Amazon S3 to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
D. Use Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon S3 hosts the static website cheaply and serverlessly, ECS on AWS Fargate runs the containerized logic tier without managing servers, and managed Amazon RDS provides the relational database, minimizing deployment effort and operational cost.
✗ CloudFront is a CDN and cannot itself host static content (it needs an origin such as S3), and ECS on EC2 requires managing the EC2 fleet, adding operational overhead compared to Fargate.

✗ EKS on Fargate works but Kubernetes adds control-plane cost and operational complexity that is unnecessary for a simple containerized logic tier, making it less aligned with simplified, low-cost deployment than ECS Fargate.
✗ EC2 Reserved Instances for static content require managing servers and EKS on EC2 requires managing the node fleet, both increasing operational overhead and cost relative to S3 plus Fargate.

text: A company seeks a storage solution for its application. The solution must be highly available and scalable. The solution also must function as a file system be mountable by multiple Linux instances in AWS and on premises through native protocols, and have no minimum size requirements. The company has set up a Site-to-Site VPN for access from its on-premises network to its VPC. Which storage solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Amazon FSx Multi-AZ deployments
B. Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volumes
C. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with multiple mount targets
D. Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a single mount target and multiple access points
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon FSx options (Windows/Lustre/etc.) are not the standard answer for a no-minimum-size, multi-Linux, native NFS file system mountable both in AWS and on premises; EFS is the purpose-built service for this.

✗ EBS Multi-Attach allows a single volume to attach to multiple EC2 instances in one AZ but is block storage, not a mountable file system, and cannot be accessed from on premises, so it fails the requirements.

✓ Amazon EFS is an elastic, highly available file system with no minimum size, mountable via NFS by multiple Linux instances, and with mount targets in each AZ it is accessible from on premises over the Site-to-Site VPN.

✗ A single mount target places the file system endpoint in one AZ, reducing availability and resiliency; the highly available design requires multiple mount targets (one per AZ), so this option does not best meet the requirements.

text: A 4-year-old media company is using the AWS Organizations all features feature set to organize its AWS accounts. According to the company's finance team, the billing information on the member accounts must not be accessible to anyone, including the root user of the member accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Add all finance team users to an IAM group. Attach an AWS managed policy named Billing to the group.
B. Attach an identity-based policy to deny access to the billing information to all users, including the root user.
C. Create a service control policy (SCP) to deny access to the billing information. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU).
D. Convert from the Organizations all features feature set to the Organizations consolidated billing feature set.
optionExplanations: ✗ Attaching the Billing managed policy to a finance IAM group grants those users access to billing but does nothing to deny billing access to other users or the root user of member accounts.
✗ An identity-based policy cannot restrict the root user, because the root account is not bound by identity-based IAM policies, so this cannot block root access to billing information.

✓ a service control policy attached at the organization/root OU level applies even to the root user of member accounts, so denying billing actions via an SCP is the only way to block billing access for everyone including root.

✗ Switching to the consolidated billing feature set reduces Organizations capabilities and would remove the ability to apply SCPs; it does not deny member-account billing access and is the wrong direction.

text: An ecommerce company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that is integrated with an on-premises warehouse solution. The company uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send order messages to an on-premises HTTPS endpoint so the warehouse application can process the orders. The local data center team has detected that some of the order messages were not received. A solutions architect needs to retain messages that are not delivered and analyze the messages for up to 14 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream target with a retention period of 14 days.
B. Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue with a retention period of 14 days between the application and Amazon SNS.
