C. Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) target with a retention period of 14 days.
D. Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon DynamoDB target with a TTL attribute set for a retention period of 14 days.
optionExplanations: ✗ An SNS dead-letter queue must be an SQS queue, not a Kinesis Data Stream; SNS DLQ does not support a Kinesis target, so this configuration is invalid.

✗ Inserting an SQS queue between the application and SNS does not capture messages that fail delivery to the on-premises HTTPS endpoint downstream of SNS, so undelivered order messages would still be lost.

✓ configuring an SNS dead-letter queue backed by an SQS queue with a 14-day retention period automatically captures messages that fail delivery to the HTTPS endpoint and retains them for analysis with the least development effort.
✗ SNS dead-letter queues only support SQS targets, not DynamoDB; you cannot directly set a DynamoDB table as an SNS DLQ, so this option is not valid.

text: A gaming company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store user information such as geographic location, player data, and leaderboards. The company needs to configure continuous backups to an Amazon S3 bucket with a minimal amount of coding. The backups must not affect availability of the application and must not affect the read capacity units (RCUs) that are defined for the table. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use an Amazon EMR cluster. Create an Apache Hive job to back up the data to Amazon S3.
B. Export the data directly from DynamoDB to Amazon S3 with continuous backups. Turn on point-in-time recovery for the table.
C. Configure Amazon DynamoDB Streams. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the stream and export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function to export the data from the database tables to Amazon S3 on a regular basis. Turn on point-in-time recovery for the table.
optionExplanations: ✗ Running an EMR cluster with a Hive job to back up DynamoDB consumes table read capacity (RCUs) and requires significant coding and cluster management, violating the no-RCU-impact and minimal-coding requirements.

✓ DynamoDB's native export to S3 (enabled by point-in-time recovery) exports table data directly to S3 without consuming RCUs and without affecting application availability, requiring essentially no code.

✗ Using DynamoDB Streams with a Lambda consumer requires writing and maintaining custom code and only captures changes (not a full continuous backup), and it captures item-level changes rather than providing a simple continuous full backup.

✗ A custom Lambda function scanning and exporting the tables consumes read capacity (RCUs) and requires writing and maintaining code, conflicting with the no-RCU-impact and minimal-coding requirements.

text: A solutions architect is designing an asynchronous application to process credit card data validation requests for a bank. The application must be secure and be able to process each request at least once. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.

B. Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use SQS managed encryption keys (SSE-SQS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.

C. Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.

D. Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.
optionExplanations: ✓ SQS standard queues offer at-least-once delivery (meeting 'process each request at least once') and are cheaper than FIFO queues, satisfying MOST cost-effective. SSE-KMS encrypts the data, and the Lambda execution role correctly needs kms:Decrypt permission to read encrypted messages.

✗ FIFO queues provide exactly-once processing but cost more than standard queues, so this is not the most cost-effective; the requirement is only 'at least once.' Also SSE-SQS uses SQS-managed keys with no separate key permission to grant, and 'encryption key invocation permission' is not the correct IAM concept.

✗ FIFO queues are more expensive than standard queues and unnecessary for an at-least-once requirement, making this not the most cost-effective option despite the otherwise correct SSE-KMS and kms:Decrypt permission.

✗ Standard queues and SSE-KMS are appropriate, but the permission needed for Lambda to decrypt SSE-KMS messages is kms:Decrypt on the execution role, not a vague 'encryption key invocation permission.'

text: A company has multiple AWS accounts for development work. Some staff consistently use oversized Amazon EC2 instances, which causes the company to exceed the yearly budget for the development accounts. The company wants to centrally restrict the creation of AWS resources in these accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Develop AWS Systems Manager templates that use an approved EC2 creation process. Use the approved Systems Manager templates to provision EC2 instances.
B. Use AWS Organizations to organize the accounts into organizational units (OUs). Define and attach a service control policy (SCP) to control the usage of EC2 instance types.
C. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function when an EC2 instance is created. Stop disallowed EC2 instance types.
D. Set up AWS Service Catalog products for the staff to create the allowed EC2 instance types. Ensure that staff can deploy EC2 instances only by using the Service Catalog products.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Systems Manager templates/automation could provision approved instances, but this requires building and maintaining custom provisioning workflows and does not centrally prevent users from launching oversized instances through other means; high development effort.

✓ AWS Organizations with a service control policy (SCP) attached to OUs can centrally deny creation of unapproved EC2 instance types across all member accounts using a condition like ec2:InstanceType. This is a declarative guardrail with the least development effort and is the correct answer.

✗ An EventBridge rule invoking a Lambda function to detect and stop disallowed instances is reactive (instances are created first), and requires writing, deploying, and maintaining custom Lambda code; more development effort and not a true preventive control.

✗ AWS Service Catalog restricts users to approved products, but it requires authoring portfolios/products, CloudFormation templates, and IAM constraints, and does not by itself block instance creation outside the catalog; more setup effort than an SCP.

text: A company wants to use artificial intelligence (AI) to determine the quality of its customer service calls. The company currently manages calls in four different languages, including English. The company will offer new languages in the future. The company does not have the resources to regularly maintain machine learning (ML) models. The company needs to create written sentiment analysis reports from the customer service call recordings. The customer service call recording text must be translated into English. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)
options: A. Use Amazon Comprehend to translate the audio recordings into English.
B. Use Amazon Lex to create the written sentiment analysis reports.
C. Use Amazon Polly to convert the audio recordings into text.
D. Use Amazon Transcribe to convert the audio recordings in any language into text.
E. Use Amazon Translate to translate text in any language to English.
F. Use Amazon Comprehend to create the sentiment analysis reports.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Comprehend is an NLP service for entity/sentiment/language analysis of text; it does not transcribe or translate audio recordings, so this is wrong.
✗ Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots and voice interfaces; it does not generate sentiment analysis reports, so this is wrong.
✗ Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service that converts text into audio, the opposite of what is needed (audio to text), so this is wrong.
✓ Amazon Transcribe is a fully managed speech-to-text service supporting many languages, converting the call recordings into text with no ML model maintenance, so this is correct.
✓ Amazon Translate is a managed neural machine translation service that translates text from many source languages into English, meeting the translation requirement, so this is correct.
✓ Amazon Comprehend performs managed sentiment analysis on text to produce the written sentiment reports without maintaining ML models, so this is correct.

text: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances to host its internal systems. As part of a deployment operation, an administrator tries to use the AWS CLI to terminate an EC2 instance. However, the administrator receives a 403 (Access Denied) error message. The administrator is using an IAM role that has the following IAM policy attached: What is the cause of the unsuccessful request?
options: A. The EC2 instance has a resource-based policy with a Deny statement.
B. The principal has not been specified in the policy statement.
C. The "Action" field does not grant the actions that are required to terminate the EC2 instance.
D. The request to terminate the EC2 instance does not originate from the CIDR blocks 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24.
optionExplanations: ✗ EC2 instances do not support resource-based policies, and the question describes an IAM policy attached to a role, not an instance resource policy, so this is not the cause.
✗ Identity-based policies attached to IAM roles/users do not require a Principal element; only resource-based policies use Principal, so a missing principal is not the cause.
✗ The scenario's policy does grant the ec2:TerminateInstances action; the denial comes from a condition, not from a missing action, so this is wrong.

✓ The policy uses an aws:SourceIp condition restricting access to the 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24 CIDR blocks; a request originating outside these ranges fails the condition and is denied, causing the 403 error.

text: A company is conducting an internal audit. The company wants to ensure that the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is associated with the company’s AWS Lake Formation data lake does not contain sensitive customer or employee data. The company wants to discover personally identifiable information (PII) or financial information, including passport numbers and credit card numbers. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Audit Manager on the account. Select the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS) for auditing.
B. Configure Amazon S3 Inventory on the S3 bucket Configure Amazon Athena to query the inventory.
C. Configure Amazon Macie to run a data discovery job that uses managed identifiers for the required data types.
D. Use Amazon S3 Select to run a report across the S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Audit Manager automates evidence collection for compliance frameworks like PCI DSS but does not scan S3 object contents to discover PII, so it cannot meet the requirement.
✗ S3 Inventory lists object metadata and Athena can query that list, but neither inspects object contents to detect PII or financial data, so this is wrong.
✓ Amazon Macie uses managed data identifiers to automatically discover sensitive data such as PII, passport numbers, and credit card numbers in S3 buckets, directly meeting the requirement.
✗ S3 Select retrieves subsets of data from individual objects using SQL but cannot automatically classify or detect PII across a bucket, so it does not meet the requirement.

text: A company uses on-premises servers to host its applications. The company is running out of storage capacity. The applications use both block storage and NFS storage. The company needs a high-performing solution that supports local caching without re-architecting its existing applications. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Mount Amazon S3 as a file system to the on-premises servers.
B. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to replace NFS storage.
C. Deploy AWS Snowball Edge to provision NFS mounts to on-premises servers.
D. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway to replace the block storage.
E. Deploy Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volumes and mount them to on-premises servers.
optionExplanations: ✗ Mounting Amazon S3 as a file system (e.g., via tools) presents object storage, not native NFS or block semantics, and does not provide the seamless local caching of a Storage Gateway without re-architecting applications.
✓ AWS Storage Gateway file gateway presents an NFS/SMB interface backed by S3 with a local cache for low-latency access, directly replacing the NFS storage without re-architecting the applications.
✗ AWS Snowball Edge is a data transfer/edge compute device for bulk migration, not a persistent, high-performing cloud-backed NFS storage extension with caching.
✓ AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway presents iSCSI block volumes backed by S3 with local caching, directly replacing the on-premises block storage without re-architecting the applications.

✗ Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system in AWS; while mountable on-premises over Direct Connect/VPN, it provides no local caching tier and is intended for cloud workloads, not a caching gateway for failing on-prem capacity.

text: A company has a service that reads and writes large amounts of data from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region. The service is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances within the private subnet of a VPC. The service communicates with Amazon S3 over a NAT gateway in the public subnet. However, the company wants a solution that will reduce the data output costs. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the public subnet. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 trafic.

B. Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the private subnet. Configure the route table for the public subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 trafic.
C. Provision a VPC gateway endpoint. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the gateway endpoint as the route for all S3 trafic.
D. Provision a second NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use this NAT gateway as the destination for all S3 trafic.
optionExplanations: ✗ A dedicated EC2 NAT instance still routes S3 traffic through a compute resource incurring data processing/transfer charges and adds operational overhead, so it is not the most cost-effective option.
✗ Placing a NAT instance in the private subnet for the public subnet's route table is misconfigured and does not reduce S3 data output costs, so this is wrong.

✓ A VPC gateway endpoint for S3 routes traffic privately within AWS at no per-GB charge and avoids NAT gateway data processing fees, making it the most cost-effective way to reach S3 in the same Region.
✗ Adding a second NAT gateway increases cost rather than reducing it, since NAT gateways charge per hour and per GB processed, so this does not meet the requirement.

text: A company uses Amazon S3 to store high-resolution pictures in an S3 bucket. To minimize application changes, the company stores the pictures as the latest version of an S3 object. The company needs to retain only the two most recent versions of the pictures. The company wants to reduce costs. The company has identified the S3 bucket as a large expense. Which solution will reduce the S3 costs with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use S3 Lifecycle to delete expired object versions and retain the two most recent versions.
B. Use an AWS Lambda function to check for older versions and delete all but the two most recent versions.
C. Use S3 Batch Operations to delete noncurrent object versions and retain only the two most recent versions.
D. Deactivate versioning on the S3 bucket and retain the two most recent versions.
optionExplanations: ✓ An S3 Lifecycle rule with NewerNoncurrentVersions can automatically expire older noncurrent versions while retaining the two most recent, providing the lowest operational overhead as a managed, automatic policy.
✗ A custom Lambda function to find and delete old versions requires development, scheduling, and ongoing maintenance, adding operational overhead compared to Lifecycle rules.
✗ S3 Batch Operations requires creating manifests and jobs and is a manual/repeated operation, adding more overhead than an automatic Lifecycle policy.
✗ Deactivating versioning stops new versions but does not delete existing older versions and would break the requirement to retain exactly the two most recent versions, so this is wrong.

text: A company needs to minimize the cost of its 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The company's average connection utilization is less than 10%. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that will reduce the cost without compromising security. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Set up a new 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
B. Set up a new 200 Mbps Direct Connect connection in the AWS Management Console.
C. Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 1 Gbps connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
D. Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 200 Mbps hosted connection for an existing AWS account.
optionExplanations: ✗ Provisioning another full 1 Gbps dedicated connection does not reduce cost (it adds cost), and sharing it does not lower the company's spend, so this is wrong.
✗ Dedicated Direct Connect connections from AWS are only available at 1 Gbps, 10 Gbps, or higher port speeds; you cannot order a 200 Mbps dedicated connection in the console, so this is wrong.
✗ Ordering another 1 Gbps connection through a Partner still costs as much as the existing one and does not reduce spend, so this is wrong.

✓ An AWS Direct Connect Partner can provide a 200 Mbps hosted connection, which is far cheaper than the underutilized 1 Gbps link while preserving the private, secure Direct Connect path, meeting the cost-reduction goal.

text: A company has multiple Windows file servers on premises. The company wants to migrate and consolidate its files into an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. File permissions must be preserved to ensure that access rights do not change. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Deploy AWS DataSync agents on premises. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
B. Copy the shares on each file server into Amazon S3 buckets by using the AWS CLI. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
C. Remove the drives from each file server. Ship the drives to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

D. Order an AWS Snowcone device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Launch AWS DataSync agents on the device. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

E. Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Copy data to the device by using the AWS CLI. Ship the device back to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS DataSync agents deployed on premises can transfer SMB data directly to FSx for Windows File Server, preserving NTFS file permissions and SMB metadata. Correct.
✗ Copying shares into S3 with the AWS CLI strips NTFS ACLs because S3 objects do not retain Windows file permissions; the subsequent DataSync transfer cannot restore lost permissions. Incorrect.
✗ Shipping drives for import into S3 also loses NTFS permissions, since S3 does not preserve Windows ACLs, so access rights would change. Incorrect.
✓ An AWS Snowcone device can run AWS DataSync agents locally, and DataSync preserves SMB file permissions/metadata when transferring to FSx for Windows File Server. Correct.
✗ Snowball Edge with AWS CLI copy imports data into S3, which does not retain NTFS ACLs, so file permissions are not preserved. Incorrect.

text: A company wants to ingest customer payment data into the company's data lake in Amazon S3. The company receives payment data every minute on average. The company wants to analyze the payment data in real time. Then the company wants to ingest the data into the data lake. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational eficiency?
options: A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.
B. Use AWS Glue to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
C. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
D. Use Amazon API Gateway to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.
optionExplanations: ✗ Kinesis Data Streams can ingest data, but it does not natively deliver to S3; you must build and operate consumers (Lambda) to both analyze and load into the data lake, which adds operational overhead.

✗ AWS Glue is a batch ETL service, not a real-time streaming ingestion service, so it is a poor fit for continuously ingesting per-minute streaming payment data and would not directly feed real-time analytics.

✓ Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed service that ingests streaming data and automatically delivers it to S3 with no servers to manage, and Kinesis Data Analytics can run SQL/Flink analysis on the stream in real time; this is the most operationally efficient combination.

✗ API Gateway plus Lambda requires building and managing the ingestion API, the analysis logic, and the code to batch and write data into S3, which is significantly more operational overhead than a managed delivery stream.

text: A company runs a website that uses a content management system (CMS) on Amazon EC2. The CMS runs on a single EC2 instance and uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance for the data tier. Website images are stored on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is mounted inside the EC2 instance. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve the performance and resilience of the website? (Choose two.)
options: A. Move the website images into an Amazon S3 bucket that is mounted on every EC2 instance
B. Share the website images by using an NFS share from the primary EC2 instance. Mount this share on the other EC2 instances.
C. Move the website images onto an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on every EC2 instance.

D. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator for the website

E. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the website.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon S3 is object storage and cannot be natively mounted as a shared POSIX file system across EC2 instances for the CMS, so this is not the appropriate shared-storage solution.
✗ Sharing images via NFS from the primary EC2 instance creates a single point of failure and does not improve resilience, so this is wrong.
✓ Amazon EFS provides a shared, scalable, highly available file system that can be mounted on all EC2 instances, removing the local EBS single point of failure and enabling horizontal scaling.

✗ AWS Global Accelerator improves network routing but does not cache web/image content; combined here it is less suited than CloudFront for a website's performance, so this option is not the best choice.

✓ Building an AMI behind an ALB in an Auto Scaling group (minimum two instances) adds resilience and scalability, and a CloudFront distribution caches and accelerates content delivery, improving performance.

text: A company runs an infrastructure monitoring service. The company is building a new feature that will enable the service to monitor data in customer AWS accounts. The new feature will call AWS APIs in customer accounts to describe Amazon EC2 instances and read Amazon CloudWatch metrics. What should the company do to obtain access to customer accounts in the MOST secure way?
options: A. Ensure that the customers create an IAM role in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions and a trust policy to the company’s account.
B. Create a serverless API that implements a token vending machine to provide temporary AWS credentials for a role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions.
C. Ensure that the customers create an IAM user in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store customer access and secret keys in a secrets management system.

D. Ensure that the customers create an Amazon Cognito user in their account to use an IAM role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store the Amazon Cognito user and password in a secrets management system.
optionExplanations: ✓ Having customers create an IAM role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions and a trust policy to the company's account enables secure cross-account access using temporary STS credentials and no long-lived keys, the most secure approach.

✗ A token vending machine issuing credentials for a role still requires a trusted cross-account assume-role relationship and adds custom infrastructure; it is more complex and not more secure than the standard cross-account role.
✗ Creating IAM users with long-lived access keys and storing them in a secrets system relies on long-term credentials that can leak, which is less secure than assuming a cross-account role.
✗ Amazon Cognito is for application end-user authentication, not cross-account AWS API access, and storing user credentials is insecure, so this does not fit the use case.

text: A company needs to connect several VPCs in the us-east-1 Region that span hundreds of AWS accounts. The company's networking team has its own AWS account to manage the cloud network. What is the MOST operationally eficient solution to connect the VPCs?
options: A. Set up VPC peering connections between each VPC. Update each associated subnet’s route table
B. Configure a NAT gateway and an internet gateway in each VPC to connect each VPC through the internet
C. Create an AWS Transit Gateway in the networking team’s AWS account. Configure static routes from each VPC.
D. Deploy VPN gateways in each VPC. Create a transit VPC in the networking team’s AWS account to connect to each VPC.
optionExplanations: ✗ Full-mesh VPC peering across hundreds of VPCs requires an unmanageable number of connections and route table updates, making it operationally inefficient and not scalable.
✗ Connecting VPCs over the internet via NAT and internet gateways is insecure and does not provide private VPC-to-VPC connectivity, so this does not meet the requirement.
✓ AWS Transit Gateway in the networking team's account acts as a central hub to interconnect hundreds of VPCs across accounts with simplified routing, the most operationally efficient solution.
✗ Building a transit VPC with VPN gateways in each VPC is complex, costly, and harder to operate at hundreds-of-VPCs scale than a Transit Gateway, so it is not the most efficient option.

text: A company has Amazon EC2 instances that run nightly batch jobs to process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that uses On- Demand billing. If a job fails on one instance, another instance will reprocess the job. The batch jobs run between 12:00 AM and 06:00 AM local time every day. Which solution will provide EC2 instances to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Purchase a 1-year Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 that covers the instance family of the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
B. Purchase a 1-year Reserved Instance for the specific instance type and operating system of the instances in the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
C. Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Set the instances to Spot Instances. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
D. Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Increase the instance size. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
optionExplanations: ✗ EC2 Instance Savings Plans give discounts for a committed hourly spend over 1 year, but the workload runs only 6 hours per night, so a continuous commitment wastes money during the 18 idle hours and is not the most cost-effective.

✗ A 1-year Reserved Instance discounts a specific instance type running continuously, but the batch jobs only run 6 hours per day, leaving the reservation mostly unused and overpaying for idle capacity.

✓ Spot Instances offer up to ~90% savings and are ideal for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch work; since failed jobs are automatically reprocessed on another instance, occasional Spot interruptions are tolerable, making this the most cost-effective choice.
✗ Increasing instance size with On-Demand billing keeps the expensive On-Demand rate and adds more cost per instance, providing no savings for this intermittent workload.

text: A social media company is building a feature for its website. The feature will give users the ability to upload photos. The company expects significant increases in demand during large events and must ensure that the website can handle the upload trafic from users. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST scalability?
options: A. Upload files from the user's browser to the application servers. Transfer the files to an Amazon S3 bucket.
B. Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file gateway.
C. Generate Amazon S3 presigned URLs in the application. Upload files directly from the user's browser into an S3 bucket.
D. Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file system.
optionExplanations: ✗ Routing uploads through application servers makes those servers a scaling bottleneck and doubles data movement, limiting scalability during spikes.
✗ Storage Gateway file gateway is for hybrid on-premises file access via NFS/SMB, not for direct browser uploads from many internet users, and it is not designed for this scale.
✓ S3 presigned URLs let users upload directly to S3, which is virtually limitless in scale and offloads all upload traffic from application servers, providing the most scalability.
✗ EFS is a POSIX file system mounted by EC2/Lambda and cannot be written to directly from a browser, nor is it intended for massive concurrent internet upload traffic.

text: A company has a web application for travel ticketing. The application is based on a database that runs in a single data center in North America. The company wants to expand the application to serve a global user base. The company needs to deploy the application to multiple AWS Regions. Average latency must be less than 1 second on updates to the reservation database. The company wants to have separate deployments of its web platform across multiple Regions. However, the company must maintain a single primary reservation database that is globally consistent. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Convert the application to use Amazon DynamoDB. Use a global table for the center reservation table. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment.
B. Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Deploy Aurora Read Replicas in each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.
C. Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Deploy MySQL read replicas in each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.

D. Migrate the application to an Amazon Aurora Serverless database. Deploy instances of the database to each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment to access the database. Use AWS Lambda functions to process event streams in each Region to synchronize the databases.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon DynamoDB global tables provide a multi-active, multi-Region model where every Region accepts writes and replicates them. This violates the explicit requirement to maintain a single primary, globally consistent reservation database, and it also requires re-architecting the application away from relational SQL.

✓ Amazon Aurora MySQL with cross-Region Read Replicas (Aurora Global Database) keeps a single writable primary while replicating to read-only Regions with typical sub-second latency (under 1 second), satisfying global consistency, low-latency updates, separate Regional web deployments using Regional read endpoints, and minimal operational overhead.

✗ Amazon RDS for MySQL cross-Region read replicas use asynchronous binlog-based replication that is slower and harder to keep under 1 second, with more replication lag and management overhead than Aurora's storage-level replication; it does not reliably meet the sub-second global update requirement.

✗ Aurora Serverless does not natively support cross-Region replication, so deploying separate instances per Region and stitching them together with Lambda event-stream synchronization creates a custom, high-overhead, eventually-consistent design that violates the single-primary globally-consistent requirement and risks exceeding the 1-second latency target.

text: A company has migrated multiple Microsoft Windows Server workloads to Amazon EC2 instances that run in the us-west-1 Region. The company manually backs up the workloads to create an image as needed. In the event of a natural disaster in the us-west-1 Region, the company wants to recover workloads quickly in the us-west-2 Region. The company wants no more than 24 hours of data loss on the EC2 instances. The company also wants to automate any backups of the EC2 instances. Which solutions will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort? (Choose two.)
options: A. Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Copy the image on demand.
B. Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Configure the copy to the us-west-2 Region.

C. Create backup vaults in us-west-1 and in us-west-2 by using AWS Backup. Create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Create an AWS Lambda function to run as a scheduled job to copy the backup data to us-west-2.

D. Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Define the destination for the copy as us-west-2. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily.

E. Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily. Copy on demand to us-west-2.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager AMI lifecycle policy automates backups, but copying the image on demand is a manual step that fails the LEAST administrative effort requirement and does not guarantee a fresh copy in us-west-2.

✓ An EC2-backed AMI lifecycle policy (Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager) creates AMIs by tag twice daily (12h RPO) and can be configured to automatically copy the AMI to us-west-2, fully automating cross-region DR with minimal admin effort.

✗ AWS Backup can do this, but adding a custom Lambda scheduled job to copy backups to us-west-2 introduces extra code and operational overhead, which is more administrative effort than AWS Backup's native cross-region copy.

✓ AWS Backup with a tag-based backup plan, a copy destination of us-west-2, and a twice-daily schedule fully automates both backups and cross-region copy (12h RPO) with the least administrative effort.

✗ AWS Backup with a tag-based plan running twice daily is automated, but copying on demand to us-west-2 is a manual step that does not meet the LEAST administrative effort or automated cross-region requirement.

text: A company operates a two-tier application for image processing. The application uses two Availability Zones, each with one public subnet and one private subnet. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the web tier uses the public subnets. Amazon EC2 instances for the application tier use the private subnets. Users report that the application is running more slowly than expected. A security audit of the web server log files shows that the application is receiving millions of illegitimate requests from a small number of IP addresses. A solutions architect needs to resolve the immediate performance problem while the company investigates a more permanent solution. What should the solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?
options: A. Modify the inbound security group for the web tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
B. Modify the network ACL for the web tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
C. Modify the inbound security group for the application tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
D. Modify the network ACL for the application tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
optionExplanations: ✗ Security groups are stateful and do not support deny rules; they only allow traffic, so you cannot block specific malicious IP addresses with a security group.

✓ Network ACLs are stateless and support explicit deny rules, so adding an inbound deny rule on the web tier subnets blocks the offending IPs at the subnet boundary, immediately stopping the illegitimate traffic.
✗ Security groups cannot contain deny rules, and the application tier is not where the internet-facing illegitimate requests arrive, so this would not resolve the problem.

✗ Blocking at the application tier NACL is too far downstream (traffic already passed the ALB/web tier), and the malicious requests target the web tier, so this does not address the immediate problem effectively.

text: A global marketing company has applications that run in the ap-southeast-2 Region and the eu-west-1 Region. Applications that run in a VPC in eu- west-1 need to communicate securely with databases that run in a VPC in ap-southeast-2. Which network design will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a VPC peering connection between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. Create an inbound rule in the eu-west-1 application security group that allows trafic from the database server IP addresses in the ap-southeast-2 security group.

B. Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.

C. Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPUpdate the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that allows trafic from the eu-west-1 application server IP addresses.

D. Create a transit gateway with a peering attachment between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. After the transit gateways are properly peered and routing is configured, create an inbound rule in the database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.
optionExplanations: ✗ Putting the inbound rule on the eu-west-1 application security group is backwards; the databases in ap-southeast-2 are what receive inbound connections, so the rule belongs on the database security group, and cross-Region SG referencing is not described correctly here.

✓ Inter-Region VPC peering connects the two VPCs, updated route tables enable routing, and the ap-southeast-2 database security group references the eu-west-1 application security group ID, which is the correct and secure design.

✗ Allowing traffic by IP address ranges is less robust and secure than referencing a security group, and across Regions referencing the eu-west-1 application server IPs is brittle; SG referencing is preferred. (Also the option contains a typo 'VPUpdate'.)

✗ Transit Gateway does not support a peering attachment directly between two VPCs; TGW peering connects transit gateways, so this attachment description is invalid and overly complex for connecting two VPCs.

text: A company is developing software that uses a PostgreSQL database schema. The company needs to configure multiple development environments and databases for the company's developers. On average, each development environment is used for half of the 8-hour workday. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database
B. Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances
C. Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database
D. Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is a high-performance, higher-cost managed cluster that runs continuously and is overkill for intermittent dev workloads, making it less cost-effective.

✓ Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances are the cheapest managed PostgreSQL option (no multi-AZ redundancy needed for dev) and can be stopped when not in use, so paying for only ~half-day usage minimizes cost; this is the MOST cost-effective fit.

✗ An Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-compatible database is provisioned Aurora billed per-hour while running; it carries Aurora's premium pricing and does not auto-pause for the idle half of the day, costing more than stoppable RDS Single-AZ.

✗ Amazon S3 with S3 Select is object storage with SQL-expression filtering over objects, not a relational PostgreSQL database engine, so it cannot run a PostgreSQL schema and does not meet the requirement.

text: A company uses AWS Organizations with resources tagged by account. The company also uses AWS Backup to back up its AWS infrastructure resources. The company needs to back up all AWS resources. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use AWS Config to identify all untagged resources. Tag the identified resources programmatically. Use tags in the backup plan.
B. Use AWS Config to identify all resources that are not running. Add those resources to the backup vault.
C. Require all AWS account owners to review their resources to identify the resources that need to be backed up.
D. Use Amazon Inspector to identify all noncompliant resources.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Config can discover and identify untagged resources, which can then be tagged programmatically so the tag-based AWS Backup plan covers all resources, achieving the goal with the least operational overhead.
✗ Identifying resources that are 'not running' is irrelevant to backing up all resources, and you cannot simply add arbitrary resources to a backup vault this way.
✗ Manual review by every account owner is high operational overhead and error-prone, the opposite of what is required.
✗ Amazon Inspector assesses workloads for software vulnerabilities and network exposure, not resource tagging or backup coverage, so it does not address this requirement.

text: A social media company wants to allow its users to upload images in an application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs a solution that automatically resizes the images so that the images can be displayed on multiple device types. The application experiences unpredictable trafic patterns throughout the day. The company is seeking a highly available solution that maximizes scalability. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a static website hosted in Amazon S3 that invokes AWS Lambda functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.
B. Create a static website hosted in Amazon CloudFront that invokes AWS Step Functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon RDS database.

C. Create a dynamic website hosted on a web server that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a process that runs on the EC2 instance to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.

D. Create a dynamic website hosted on an automatically scaling Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that creates a resize job in Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Set up an image-resizing program that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance to process the resize jobs.
optionExplanations: ✓ An S3-hosted static website that triggers Lambda functions to resize images and stores them back in S3 is fully serverless, highly available, and scales automatically to handle unpredictable traffic, meeting all requirements.

✗ CloudFront is a CDN that distributes content and cannot 'host a static website' that invokes Step Functions for resizing, and storing many resized images in an RDS relational database is inappropriate.
✗ A single EC2 instance running the resize process is not highly available and does not scale automatically, failing the availability and scalability requirements.
✗ Running the image-resizing program on a single EC2 instance creates a non-scaling, single-point-of-failure bottleneck even though ECS and SQS scale, so it does not maximize scalability.

text: A company is running a microservices application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for scalability. The company must configure the Amazon EKS control plane with endpoint private access set to true and endpoint public access set to false to maintain security compliance. The company must also put the data plane in private subnets. However, the company has received error notifications because the node cannot join the cluster. Which solution will allow the node to join the cluster?
options: A. Grant the required permission in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to the AmazonEKSNodeRole IAM role.
B. Create interface VPC endpoints to allow nodes to access the control plane.
C. Recreate nodes in the public subnet. Restrict security groups for EC2 nodes.
D. Allow outbound trafic in the security group of the nodes.
optionExplanations: ✗ The node IAM role permissions are not the issue here; the problem is private nodes cannot reach the control plane endpoint because public access is disabled, and the role is presumably already attached.

✓ With public endpoint access disabled and nodes in private subnets, nodes need a private path to the EKS API and related AWS services, so creating interface VPC endpoints (and using the private control plane endpoint) lets nodes reach the control plane and join the cluster.
✗ Recreating nodes in public subnets violates the requirement that the data plane stay in private subnets, so this is not an acceptable solution.

✗ Allowing outbound traffic alone does not provide connectivity to a private-only control plane endpoint without a network path (VPC endpoints or NAT to the private API), so it does not resolve the join failure under these constraints.

text: A company is migrating an on-premises application to AWS. The company wants to use Amazon Redshift as a solution. Which use cases are suitable for Amazon Redshift in this scenario? (Choose three.)
options: A. Supporting data APIs to access data with traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications
B. Supporting client-side and server-side encryption
C. Building analytics workloads during specified hours and when the application is not active
D. Caching data to reduce the pressure on the backend database
E. Scaling globally to support petabytes of data and tens of millions of requests per minute
F. Creating a secondary replica of the cluster by using the AWS Management Console
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon Redshift provides the Redshift Data API, which lets traditional, containerized, and event-driven (e.g., Lambda) applications query data without managing persistent JDBC/ODBC connections.
✓ Amazon Redshift supports server-side encryption (KMS/HSM, encryption at rest) and client-side encryption for data loaded via services like Amazon S3, satisfying common security requirements.

✓ Redshift is an OLAP data warehouse well suited to running analytics/reporting workloads during specified windows; clusters can be paused/resumed or scheduled to run during off-peak hours when the source application is idle.

✗ Caching data to relieve pressure on a backend database is the role of Amazon ElastiCache (or DynamoDB DAX), not Amazon Redshift, which is an analytical data warehouse rather than a low-latency cache.

✗ Globally scaling to support petabytes with tens of millions of requests per minute describes a NoSQL store like Amazon DynamoDB with global tables; Redshift is a regional analytics warehouse, not a high-throughput global transactional request service.

✗ Creating a secondary read replica through the AWS Management Console is an Amazon RDS feature; Redshift achieves durability/availability through cluster snapshots and multi-AZ deployments, not a console-created secondary replica.

text: A company provides an API interface to customers so the customers can retrieve their financial information. Еhe company expects a larger number of requests during peak usage times of the year. The company requires the API to respond consistently with low latency to ensure customer satisfaction. The company needs to provide a compute host for the API. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use an Application Load Balancer and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
B. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency.
C. Use an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.
D. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with reserved concurrency.
optionExplanations: ✗ ALB with ECS requires managing containers, tasks, and scaling, adding more operational overhead than a serverless API Gateway plus Lambda solution.

✓ API Gateway with Lambda is fully serverless (least operational overhead), and provisioned concurrency keeps functions pre-initialized to eliminate cold starts, delivering consistent low latency even during peak usage.
✗ ALB with an EKS cluster requires significant Kubernetes management and node operations, which is far more operational overhead than a serverless approach.
✗ Reserved concurrency only caps the maximum concurrency for a function and does not pre-warm execution environments, so it does not eliminate cold-start latency the way provisioned concurrency does.

text: A company wants to send all AWS Systems Manager Session Manager logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for archival purposes. Which solution will meet this requirement with the MOST operational eficiency?
options: A. Enable S3 logging in the Systems Manager console. Choose an S3 bucket to send the session data to.
B. Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Export the logs to an S3 bucket from the group for archival purposes.
C. Create a Systems Manager document to upload all server logs to a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge to run the Systems Manager document against all servers that are in the account daily.

D. Install an Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch logs subscription that pushes any incoming log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Set Amazon S3 as the destination.
optionExplanations: ✓ Session Manager natively supports sending session output to S3; you simply enable S3 logging in Session Manager preferences and pick a bucket, requiring no agents or pipelines, so this is the most operationally efficient choice.
✗ Installing the CloudWatch agent, pushing to a log group, then exporting to S3 adds an agent and a manual/extra export step, which is far more overhead than Session Manager's built-in S3 logging.
✗ Building a custom SSM document run daily by EventBridge to upload arbitrary server logs does not capture Session Manager session logs and adds heavy custom orchestration overhead.

✗ Routing logs through the CloudWatch agent, a log group, a subscription filter, and Kinesis Data Firehose to S3 is a complex multi-service pipeline with much more overhead than the native S3 logging option.

text: An application uses an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The RDS database is becoming low on disk space. A solutions architect wants to increase the disk space without downtime. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?
options: A. Enable storage autoscaling in RDS
B. Increase the RDS database instance size
C. Change the RDS database instance storage type to Provisioned IOPS
D. Back up the RDS database, increase the storage capacity, restore the database, and stop the previous instance
optionExplanations: ✓ RDS storage autoscaling automatically increases allocated storage when space runs low, with no downtime and essentially no ongoing effort once enabled, meeting the requirement with the least effort.

✗ Increasing the DB instance size changes compute (vCPU/RAM), not storage capacity, and a class change typically incurs a brief failover/downtime, so it does not address low disk space with least effort.
✗ Switching to Provisioned IOPS changes storage performance characteristics, not necessarily capacity, and a storage-type conversion is a heavier operation than enabling autoscaling.
✗ Backing up, increasing storage, restoring, and decommissioning the old instance is a manual multi-step process that causes downtime and is the highest-effort option.

text: A consulting company provides professional services to customers worldwide. The company provides solutions and tools for customers to expedite gathering and analyzing data on AWS. The company needs to centrally manage and deploy a common set of solutions and tools for customers to use for self-service purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create AWS CloudFormation templates for the customers.
B. Create AWS Service Catalog products for the customers.
C. Create AWS Systems Manager templates for the customers.
D. Create AWS Config items for the customers.
optionExplanations: ✗ Raw CloudFormation templates can provision resources but lack the centralized catalog, governance, versioning, and self-service portal that a company distributing tools to many customers needs.

✓ AWS Service Catalog lets the company centrally create, manage, version, and share a curated set of products (tools/solutions) that customers can deploy on a self-service basis, exactly matching the requirement.
✗ There is no general 'Systems Manager template' product for self-service distribution of solutions; SSM documents automate operational tasks rather than provide a self-service solution catalog.
✗ AWS Config items represent configuration state of resources for compliance/auditing and are not a mechanism to deploy or distribute solutions to customers.

text: A company is designing a new web application that will run on Amazon EC2 Instances. The application will use Amazon DynamoDB for backend data storage. The application trafic will be unpredictable. The company expects that the application read and write throughput to the database will be moderate to high. The company needs to scale in response to application trafic. Which DynamoDB table configuration will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
B. Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard table class.
C. Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
D. Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class.
optionExplanations: ✗ Provisioned capacity with auto scaling can work but reacts to traffic with lag and risks throttling on unpredictable spikes; it requires tuning and is less cost-effective than on-demand for truly unpredictable workloads.

✓ On-demand mode with the Standard table class scales instantly to unpredictable traffic with no capacity planning and charges per request, making it the most cost-effective and operationally simple fit for moderate-to-high unpredictable throughput.
✗ Standard-IA is for infrequently accessed data and charges more for reads/writes; pairing it with provisioned capacity is wrong for a moderate-to-high frequently accessed workload.
✗ On-demand mode is appropriate, but the Standard-IA table class raises per-request throughput costs for frequently accessed data, making it less cost-effective than the Standard class here.

text: A retail company has several businesses. The IT team for each business manages its own AWS account. Each team account is part of an organization in AWS Organizations. Each team monitors its product inventory levels in an Amazon DynamoDB table in the team's own AWS account. The company is deploying a central inventory reporting application into a shared AWS account. The application must be able to read items from all the teams' DynamoDB tables. Which authentication option will meet these requirements MOST securely?
options: A. Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Secrets Manager in the inventory application account. Configure the application to use the correct secret from Secrets Manager to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table. Schedule secret rotation for every 30 days.

B. In every business account, create an IAM user that has programmatic access. Configure the application to use the correct IAM user access key ID and secret access key to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table. Manually rotate IAM access keys every 30 days.

C. In every business account, create an IAM role named BU_ROLE with a policy that gives the role access to the DynamoDB table and a trust policy to trust a specific role in the inventory application account. In the inventory account, create a role named APP_ROLE that allows access to the STS AssumeRole API operation. Configure the application to use APP_ROLE and assume the crossaccount role BU_ROLE to read the DynamoDB table.

D. Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Generate identity certificates to authenticate DynamoDB. Configure the application to use the correct certificate to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table.
optionExplanations: ✗ Secrets Manager stores credentials, not native DynamoDB authentication; DynamoDB does not authenticate via Secrets Manager secrets, so this approach is invalid and relies on long-lived secrets.
✗ Creating IAM users with static access keys in every account and rotating them manually relies on long-lived credentials and is the least secure, highest-maintenance approach.

✓ Cross-account IAM roles with a trust policy plus the application assuming BU_ROLE via STS provide temporary, scoped, auditable credentials and follow AWS best practice, making this the most secure option.
✗ ACM issues TLS certificates for encryption, not identity certificates that DynamoDB accepts for authentication, so this option is technically invalid.

text: A company runs container applications by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company's workload is not consistent throughout the day. The company wants Amazon EKS to scale in and out according to the workload. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)
options: A. Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster.
B. Use the Kubernetes Metrics Server to activate horizontal pod autoscaling.
C. Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.
D. Use Amazon API Gateway and connect it to Amazon EKS.
E. Use AWS App Mesh to observe network activity.
optionExplanations: ✗ A custom Lambda function to resize the cluster is custom code that must be built and maintained, adding operational overhead compared to native autoscaling mechanisms.
✓ The Kubernetes Metrics Server enabling Horizontal Pod Autoscaling scales the number of pods based on workload metrics, a native, low-overhead way to scale the application in and out.
✓ The Cluster Autoscaler adjusts the number of EC2 worker nodes as pod demand changes, complementing HPA to scale the cluster's underlying capacity with minimal operational overhead.
✗ API Gateway fronts and manages APIs; it does not scale EKS nodes or pods based on workload and is irrelevant to autoscaling the cluster.
✗ App Mesh provides service-mesh observability and traffic control but does not perform autoscaling of pods or nodes.

text: A company runs a microservice-based serverless web application. The application must be able to retrieve data from multiple Amazon DynamoDB tables A solutions architect needs to give the application the ability to retrieve the data with no impact on the baseline performance of the application. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally eficient way?
options: A. AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers
B. Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge functions
C. Edge-optimized Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions
D. Amazon Athena Federated Query with a DynamoDB connector
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers let a single GraphQL request execute a sequence of resolver functions to fetch and combine data from multiple DynamoDB tables natively, with no extra compute to manage and no impact on baseline application performance. This is the most operationally efficient fit for a serverless microservice retrieving from multiple tables.

✗ Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge is a CDN/edge-compute pattern for caching and request manipulation at edge locations, not a managed way to query and join multiple DynamoDB tables; it adds Lambda code to maintain and is not designed for this retrieval pattern.

✗ Edge-optimized API Gateway with Lambda functions would work but requires writing and maintaining Lambda code to orchestrate the DynamoDB queries, adding operational overhead compared to AppSync's built-in pipeline resolvers.

✗ Amazon Athena Federated Query with a DynamoDB connector is for ad-hoc SQL analytics across data sources; it has high query latency and is not suited for low-latency application data retrieval, and the federation/connector setup adds operational overhead.

text: A company wants to analyze and troubleshoot Access Denied errors and Unauthorized errors that are related to IAM permissions. The company has AWS CloudTrail turned on. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?
options: A. Use AWS Glue and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
B. Use AWS Batch and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
C. Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon Athena queries to identify the errors.
D. Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon QuickSight. Create a dashboard to identify the errors.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Glue plus custom scripts to query CloudTrail requires building ETL jobs and code, which is far more effort than directly querying the logs.
✗ AWS Batch plus custom scripts requires provisioning compute and writing and maintaining query code, far more effort than a direct query service.
✓ Amazon Athena can query CloudTrail logs in S3 directly with SQL to find Access Denied and Unauthorized errors with minimal setup, meeting the requirement with the least effort.
✗ QuickSight is a BI visualization tool that needs a data source (often Athena) underneath; building dashboards is more effort than simply running Athena queries to find the errors.

text: A company wants to add its existing AWS usage cost to its operation cost dashboard. A solutions architect needs to recommend a solution that will give the company access to its usage cost programmatically. The company must be able to access cost data for the current year and forecast costs for the next 12 months. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Access usage cost-related data by using the AWS Cost Explorer API with pagination.
B. Access usage cost-related data by using downloadable AWS Cost Explorer report .csv files.
C. Configure AWS Budgets actions to send usage cost data to the company through FTP.
D. Create AWS Budgets reports for usage cost data. Send the data to the company through SMTP.
optionExplanations: ✓ The Cost Explorer API provides programmatic access to current-year usage cost data and can return cost forecasts for up to 12 months, with pagination handling large result sets, meeting the need with the least operational overhead.
✗ Downloadable CSV report files require manual downloading and parsing rather than direct programmatic API access, adding operational overhead.
✗ AWS Budgets actions trigger remediation/notifications and do not deliver detailed cost data over FTP, so this does not meet the programmatic cost-and-forecast requirement.
✗ AWS Budgets reports sent via SMTP are email summaries, not a programmatic data feed, and do not provide flexible access to detailed current and forecasted cost data.

text: A solutions architect is reviewing the resilience of an application. The solutions architect notices that a database administrator recently failed over the application's Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database writer instance as part of a scaling exercise. The failover resulted in 3 minutes of downtime for the application. Which solution will reduce the downtime for scaling exercises with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create more Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas in the cluster to handle the load during failover.
B. Set up a secondary Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in the same AWS Region. During failover, update the application to use the secondary cluster's writer endpoint.
C. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to handle the load during failover.
D. Set up an Amazon RDS proxy for the database. Update the application to use the proxy endpoint.
optionExplanations: ✗ Adding more read replicas helps read scaling and provides failover targets, but it does not by itself reduce the application's connection downtime during a writer failover.
✗ Running a separate secondary Aurora cluster and manually repointing the application to its writer endpoint adds significant operational overhead and is not a low-overhead fix.
✗ An ElastiCache for Memcached cluster caches data but does nothing to shorten the database writer failover time or preserve database connections.

✓ RDS Proxy maintains a connection pool and transparently routes connections through the new writer during failover, drastically reducing failover downtime with minimal application change and low operational overhead.

text: A company has a regional subscription-based streaming service that runs in a single AWS Region. The architecture consists of web servers and application servers on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in Auto Scaling groups behind Elastic Load Balancers. The architecture includes an Amazon Aurora global database cluster that extends across multiple Availability Zones. The company wants to expand globally and to ensure that its application has minimal downtime. Which solution will provide the MOST fault tolerance?
options: A. Extend the Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and the application tier to deploy instances in Availability Zones in a second Region. Use an Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.

B. Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Add an Aurora PostgreSQL cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.

C. Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Create an Aurora PostgreSQL database in the second Region. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the primary database to the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.

D. Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Use an Amazon Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.
optionExplanations: ✗ Extending a single Auto Scaling group across Availability Zones in a second Region is not possible. Auto Scaling groups are Region-scoped and cannot span Regions, so this design is technically invalid.

✗ A cross-Region Aurora Replica is a single replica with higher replication lag and more limited fast-failover capability than an Aurora global database; it provides less fault tolerance and is the legacy approach the global database supersedes for multi-Region resilience.

✗ Using AWS DMS to continuously replicate Aurora across Regions adds significant operational overhead and does not match the sub-second replication and managed cross-Region failover of an Aurora global database; it is inferior for fault tolerance.

✓ Deploying independent web and application tiers in a second Region, using an Aurora global database (sub-second cross-Region replication, fast secondary promotion) with Route 53 health checks and failover routing, provides the most fault tolerance with minimal downtime for global expansion.

text: A data analytics company wants to migrate its batch processing system to AWS. The company receives thousands of small data files periodically during the day through FTP. An on-premises batch job processes the data files overnight. However, the batch job takes hours to finish running. The company wants the AWS solution to process incoming data files as soon as possible with minimal changes to the FTP clients that send the files. The solution must delete the incoming data files after the files have been processed successfully. Processing for each file needs to take 3-8 minutes. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally eficient way?
options: A. Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files as objects in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the objects nightly from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Delete the objects after the job has processed the objects.

B. Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the files nightly from the EBS volume. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.

C. Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use an Amazon S3 event notification when each file arrives to invoke the job in AWS Batch. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.

D. Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files in Amazon S3 Standard. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the files and to delete the files after they are processed. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when the files arrive.
optionExplanations: ✗ Running a self-managed FTP server on EC2 and storing files in Glacier Flexible Retrieval adds server management and retrieval latency, and nightly batch processing fails the 'as soon as possible' requirement.
✗ A self-managed EC2 FTP server writing to an EBS volume with nightly AWS Batch processing keeps the slow overnight batch model and adds undifferentiated server management overhead.
✗ Although Transfer Family removes the FTP server management, S3 event notifications fire on S3 object creation, not on files written to an EBS volume, so this configuration is technically broken.

✓ AWS Transfer Family provides a managed FTP endpoint storing files in S3 with minimal client changes, and an S3 event notification invokes a Lambda function to process each file immediately and delete it; the 3-8 minute processing fits within Lambda's 15-minute limit, making this the most operationally efficient solution.

text: A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has transactional and sensitive data in its databases. The company wants to use AWS Cloud solutions to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
B. Migrate the databases to Amazon RDS Configure encryption at rest.
C. Migrate the data to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Macie for data security and protection
D. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs for data security and protection.
optionExplanations: ✗ Migrating databases to self-managed Amazon EC2 leaves the company responsible for patching, backups, and HA, which increases rather than reduces operational overhead.
✓ Amazon RDS is a fully managed service that offloads patching/backups and supports encryption at rest via AWS KMS, increasing security while reducing operational overhead for transactional data.
✗ Amazon S3 with Macie is for object storage and PII discovery, not for transactional relational database workloads.
✗ Amazon CloudWatch Logs is for log monitoring, not a data security or encryption mechanism for the database itself.

text: A company has an online gaming application that has TCP and UDP multiplayer gaming capabilities. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to point the application trafic to multiple Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in different AWS Regions. The company needs to improve application performance and decrease latency for the online game in preparation for user growth. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs. Increase the Cache-Control max-age parameter.
B. Replace the NLBs with Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Configure Route 53 to use latency-based routing.
C. Add AWS Global Accelerator in front of the NLBs. Configure a Global Accelerator endpoint to use the correct listener ports.
D. Add an Amazon API Gateway endpoint behind the NLBs. Enable API caching. Override method caching for the different stages.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon CloudFront is an HTTP/HTTPS content cache and does not support raw TCP/UDP gaming traffic; caching also does not help dynamic multiplayer sessions.
✗ Application Load Balancers operate at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and cannot handle UDP traffic required for the game.
✓ AWS Global Accelerator uses the AWS backbone and anycast IPs to route TCP and UDP traffic to the nearest healthy NLB endpoint, improving performance and reducing latency for global users.
✗ Amazon API Gateway is for HTTP/REST APIs and cannot front NLBs for TCP/UDP multiplayer gaming traffic.

text: A company needs to integrate with a third-party data feed. The data feed sends a webhook to notify an external service when new data is ready for consumption. A developer wrote an AWS Lambda function to retrieve data when the company receives a webhook callback. The developer must make the Lambda function available for the third party to call. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational eficiency?
options: A. Create a function URL for the Lambda function. Provide the Lambda function URL to the third party for the webhook.
B. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the Lambda function. Provide the ALB URL to the third party for the webhook.
C. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Attach the topic to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SNS topic to the third party for the webhook.
D. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Attach the queue to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SQS queue to the third party for the webhook.
optionExplanations: ✓ A Lambda function URL provides a dedicated HTTPS endpoint directly on the function with no extra infrastructure, the most operationally efficient way to receive a third-party webhook callback.
✗ Deploying an ALB in front of Lambda adds unnecessary cost and management overhead compared to a built-in function URL.
✗ Amazon SNS is a pub/sub messaging service that does not provide an inbound public webhook hostname that a third party can POST to.
✗ Amazon SQS is a queue accessed via the AWS API/SDK and does not expose a public hostname suitable for a third-party webhook callback.

text: A company has a workload in an AWS Region. Customers connect to and access the workload by using an Amazon API Gateway REST API. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company wants to provide individual and secure URLs for all customers. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the MOST operational eficiency? (Choose three.)
options: A. Register the required domain in a registrar. Create a wildcard custom domain name in a Route 53 hosted zone and record in the zone that points to the API Gateway endpoint.
B. Request a wildcard certificate that matches the domains in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in a different Region.
