C. Create hosted zones for each customer as required in Route 53. Create zone records that point to the API Gateway endpoint.
D. Request a wildcard certificate that matches the custom domain name in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region.
E. Create multiple API endpoints for each customer in API Gateway.
F. Create a custom domain name in API Gateway for the REST API. Import the certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).
optionExplanations: ✓ Registering the domain and creating a single wildcard custom domain name in a Route 53 hosted zone with a record pointing to the API Gateway endpoint lets one record serve every customer subdomain, which is the most operationally efficient DNS approach. Correct.

✗ Requesting the wildcard ACM certificate in a DIFFERENT Region is wrong; for a REST API custom domain the certificate must be in the same Region as the regional API (or us-east-1 for edge-optimized), not an arbitrary different Region.
✗ Creating a separate Route 53 hosted zone for every customer adds significant per-customer management overhead, which is the opposite of operational efficiency. Incorrect.
✓ Requesting a single wildcard ACM certificate in the same Region as the API matches all customer subdomains under the custom domain and avoids per-customer certificate management. Correct.
✗ Creating a separate API Gateway endpoint per customer multiplies APIs to maintain and is highly inefficient operationally. Incorrect.
✓ Creating a custom domain name in API Gateway for the REST API and importing/associating the ACM wildcard certificate is required to map the secure custom domain to the API. Correct.

text: A company stores data in Amazon S3. According to regulations, the data must not contain personally identifiable information (PII). The company recently discovered that S3 buckets have some objects that contain PII. The company needs to automatically detect PII in S3 buckets and to notify the company’s security team. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.

B. Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to the security team.

C. Use Amazon Macie. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the SensitiveData:S3Object/Personal event type from Macie findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.

D. Use Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to filter the CRITICAL event type from GuardDuty findings and to send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) notification to the security team.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon Macie discovers PII in S3, and an EventBridge rule filtering the SensitiveData finding type to notify via SNS automatically alerts the security team.
✗ Amazon GuardDuty detects threats and malicious activity, not PII content within S3 objects.
✗ Macie correctly detects PII, but routing the finding to an SQS queue does not actively notify the security team and the event filter type is also less standard than SensitiveData.
✗ Amazon GuardDuty does not perform PII content discovery, and SQS does not directly notify the security team.

text: A company wants to build a logging solution for its multiple AWS accounts. The company currently stores the logs from all accounts in a centralized account. The company has created an Amazon S3 bucket in the centralized account to store the VPC fiow logs and AWS CloudTrail logs. All logs must be highly available for 30 days for frequent analysis, retained for an additional 60 days for backup purposes, and deleted 90 days after creation. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.

B. Transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class 30 days after creation. Move all objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class after 90 days. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
C. Transition objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class 30 days after creation. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.

D. Transition objects to the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class 30 days after creation. Move all objects to the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class after 90 days. Write an expiration action that directs Amazon S3 to delete objects after 90 days.
optionExplanations: ✗ Keeping objects in S3 Standard for the entire lifecycle does not reduce cost during the 60-day backup period, so it is not the most cost-effective option.

✓ Transitioning to S3 Standard-IA at 30 days keeps logs highly available and durable across AZs at lower cost during the backup window, then deletes at 90 days, meeting the requirements cost-effectively.

✗ S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval at 30 days adds retrieval latency that conflicts with the requirement for highly available data still needed analysis-side and offers no benefit since deletion occurs at 90 days.
✗ S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, reducing availability/durability and failing the high-availability requirement for the backup retention period.

text: A company is building an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for its workloads. All secrets that are stored in Amazon EKS must be encrypted in the Kubernetes etcd key-value store. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage, rotate, and store all secrets in Amazon EKS.
B. Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable Amazon EKS KMS secrets encryption on the Amazon EKS cluster.
C. Create the Amazon EKS cluster with default options. Use the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver as an add-on.
D. Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key with the alias/aws/ebs alias. Enable default Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume encryption for the account.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets externally and does not encrypt the Kubernetes secrets stored inside the EKS etcd key-value store.
✓ Enabling EKS KMS secrets encryption with a customer KMS key provides envelope encryption of Kubernetes secrets at rest in etcd, exactly meeting the requirement.
✗ The EBS CSI driver provides persistent volume storage and does not encrypt secrets in etcd.
✗ Default EBS volume encryption protects block storage volumes, not the Kubernetes secrets stored in the EKS etcd key-value store.

text: A company wants to provide data scientists with near real-time read-only access to the company's production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The database is currently configured as a Single-AZ database. The data scientists use complex queries that will not affect the production database. The company needs a solution that is highly available. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Scale the existing production database in a maintenance window to provide enough power for the data scientists.
B. Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment with a larger secondary standby instance. Provide the data scientists access to the secondary instance.
C. Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment. Provide two additional read replicas for the data scientists.
D. Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ cluster deployment with two readable standby instances. Provide read endpoints to the data scientists.
optionExplanations: ✗ Scaling the single instance does not add high availability or a separate read target and impacts the production database during the maintenance window.
✗ The Multi-AZ instance standby is not readable; it exists only for failover, so data scientists cannot query it.
✗ A Multi-AZ instance plus two read replicas works but is more expensive and operationally heavier than a Multi-AZ DB cluster with built-in readable standbys.

✓ A Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment provides two readable standby instances with low replication lag and built-in high availability, and exposing the read endpoint offloads complex queries cost-effectively.

text: A company runs a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud that operates across three Availability Zones. The application architecture has an Application Load Balancer, an Amazon EC2 web server that hosts user session states, and a MySQL database that runs on an EC2 instance. The company expects sudden increases in application trafic. The company wants to be able to scale to meet future application capacity demands and to ensure high availability across all three Availability Zones. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

B. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

C. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon DynamoDB Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache reads. Store the session data in DynamoDB. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

D. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL in a single Availability Zone. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
optionExplanations: ✓ RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ cluster gives a highly available database, ElastiCache for Redis supports replication/HA for shared session state and read caching, and an Auto Scaling group across three AZs scales the web tier.
✗ ElastiCache for Memcached does not support replication or automatic failover, so it cannot provide highly available session storage.
✗ Migrating MySQL to DynamoDB is a major data-model change unnecessary here, and storing relational data in DynamoDB does not fit the existing MySQL application.
✗ Running RDS for MySQL in a single Availability Zone fails the high-availability requirement across three AZs.

text: A global video streaming company uses Amazon CloudFront as a content distribution network (CDN). The company wants to roll out content in a phased manner across multiple countries. The company needs to ensure that viewers who are outside the countries to which the company rolls out content are not able to view the content. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Add geographic restrictions to the content in CloudFront by using an allow list. Set up a custom error message.
B. Set up a new URL tor restricted content. Authorize access by using a signed URL and cookies. Set up a custom error message.
C. Encrypt the data for the content that the company distributes. Set up a custom error message.
D. Create a new URL for restricted content. Set up a time-restricted access policy for signed URLs.
optionExplanations: ✓ CloudFront geographic restrictions (geo-blocking) using an allow list lets you specify exactly which countries can access content, blocking all others by IP-based country lookup; a custom error message handles blocked viewers. This directly meets the phased per-country rollout requirement.

✗ Signed URLs and signed cookies control access based on possession of a signed token (e.g., time/IP), not viewer country. They cannot restrict access by the geographic location of the viewer, so they do not meet the country-based requirement.
✗ Encrypting the content protects data confidentiality but does nothing to determine or restrict a viewer's country, so it cannot prevent out-of-country viewers from accessing content.
✗ A time-restricted signed URL policy limits access based on time windows, not geography, so it cannot block viewers based on their country.

text: A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to improve its on-premises disaster recovery (DR) configuration. The company's core production business application uses Microsoft SQL Server Standard, which runs on a virtual machine (VM). The application has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 30 seconds or fewer and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 60 minutes. The DR solution needs to minimize costs wherever possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure a multi-site active/active setup between the on-premises server and AWS by using Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise with Always On availability groups.
B. Configure a warm standby Amazon RDS for SQL Server database on AWS. Configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to use change data capture (CDC).
C. Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery configured to replicate disk changes to AWS as a pilot light.
D. Use third-party backup software to capture backups every night. Store a secondary set of backups in Amazon S3.
optionExplanations: ✗ SQL Server Enterprise with Always On in a multi-site active/active setup requires costly Enterprise licensing and full standby infrastructure, conflicting with the cost-minimization requirement.
✗ A warm standby RDS with DMS CDC keeps a running database continuously and adds DMS overhead/cost, which is more expensive than a pilot light approach.
✓ AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates disk changes (sub-minute RPO) using a low-cost pilot light, then launches instances on failover within the 60-minute RTO, minimizing cost.
✗ Nightly backups to S3 yield an RPO of up to 24 hours, far exceeding the required 30-second RPO.

text: A company has an on-premises server that uses an Oracle database to process and store customer information. The company wants to use an AWS database service to achieve higher availability and to improve application performance. The company also wants to ofioad reporting from its primary database system. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally eficient way?
options: A. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create an Amazon RDS DB instance in multiple AWS Regions. Point the reporting functions toward a separate DB instance from the primary DB instance.
B. Use Amazon RDS in a Single-AZ deployment to create an Oracle database. Create a read replica in the same zone as the primary DB instance. Direct the reporting functions to the read replica.
C. Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ cluster deployment to create an Oracle database. Direct the reporting functions to use the reader instance in the cluster deployment.
D. Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ instance deployment to create an Amazon Aurora database. Direct the reporting functions to the reader instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS DMS deploying RDS instances across multiple Regions is a migration/cross-Region pattern with high operational overhead and does not natively provide Multi-AZ HA; pointing reporting at a separate DB instance is not a managed read replica, so this is not the most operationally efficient choice.
✗ A Single-AZ RDS deployment does not provide higher availability, and placing the read replica in the same AZ as the primary fails the availability and resilience goals.

✓ RDS Multi-AZ cluster deployment provides higher availability with a standby plus readable reader instance, letting reporting be offloaded to the reader with minimal operational effort while keeping a managed Oracle-style RDS database; this is the most operationally efficient option presented.

✗ Amazon Aurora does not support the Oracle engine (only MySQL/PostgreSQL compatibility), and a Multi-AZ instance deployment has no readable standby, so directing reporting to reader instances does not apply here.

text: A company wants to build a web application on AWS. Client access requests to the website are not predictable and can be idle for a long time. Only customers who have paid a subscription fee can have the ability to sign in and use the web application. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)
options: A. Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve user information from Amazon DynamoDB. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API calls to the Lambda function.

B. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service behind an Application Load Balancer to retrieve user information from Amazon RDS. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API calls to the Lambda function.
C. Create an Amazon Cognito user pool to authenticate users.
D. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool to authenticate users.
E. Use AWS Amplify to serve the frontend web content with HTML, CSS, and JS. Use an integrated Amazon CloudFront configuration.
F. Use Amazon S3 static web hosting with PHP, CSS, and JS. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the frontend web content.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Lambda with API Gateway and DynamoDB is fully serverless and pay-per-use, scaling to zero during idle periods, making it the most cost-effective backend for unpredictable traffic.

✗ An ECS service behind an Application Load Balancer with RDS runs continuously and incurs cost even when idle (ALB hourly charges and always-on RDS), so it is not cost-effective for unpredictable/idle traffic; the option is also self-contradictory referencing Lambda.
✓ An Amazon Cognito user pool is a managed user directory that authenticates users at sign-in, which is exactly what is needed to gate access to paid subscribers.

✗ An Amazon Cognito identity pool provides temporary AWS credentials for authorization to AWS resources (federated identities), not user sign-in authentication, so it does not satisfy the subscriber sign-in requirement.
✓ AWS Amplify hosting with integrated CloudFront cost-effectively serves the static HTML/CSS/JS frontend with global CDN delivery, fitting a serverless web app.
✗ Amazon S3 static website hosting cannot execute server-side PHP code, so using PHP makes this option technically invalid for static hosting.

text: A media company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver content over the internet. The company wants only premium customers to have access to the media streams and file content. The company stores all content in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company also delivers content on demand to customers for a specific purpose, such as movie rentals or music downloads. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Generate and provide S3 signed cookies to premium customers.
B. Generate and provide CloudFront signed URLs to premium customers.
C. Use origin access control (OAC) to limit the access of non-premium customers.
D. Generate and activate field-level encryption to block non-premium customers.
optionExplanations: ✗ There is no such thing as S3 signed cookies for CloudFront access; signed cookies are a CloudFront feature, and cookies are best for granting access to many files rather than individual on-demand items.
✓ CloudFront signed URLs restrict access to individual files and are ideal for on-demand single-item delivery such as a movie rental or music download to a premium customer.
✗ Origin access control (OAC) only restricts S3 so the bucket is reachable solely through CloudFront; it does not differentiate premium from non-premium end users.
✗ CloudFront field-level encryption encrypts specific sensitive form fields end-to-end; it does not control or block viewer access to content.

text: A company runs Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS accounts that are individually bled. The company recently purchased a Savings Pian. Because of changes in the company’s business requirements, the company has decommissioned a large number of EC2 instances. The company wants to use its Savings Plan discounts on its other AWS accounts. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. From the AWS Account Management Console of the management account, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section.
B. From the AWS Account Management Console of the account that purchased the existing Savings Plan, turn on discount sharing from the billing preferences section. Include all accounts.
C. From the AWS Organizations management account, use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Savings Plan with other accounts.
D. Create an organization in AWS Organizations in a new payer account. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.

E. Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the existing AWS account with the existing EC2 instances and Savings Plan. Invite the other AWS accounts to join the organization from the management account.
optionExplanations: ✓ Discount sharing (RI and Savings Plan discount sharing) is enabled from the billing preferences of the AWS Organizations management/payer account, not from a member account, so turning it on from the management account's billing preferences is the correct way to share Savings Plan discounts across accounts.

✗ Savings Plan discount sharing can only be enabled by the management (payer) account; the account that merely purchased the Savings Plan (a member account) cannot enable organization-wide discount sharing from its own billing preferences, so this is incorrect.

✗ AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) shares resources like subnets, Transit Gateways, and License Manager configurations; it does not share Savings Plan or Reserved Instance billing discounts, which are handled through Organizations consolidated billing and discount sharing preferences.

✗ A new, empty payer account would not own the existing Savings Plan, so the purchased Savings Plan's discounts would not be associated with consolidated billing; the organization should be created on the existing account that holds the Savings Plan, making this incorrect.

✓ Creating the AWS Organization in the existing account that holds the EC2 instances and Savings Plan makes that account the management/payer account, and inviting the other accounts lets consolidated billing and discount sharing apply the unused Savings Plan discounts to those accounts.

text: A retail company uses a regional Amazon API Gateway API for its public REST APIs. The API Gateway endpoint is a custom domain name that points to an Amazon Route 53 alias record. A solutions architect needs to create a solution that has minimal effects on customers and minimal data loss to release the new version of APIs. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a canary release deployment stage for API Gateway. Deploy the latest API version. Point an appropriate percentage of trafic to the canary stage. After API verification, promote the canary stage to the production stage.

B. Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI YAML file format. Use the import-to-update operation in merge mode into the API in API Gateway. Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.

C. Create a new API Gateway endpoint with a new version of the API in OpenAPI JSON file format. Use the import-to-update operation in overwrite mode into the API in API Gateway. Deploy the new version of the API to the production stage.

D. Create a new API Gateway endpoint with new versions of the API definitions. Create a custom domain name for the new API Gateway API. Point the Route 53 alias record to the new API Gateway API custom domain name.
optionExplanations: ✓ A canary release deployment routes a small percentage of traffic to the new version for verification, minimizing customer impact and data loss, then promotes the canary to production.
✗ Importing in merge mode and deploying straight to production exposes all users to the new version at once with no gradual rollout, increasing risk to customers.
✗ Importing in overwrite mode replaces the existing definition entirely and deploys to production immediately, risking customer impact and loss with no canary safeguard.
✗ Creating a new endpoint and repointing the Route 53 alias is a hard cutover with no traffic-percentage control, providing no gradual validation and risking data loss.

text: A company wants to direct its users to a backup static error page if the company's primary website is unavailable. The primary website's DNS records are hosted in Amazon Route 53. The domain is pointing to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company needs a solution that minimizes changes and infrastructure overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Update the Route 53 records to use a latency routing policy. Add a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket to the records so that the trafic is sent to the most responsive endpoints.

B. Set up a Route 53 active-passive failover configuration. Direct trafic to a static error page that is hosted in an Amazon S3 bucket when Route 53 health checks determine that the ALB endpoint is unhealthy.

C. Set up a Route 53 active-active configuration with the ALB and an Amazon EC2 instance that hosts a static error page as endpoints. Configure Route 53 to send requests to the instance only if the health checks fail for the ALB.

D. Update the Route 53 records to use a multivalue answer routing policy. Create a health check. Direct trafic to the website if the health check passes. Direct trafic to a static error page that is hosted in Amazon S3 if the health check does not pass.
optionExplanations: ✗ A latency routing policy chooses the lowest-latency endpoint, not a failover behavior, so it will not reliably divert traffic to the error page only when the ALB is down.

✓ Route 53 active-passive failover with health checks on the ALB and an S3-hosted static error page as the passive record sends users to the backup page only when the primary is unhealthy, with minimal changes and overhead.

✗ Adding and maintaining an EC2 instance to host the static error page increases infrastructure overhead unnecessarily compared to an S3 static page, and active-active is not the right failover model here.
✗ A multivalue answer routing policy returns multiple healthy records for client-side balancing; it does not provide clean primary-to-backup failover to a single error page.

text: A recent analysis of a company's IT expenses highlights the need to reduce backup costs. The company's chief information oficer wants to simplify the on-premises backup infrastructure and reduce costs by eliminating the use of physical backup tapes. The company must preserve the existing investment in the on-premises backup applications and workfiows. What should a solutions architect recommend?
options: A. Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
B. Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the NFS interface.
C. Set up an Amazon EFS file system that connects with the backup applications using the iSCSI interface.
D. Set up AWS Storage Gateway to connect with the backup applications using the iSCSI-virtual tape library (VTL) interface.
optionExplanations: ✗ Storage Gateway's NFS (File Gateway) interface presents file shares, not virtual tapes, so it does not preserve the existing tape-based backup applications and workflows.
✗ Amazon EFS is a file system over NFS and is not a replacement for physical tape backups; it does not integrate with tape-oriented backup software workflows.
✗ Amazon EFS does not provide an iSCSI interface, and even as a file system it does not emulate tapes for existing backup applications.

✓ AWS Storage Gateway's Tape Gateway exposes an iSCSI virtual tape library (VTL), which lets existing on-premises backup applications write to virtual tapes stored in S3/Glacier, eliminating physical tapes while preserving workflows.

text: A company has data collection sensors at different locations. The data collection sensors stream a high volume of data to the company. The company wants to design a platform on AWS to ingest and process high-volume streaming data. The solution must be scalable and support data collection in near real time. The company must store the data in Amazon S3 for future reporting. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
B. Use AWS Glue to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
C. Use AWS Lambda to deliver streaming data and store the data to Amazon S3.
D. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed service that ingests high-volume streaming data and delivers it to S3 in near real time with minimal operational overhead.
✗ AWS Glue is an ETL/data-catalog service oriented to batch processing, not a managed high-volume streaming ingestion-to-S3 delivery service.
✗ Building custom Lambda functions to ingest and persist the stream adds significant code and operational overhead compared with a managed delivery service.
✗ AWS DMS migrates and replicates databases; it is not designed to ingest sensor streaming data into S3.

text: A company has separate AWS accounts for its finance, data analytics, and development departments. Because of costs and security concerns, the company wants to control which services each AWS account can use. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager templates to control which AWS services each department can use.
B. Create organization units (OUs) for each department in AWS Organizations. Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the OUs.
C. Use AWS CloudFormation to automatically provision only the AWS services that each department can use.
D. Set up a list of products in AWS Service Catalog in the AWS accounts to manage and control the usage of specific AWS services.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Systems Manager manages and automates operations on resources; it does not provide org-wide guardrails to restrict which AWS services an account may use.
✓ Organizing accounts into OUs in AWS Organizations and attaching service control policies (SCPs) centrally enforces which AWS services each department can use with the least operational overhead.
✗ AWS CloudFormation provisions infrastructure but does not prevent an account from using services outside its templates, so it cannot enforce service restrictions.
✗ AWS Service Catalog curates approved products for self-service provisioning but does not block direct use of other AWS services, requiring more ongoing management.

text: A company has created a multi-tier application for its ecommerce website. The website uses an Application Load Balancer that resides in the public subnets, a web tier in the public subnets, and a MySQL cluster hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets. The MySQL database needs to retrieve product catalog and pricing information that is hosted on the internet by a third-party provider. A solutions architect must devise a strategy that maximizes security without increasing operational overhead. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy a NAT instance in the VPC. Route all the internet-based trafic through the NAT instance.
B. Deploy a NAT gateway in the public subnets. Modify the private subnet route table to direct all internet-bound trafic to the NAT gateway.
C. Configure an internet gateway and attach it to the VPModify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound trafic to the internet gateway.
D. Configure a virtual private gateway and attach it to the VPC. Modify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound trafic to the virtual private gateway.
optionExplanations: ✗ A NAT instance does enable outbound-only internet access but requires you to manage, patch, and scale the EC2 instance, adding operational overhead.

✓ A managed NAT gateway in a public subnet with the private route table pointing internet-bound traffic to it gives the database outbound-only internet access while keeping it unreachable from the internet, with no instance to manage.
✗ Routing the private subnet directly to an internet gateway would give the database instances public reachability, reducing security.
✗ A virtual private gateway is for VPN/Direct Connect connectivity to on-premises networks, not for reaching a third-party provider on the public internet.

text: A company is using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt AWS Lambda environment variables. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the required permissions are in place to decrypt and use the environment variables. Which steps must the solutions architect take to implement the correct permissions? (Choose two.)
options: A. Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda resource policy.
B. Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda execution role.
C. Add AWS KMS permissions in the Lambda function policy.
D. Allow the Lambda execution role in the AWS KMS key policy.
E. Allow the Lambda resource policy in the AWS KMS key policy.
optionExplanations: ✗ A Lambda resource policy controls who can invoke the function; it does not grant the function permission to call KMS to decrypt environment variables.
✓ The Lambda execution role needs kms:Decrypt permission so the function's identity is authorized to decrypt the encrypted environment variables.
✗ The Lambda function (resource) policy governs invocation permissions, not the function's ability to use KMS.
✓ The KMS key policy must allow the Lambda execution role to use the key, since KMS requires both IAM identity permissions and key policy authorization.
✗ A KMS key policy grants principals (roles/users), not a Lambda resource policy; you cannot reference a resource policy in a key policy.

text: A company has a financial application that produces reports. The reports average 50 KB in size and are stored in Amazon S3. The reports are frequently accessed during the first week after production and must be stored for several years. The reports must be retrievable within 6 hours. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Glacier after 7 days.
B. Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 7 days.
C. Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to transition the reports to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) and S3 Glacier.
D. Use S3 Standard. Use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the reports to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 7 days.
optionExplanations: ✓ S3 Standard handles the frequent first-week access, and transitioning to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 7 days gives the lowest long-term storage cost while standard retrieval (3-5 hours) satisfies the 6-hour retrieval requirement. Correct.
✗ S3 Standard-IA storage is far more expensive per GB than Glacier for multi-year retention, so it is not the MOST cost-effective option for archival storage. Incorrect.

✗ S3 Intelligent-Tiering charges a per-object monitoring fee and does not auto-tier objects smaller than 128 KB; with 50 KB reports these stay in the frequent-access tier and incur extra monitoring costs, making it less cost-effective. Incorrect.
✗ S3 Glacier Deep Archive is cheapest for storage but its standard retrieval takes up to 12 hours, violating the 6-hour retrieval requirement. Incorrect.

text: A company needs to optimize the cost of its Amazon EC2 instances. The company also needs to change the type and family of its EC2 instances every 2-3 months. What should the company do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Purchase Partial Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3-year term.
B. Purchase a No Upfront Compute Savings Plan for a 1-year term.
C. Purchase All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 1-year term.
D. Purchase an All Upfront EC2 Instance Savings Plan for a 1-year term.
optionExplanations: ✗ A 3-year Partial Upfront Reserved Instance locks you into specific terms and lacks the flexibility to freely change instance family and type every few months.

✓ A No Upfront Compute Savings Plan provides discounted rates while allowing the company to change instance type, family, size, region, and even compute service, fitting the need to switch every 2-3 months.
✗ All Upfront Reserved Instances commit capital and are tied to specific instance attributes, conflicting with frequent changes of instance type and family.
✗ An EC2 Instance Savings Plan locks you to a specific instance family in a region, so changing families every few months would not retain the discount.

text: A solutions architect needs to review a company's Amazon S3 buckets to discover personally identifiable information (PII). The company stores the PII data in the us-east-1 Region and us-west-2 Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Configure Amazon Macie in each Region. Create a job to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
B. Configure AWS Security Hub for all Regions. Create an AWS Config rule to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
C. Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
D. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon Macie is the purpose-built service for discovering PII in S3 using managed data identifiers; since Macie is regional, configuring it in each Region (us-east-1 and us-west-2) and running discovery jobs meets the requirement with the least overhead.
✗ Wrong. AWS Security Hub aggregates security findings and AWS Config evaluates resource configurations; neither inspects object contents to find PII inside S3 data.
✗ Wrong. Amazon Inspector scans EC2, ECR images, and Lambda for software vulnerabilities and network exposure; it does not classify or discover PII in S3 objects.
✗ Wrong. Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service analyzing logs for malicious activity (including S3 anomalies), but it does not classify object contents to discover PII.

text: A company's SAP application has a backend SQL Server database in an on-premises environment. The company wants to migrate its on-premises application and database server to AWS. The company needs an instance type that meets the high demands of its SAP database. On-premises performance data shows that both the SAP application and the database have high memory utilization. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use the compute optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.
B. Use the storage optimized instance family for both the application and the database.
C. Use the memory optimized instance family for both the application and the database.
D. Use the high performance computing (HPC) optimized instance family for the application. Use the memory optimized instance family for the database.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. Compute optimized instances suit CPU-bound workloads; the application here has high memory utilization, so compute optimized is a poor fit for the app tier.
✗ Wrong. Storage optimized instances target high sequential/random disk I/O and throughput, not the high memory demands described for both the application and database.

✓ Both the SAP application and the SQL Server database show high memory utilization, so the memory optimized instance family (e.g., R-series / SAP-certified X-series) is the right choice for both tiers.
✗ Wrong. HPC optimized instances are built for tightly coupled parallel compute and high network throughput, not for a memory-bound SAP application tier.

text: A company runs an application in a VPC with public and private subnets. The VPC extends across multiple Availability Zones. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application uses an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. A solutions architect needs to design a secure solution to establish a connection between the EC2 instances and the SQS queue. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the private subnets. Add to the endpoint a security group that has an inbound access rule that allows trafic from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.

B. Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets. Attach to the interface endpoint a VPC endpoint policy that allows access from the EC2 instances that are in the private subnets.

C. Implement an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Configure the endpoint to use the public subnets. Attach an Amazon SQS access policy to the interface VPC endpoint that allows requests from only a specified VPC endpoint.
D. Implement a gateway endpoint for Amazon SQS. Add a NAT gateway to the private subnets. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instances that allows access to the SQS queue.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon SQS supports interface VPC endpoints (powered by AWS PrivateLink). Placing the endpoint in the private subnets where the EC2 instances reside and attaching a security group whose inbound rule allows traffic from the EC2 instances provides a secure, private connection that does not traverse the internet.

✗ The interface endpoint should be placed in the private subnets near the EC2 instances, not the public subnets. The instances are in private subnets, so configuring the endpoint in public subnets does not align with the secure private design, and a VPC endpoint policy controls API actions rather than network-level access.

✗ Same issue of using public subnets. An SQS resource (access) policy controls which principals can act on the queue but is not the network mechanism for connecting private instances; placing the endpoint in public subnets is not the secure design intended here.

✗ Amazon SQS does not support gateway VPC endpoints; gateway endpoints exist only for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB. Adding a NAT gateway would route traffic over the public internet, which is less secure and unnecessary.

text: A solutions architect is using an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy a three-tier web application. The web application consists of a web tier and an application tier that stores and retrieves user data in Amazon DynamoDB tables. The web and application tiers are hosted on Amazon EC2 instances, and the database tier is not publicly accessible. The application EC2 instances need to access the DynamoDB tables without exposing API credentials in the template. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM role to read the DynamoDB tables. Associate the role with the application instances by referencing an instance profile.

B. Create an IAM role that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Add the role to the EC2 instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the application instances.

C. Use the parameter section in the AWS CloudFormation template to have the user input access and secret keys from an already-created IAM user that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables.

D. Create an IAM user in the AWS CloudFormation template that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Use the GetAtt function to retrieve the access and secret keys, and pass them to the application instances through the user data.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. The application stores and retrieves user data, so it needs read and write access; a role granting only read access to DynamoDB would not satisfy the write requirement.

✓ An IAM role with read and write permissions attached via an EC2 instance profile lets the application instances access DynamoDB using temporary credentials without exposing any API keys in the template.
✗ Wrong. Passing static access and secret keys through CloudFormation parameters exposes long-lived credentials and contradicts the requirement to avoid exposing API credentials.
✗ Wrong. Creating an IAM user and passing its access/secret keys via user data exposes static credentials; GetAtt also cannot retrieve a secret key in this manner, and roles are the correct approach.

text: A solutions architect manages an analytics application. The application stores large amounts of semistructured data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect wants to use parallel data processing to process the data more quickly. The solutions architect also wants to use information that is stored in an Amazon Redshift database to enrich the data. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon Athena to process the S3 data. Use AWS Glue with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
B. Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon EMR with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
C. Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to move the S3 data into Amazon Redshift so that the data can be enriched.
D. Use AWS Glue to process the S3 data. Use AWS Lake Formation with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Athena queries S3 with SQL but is serverless interactive querying, not the parallel data-processing engine implied; AWS Glue can connect to Redshift, but combining two services adds overhead and Glue is ETL rather than the parallel-compute model the scenario favors.

✓ Amazon EMR runs distributed frameworks (Spark/Hadoop) that provide true parallel data processing of large semistructured S3 data, and the same EMR cluster can connect to Amazon Redshift (via the Spark-Redshift/JDBC connector) to read and enrich the data in one solution. This is the best fit.

✗ Amazon EMR correctly handles parallel processing, but Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is for real-time streaming ingestion, not for moving existing static S3 data into Redshift; this misuses Kinesis and adds unnecessary complexity.

✗ AWS Glue can process S3 data via Spark jobs, but AWS Lake Formation is a data lake governance/permissions and cataloging service, not an enrichment-with-Redshift mechanism, so it does not satisfy the requirement to enrich using Redshift data.

text: A company has two VPCs that are located in the us-west-2 Region within the same AWS account. The company needs to allow network trafic between these VPCs. Approximately 500 GB of data transfer will occur between the VPCs each month. What is the MOST cost-effective solution to connect these VPCs?
options: A. Implement AWS Transit Gateway to connect the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the transit gateway for inter-VPC communication.
B. Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPN tunnel for inter-VPC communication.
C. Set up a VPC peering connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPC peering connection for inter-VPC communication.
D. Set up a 1 GB AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the Direct Connect connection for inter-VPC communication.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. Transit Gateway adds hourly attachment charges plus data processing fees, making it more expensive than peering for just two VPCs in the same Region.
✗ Wrong. A Site-to-Site VPN incurs hourly tunnel charges and adds unnecessary complexity for connecting two same-account, same-Region VPCs.
✓ VPC peering between two VPCs in the same Region has no per-hour charge, and intra-Region data transfer over peering is the most cost-effective option for ~500 GB/month.
✗ Wrong. Direct Connect is for connecting on-premises networks to AWS, not for inter-VPC connectivity, and it carries port-hour and circuit costs that are far more expensive.

text: A company hosts multiple applications on AWS for different product lines. The applications use different compute resources, including Amazon EC2 instances and Application Load Balancers. The applications run in different AWS accounts under the same organization in AWS Organizations across multiple AWS Regions. Teams for each product line have tagged each compute resource in the individual accounts. The company wants more details about the cost for each product line from the consolidated billing feature in Organizations. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Select a specific AWS generated tag in the AWS Billing console.
B. Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Billing console.
C. Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Resource Groups console.
D. Activate the selected tag from each AWS account.
E. Activate the selected tag from the Organizations management account.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. The teams applied their own user-defined tags to resources, not AWS-generated tags, so selecting an AWS-generated cost allocation tag would not break down cost by product line.
✓ The product-line cost breakdown comes from activating the team-applied user-defined tag as a cost allocation tag in the AWS Billing console.
✗ Wrong. Cost allocation tags are activated in the Billing console, not the Resource Groups console; Resource Groups does not enable tags for billing.
✗ Wrong. Cost allocation tags are activated centrally in the consolidated billing (management) account, not individually from each member account.
✓ User-defined cost allocation tags must be activated from the Organizations management (payer) account so they appear in consolidated billing/Cost Explorer.

text: A company's solutions architect is designing an AWS multi-account solution that uses AWS Organizations. The solutions architect has organized the company's accounts into organizational units (OUs). The solutions architect needs a solution that will identify any changes to the OU hierarchy. The solution also needs to notify the company's operations team of any changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use account drift notifications to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
B. Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use AWS Config aggregated rules to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
C. Use AWS Service Catalog to create accounts in Organizations. Use an AWS CloudTrail organization trail to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
D. Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create accounts in Organizations. Use the drift detection operation on a stack to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Control Tower governs OUs and emits drift notifications when the OU hierarchy or structure changes, with managed SNS notifications providing the least operational overhead.
✗ Wrong. AWS Config aggregated rules evaluate resource configurations within accounts; they are not designed to detect changes to the Organizations OU hierarchy and require more setup.

✗ Wrong. While a CloudTrail organization trail can log Organizations API events, building detection and notification on top of raw CloudTrail events adds more operational overhead than Control Tower drift notifications.
✗ Wrong. CloudFormation drift detection compares stack resources to templates and does not natively track or notify on OU hierarchy changes; it also requires manual or scheduled invocation.

text: A company's website handles millions of requests each day, and the number of requests continues to increase. A solutions architect needs to improve the response time of the web application. The solutions architect determines that the application needs to decrease latency when retrieving product details from the Amazon DynamoDB table. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
options: A. Set up a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Route all read requests through DAX.
B. Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Redis between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Redis.
C. Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Memcached.
D. Set up Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table, and have AWS Lambda read from the table and populate Amazon ElastiCache. Route all read requests through ElastiCache.
optionExplanations: ✓ DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, in-memory cache purpose-built for DynamoDB; routing reads through DAX cuts latency to microseconds with minimal operational overhead and no application caching logic.
✗ Wrong. ElastiCache for Redis requires you to manage cache population, invalidation, and the cluster yourself, adding operational overhead compared to the DynamoDB-native DAX.
✗ Wrong. ElastiCache for Memcached likewise requires custom cache-aside logic and cluster management, more overhead than the purpose-built DAX cache.
✗ Wrong. Using DynamoDB Streams plus Lambda to populate ElastiCache builds a complex pipeline with significant operational overhead, the opposite of the least-effort requirement.

text: A solutions architect needs to ensure that API calls to Amazon DynamoDB from Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC do not travel across the internet. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)
options: A. Create a route table entry for the endpoint.
B. Create a gateway endpoint for DynamoDB.
C. Create an interface endpoint for Amazon EC2.
D. Create an elastic network interface for the endpoint in each of the subnets of the VPC.
E. Create a security group entry in the endpoint's security group to provide access.
optionExplanations: ✓ A gateway endpoint for DynamoDB works via route table entries, so you must add a route table entry pointing to the endpoint prefix list to keep traffic off the internet.
✓ DynamoDB is accessed privately through a gateway VPC endpoint (one of only two services, with S3, that use gateway endpoints), keeping API calls on the AWS network.
✗ Wrong. An interface endpoint for Amazon EC2 relates to the EC2 control-plane API, not to DynamoDB access, so it does not satisfy this requirement.
✗ Wrong. Gateway endpoints (used by DynamoDB) do not create elastic network interfaces in subnets; ENIs are a feature of interface endpoints.
✗ Wrong. Gateway endpoints do not use security groups; security group rules apply to interface endpoints, so this step is unnecessary for a DynamoDB gateway endpoint.

text: A company runs its applications on both Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters and on-premises Kubernetes clusters. The company wants to view all clusters and workloads from a central location. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to collect and group the cluster information.
B. Use Amazon EKS Connector to register and connect all Kubernetes clusters.
C. Use AWS Systems Manager to collect and view the cluster information.
D. Use Amazon EKS Anywhere as the primary cluster to view the other clusters with native Kubernetes commands.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. CloudWatch Container Insights collects metrics and logs but does not provide a unified single view to register and manage both EKS and external on-premises Kubernetes clusters and their workloads.
✓ Amazon EKS Connector registers external (including on-premises) Kubernetes clusters with EKS so all clusters and workloads can be viewed centrally in the EKS console with minimal overhead.
✗ Wrong. AWS Systems Manager manages instances and operational tasks, not centralized visualization of Kubernetes clusters and workloads across EKS and on-premises.
✗ Wrong. EKS Anywhere is software to run Kubernetes on-premises; it does not serve as a central console to view and manage other clusters.

text: A company is building an ecommerce application and needs to store sensitive customer information. The company needs to give customers the ability to complete purchase transactions on the website. The company also needs to ensure that sensitive customer data is protected, even from database administrators. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Store sensitive data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use EBS encryption to encrypt the data. Use an IAM instance role to restrict access.
B. Store sensitive data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) client-side encryption to encrypt the data.
C. Store sensitive data in Amazon S3. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) server-side encryption to encrypt the data. Use S3 bucket policies to restrict access.
D. Store sensitive data in Amazon FSx for Windows Server. Mount the file share on application servers. Use Windows file permissions to restrict access.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. EBS encryption protects data at rest at the volume level but the database engine and administrators still see plaintext data, so it does not protect sensitive data from database administrators.

✓ Storing data in RDS for MySQL with AWS KMS client-side encryption means the application encrypts fields before they reach the database, so the stored ciphertext is unreadable even to database administrators.

✗ Wrong. S3 with KMS server-side encryption stores the data encrypted at rest, but it is decrypted on access and is not a transactional database for completing purchase transactions, and admins with access still see plaintext.

✗ Wrong. FSx for Windows Server with Windows file permissions controls access but does not protect contents from administrators, and it is a file share rather than a transactional database for purchases.

text: A company has an on-premises MySQL database that handles transactional data. The company is migrating the database to the AWS Cloud. The migrated database must maintain compatibility with the company's applications that use the database. The migrated database also must scale automatically during periods of increased demand. Which migration solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use native MySQL tools to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Configure elastic storage scaling.
B. Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift by using the mysqldump utility. Turn on Auto Scaling for the Amazon Redshift cluster.
C. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon Aurora. Turn on Aurora Auto Scaling.
D. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure an Auto Scaling policy.
optionExplanations: ✗ RDS for MySQL maintains application compatibility, but its storage can auto-scale only for capacity, not compute; it does not automatically scale to handle increased demand the way Aurora Auto Scaling does, making it weaker than C.
✗ Amazon Redshift is a columnar data warehouse for analytics, not a transactional MySQL-compatible engine, so it breaks application compatibility and is wrong.

✓ AWS DMS can migrate MySQL to Aurora MySQL (MySQL-compatible, preserving application compatibility), and Aurora Auto Scaling automatically adds read replicas during demand spikes, meeting both requirements.
✗ DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store with no MySQL/SQL compatibility, so migrating to it would break the existing applications.

text: A company runs multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC across two Availability Zones. The instances host applications that use a hierarchical directory structure. The applications need to read and write rapidly and concurrently to shared storage. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Allow access from all the EC2 instances in the VPC.
B. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system from each EC2 instance.
C. Create a file system on a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Attach the EBS volume to all the EC2 instances.
D. Create file systems on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that are attached to each EC2 instance. Synchronize the EBS volumes across the different EC2 instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon S3 is object storage with a flat namespace and no POSIX file semantics, so it does not support a true hierarchical directory structure with rapid concurrent file reads/writes.

✓ Amazon EFS is a managed POSIX file system that can be concurrently mounted by many EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones, providing the shared hierarchical storage with concurrent read/write access required.

✗ An io2 EBS volume cannot be simultaneously attached as a shared file system to many instances across two AZs (EBS is AZ-bound and Multi-Attach is limited to one AZ and not a managed shared file system), so it fails the concurrent shared-access requirement.
✗ Per-instance EBS volumes with manual synchronization adds heavy operational overhead and does not provide true concurrent shared access, so it does not meet the requirement.

text: A solutions architect is designing a workload that will store hourly energy consumption by business tenants in a building. The sensors will feed a database through HTTP requests that will add up usage for each tenant. The solutions architect must use managed services when possible. The workload will receive more features in the future as the solutions architect adds independent components. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table.

B. Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon S3 bucket to store the processed data.
C. Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions to receive the data from the sensors, process the data, and store the data in a Microsoft SQL Server Express database on an Amazon EC2 instance.

D. Use an Elastic Load Balancer that is supported by an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to receive and process the data from the sensors. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) shared file system to store the processed data.
optionExplanations: ✓ API Gateway plus Lambda plus DynamoDB is a fully managed, serverless, event-driven architecture with the least operational overhead and easily extends with new independent components, meeting all requirements.
✗ An ELB with an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances requires managing servers, patching, and scaling, which is far more operational overhead than a serverless approach.
✗ Running SQL Server Express on an EC2 instance means managing the OS and database server, adding significant operational overhead compared to a managed datastore.
✗ ELB with EC2 Auto Scaling plus EFS still requires managing EC2 fleets, so it has more operational overhead than the serverless option.

text: A solutions architect is designing the storage architecture for a new web application used for storing and viewing engineering drawings. All application components will be deployed on the AWS infrastructure. The application design must support caching to minimize the amount of time that users wait for the engineering drawings to load. The application must be able to store petabytes of data. Which combination of storage and caching should the solutions architect use?
options: A. Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront
B. Amazon S3 Glacier with Amazon ElastiCache
C. Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes with Amazon CloudFront
D. AWS Storage Gateway with Amazon ElastiCache
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon S3 provides virtually unlimited (petabyte-scale) durable object storage, and Amazon CloudFront caches the engineering drawings at edge locations to minimize load time, meeting both requirements.

✗ S3 Glacier is archival storage with retrieval delays unsuitable for interactive viewing, and ElastiCache is an in-memory cache not designed to front static file downloads, so this fails the low-latency viewing need.
✗ EBS volumes are block storage limited in size per volume and attached to single instances, so they cannot scale to petabytes for a web application backing store.

✗ Storage Gateway is for hybrid on-premises-to-cloud storage integration, and ElastiCache is not a content delivery cache, so this combination does not fit a cloud-native petabyte web store with edge caching.

text: An Amazon EventBridge rule targets a third-party API. The third-party API has not received any incoming trafic. A solutions architect needs to determine whether the rule conditions are being met and if the rule's target is being invoked. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Check for metrics in Amazon CloudWatch in the namespace for AWS/Events.
B. Review events in the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue.
C. Check for the events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
D. Check the trails in AWS CloudTrail for the EventBridge events.
optionExplanations: ✓ EventBridge publishes metrics such as TriggeredRules, Invocations, and FailedInvocations to the AWS/Events namespace in CloudWatch, which lets you confirm whether the rule matched events and whether its target was invoked.
✗ An SQS dead-letter queue only captures failed deliveries and only if one is configured; it does not tell you whether the rule's conditions were met or whether invocations occurred in general.
✗ EventBridge does not write rule-matching or invocation activity to CloudWatch Logs unless explicitly configured as a target, so logs would not reliably show whether the rule fired.
✗ CloudTrail records management API calls (control plane), not the runtime matching of EventBridge rules or target invocation counts, so it does not answer whether the rule conditions were met.

text: A company has a large workload that runs every Friday evening. The workload runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in two Availability Zones in the us-east-1 Region. Normally, the company must run no more than two instances at all times. However, the company wants to scale up to six instances each Friday to handle a regularly repeating increased workload. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create a reminder in Amazon EventBridge to scale the instances.
B. Create an Auto Scaling group that has a scheduled action.
C. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses manual scaling.
D. Create an Auto Scaling group that uses automatic scaling.
optionExplanations: ✗ An EventBridge reminder does not perform scaling itself; it would still require additional automation, adding overhead, so it is not the simplest solution.
✓ An Auto Scaling group with a scheduled action lets you predictably scale up to six instances each Friday and back down on a recurring schedule with the least operational overhead.
✗ Manual scaling requires a person to intervene every Friday, which is operationally burdensome and error-prone.
✗ Dynamic/automatic scaling reacts to metrics rather than a known recurring schedule, so it is less precise and less efficient than a scheduled action for a predictable weekly event.

text: A company is creating a REST API. The company has strict requirements for the use of TLS. The company requires TLSv1.3 on the API endpoints. The company also requires a specific public third-party certificate authority (CA) to sign the TLS certificate. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use a local machine to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CImport the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.

B. Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.

C. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CA. Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.

D. Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.
optionExplanations: ✗ Importing a locally created third-party-signed certificate works, but pairing it with an HTTP API custom domain that does not enforce TLSv1.3 is unnecessary; more importantly API Gateway custom domains must enforce TLS 1.3 via the security policy, and this option needlessly relies on a self-managed local certificate process, making B the cleaner correct choice.

✓ Creating an ACM certificate signed by the third-party CA and using it on an API Gateway HTTP API custom domain (which supports a TLS 1.3 security policy) meets the requirement for both a third-party CA-signed certificate and TLSv1.3 enforcement.

✗ ACM does not create certificates signed by an external third-party CA (ACM-issued certs are signed by Amazon's CA), so this step is technically incorrect, and Lambda function URLs do not let you attach a custom ACM certificate or enforce a TLS version.
✗ Lambda function URLs do not support custom domains or custom ACM certificates and do not allow enforcing a specific TLS version, so they cannot meet the third-party CA and TLSv1.3 requirements.

text: A company runs an application on AWS. The application receives inconsistent amounts of usage. The application uses AWS Direct Connect to connect to an on-premises MySQL-compatible database. The on-premises database consistently uses a minimum of 2 GiB of memory. The company wants to migrate the on-premises database to a managed AWS service. The company wants to use auto scaling capabilities to manage unexpected workload increases. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
options: A. Provision an Amazon DynamoDB database with default read and write capacity settings.
B. Provision an Amazon Aurora database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).
C. Provision an Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 database with a minimum capacity of 1 Aurora capacity unit (ACU).
D. Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL database with 2 GiB of memory.
optionExplanations: ✗ DynamoDB is a NoSQL store, not MySQL-compatible, so it would not properly serve a MySQL-compatible workload and changes the data model.

✗ Aurora provisioned (non-serverless) does not measure capacity in ACUs and does not auto-scale compute down to handle inconsistent usage as seamlessly; this option misstates Aurora provisioned configuration.

✓ Aurora Serverless v2 is MySQL-compatible, auto-scales compute (in ACUs) up and down to handle inconsistent and unexpected workloads, and is fully managed, meeting the requirements with the least administrative overhead.
✗ RDS for MySQL with a fixed 2 GiB instance does not auto-scale compute for unexpected workload increases, so it fails the auto-scaling requirement.

text: A company wants to use an event-driven programming model with AWS Lambda. The company wants to reduce startup latency for Lambda functions that run on Java 11. The company does not have strict latency requirements for the applications. The company wants to reduce cold starts and outlier latencies when a function scales up. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency.
B. Increase the timeout of the Lambda functions.
C. Increase the memory of the Lambda functions.
D. Configure Lambda SnapStart.
optionExplanations: ✗ Provisioned concurrency reduces cold starts but incurs ongoing cost for keeping instances warm, so it is not the most cost-effective option, especially when strict latency is not required.
✗ Increasing the function timeout only changes how long a function may run; it does nothing to reduce startup latency or cold starts.
✗ Increasing memory can modestly speed execution but does not address Java initialization cold-start latency and raises cost, so it does not best meet the requirement.

✓ Lambda SnapStart caches and reuses an initialized snapshot of the Java execution environment, significantly reducing cold-start and outlier latency at no additional charge, making it the most cost-effective fit for Java 11.

text: A financial services company launched a new application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company uses the application to track stock market trends. The company needs to operate the application for only 2 hours at the end of each week. The company needs to optimize the cost of running the database. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL database cluster.
B. Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora MySQL database cluster.
C. Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs MySQL. Purchase an instance reservation for the EC2 instance.
D. Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses MySQL container images to run tasks.
optionExplanations: ✓ Aurora Serverless v2 automatically scales database capacity up and down based on demand and can scale down to minimal (or zero) capacity when idle, so a workload running only 2 hours per week incurs near-zero cost the rest of the time. This is the most cost-effective option for highly intermittent usage.

✗ A standard provisioned Aurora MySQL cluster runs (and bills) continuously on always-on instances regardless of usage, so paying 24/7 for a database used only 2 hours weekly is far more expensive than a serverless option.

✗ Running MySQL on a reserved EC2 instance commits to paying for the instance continuously over the reservation term, which is wasteful for a database needed only 2 hours per week and also adds significant operational overhead to self-manage MySQL.

✗ Running MySQL containers on an ECS cluster requires continuously running underlying capacity (EC2 or Fargate tasks) plus high operational complexity for stateful database management, making it both costly for intermittent use and operationally burdensome.

text: A company deploys its applications on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) behind an Application Load Balancer in an AWS Region. The application needs to store data in a PostgreSQL database engine. The company wants the data in the database to be highly available. The company also needs increased capacity for read workloads. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational eficiency?
options: A. Create an Amazon DynamoDB database table configured with global tables.
B. Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ deployments.
C. Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.
D. Create an Amazon RDS database configured with cross-Region read replicas.
optionExplanations: ✗ DynamoDB is a NoSQL service, not a PostgreSQL engine, so it does not meet the requirement for a PostgreSQL database.
✗ RDS Multi-AZ (single standby) provides high availability but the standby cannot serve reads, so it does not add read capacity as required.

✓ An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment provisions one writer and two readable standby instances across AZs, providing both high availability and increased read capacity with high operational efficiency.

✗ Cross-Region read replicas add read capacity but introduce cross-Region complexity and asynchronous lag and are not designed primarily for in-Region high availability, making them less operationally efficient than a Multi-AZ DB cluster.

text: A company is building a RESTful serverless web application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The users of this web application will be geographically distributed, and the company wants to reduce the latency of API requests to these users. Which type of endpoint should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?
options: A. Private endpoint
B. Regional endpoint
C. Interface VPC endpoint
D. Edge-optimized endpoint
optionExplanations: ✗ A private endpoint exposes the API only within a VPC via an interface endpoint and does not reduce latency for geographically distributed public users.
✗ A regional endpoint serves requests from a single Region without edge caching/routing, so distant users experience higher latency than with an edge-optimized endpoint.
✗ An interface VPC endpoint provides private connectivity inside a VPC and is not a public-facing low-latency distribution mechanism for global users.
✓ An edge-optimized endpoint routes requests through CloudFront edge locations, reducing latency for geographically distributed users, which meets the requirement.

text: A company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve content pages for its website. The company needs to ensure that clients use a TLS certificate when accessing the company's website. The company wants to automate the creation and renewal of the TLS certificates. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational eficiency?
options: A. Use a CloudFront security policy to create a certificate.
B. Use a CloudFront origin access control (OAC) to create a certificate.
C. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use DNS validation for the domain.
D. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate. Use email validation for the domain.
optionExplanations: ✗ A CloudFront security policy defines the TLS protocol versions and cipher suites for connections; it does not create or issue TLS certificates.
✗ CloudFront origin access control (OAC) restricts S3 origin access to CloudFront only; it has nothing to do with issuing or renewing TLS certificates.

✓ AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) issues free public TLS certificates and, with DNS validation, can automatically renew them indefinitely (CNAME stays in place), giving the most operationally efficient automated lifecycle for a CloudFront distribution.
✗ ACM with email validation works but requires a manual email approval action on each renewal, so it is less operationally efficient and not fully automated.

text: A company deployed a serverless application that uses Amazon DynamoDB as a database layer. The application has experienced a large increase in users. The company wants to improve database response time from milliseconds to microseconds and to cache requests to the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
B. Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift.
C. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS.
