D. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
optionExplanations: ✓ DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, in-memory cache purpose-built for DynamoDB that delivers microsecond read response times with no application rewrite, meeting the requirements with the least operational overhead.
✗ Migrating to Amazon Redshift would require a full data-store change and is a data-warehouse for analytics, not a low-latency microsecond cache for an OLTP serverless app.
✗ Migrating to Amazon RDS replaces the database entirely, adds significant operational overhead, and does not provide microsecond caching.
✗ Amazon ElastiCache for Redis can cache requests but requires custom application-side cache management and is not natively integrated with DynamoDB, so it adds more operational overhead than DAX.

text: A company runs an application that uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The application receives trafic only on weekdays during business hours. The company wants to optimize costs and reduce operational overhead based on this usage. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use the Instance Scheduler on AWS to configure start and stop schedules.
B. Turn off automatic backups. Create weekly manual snapshots of the database.
C. Create a custom AWS Lambda function to start and stop the database based on minimum CPU utilization.
D. Purchase All Upfront reserved DB instances.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Instance Scheduler provides a managed, configurable mechanism to automatically start and stop RDS instances on a defined schedule (weekday business hours), optimizing cost with minimal operational overhead.
✗ Turning off automatic backups and creating weekly manual snapshots reduces durability and does not address the goal of stopping the instance during idle periods to save cost.
✗ A custom Lambda function based on CPU utilization adds development and maintenance overhead and is fragile compared to a schedule-driven approach for a predictable weekday-only workload.
✗ All Upfront Reserved Instances assume continuous 24/7 usage and provide no benefit for an instance that should be stopped nights and weekends, so it does not optimize cost for intermittent usage.

text: A company uses locally attached storage to run a latency-sensitive application on premises. The company is using a lift and shift method to move the application to the AWS Cloud. The company does not want to change the application architecture. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system to run the application.
B. Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP2 volume to run the application.
C. Configure an Auto Scaling group with an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system to run the application.
D. Host the application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) GP3 volume to run the application.
optionExplanations: ✗ FSx for Lustre is a high-performance shared file system for HPC/ML workloads, not block storage; it changes the architecture and is far more expensive than EBS, and the Auto Scaling group is unnecessary overhead for a single locally-attached-storage lift-and-shift.

✗ Hosting on EC2 with an EBS volume correctly mimics locally attached block storage, but GP2 is the older generation and costs more per GB than GP3 while bundling IOPS/throughput to volume size, so it is not the most cost-effective choice.

✗ FSx for OpenZFS is a managed file-system service, not block storage equivalent to local disks; it adds cost and changes the architecture, and the Auto Scaling group adds unneeded complexity for this lift-and-shift.

✓ EC2 with an EBS GP3 volume best replicates locally attached block storage without changing the architecture, and GP3 is about 20% cheaper per GB than GP2 with a 3,000 IOPS / 125 MBps baseline included, making it the most cost-effective option for this latency-sensitive workload.

text: A company runs a stateful production application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application requires at least two EC2 instances to always be running. A solutions architect needs to design a highly available and fault-tolerant architecture for the application. The solutions architect creates an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances. Which set of additional steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?
options: A. Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy one On-Demand Instance in one Availability Zone and one On-Demand Instance in a second Availability Zone.
B. Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two On-Demand Instances in a second Availability Zone.
C. Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to two. Deploy four Spot Instances in one Availability Zone.
D. Set the Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to four. Deploy two On-Demand Instances in one Availability Zone and two Spot Instances in a second Availability Zone.
optionExplanations: ✗ Minimum capacity of two with one instance in each of two AZs is highly available, but if one AZ fails only one instance remains, violating the requirement that at least two instances always run.

✓ Minimum capacity of four with two On-Demand Instances in each of two AZs ensures that even after a full AZ failure two instances still run, satisfying the always-at-least-two and fault-tolerance requirements.
✗ Four Spot Instances in a single AZ are not fault-tolerant (single AZ) and Spot can be interrupted, so it cannot guarantee two always-running instances for a stateful production app.
✗ Mixing On-Demand and Spot across two AZs risks losing the Spot instances on interruption, so it cannot reliably guarantee two instances always running.

text: An ecommerce company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company hosts its website on premises and in the AWS Cloud. The company's on-premises data center is near the us-west-1 Region. The company uses the eu-central-1 Region to host the website. The company wants to minimize load time for the website as much as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Set up a geolocation routing policy. Send the trafic that is near us-west-1 to the on-premises data center. Send the trafic that is near eu- central-1 to eu-central-1.
B. Set up a simple routing policy that routes all trafic that is near eu-central-1 to eu-central-1 and routes all trafic that is near the on-premises datacenter to the on-premises data center.
C. Set up a latency routing policy. Associate the policy with us-west-1.
D. Set up a weighted routing policy. Split the trafic evenly between eu-central-1 and the on-premises data center.
optionExplanations: ✓ A geolocation routing policy directs users near us-west-1 to the closer on-premises data center and users near eu-central-1 to the eu-central-1 site, minimizing load time by serving each population from its nearest endpoint.
✗ Simple routing returns records without any geographic or location-based decision, so it cannot route different users to their nearest site.
✗ A latency routing policy compares latency only among AWS Regions and cannot evaluate an on-premises data center, so it does not solve routing across the on-prem and AWS sites.
✗ Weighted routing splits traffic by assigned weights regardless of user location, which would send many users to a distant endpoint and not minimize load time.

text: A company has 5 PB of archived data on physical tapes. The company needs to preserve the data on the tapes for another 10 years for compliance purposes. The company wants to migrate to AWS in the next 6 months. The data center that stores the tapes has a 1 Gbps uplink internet connectivity. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Read the data from the tapes on premises. Stage the data in a local NFS storage. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
B. Use an on-premises backup application to read the data from the tapes and to write directly to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

C. Order multiple AWS Snowball devices that have Tape Gateway. Copy the physical tapes to virtual tapes in Snowball. Ship the Snowball devices to AWS. Create a lifecycle policy to move the tapes to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
D. Configure an on-premises Tape Gateway. Create virtual tapes in the AWS Cloud. Use backup software to copy the physical tape to the virtual tape.
optionExplanations: ✗ DataSync over the 1 Gbps internet uplink cannot move 5 PB within 6 months (1 Gbps yields only a few TB/day, requiring years), and Glacier Flexible Retrieval is more expensive than Deep Archive for 10-year compliance archival; the network bottleneck makes this infeasible.

✗ Writing 5 PB directly to S3 Glacier Deep Archive over the 1 Gbps link is impossible in the timeframe due to the same bandwidth constraint, even though Deep Archive itself is the correct storage class.

✓ AWS Snowball Edge devices with Tape Gateway capability let you copy physical tapes to virtual tapes offline, ship the devices to AWS (bypassing the slow link), and a lifecycle policy moves the virtual tapes to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, the lowest-cost class for 10-year compliance retention.
✗ An on-premises Tape Gateway uploads virtual tape data to AWS over the network connection, so it is still bottlenecked by the 1 Gbps uplink and cannot transfer 5 PB within 6 months.

text: A company is deploying an application that processes large quantities of data in parallel. The company plans to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload. The network architecture must be configurable to prevent groups of nodes from sharing the same underlying hardware. Which networking solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Run the EC2 instances in a spread placement group.
B. Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
C. Configure the EC2 instances with dedicated tenancy.
D. Configure the EC2 instances with shared tenancy.
optionExplanations: ✓ A spread placement group places each EC2 instance on distinct underlying hardware (separate racks), directly preventing groups of nodes from sharing the same physical host.
✗ Grouping instances in separate accounts is an organizational/billing boundary and provides no guarantee about underlying hardware isolation.
✗ Dedicated tenancy isolates an account's instances from other AWS customers but does not prevent the company's own instances from sharing the same physical host, and is not a networking solution.
✗ Shared tenancy is the default and explicitly allows instances to share underlying hardware, which is the opposite of the requirement.

text: A solutions architect is designing a disaster recovery (DR) strategy to provide Amazon EC2 capacity in a failover AWS Region. Business requirements state that the DR strategy must meet capacity in the failover Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Purchase On-Demand Instances in the failover Region.
B. Purchase an EC2 Savings Plan in the failover Region.
C. Purchase regional Reserved Instances in the failover Region.
D. Purchase a Capacity Reservation in the failover Region.
optionExplanations: ✗ On-Demand Instances provide no capacity guarantee, so during a regional failover event when many customers compete for capacity, the instances may not launch.
✗ An EC2 Savings Plan is a billing discount commitment and does not reserve or guarantee any compute capacity in the failover Region.
✗ Regional Reserved Instances provide a billing discount and capacity is not reserved to a specific AZ, so they do not guarantee capacity availability for DR failover.
✓ An On-Demand Capacity Reservation reserves EC2 capacity in the failover Region so the instances are guaranteed to be available when failover is triggered, meeting the capacity requirement.

text: A company has five organizational units (OUs) as part of its organization in AWS Organizations. Each OU correlates to the five businesses that the company owns. The company's research and development (R&D) business is separating from the company and will need its own organization. A solutions architect creates a separate new management account for this purpose. What should the solutions architect do next in the new management account?
options: A. Have the R&D AWS account be part of both organizations during the transition.
B. Invite the R&D AWS account to be part of the new organization after the R&D AWS account has left the prior organization.
C. Create a new R&D AWS account in the new organization. Migrate resources from the prior R&D AWS account to the new R&D AWS account.
D. Have the R&D AWS account join the new organization. Make the new management account a member of the prior organization.
optionExplanations: ✗ An AWS account can belong to only one organization at a time, so the R&D account cannot be part of both organizations during the transition.
✓ The correct process is to remove (leave) the R&D account from the prior organization and then invite it into the new organization, preserving the account and its resources without migration.
✗ Creating a brand-new account and migrating all resources is unnecessary, error-prone, and far more work than simply moving the existing account between organizations.

✗ An account can be in only one organization, so the R&D account cannot join the new organization while the new management account remains a member of the prior organization; a management account also cannot be a member of another organization.

text: A company is designing a solution to capture customer activity in different web applications to process analytics and make predictions. Customer activity in the web applications is unpredictable and can increase suddenly. The company requires a solution that integrates with other web applications. The solution must include an authorization step for security purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Authorization is resolved at the GWLB.

B. Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis data stream that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.

C. Configure an Amazon API Gateway endpoint in front of an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose that stores the information that the company receives in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an API Gateway Lambda authorizer to resolve authorization.

D. Configure a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in front of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) container instance that stores the information that the company receives on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Use an AWS Lambda function to resolve authorization.
optionExplanations: ✗ A Gateway Load Balancer is for inserting third-party virtual appliances and does not resolve application authorization; storing to EFS via ECS does not match the unpredictable streaming-ingest and authorization needs.

✗ API Gateway in front of a Kinesis data stream can scale, but a raw Kinesis Data Stream does not natively deliver to S3 (requires extra consumer code), and using a separate Lambda rather than an API Gateway authorizer is a less integrated authorization step than a Lambda authorizer.

✓ API Gateway fronting Kinesis Data Firehose auto-scales for unpredictable spikes and delivers directly to S3 with no servers to manage, while an API Gateway Lambda authorizer provides the required authorization step at the entry point, integrating cleanly with other web apps.

✗ A Gateway Load Balancer plus ECS storing to EFS does not provide the scalable streaming ingestion and is not designed for HTTP application authorization, making it unsuitable for unpredictable web-activity capture.

text: An ecommerce company wants a disaster recovery solution for its Amazon RDS DB instances that run Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise Edition. The company's current recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) are 24 hours. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Create a cross-Region read replica and promote the read replica to the primary instance.
B. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create RDS cross-Region replication.
C. Use cross-Region replication every 24 hours to copy native backups to an Amazon S3 bucket.
D. Copy automatic snapshots to another Region every 24 hours.
optionExplanations: ✗ A cross-Region read replica is not supported by Amazon RDS for SQL Server (read replicas exist only for MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and Oracle), and a continuously running replica would also be costlier than needed for a 24-hour RPO/RTO.
✗ AWS DMS provides continuous data replication, which is far more expensive and operationally complex than necessary for a relaxed 24-hour RPO/RTO disaster recovery target.

✗ Copying native SQL Server backups to S3 with cross-Region replication works but adds operational overhead (manual native backup and restore handling) and S3 Cross-Region Replication is continuous rather than a clean 24-hour cycle, making it less cost-effective than snapshot copy.

✓ Copying automatic RDS snapshots to another Region every 24 hours is a built-in, low-cost RDS feature that exactly satisfies the 24-hour RPO/RTO with minimal operational overhead, making it the most cost-effective solution.

text: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer that has sticky sessions enabled. The web server currently hosts the user session state. The company wants to ensure high availability and avoid user session state loss in the event of a web server outage. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance to store the session data. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Memcached to store the session state.
B. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state. Update the application to use ElastiCache for Redis to store the session state.
C. Use an AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store session data. Update the application to use AWS Storage Gateway cached volume to store the session state.
D. Use Amazon RDS to store the session state. Update the application to use Amazon RDS to store the session state.
optionExplanations: ✗ ElastiCache for Memcached does not support replication or persistence, so a node failure loses the session data it holds, failing the high-availability requirement.
✓ ElastiCache for Redis supports replication and Multi-AZ with automatic failover, so externalizing session state to Redis survives a web server outage without losing sessions.
✗ AWS Storage Gateway cached volumes are a hybrid block storage service for on-premises workloads backed by S3, not a low-latency session store for a web application.
✗ Amazon RDS could persist sessions but a relational database adds latency and operational overhead and is not the purpose-built choice for ephemeral key-value session state.

text: A company migrated a MySQL database from the company's on-premises data center to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company sized the RDS DB instance to meet the company's average daily workload. Once a month, the database performs slowly when the company runs queries for a report. The company wants to have the ability to run reports and maintain the performance of the daily workloads. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a read replica of the database. Direct the queries to the read replica.
B. Create a backup of the database. Restore the backup to another DB instance. Direct the queries to the new database.
C. Export the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the S3 bucket.
D. Resize the DB instance to accommodate the additional workload.
optionExplanations: ✓ A read replica offloads the monthly read-heavy reporting queries from the primary instance, preserving performance of the daily write workload at low cost.
✗ Restoring a backup to a separate DB instance is a heavy, point-in-time operation that does not stay current and is far more operationally costly than a read replica.
✗ Exporting to S3 and querying with Athena requires building an export pipeline and the data would be stale, adding complexity for a routine monthly report.
✗ Resizing the instance increases cost permanently to handle a once-a-month spike, which is wasteful since the daily workload does not need the larger size.

text: A company runs a container application by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application includes microservices that manage customers and place orders. The company needs to route incoming requests to the appropriate microservices. Which solution will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision a Network Load Balancer.
B. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to provision an Application Load Balancer.
C. Use an AWS Lambda function to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.
D. Use Amazon API Gateway to connect the requests to Amazon EKS.
optionExplanations: ✗ A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and cannot perform path/host-based routing to different microservices based on HTTP request attributes.

✓ The AWS Load Balancer Controller provisions an Application Load Balancer that supports Layer 7 path-based and host-based routing to route requests to the customer and order microservices cost-effectively.
✗ Using a Lambda function as a proxy to EKS adds custom code and per-invocation cost and is not a standard or cost-effective request-routing mechanism for in-cluster microservices.
✗ Amazon API Gateway adds per-request charges and management overhead beyond what an ALB provides for simple internal microservice routing.

text: A company uses AWS and sells access to copyrighted images. The company’s global customer base needs to be able to access these images quickly. The company must deny access to users from specific countries. The company wants to minimize costs as much as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA) and public bucket access. Provide customers with a link to the S3 bucket.
B. Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Create an IAM user for each customer. Add the users to a group that has permission to access the S3 bucket.

C. Use Amazon EC2 instances that are behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) to store the images. Deploy the instances only in the countries the company services. Provide customers with links to the ALBs for their specific country's instances.
D. Use Amazon S3 to store the images. Use Amazon CloudFront to distribute the images with geographic restrictions. Provide a signed URL for each customer to access the data in CloudFront.
optionExplanations: ✗ Enabling public bucket access exposes the copyrighted images to anyone, and MFA does not control per-country access or provide global low-latency delivery.
✗ Creating an IAM user per customer does not scale, gives no geographic restriction, and S3 alone does not provide global edge caching for fast access.
✗ Running EC2 instances behind ALBs in each country is far more expensive and operationally complex than serverless edge delivery and does not cleanly enforce copyright controls.
✓ CloudFront caches images at edge locations for fast global access, supports geo restriction to deny specific countries, and signed URLs protect the copyrighted content, all cost-effectively.

text: A solutions architect is designing a highly available Amazon ElastiCache for Redis based solution. The solutions architect needs to ensure that failures do not result in performance degradation or loss of data locally and within an AWS Region. The solution needs to provide high availability at the node level and at the Region level. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with shards that contain multiple nodes.
B. Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Redis append only files (AOF) turned on.
C. Use a Multi-AZ Redis cluster with more than one read replica in the replication group.
D. Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Auto Scaling turned on.
optionExplanations: ✓ Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with shards containing multiple nodes provide node-level high availability via replicas with automatic failover and Region/AZ-level resilience across Availability Zones, preventing performance degradation and data loss.
✗ AOF persistence only protects data on a single node and is not a substitute for replication; it does not provide cross-AZ high availability and can affect performance.

✗ A Multi-AZ cluster with read replicas provides node-level HA but the option omits sharding for scale; the Multi-AZ replication group with multi-node shards is the more complete answer addressing both node and Region/AZ availability.
✗ ElastiCache for Redis does not provide an auto scaling feature that delivers cross-AZ high availability and failover; auto scaling adjusts capacity, not availability.

text: A company plans to migrate to AWS and use Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances for its application. During the migration testing phase, a technical team observes that the application takes a long time to launch and load memory to become fully productive. Which solution will reduce the launch time of the application during the next testing phase?
options: A. Launch two or more EC2 On-Demand Instances. Turn on auto scaling features and make the EC2 On-Demand Instances available during the next testing phase.
B. Launch EC2 Spot Instances to support the application and to scale the application so it is available during the next testing phase.
C. Launch the EC2 On-Demand Instances with hibernation turned on. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools during the next testing phase.
D. Launch EC2 On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Start additional EC2 instances during the next testing phase.
optionExplanations: ✗ Launching multiple On-Demand Instances with Auto Scaling adds capacity and availability but does nothing to pre-warm memory or shorten the per-instance application initialization time, so it does not reduce launch time.
✗ Spot Instances change the pricing model and risk interruption; they do not reduce application launch or memory-load time and are inappropriate for a productivity-sensitive workload.

✓ EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools keep pre-initialized instances in a stopped/hibernated state, and hibernation preserves the loaded in-memory state to disk so resumed instances skip the lengthy memory-load/boot, directly reducing application launch time.
✗ Capacity Reservations only guarantee that capacity is available in an Availability Zone; they do not pre-load memory or reduce the application's startup/initialization time.

text: A company's applications run on Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. The company notices that its applications experience sudden trafic increases on random days of the week. The company wants to maintain application performance during sudden trafic increases. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Use manual scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
B. Use predictive scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
C. Use dynamic scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
D. Use schedule scaling to change the size of the Auto Scaling group.
optionExplanations: ✗ Manual scaling requires a human to change the Auto Scaling group size on demand, which cannot respond to sudden, random traffic increases in time and is operationally impractical.

✗ Predictive scaling uses machine learning on historical, recurring patterns to provision capacity ahead of expected load; it does not handle random, non-cyclical spikes well, so it is not the best fit here.

✓ Dynamic scaling (target tracking / step / simple scaling) reacts automatically to real-time CloudWatch metrics, adding capacity when sudden random traffic arrives and removing it afterward, providing the most cost-effective response to unpredictable spikes.
✗ Scheduled scaling adjusts capacity at fixed, known times; since the traffic increases occur on random days with no predictable schedule, it cannot reliably meet the requirement.

text: An ecommerce application uses a PostgreSQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. During a monthly sales event, database usage increases and causes database connection issues for the application. The trafic is unpredictable for subsequent monthly sales events, which impacts the sales forecast. The company needs to maintain performance when there is an unpredictable increase in trafic. Which solution resolves this issue in the MOST cost-effective way?
options: A. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora Serverless v2.
B. Enable auto scaling for the PostgreSQL database on the EC2 instance to accommodate increased usage.
C. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with a larger instance type.
D. Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Redshift to accommodate increased usage.
optionExplanations: ✓ Aurora Serverless v2 automatically scales database capacity up and down to match unpredictable traffic, maintaining performance during sales events while keeping costs low during idle periods.
✗ There is no native PostgreSQL auto scaling for compute on a single EC2 instance; you would have to manually resize, which does not handle unpredictable spikes automatically.
✗ Provisioning a larger fixed RDS instance pays for peak capacity year-round to cover an unpredictable monthly spike, which is not cost-effective.
✗ Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not a transactional OLTP database for an ecommerce application's connection-heavy workload.

text: A company hosts an internal serverless application on AWS by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The company’s employees report issues with high latency when they begin using the application each day. The company wants to reduce latency. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Increase the API Gateway throttling limit.
B. Set up a scheduled scaling to increase Lambda provisioned concurrency before employees begin to use the application each day.
C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to initiate a Lambda function as a target for the alarm at the beginning of each day.
D. Increase the Lambda function memory.
optionExplanations: ✗ Increasing the API Gateway throttling limit addresses request rate limits, not the Lambda cold-start latency that occurs when employees first invoke the function each morning.

✓ Scheduling provisioned concurrency to scale up before the daily usage window keeps Lambda execution environments warm, eliminating the cold-start latency employees experience at the start of each day.
✗ A CloudWatch alarm invoking a single Lambda once each day does not pre-warm enough concurrent environments to remove cold-start latency across concurrent user requests.
✗ Increasing function memory speeds CPU-bound execution but does not eliminate the cold-start initialization latency that causes the start-of-day slowness.

text: A research company uses on-premises devices to generate data for analysis. The company wants to use the AWS Cloud to analyze the data. The devices generate .csv files and support writing the data to an SMB file share. Company analysts must be able to use SQL commands to query the data. The analysts will run queries periodically throughout the day. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)
options: A. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon S3 File Gateway mode.
B. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway on premises in Amazon FSx File Gateway made.
C. Set up an AWS Glue crawler to create a table based on the data that is in Amazon S3.
D. Set up an Amazon EMR cluster with EMR File System (EMRFS) to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
E. Set up an Amazon Redshift cluster to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
F. Setup Amazon Athena to query the data that is in Amazon S3. Provide access to analysts.
optionExplanations: ✓ S3 File Gateway presents an SMB file share on premises that the devices can write the .csv files to, and it transfers them into Amazon S3 - exactly what is needed and cost-effective.
✗ FSx File Gateway provides low-latency on-prem access to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system; it does not land data in S3 for Athena/Glue querying, so it does not fit this workflow.
✓ An AWS Glue crawler scans the .csv data in S3 and creates a Data Catalog table with schema, which Athena uses to run SQL queries - required for the serverless query approach.
✗ An Amazon EMR cluster running EMRFS is powerful but requires provisioning and paying for cluster nodes, which is far more expensive and operationally heavy than needed for periodic SQL queries.
✗ An Amazon Redshift cluster incurs continuous compute costs for an always-running cluster, which is not cost-effective for queries run only periodically throughout the day.

✓ Amazon Athena is serverless and charges per query/data scanned, allowing analysts to run SQL directly against the S3 .csv data via the Glue table - the most cost-effective option for periodic queries.

text: A company wants to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters and Amazon RDS DB instances to build and run a payment processing application. The company will run the application in its on-premises data center for compliance purposes. A solutions architect wants to use AWS Outposts as part of the solution. The solutions architect is working with the company's operational team to build the application. Which activities are the responsibility of the company's operational team? (Choose three.)
options: A. Providing resilient power and network connectivity to the Outposts racks
B. Managing the virtualization hypervisor, storage systems, and the AWS services that run on Outposts
C. Physical security and access controls of the data center environment
D. Availability of the Outposts infrastructure including the power supplies, servers, and networking equipment within the Outposts racks
E. Physical maintenance of Outposts components
F. Providing extra capacity for Amazon ECS clusters to mitigate server failures and maintenance events
optionExplanations: ✓ Providing resilient power and network connectivity to the Outposts racks is the customer's responsibility under the shared responsibility model for Outposts.
✗ Managing the virtualization hypervisor, storage systems, and AWS services that run on Outposts is AWS's responsibility, not the customer's.
✓ Physical security and access controls of the data center hosting the Outposts is the customer's responsibility since the equipment resides in their facility.
✗ Availability of the Outposts infrastructure components such as power supplies, servers, and networking equipment within the racks is managed and maintained by AWS.
✓ Physical maintenance of Outposts components (e.g., escorting AWS personnel, the physical environment) is a customer responsibility, while AWS performs the actual hardware servicing it dispatches.

✗ Providing extra capacity to mitigate server failures and maintenance events is a recommended planning practice but AWS manages the underlying infrastructure availability; this is not listed as the operational team's defined responsibility.

text: A company is planning to migrate a TCP-based application into the company's VPC. The application is publicly accessible on a nonstandard TCP port through a hardware appliance in the company's data center. This public endpoint can process up to 3 million requests per second with low latency. The company requires the same level of performance for the new public endpoint in AWS. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?
options: A. Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure the NLB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
B. Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the ALB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
C. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that listens on the TCP port that the application requires. Use an Application Load Balancer as the origin.
D. Deploy an Amazon API Gateway API that is configured with the TCP port that the application requires. Configure AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency to process the requests.
optionExplanations: ✓ A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4, supports arbitrary TCP ports, handles millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency, and can be made publicly accessible, matching the requirement.
✗ An Application Load Balancer is a Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS balancer and does not support arbitrary nonstandard TCP ports or match NLB's raw TCP throughput and latency.
✗ CloudFront is an HTTP/HTTPS content delivery network and cannot listen on arbitrary TCP ports for a generic TCP-based application.
✗ API Gateway with Lambda is for HTTP/REST/WebSocket APIs, cannot serve a raw nonstandard TCP port, and would not sustain 3 million TCP requests per second at low latency.

text: A company runs its critical database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company wants to migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime and data loss. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create a DB snapshot of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance to populate a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
B. Create an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Promote the Aurora read replicate to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
C. Use data import from Amazon S3 to migrate the database to an Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
D. Use the pg_dump utility to back up the RDS for PostgreSQL database. Restore the backup to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Restoring from a DB snapshot is a point-in-time copy, so any writes after the snapshot are lost and the source must stop accepting writes, causing significant downtime and data loss.

✓ B. Creating an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL instance keeps it continuously in sync via replication, then promoting it after replication lag reaches zero allows cutover with minimal downtime and no data loss, all managed by RDS with low operational overhead.
✗ C. Importing data from Amazon S3 requires first exporting/dumping the data and is a bulk one-time load, so it does not capture ongoing changes and incurs downtime and potential data loss.
✗ D. Using pg_dump and restore is a manual logical export/import that requires stopping writes during the migration window, resulting in downtime, data loss risk, and higher operational effort.

text: A company's infrastructure consists of hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. A solutions architect must ensure that every EC2 instance can be recovered after a disaster. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of effort?
options: A. Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Create an AWS CloudFormation template to launch new EC2 instances from the EBS storage.
B. Take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to set the environment based on the EC2 template and attach the EBS storage.
C. Use AWS Backup to set up a backup plan for the entire group of EC2 instances. Use the AWS Backup API or the AWS CLI to speed up the restore process for multiple EC2 instances.

D. Create an AWS Lambda function to take a snapshot of the EBS storage that is attached to each EC2 instance and copy the Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). Create another Lambda function to perform the restores with the copied AMIs and attach the EBS storage.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Snapshotting each EBS volume and using CloudFormation to relaunch instances is manual and CloudFormation does not natively orchestrate per-instance EBS snapshot recovery, requiring substantial custom effort.
✗ B. Elastic Beanstalk is for deploying and managing application environments, not for backing up and restoring hundreds of arbitrary EC2 instances from EBS snapshots, so it is the wrong tool.

✓ C. AWS Backup lets you create a single centralized, policy-driven backup plan for the whole fleet (EC2/EBS) and restore many instances via the API or CLI, meeting the recovery requirement with the least effort.
✗ D. Writing custom Lambda functions to snapshot, copy AMIs, and restore reinvents what AWS Backup provides natively and requires significant development and maintenance effort.

text: A company recently migrated to the AWS Cloud. The company wants a serverless solution for large-scale parallel on-demand processing of a semistructured dataset. The data consists of logs, media files, sales transactions, and IoT sensor data that is stored in Amazon S3. The company wants the solution to process thousands of items in the dataset in parallel. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational eficiency?
options: A. Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Inline mode to process the data in parallel.
B. Use the AWS Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode to process the data in parallel.
C. Use AWS Glue to process the data in parallel.
D. Use several AWS Lambda functions to process the data in parallel.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Step Functions Map state in Inline mode is limited to 40 concurrent iterations and a 256 KB payload, so it cannot process thousands of items in parallel at large scale.

✓ B. Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode is purpose-built for large-scale parallel processing of millions of S3 objects/records with up to 10,000 concurrent executions, providing a serverless, on-demand solution with the most operational efficiency.

✗ C. AWS Glue is an Apache Spark-based ETL service optimized for structured/semistructured transformations, but it is heavier to operate for arbitrary mixed item types (logs, media, transactions) and is not the most efficient fit for simple large-scale parallel item processing.

✗ D. Manually orchestrating several Lambda functions requires you to build and manage the fan-out, concurrency, and error handling yourself, which is far less operationally efficient than the managed Distributed Map.

text: A company will migrate 10 PB of data to Amazon S3 in 6 weeks. The current data center has a 500 Mbps uplink to the internet. Other on-premises applications share the uplink. The company can use 80% of the internet bandwidth for this one-time migration task. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon S3 and to automatically verify the data.
B. Use rsync to transfer the data directly to Amazon S3.
C. Use the AWS CLI and multiple copy processes to send the data directly to Amazon S3.
D. Order multiple AWS Snowball devices. Copy the data to the devices. Send the devices to AWS to copy the data to Amazon S3.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. DataSync transfers over the network, but at 400 Mbps (80% of 500 Mbps) moving 10 PB would take years, far exceeding the 6-week window.
✗ B. rsync over the limited internet uplink would take years to move 10 PB, so it cannot meet the deadline.
✗ C. AWS CLI copy processes still depend on the 400 Mbps uplink, which is nowhere near enough bandwidth to move 10 PB in 6 weeks.
✓ D. Multiple AWS Snowball devices ship the 10 PB physically, bypassing the bandwidth-constrained internet link entirely, which is the only practical way to move that volume within 6 weeks.

text: A company has several on-premises Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (ISCSI) network storage servers. The company wants to reduce the number of these servers by moving to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect must provide low-latency access to frequently used data and reduce the dependency on on-premises servers with a minimal number of infrastructure changes. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway.
B. Deploy Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage with backups to Amazon S3.
C. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with stored volumes.
D. Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway that is configured with cached volumes.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon S3 File Gateway presents NFS/SMB file shares, not iSCSI block volumes, so it does not match the existing iSCSI block storage workload.

✗ Amazon EBS volumes attach only to EC2 instances in AWS and cannot be presented to on-premises iSCSI initiators, so it would require major application/infrastructure changes and does not provide on-prem iSCSI access.

✗ AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway with stored volumes keeps the entire dataset on-premises (asynchronously backed up to S3), so it does not reduce the dependency on or the amount of on-premises storage servers.

✓ AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway with cached volumes stores the primary dataset in Amazon S3 while caching frequently accessed data locally over iSCSI, providing low-latency access to hot data and reducing on-premises storage with minimal changes.

text: A solutions architect is designing an application that will allow business users to upload objects to Amazon S3. The solution needs to maximize object durability. Objects also must be readily available at any time and for any length of time. Users will access objects frequently within the first 30 days after the objects are uploaded, but users are much less likely to access objects that are older than 30 days. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Glacier after 30 days.
B. Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
C. Store all the objects in S3 Standard with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 30 days.
D. Store all the objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering with an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days.
optionExplanations: ✗ Glacier is not readily available at any time without restore delays (or higher costs for expedited retrieval), violating the requirement that objects be immediately available for any length of time.

✓ S3 Standard-IA offers the same 11 nines durability and multi-AZ availability as Standard, is immediately accessible, and has lower storage cost for objects accessed less than monthly, making it the most cost-effective fit for the 30-day access pattern.

✗ S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, reducing durability/availability and conflicting with the requirement to maximize durability and ensure objects are readily available at all times.

✗ Intelligent-Tiering already auto-tiers based on access; adding a Lifecycle rule to force a transition to Standard-IA is redundant and adds the per-object monitoring fee, making it less cost-effective and operationally odd compared to a simple Standard-to-Standard-IA rule.

text: A company has migrated a two-tier application from its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The data tier is a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for Oracle with 12 TB of General Purpose SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. The application is designed to process and store documents in the database as binary large objects (blobs) with an average document size of 6 MB. The database size has grown over time, reducing the performance and increasing the cost of storage. The company must improve the database performance and needs a solution that is highly available and resilient. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Reduce the RDS DB instance size. Increase the storage capacity to 24 TiB. Change the storage type to Magnetic.
B. Increase the RDS DB instance size. Increase the storage capacity to 24 TiChange the storage type to Provisioned IOPS.
C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the application to store documents in the S3 bucket. Store the object metadata in the existing database.
D. Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Update the application to use DynamoDB. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate data from the Oracle database to DynamoDB.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. Reducing instance size and switching to Magnetic storage would degrade performance, and Magnetic is legacy/low-performance, so this worsens rather than improves performance.

✗ B. Increasing instance size and using Provisioned IOPS improves performance but is the most expensive storage option and does not address storing large 6 MB blobs inefficiently in the database, so it is not the most cost-effective.

✓ C. Moving the 6 MB document blobs to an Amazon S3 bucket and keeping only metadata in RDS dramatically shrinks the database, improves database performance, lowers storage cost, and S3 is highly available and durable, meeting all requirements cost-effectively.
✗ D. Migrating to DynamoDB requires re-architecting the relational application and DynamoDB items are capped at 400 KB, which cannot hold 6 MB documents, so this is unsuitable.

text: A company has an application that serves clients that are deployed in more than 20.000 retail storefront locations around the world. The application consists of backend web services that are exposed over HTTPS on port 443. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The retail locations communicate with the web application over the public internet. The company allows each retail location to register the IP address that the retail location has been allocated by its local ISP. The company's security team recommends to increase the security of the application endpoint by restricting access to only the IP addresses registered by the retail locations. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB. Use IP rule sets on the ALB to filter trafic. Update the IP addresses in the rule to include the registered IP addresses.
B. Deploy AWS Firewall Manager to manage the ALConfigure firewall rules to restrict trafic to the ALModify the firewall rules to include the registered IP addresses.
C. Store the IP addresses in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure an AWS Lambda authorization function on the ALB to validate that incoming requests are from the registered IP addresses.
D. Configure the network ACL on the subnet that contains the public interface of the ALB. Update the ingress rules on the network ACL with entries for each of the registered IP addresses.
optionExplanations: ✓ A. An AWS WAF web ACL associated with the ALB with an IP set rule allows the company to allow only the registered ISP IP addresses and easily update the list, supporting large numbers of IPs at scale, which directly meets the requirement.

✗ B. AWS Firewall Manager is a central policy orchestrator for WAF/Shield/security groups across accounts; it does not itself filter ALB traffic and is overkill, with the actual filtering still done by WAF.
✗ C. ALBs do not support Lambda authorizer functions (that is an API Gateway feature), so configuring a Lambda authorization function on the ALB is not possible.
✗ D. Network ACLs have a low rule limit (around 20-40 entries) and are stateless, so they cannot scale to the large number of registered IP addresses from 20,000 retail locations.

text: A company is building a data analysis platform on AWS by using AWS Lake Formation. The platform will ingest data from different sources such as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS. The company needs a secure solution to prevent access to portions of the data that contain sensitive information. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an IAM role that includes permissions to access Lake Formation tables.
B. Create data filters to implement row-level security and cell-level security.
C. Create an AWS Lambda function that removes sensitive information before Lake Formation ingests the data.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that periodically queries and removes sensitive information from Lake Formation tables.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. An IAM role granting table access controls which principals can access tables but cannot mask or hide specific sensitive rows/columns within the data, so it does not meet the fine-grained requirement.

✓ B. Lake Formation data filters provide built-in row-level and cell-level (column/cell) security, restricting access to sensitive portions of the data declaratively with the least operational overhead.
✗ C. A Lambda function that strips sensitive data before ingestion requires building and maintaining custom pre-processing and loses the sensitive data entirely, adding operational overhead.
✗ D. A Lambda function that periodically queries and removes sensitive data is custom, error-prone, and reactive rather than enforcing access control, adding significant operational overhead.

text: A company deploys Amazon EC2 instances that run in a VPC. The EC2 instances load source data into Amazon S3 buckets so that the data can be processed in the future. According to compliance laws, the data must not be transmitted over the public internet. Servers in the company's on- premises data center will consume the output from an application that runs on the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon EC2. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
B. Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and the VPC.
C. Set up an AWS Transit Gateway connection from the VPC to the S3 buckets. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
D. Set up proxy EC2 instances that have routes to NAT gateways. Configure the proxy EC2 instances to fetch S3 data and feed the application instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. An interface VPC endpoint for Amazon EC2 governs EC2 API calls, not S3 data traffic, so it does not keep the S3 data path off the public internet.

✓ B. A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 keeps EC2-to-S3 traffic on the private AWS network, and AWS Direct Connect provides a private link for the on-premises servers to consume the application output, satisfying the no-public-internet requirement.

✗ C. Transit Gateway does not connect directly to S3 buckets (it routes VPC/VPN/Direct Connect traffic), so 'a Transit Gateway connection to the S3 buckets' is not a valid construct for private S3 access.
✗ D. Proxy EC2 instances using NAT gateways send S3 traffic out through the NAT to the public S3 endpoint over the internet, violating the requirement that data not traverse the public internet.

text: A company has an application with a REST-based interface that allows data to be received in near-real time from a third-party vendor. Once received, the application processes and stores the data for further analysis. The application is running on Amazon EC2 instances. The third-party vendor has received many 503 Service Unavailable Errors when sending data to the application. When the data volume spikes, the compute capacity reaches its maximum limit and the application is unable to process all requests. Which design should a solutions architect recommend to provide a more scalable solution?
options: A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. Process the data using AWS Lambda functions.
B. Use Amazon API Gateway on top of the existing application. Create a usage plan with a quota limit for the third-party vendor.
C. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to ingest the data. Put the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
D. Repackage the application as a container. Deploy the application using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using the EC2 launch type with an Auto Scaling group.
optionExplanations: ✓ A. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams buffers and ingests the near-real-time data, decoupling ingestion from processing, and Lambda scales to process records in parallel, so spikes are absorbed without 503 errors and the solution scales elastically.
✗ B. API Gateway with a usage plan/quota would throttle the vendor rather than scale to handle the data, which limits throughput instead of solving the capacity problem.

✗ C. Amazon SNS is a pub/sub notification service that does not durably buffer/ingest a stream for later processing, and it is not designed to absorb high-volume data ingestion spikes the way a streaming service is.

✗ D. Repackaging as ECS on EC2 with Auto Scaling still relies on synchronous compute scaling that may lag behind sudden spikes, so requests can still be dropped before capacity scales, unlike a buffered streaming approach.

text: A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to process sensitive information from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application must not use the internet to connect to the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure an internet gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the internet gateway. Update the application to use the new internet gateway.
B. Configure a VPN connection. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPN connection. Update the application to use the new VPN connection.
C. Configure a NAT gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the NAT gateway. Update the application to use the new NAT gateway.
D. Configure a VPC endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPC endpoint. Update the application to use the new VPC endpoint.
optionExplanations: ✗ A. An internet gateway provides public internet connectivity, which is exactly what the requirement forbids, and S3 bucket policies cannot reference an internet gateway.
✗ B. A VPN connection is for connecting networks (e.g., on-premises to VPC) and does not provide a private path from the VPC to S3; bucket policies cannot reference a VPN connection.
✗ C. A NAT gateway routes private subnet traffic out to the public internet to reach S3's public endpoint, which violates the no-internet requirement.

✓ D. A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 lets the private-subnet EC2 instances reach the S3 bucket entirely over the AWS private network, and the bucket policy can restrict access to that endpoint, meeting the no-internet requirement.

text: A company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run a container application. The EKS cluster stores sensitive information in the Kubernetes secrets object. The company wants to ensure that the information is encrypted. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use the container application to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
B. Enable secrets encryption in the EKS cluster by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
C. Implement an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
D. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
optionExplanations: ✗ Having the container application encrypt secrets with KMS pushes encryption logic into application code, adding significant development and operational overhead instead of using native EKS envelope encryption.

✓ EKS natively supports envelope encryption of Kubernetes secrets using a KMS key. Enabling secrets encryption with KMS is a built-in feature requiring minimal configuration and no custom code, giving the least operational overhead.
✗ A custom Lambda function to encrypt secrets with KMS requires building, deploying, and maintaining code and integration plumbing, far more overhead than the native EKS KMS feature.

✗ SSM Parameter Store with KMS can store encrypted values, but it moves secrets out of the native Kubernetes secrets object and requires re-architecting how the app retrieves them, adding overhead versus encrypting EKS secrets in place.

text: A company is designing a new multi-tier web application that consists of the following components: • Web and application servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances as part of Auto Scaling groups • An Amazon RDS DB instance for data storage A solutions architect needs to limit access to the application servers so that only the web servers can access them. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy AWS PrivateLink in front of the application servers. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
B. Deploy a VPC endpoint in front of the application servers. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.

C. Deploy a Network Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the network ACL to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.

D. Deploy an Application Load Balancer with a target group that contains the application servers' Auto Scaling group. Configure the security group to allow only the web servers to access the application servers.
optionExplanations: ✗ PrivateLink exposes a service across VPCs/accounts via endpoints and is overkill here; also security is best enforced with security groups, not network ACLs, which are stateless and harder to manage for instance-to-instance access.

✗ A VPC endpoint provides private connectivity to AWS services (or PrivateLink services), not a mechanism to front internal EC2 application servers within the same VPC, so it does not fit this requirement.

✗ A Network Load Balancer can front the app servers, but NLB does not have security groups in this scenario and the answer relies on network ACLs, which are stateless and a poor tool for restricting source instances compared to security groups.

✓ An Application Load Balancer fronts the application servers' Auto Scaling group, and configuring its (and the instances') security group to allow inbound traffic only from the web servers' security group cleanly restricts access so only web servers reach the app tier.

text: A company runs a critical, customer-facing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application has a microservices architecture. The company needs to implement a solution that collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from the application in a centralized location. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Run the Amazon CloudWatch agent in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
B. Run AWS App Mesh in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the App Mesh console.
C. Configure AWS CloudTrail to capture data events. Query CloudTrail by using Amazon OpenSearch Service.
D. Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
optionExplanations: ✗ Running the CloudWatch agent in EKS can collect some metrics and logs, but it requires more manual configuration and does not provide the automatic per-pod/per-service container-level aggregation and summarized dashboards that Container Insights gives.

✗ AWS App Mesh is a service mesh for traffic control and observability instrumentation; it is not a centralized collection/aggregation/summarization solution for cluster metrics and logs and has no metrics/logs console of its own.

✗ CloudTrail captures API management/data events for auditing, not application metrics and logs; querying it via OpenSearch does not meet the requirement to aggregate application performance metrics and logs.

✓ CloudWatch Container Insights is purpose-built to collect, aggregate, and summarize metrics and logs from EKS containers, services, and pods, with everything viewable centrally in the CloudWatch console.

text: A company has deployed its newest product on AWS. The product runs in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer. The company stores the product’s objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company recently experienced malicious attacks against its systems. The company needs a solution that continuously monitors for malicious activity in the AWS account, workloads, and access patterns to the S3 bucket. The solution must also report suspicious activity and display the information on a dashboard. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure Amazon Macie to monitor and report findings to AWS Config.
B. Configure Amazon Inspector to monitor and report findings to AWS CloudTrail.
C. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor and report findings to AWS Security Hub.
D. Configure AWS Config to monitor and report findings to Amazon EventBridge.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data in S3; it does not continuously monitor account-wide malicious activity or threat access patterns, and AWS Config is not a findings dashboard target for Macie.

✗ Amazon Inspector assesses workloads for software vulnerabilities and network exposure, not continuous malicious-activity/threat detection across the account and S3 access patterns, and CloudTrail is not a findings reporting destination.

✓ Amazon GuardDuty continuously monitors the AWS account, workloads, and S3 access patterns (via CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs) for malicious activity and threats, and sends findings to AWS Security Hub for a centralized dashboard.

✗ AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, not malicious activity or threat detection; sending findings to EventBridge would not provide threat monitoring of access patterns or a security dashboard.

text: A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts a storage server that stores data in an NFS-based file system. The storage server holds 200 GB of data. The company needs to migrate the data without interruption to existing services. Multiple resources in AWS must be able to access the data by using the NFS protocol. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
options: A. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
B. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to receive the data.
D. Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data into the AWS destination.
E. Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center. Use a DataSync task between the on-premises location and AWS.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon FSx for Lustre is a high-performance file system for HPC/ML workloads using the Lustre protocol, not NFS; it is far more expensive than EFS and unnecessary for sharing 200 GB over NFS.

✓ Amazon EFS provides a fully managed, elastic NFS file system that multiple AWS resources can mount and access concurrently via the NFS protocol, making it the cost-effective destination that meets the requirement.
✗ An Amazon S3 bucket is object storage accessed via HTTP/S APIs, not the NFS protocol, so it cannot natively serve as an NFS mount target for multiple resources.

✗ Manually using an OS copy command is operationally heavy, error-prone, lacks built-in encryption/verification/scheduling, and risks interrupting existing services, so it is not the recommended migration method.

✓ Installing an AWS DataSync agent on premises and running a DataSync task automates, accelerates, and securely transfers the NFS data to AWS with verification and minimal disruption, making it the cost-effective migration step.

text: A company wants to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for its Amazon EC2 instances that have an SMB file share mounted as a volume in the us-east-1 Region. The company has a recovery point objective (RPO) of 5 minutes for planned system maintenance or unplanned service disruptions. The company needs to replicate the file system to the us-west-2 Region. The replicated data must not be deleted by any user for 5 years. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

B. Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

C. Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Multi-AZ deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.

D. Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in us-east-1 that has a Single-AZ 2 deployment type. Use AWS Backup to create a daily backup plan that includes a backup rule that copies the backup to us-west-2. Configure AWS Backup Vault Lock in governance mode for a target vault in us-west-2. Configure a minimum duration of 5 years.
optionExplanations: ✗ Single-AZ 2 does not protect against an AZ-level disruption, so it fails the 5-minute RPO requirement for unplanned service disruptions; compliance-mode lock is correct but the deployment type is wrong.
✗ Multi-AZ correctly meets the RPO, but governance-mode Vault Lock can be bypassed/overridden by users with sufficient IAM permissions, so data could still be deleted within the 5 years.

✓ Multi-AZ FSx for Windows provides synchronous standby replication meeting the 5-minute RPO, AWS Backup copies daily backups to us-west-2, and compliance-mode Vault Lock makes the recovery points immutable so no user (including root) can delete them for the 5-year minimum.
✗ Single-AZ 2 does not satisfy the RPO for AZ-level disruptions, and governance mode does not enforce true immutability against privileged users, so this fails both requirements.

text: A solutions architect is designing a security solution for a company that wants to provide developers with individual AWS accounts through AWS Organizations, while also maintaining standard security controls. Because the individual developers will have AWS account root user-level access to their own accounts, the solutions architect wants to ensure that the mandatory AWS CloudTrail configuration that is applied to new developer accounts is not modified. Which action meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM policy that prohibits changes to CloudTrail. and attach it to the root user.
B. Create a new trail in CloudTrail from within the developer accounts with the organization trails option enabled.
C. Create a service control policy (SCP) that prohibits changes to CloudTrail, and attach it the developer accounts.
D. Create a service-linked role for CloudTrail with a policy condition that allows changes only from an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the management account.
optionExplanations: ✗ You cannot attach IAM policies to the AWS account root user to restrict it, and IAM policies do not constrain the root user, so this cannot prevent developers from modifying CloudTrail in their own accounts.
✗ Creating a trail from within a developer account does not protect the mandatory configuration; the developer root user could still modify or delete that trail, so it fails the requirement.

✓ A service control policy attached to the developer accounts via AWS Organizations sets a permission boundary that even the account root user cannot exceed, so it can prohibit any changes to the mandatory CloudTrail configuration.

✗ Service-linked roles for CloudTrail are used by the service to perform actions on your behalf and cannot be configured to block account root users from changing the trail configuration, so this does not enforce the protection.

text: A company is planning to deploy a business-critical application in the AWS Cloud. The application requires durable storage with consistent, low- latency performance. Which type of storage should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Instance store volume
B. Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster
C. Provisioned IOPS SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
D. Throughput Optimized HDD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
optionExplanations: ✗ Instance store volumes are ephemeral and lost when the instance stops or fails, so they are not durable storage for a business-critical application.
✗ ElastiCache for Memcached is an in-memory cache that is not durable and is not designed as a primary persistent storage layer.
✓ A Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) EBS volume provides durable block storage with consistent, low-latency performance and a guaranteed IOPS level, matching the requirement.

✗ Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) is designed for large sequential throughput workloads, not low-latency consistent performance, and cannot be a boot volume; it does not meet the low-latency requirement.

text: An online photo-sharing company stores its photos in an Amazon S3 bucket that exists in the us-west-1 Region. The company needs to store a copy of all new photos in the us-east-1 Region. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.
B. Create a cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration of the existing S3 bucket. Specify us-east-1 in the CORS rule's AllowedOrigin element.
C. Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1 across multiple Availability Zones. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to save photos into the second S3 bucket.

D. Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 event notifications on object creation and update events to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✓ Creating a second bucket in us-east-1 and enabling S3 Cross-Region Replication automatically and asynchronously copies all new objects to the other Region with no custom code, giving the least operational effort.
✗ CORS controls which web origins can make browser requests to a bucket; it does not copy or replicate objects between Regions, so it does not meet the requirement.
✗ S3 Lifecycle rules transition or expire objects within storage classes and cannot copy objects into a different bucket or Region, so this does not replicate the photos.

✗ S3 event notifications invoking a Lambda function to copy each object works but requires writing, deploying, and maintaining custom code and handling failures, which is far more operational effort than native Cross-Region Replication.

text: A company is creating a new web application for its subscribers. The application will consist of a static single page and a persistent database layer. The application will have millions of users for 4 hours in the morning, but the application will have only a few thousand users during the rest of the day. The company's data architects have requested the ability to rapidly evolve their schema. Which solutions will meet these requirements and provide the MOST scalability? (Choose two.)
options: A. Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution. Provision on-demand capacity.
B. Deploy Amazon Aurora as the database solution. Choose the serverless DB engine mode.
C. Deploy Amazon DynamoDB as the database solution. Ensure that DynamoDB auto scaling is enabled.
D. Deploy the static content into an Amazon S3 bucket. Provision an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin.

E. Deploy the web servers for static content across a fieet of Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. Configure the instances to periodically refresh the content from an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume.
optionExplanations: ✓ DynamoDB is a schemaless NoSQL database allowing rapid schema evolution, and on-demand capacity instantly scales to the massive 4-hour morning spike and back down without capacity planning, providing the most scalability for the database layer.

✗ Aurora Serverless scales compute automatically but is a relational SQL engine with a defined schema, so it does not satisfy the data architects' need to rapidly evolve their schema as well as DynamoDB does.

✗ DynamoDB with auto scaling adjusts provisioned capacity, but auto scaling reacts more slowly to sudden, extreme spikes than on-demand capacity, so it is less ideal than on-demand for the bursty millions-of-users pattern.

✓ Hosting the static single-page content in S3 with a CloudFront distribution provides virtually unlimited, highly scalable, low-latency global delivery of the static front end with no servers to manage.

✗ Serving static content from EC2 Auto Scaling groups refreshing from EFS adds server management and slower scaling, providing far less scalability and more operational overhead than S3 plus CloudFront for static content.

text: A company uses Amazon API Gateway to manage its REST APIs that third-party service providers access. The company must protect the REST APIs from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. What is the MOST operationally eficient solution that meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Shield.
B. Configure AWS WAF.
C. Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS Shield in CloudFront.
D. Set up API Gateway with an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure AWS WAF in CloudFront.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks; it does not inspect requests for SQL injection or cross-site scripting, so it does not meet the requirement.

✓ AWS WAF can be associated directly with the API Gateway REST API stage and uses managed rule groups to block SQL injection and XSS attacks, the most operationally efficient solution since it needs no extra CloudFront layer.
✗ Adding a CloudFront distribution and Shield introduces an unnecessary layer and Shield still does not address SQLi/XSS, making this less efficient and not meeting the requirement.

✗ Putting CloudFront in front of API Gateway with WAF would work for SQLi/XSS but adds an extra CloudFront distribution to manage, which is less operationally efficient than attaching WAF directly to API Gateway.

text: A company wants to provide users with access to AWS resources.
