The company has 1,500 users and manages their access to on-premises resources through Active Directory user groups on the corporate network. However, the company does not want users to have to maintain another identity to access the resources. A solutions architect must manage user access to the AWS resources while preserving access to the on- premises resources. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM user for each user in the company. Attach the appropriate policies to each user.
B. Use Amazon Cognito with an Active Directory user pool. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached.
C. Define cross-account roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
D. Configure Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2 0-based federation. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
optionExplanations: ✗ Creating an individual IAM user for each of the 1,500 users forces a separate AWS identity, which is exactly what the company wants to avoid and is operationally unsustainable.

✗ Amazon Cognito user pools target application end-user authentication (web/mobile apps), not federated workforce access to AWS resources from an existing corporate Active Directory, so it is not the right fit.
✗ Cross-account roles share access between AWS accounts; they do not federate on-premises Active Directory users into AWS or let users keep a single corporate identity.

✓ Configuring SAML 2.0 federation between the corporate Active Directory and AWS, with IAM roles mapped to AD groups, lets the 1,500 users sign in with their existing AD credentials to access AWS resources while retaining on-premises access, avoiding a second identity.

text: A company is hosting a website behind multiple Application Load Balancers. The company has different distribution rights for its content around the world. A solutions architect needs to ensure that users are served the correct content without violating distribution rights. Which configuration should the solutions architect choose to meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure Amazon CloudFront with AWS WAF.
B. Configure Application Load Balancers with AWS WAF
C. Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation policy
D. Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geoproximity routing policy
optionExplanations: ✗ CloudFront with AWS WAF is a CDN with web ACL filtering; while CloudFront supports geo-restriction (allow/block by country), the requirement is to route users to the correct content/ALB based on location, not just block. WAF does not select content by geography.

✗ AWS WAF on the ALBs provides web request filtering (SQLi, XSS, rate limiting, and geo-match conditions to block), but it does not route or serve different content per region; it is a security filter, not a routing mechanism.

✓ Route 53 geolocation routing policy routes DNS queries to specific endpoints based on the geographic location of the user, which lets each region's users reach the ALB serving content licensed for their region, satisfying distribution rights. Correct.

✗ Route 53 geoproximity routing routes based on the proximity of resources to users and allows shifting traffic with a bias; it is for balancing/optimizing traffic by distance, not for enforcing per-country content distribution rights, making it less appropriate than geolocation.

text: A company stores its data on premises. The amount of data is growing beyond the company's available capacity. The company wants to migrate its data from the on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs a solution that will automatically validate the integrity of the data after the transfer. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Order an AWS Snowball Edge device. Configure the Snowball Edge device to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket
B. Deploy an AWS DataSync agent on premises. Configure the DataSync agent to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
C. Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises Configure the S3 File Gateway to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket
D. Configure an accelerator in Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on premises. Configure the accelerator to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Snowball Edge is for offline/physical bulk transfer and is described here as 'online' transfer, which is incorrect; it is also not the intended online solution and does not natively provide automatic post-transfer integrity validation as DataSync does.

✓ AWS DataSync uses an on-premises agent to perform online transfers to S3 and automatically performs data integrity verification (checksum validation) during and after the transfer, exactly meeting the requirement.

✗ Amazon S3 File Gateway provides a hybrid NFS/SMB file interface backed by S3 for ongoing access, but it is designed for file caching/access rather than one-time bulk migration with automatic end-to-end integrity validation.

✗ S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront edge locations to speed uploads over long distances but does not provide automatic data integrity validation of the transferred dataset, so it does not meet the requirement.

text: A company wants to migrate two DNS servers to AWS. The servers host a total of approximately 200 zones and receive 1 million requests each day on average. The company wants to maximize availability while minimizing the operational overhead that is related to the management of the two servers. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create 200 new hosted zones in the Amazon Route 53 console Import zone files.
B. Launch a single large Amazon EC2 instance Import zone tiles. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.
C. Migrate the servers to AWS by using AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.

D. Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones. Import zone files. Set the desired capacity to 1 and the maximum capacity to 3 for the Auto Scaling group. Configure scaling alarms to scale based on CPU utilization.
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon Route 53 is a fully managed, highly available DNS service; creating 200 hosted zones and importing the zone files removes server management entirely and provides built-in high availability, matching the requirements.
✗ A single large EC2 instance is a single point of failure with no high availability and requires managing the DNS software, which is the opposite of minimizing operational overhead.
✗ AWS SMS migrates server workloads as-is to EC2, leaving the company to manage self-hosted DNS servers and their availability, which does not minimize operational overhead.

✗ An EC2 Auto Scaling group adds resilience but still requires managing the DNS software and instances; CPU-based scaling is irrelevant for a low-volume DNS workload, so it is far more overhead than managed Route 53.

text: A global company runs its applications in multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The company's applications use multipart uploads to upload data to multiple Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions. The company wants to report on incomplete multipart uploads for cost compliance purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Configure AWS Config with a rule to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
B. Create a service control policy (SCP) to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
C. Configure S3 Storage Lens to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
D. Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Config tracks resource configuration and compliance but does not natively report object-level metrics like incomplete multipart upload counts across buckets and accounts.
✗ An SCP is a guardrail that restricts permissions across accounts; it cannot generate reports or count incomplete multipart uploads.

✓ S3 Storage Lens provides organization-wide storage analytics, including an incomplete multipart upload bytes/count metric aggregated across accounts and Regions, meeting the requirement with the least operational overhead.
✗ An S3 Multi-Region Access Point routes requests to buckets across Regions for access; it does not report on incomplete multipart uploads.

text: A company runs a production database on Amazon RDS for MySQL. The company wants to upgrade the database version for security compliance reasons. Because the database contains critical data, the company wants a quick solution to upgrade and test functionality without losing any data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an RDS manual snapshot. Upgrade to the new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
B. Use native backup and restore. Restore the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
C. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
D. Use Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments to deploy and test production changes.
optionExplanations: ✗ Taking a manual snapshot and upgrading in place protects against data loss but causes downtime and provides no isolated environment to test the new version before cutover.
✗ Native backup and restore to a new upgraded instance is slow, manual, and risks data drift; it is not a quick, low-overhead test-and-cutover approach.
✗ AWS DMS can replicate to an upgraded instance but requires setting up and managing migration tasks and endpoints, adding operational overhead versus a managed clone-and-switch.

✓ RDS Blue/Green Deployments create a synchronized green environment on the new version for safe testing and a fast, low-risk switchover with minimal downtime and no data loss, giving the least operational overhead.

text: A solutions architect is creating a data processing job that runs once daily and can take up to 2 hours to complete. If the job is interrupted, it has to restart from the beginning. How should the solutions architect address this issue in the MOST cost-effective manner?
options: A. Create a script that runs locally on an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance that is triggered by a cron job.
B. Create an AWS Lambda function triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
C. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Fargate task triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
D. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task running on Amazon EC2 triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
optionExplanations: ✗ An EC2 Reserved Instance runs (and bills) continuously even though the job runs only 2 hours per day, which is not cost-effective for an intermittent workload.
✗ Lambda has a maximum execution timeout of 15 minutes, so it cannot run a job that takes up to 2 hours.
✓ ECS Fargate triggered by an EventBridge schedule runs the task only when needed, billing per task for the 2-hour run with no idle servers to manage, making it the most cost-effective fit.
✗ ECS on EC2 requires running and paying for the underlying EC2 capacity (and managing it), which is less cost-effective than Fargate for a once-daily short-lived task.

text: A social media company wants to store its database of user profiles, relationships, and interactions in the AWS Cloud. The company needs an application to monitor any changes in the database. The application needs to analyze the relationships between the data entities and to provide recommendations to users. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
B. Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
C. Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
D. Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
optionExplanations: ✗ Neptune is the correct graph database for relationships and recommendations, but Kinesis Data Streams would require building a custom mechanism to capture database changes, adding operational overhead compared to native streams.

✓ Amazon Neptune stores the highly connected user-profile/relationship data and supports recommendation queries, and Neptune Streams natively captures and processes change data with the least operational overhead.
✗ QLDB is an immutable ledger database, not a graph database, so it cannot efficiently model and analyze relationships or generate graph-based recommendations.
✗ QLDB is the wrong store for relationship analysis, and Neptune Streams is a Neptune feature that does not apply to QLDB, so this combination is invalid.

text: A company is creating a new application that will store a large amount of data. The data will be analyzed hourly and will be modified by several Amazon EC2 Linux instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zones. The needed amount of storage space will continue to grow for the next 6 months. Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
options: A. Store the data in Amazon S3 Glacier. Update the S3 Glacier vault policy to allow access to the application instances.
B. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on the application instances.
C. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the file system on the application instances.
D. Store the data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Provisioned IOPS volume shared between the application instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ S3 Glacier is archival cold storage with retrieval delays and is not a file system that EC2 instances can mount and modify for active hourly analysis.
✗ A standard EBS volume cannot be concurrently mounted and modified by multiple EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones (it is single-AZ, single-attach for general use).
✓ Amazon EFS is a shared, elastic NFS file system that multiple Linux EC2 instances across multiple AZs can mount and write to concurrently, and it grows automatically as storage needs increase.
✗ EBS Provisioned IOPS volumes are tied to a single AZ; even Multi-Attach io2 is single-AZ and not designed for general multi-instance file workloads across multiple Availability Zones.

text: A company manages an application that stores data on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Increases in trafic are causing performance problems. The company determines that database queries are the primary reason for the slow performance. What should a solutions architect do to improve the application's performance?
options: A. Serve read trafic from the Multi-AZ standby replica.
B. Configure the DB instance to use Transfer Acceleration.
C. Create a read replica from the source DB instance. Serve read trafic from the read replica.
D. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose between the application and Amazon RDS to increase the concurrency of database requests.
optionExplanations: ✗ The Multi-AZ standby replica cannot serve read traffic; it is a passive failover target that only becomes active during failover.
✗ Transfer Acceleration is an Amazon S3 feature for faster uploads and does not apply to RDS or to improving query performance.
✓ Creating a read replica and directing read traffic to it offloads read queries from the primary instance, relieving the query-driven performance bottleneck.
✗ Kinesis Data Firehose is a streaming delivery service to data stores like S3/Redshift; it does not sit between an application and RDS to increase query concurrency.

text: A company collects 10 GB of telemetry data daily from various machines. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket in a source data account. The company has hired several consulting agencies to use this data for analysis. Each agency needs read access to the data for its analysts. The company must share the data from the source data account by choosing a solution that maximizes security and operational eficiency. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure S3 global tables to replicate data for each agency.
B. Make the S3 bucket public for a limited time. Inform only the agencies.
C. Configure cross-account access for the S3 bucket to the accounts that the agencies own.
D. Set up an IAM user for each analyst in the source data account. Grant each user access to the S3 bucket.
optionExplanations: ✗ There is no 'S3 global tables' feature (global tables are a DynamoDB concept); replicating copies to each agency would also be insecure and operationally inefficient.
✗ Making the S3 bucket public, even temporarily, is a severe security risk and does not restrict access to only the intended agencies.

✓ Configuring cross-account access via bucket policy/IAM roles to the agencies' AWS accounts grants scoped read access without managing individual users or copying data, maximizing security and operational efficiency.
✗ Creating an IAM user per analyst in the source account is high-maintenance, scales poorly, and is less secure than delegating access to the agencies' own accounts.

text: A company uses Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP in its primary AWS Region for CIFS and NFS file shares. Applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances access the file shares. The company needs a storage disaster recovery (DR) solution in a secondary Region. The data that is replicated in the secondary Region needs to be accessed by using the same protocols as the primary Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an AWS Lambda function to copy the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Replicate the S3 bucket to the secondary Region.
B. Create a backup of the FSx for ONTAP volumes by using AWS Backup. Copy the volumes to the secondary Region. Create a new FSx for ONTAP instance from the backup.
C. Create an FSx for ONTAP instance in the secondary Region. Use NetApp SnapMirror to replicate data from the primary Region to the secondary Region.
D. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Migrate the current data to the volume. Replicate the volume to the secondary Region.
optionExplanations: ✗ Copying data to S3 via Lambda changes the storage protocol (objects instead of CIFS/NFS shares) and requires custom code, so it does not preserve the same file protocols with low overhead.
✗ AWS Backup of ONTAP volumes and rebuilding from backup is a manual, non-continuous DR process with higher RPO and more operational steps than native replication.

✓ Creating an FSx for ONTAP instance in the secondary Region and using NetApp SnapMirror provides continuous, native block-level replication, preserving the same CIFS/NFS access with the least operational overhead.
✗ Amazon EFS supports only NFS (not CIFS) and would require migrating off ONTAP, so it cannot serve the same protocols and adds migration overhead.

text: A development team is creating an event-based application that uses AWS Lambda functions. Events will be generated when files are added to an Amazon S3 bucket. The development team currently has Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) configured as the event target from Amazon S3. What should a solutions architect do to process the events from Amazon S3 in a scalable way?
options: A. Create an SNS subscription that processes the event in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) before the event runs in Lambda.
B. Create an SNS subscription that processes the event in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) before the event runs in Lambda
C. Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Configure the SOS queue to trigger a Lambda function.
D. Create an SNS subscription that sends the event to AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure the Lambda function to poll from the SMS event.
optionExplanations: ✗ Subscribing ECS to SNS to process events before Lambda is not a native SNS integration pattern and adds unnecessary complexity rather than scalable, decoupled processing.
✗ Subscribing EKS to SNS before Lambda introduces a managed Kubernetes cluster to operate and is not a standard scalable event-processing pattern for this use case.
✓ Fanning out SNS to an SQS queue that triggers Lambda decouples and buffers the events, absorbing spikes and enabling reliable, scalable, retry-capable processing.
✗ AWS SMS is the Server Migration Service and is unrelated to event processing; SNS cannot deliver events to it and Lambda cannot poll it.

text: A solutions architect is designing a new service behind Amazon API Gateway. The request patterns for the service will be unpredictable and can change suddenly from 0 requests to over 500 per second. The total size of the data that needs to be persisted in a backend database is currently less than 1 GB with unpredictable future growth. Data can be queried using simple key-value requests. Which combination ofAWS services would meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. AWS Fargate
B. AWS Lambda
C. Amazon DynamoDB
D. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
E. MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Fargate is serverless container compute but is more complex than Lambda for a simple API backend and does not scale instantly from 0 to 500 req/s as seamlessly; not the best fit here.
✓ AWS Lambda integrates natively with API Gateway and scales automatically and instantly from 0 to high concurrency, making it ideal for unpredictable, spiky request patterns.
✓ Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless key-value store with on-demand capacity that handles unpredictable growth and key-value queries with no capacity planning, fitting the sub-1GB data perfectly.
✗ EC2 Auto Scaling reacts to metrics over minutes and cannot instantly absorb a jump from 0 to 500 req/s; it also carries more operational overhead than serverless options.
✗ Aurora MySQL is a relational database that requires provisioned instances (or slower-scaling Serverless), is overkill for simple key-value access, and adds cost and management overhead.

text: A company collects and shares research data with the company's employees all over the world. The company wants to collect and store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket and process the data in the AWS Cloud. The company will share the data with the company's employees. The company needs a secure solution in the AWS Cloud that minimizes operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use an AWS Lambda function to create an S3 presigned URL. Instruct employees to use the URL.
B. Create an IAM user for each employee. Create an IAM policy for each employee to allow S3 access. Instruct employees to use the AWS Management Console.
C. Create an S3 File Gateway. Create a share for uploading and a share for downloading. Allow employees to mount shares on their local computers to use S3 File Gateway.
D. Configure AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoints. Select the custom identity provider options. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage the user credentials Instruct employees to use Transfer Family.
optionExplanations: ✓ An AWS Lambda function that generates S3 presigned URLs is serverless and fully managed, providing secure, time-limited access for employees to upload and download data with minimal operational overhead. Correct.

✗ Creating an IAM user and policy for each employee is high operational overhead, does not scale for a global workforce, and IAM users are not the recommended way to grant many human identities S3 access. Wrong.

✗ S3 File Gateway is a hybrid storage appliance for on-premises NFS/SMB access to S3 and requires deploying and maintaining gateway hardware/VMs, adding operational overhead and not suiting globally distributed employees. Wrong.

✗ AWS Transfer Family SFTP with a custom identity provider and Secrets Manager is workable but incurs always-on endpoint costs and the overhead of building and maintaining the custom identity provider integration, more operational burden than presigned URLs. Wrong.

text: A company is building a new furniture inventory application. The company has deployed the application on a fieet ofAmazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in their VPC. A solutions architect has observed that incoming trafic seems to favor one EC2 instance, resulting in latency for some requests. What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue?
options: A. Disable session afinity (sticky sessions) on the ALB
B. Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer
C. Increase the number of EC2 instances in each Availability Zone
D. Adjust the frequency of the health checks on the ALB's target group
optionExplanations: ✓ Disabling session affinity (sticky sessions) on the ALB removes the cookie that pins each client to a single target, allowing the ALB's round-robin/least-outstanding-requests algorithm to distribute traffic evenly. This is the classic cause and fix for traffic favoring one instance.

✗ Replacing the ALB with a Network Load Balancer does not address uneven distribution; an NLB operates at Layer 4, uses flow hashing, and is intended for TCP/UDP/low-latency use cases, not for fixing an ALB stickiness imbalance.

✗ Increasing the number of EC2 instances per AZ adds capacity but does not change the routing behavior; if sticky sessions are pinning traffic to one instance, the imbalance persists regardless of how many instances exist.
✗ Adjusting health check frequency only changes how quickly unhealthy targets are detected and removed; it has no effect on how traffic is balanced across healthy targets.

text: A company has an application workfiow that uses an AWS Lambda function to download and decrypt files from Amazon S3. These files are encrypted using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that will ensure the required permissions are set correctly. Which combination of actions accomplish this? (Choose two.)
options: A. Attach the kms:decrypt permission to the Lambda function’s resource policy
B. Grant the decrypt permission for the Lambda IAM role in the KMS key's policy
C. Grant the decrypt permission for the Lambda resource policy in the KMS key's policy.
D. Create a new IAM policy with the kms:decrypt permission and attach the policy to the Lambda function.
E. Create a new IAM role with the kms:decrypt permission and attach the execution role to the Lambda function.
optionExplanations: ✗ Wrong. Lambda resource policies (the function policy) control which principals can invoke the function; they do not grant the function permission to call kms:Decrypt. KMS permissions for the function come from its execution role, not its resource policy.
✓ KMS keys are protected by a key policy; granting kms:Decrypt to the Lambda execution role (an IAM principal) in the key policy is required to authorize that role to use the key.

✗ Wrong. A KMS key policy grants access to IAM principals (users/roles), not to a Lambda resource policy. A resource policy is not a principal and cannot be referenced as a grantee in a KMS key policy.

✗ Plausible but not the best pairing. Attaching an IAM policy with kms:Decrypt works only if it is attached to the Lambda execution role; you cannot attach an identity-based policy directly to a Lambda function. Option E correctly describes giving the permission via the execution role.

✓ The Lambda function needs an execution role, and granting kms:Decrypt to that role via IAM gives the function the identity-side permission required to decrypt the files (paired with the KMS key policy grant in B).

text: A company wants to monitor its AWS costs for financial review. The cloud operations team is designing an architecture in the AWS Organizations management account to query AWS Cost and Usage Reports for all member accounts. The team must run this query once a month and provide a detailed analysis of the bill. Which solution is the MOST scalable and cost-effective way to meet these requirements?
options: A. Enable Cost and Usage Reports in the management account. Deliver reports to Amazon Kinesis. Use Amazon EMR for analysis.
B. Enable Cost and Usage Reports in the management account. Deliver the reports to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Athena for analysis.
C. Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Redshift for analysis.
D. Enable Cost and Usage Reports for member accounts. Deliver the reports to Amazon Kinesis. Use Amazon QuickSight tor analysis.
optionExplanations: ✗ CUR can be enabled in the management account to cover all member accounts, but Kinesis is a streaming service unsuited for monthly batch CUR delivery, and EMR is heavyweight and costly for a once-a-month query, failing the cost-effective and low-overhead requirement.

✓ enabling CUR in the Organizations management account captures all member account data, delivering to S3 is the native CUR destination, and Amazon Athena provides serverless, pay-per-query SQL analysis that is the most scalable and cost-effective option for a monthly query.

✗ Enabling CUR per member account adds operational overhead versus consolidating in the management account, and Amazon Redshift requires a provisioned cluster that is expensive and over-provisioned for a once-a-month query.
✗ CUR cannot natively deliver to Kinesis (it delivers to S3), and per-member-account enablement plus QuickSight does not match the serverless query requirement; this is the least appropriate option.

text: A company wants to run a gaming application on Amazon EC2 instances that are part of an Auto Scaling group in the AWS Cloud. The application will transmit data by using UDP packets. The company wants to ensure that the application can scale out and in as trafic increases and decreases. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Attach a Network Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
B. Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
C. Deploy an Amazon Route 53 record set with a weighted policy to route trafic appropriately.
D. Deploy a NAT instance that is configured with port forwarding to the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group.
optionExplanations: ✓ A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and supports UDP, distributing the gaming traffic across the Auto Scaling group while scaling out and in.
✗ An Application Load Balancer only handles HTTP/HTTPS at Layer 7 and does not support UDP traffic.
✗ A Route 53 weighted record routes by DNS but does not provide the connection-level load balancing or seamless integration with an Auto Scaling group that the NLB does.
✗ A NAT instance with port forwarding is a single point of failure, does not scale, and is not a load-balancing solution for an Auto Scaling group.

text: A company runs several websites on AWS for its different brands. Each website generates tens of gigabytes of web trafic logs each day. A solutions architect needs to design a scalable solution to give the company's developers the ability to analyze trafic patterns across all the company's websites. This analysis by the developers will occur on demand once a week over the course of several months. The solution must support queries with standard SQL. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena tor analysis.
B. Store the logs in Amazon RDS. Use a database client for analysis.
C. Store the logs in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Use OpenSearch Service for analysis.
D. Store the logs in an Amazon EMR cluster Use a supported open-source framework for SQL-based analysis.
optionExplanations: ✓ Storing logs in S3 and querying with serverless Athena using standard SQL is the most cost-effective option, since you pay only per on-demand query rather than for always-on infrastructure.
✗ Amazon RDS requires ingesting logs into a running relational database, which is costly and operationally heavy for tens of gigabytes of logs queried only weekly.
✗ OpenSearch Service requires an always-running cluster, making it expensive for infrequent weekly analysis, and its query syntax is not standard SQL.
✗ An EMR cluster incurs ongoing or repeated cluster costs and management overhead, which is not cost-effective for on-demand weekly SQL queries compared to serverless Athena.

text: An international company has a subdomain for each country that the company operates in. The subdomains are formatted as example.com, country1.example.com, and country2.example.com. The company's workloads are behind an Application Load Balancer. The company wants to encrypt the website data that is in transit. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a public certificate for the apex top domain example com and a wildcard certificate for *.example.com.
B. Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a private certificate for the apex top domain example.com and a wildcard certificate for *.example.com.
C. Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a public and private certificate for the apex top domain example.com.
D. Validate domain ownership by email address. Switch to DNS validation by adding the required DNS records to the DNS provider.
E. Validate domain ownership for the domain by adding the required DNS records to the DNS provider.
optionExplanations: ✓ Requesting a public ACM certificate for the apex example.com plus a wildcard *.example.com covers the apex and all country subdomains, enabling TLS encryption in transit on the public-facing ALB.
✗ A private certificate (from ACM Private CA) is for internal use and is not trusted by public browsers, so it does not work for public website encryption.
✗ Requesting both a public and private certificate for only the apex domain fails to cover the subdomains and the private cert is unneeded for public TLS.
✗ Email validation followed by switching to DNS validation is unnecessarily convoluted; the requirement is met directly with DNS validation alone.
✓ Validating domain ownership by adding the required DNS records (DNS validation) confirms ownership and supports automatic renewal, which is the recommended ACM validation method.

text: A company is required to use cryptographic keys in its on-premises key manager. The key manager is outside of the AWS Cloud because of regulatory and compliance requirements. The company wants to manage encryption and decryption by using cryptographic keys that are retained outside of the AWS Cloud and that support a variety of external key managers from different vendors. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use AWS CloudHSM key store backed by a CloudHSM cluster.
B. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) external key store backed by an external key manager.
C. Use the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) managed key store.
D. Use a custom key store backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster.
optionExplanations: ✗ A CloudHSM key store stores keys in an AWS-hosted CloudHSM cluster, not outside the AWS Cloud, and does not integrate with third-party external key managers.

✓ AWS KMS External Key Store (XKS) lets KMS use cryptographic keys that remain in an external key manager outside AWS from various vendors, with minimal operational overhead while keeping KMS integration.
✗ The default KMS managed key store keeps keys within AWS KMS, not in an external on-premises key manager, so it does not meet the regulatory requirement.
✗ A custom key store backed by CloudHSM still keeps keys within an AWS-managed CloudHSM cluster, not in an external third-party key manager outside AWS.

text: A solutions architect needs to host a high performance computing (HPC) workload in the AWS Cloud. The workload will run on hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances and will require parallel access to a shared file system to enable distributed processing of large datasets. Datasets will be accessed across multiple instances simultaneously. The workload requires access latency within 1 ms. After processing has completed, engineers will need access to the dataset for manual postprocessing. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) as a shared file system. Access the dataset from Amazon EFS.
B. Mount an Amazon S3 bucket to serve as the shared file system. Perform postprocessing directly from the S3 bucket.
C. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre as a shared file system. Link the file system to an Amazon S3 bucket for postprocessing.
D. Configure AWS Resource Access Manager to share an Amazon S3 bucket so that it can be mounted to all instances for processing and postprocessing.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon EFS provides shared NFS access but cannot deliver the sub-millisecond, hundreds-of-GB/s throughput that HPC parallel workloads require.
✗ Mounting an S3 bucket as a file system does not provide the low-latency, high-throughput POSIX file access needed for distributed HPC processing.
✓ FSx for Lustre is purpose-built for HPC with sub-millisecond latency and massive parallel throughput, and it can link to an S3 bucket so engineers can access the dataset for postprocessing.
✗ AWS RAM shares resources across accounts and does not provide a high-performance shared file system; S3 is not mountable as a low-latency parallel file system this way.

text: A gaming company is building an application with Voice over IP capabilities. The application will serve trafic to users across the world. The application needs to be highly available with an automated failover across AWS Regions. The company wants to minimize the latency of users without relying on IP address caching on user devices. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Global Accelerator with health checks.
B. Use Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation routing policy.
C. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that includes multiple origins.
D. Create an Application Load Balancer that uses path-based routing.
optionExplanations: ✓ AWS Global Accelerator uses anycast static IPs with health checks to provide automated cross-Region failover and low-latency routing over the AWS backbone, avoiding client-side IP caching issues inherent to DNS.
✗ Route 53 geolocation routing relies on DNS, which is subject to client-side IP/DNS caching and provides slower failover, conflicting with the no-caching requirement.
✗ CloudFront is optimized for HTTP/HTTPS content delivery and caching, not for real-time VoIP traffic requiring cross-Region failover.
✗ An Application Load Balancer with path-based routing operates within a single Region and does not provide cross-Region failover for global VoIP traffic.

text: A weather forecasting company needs to process hundreds of gigabytes of data with sub-millisecond latency. The company has a high performance computing (HPC) environment in its data center and wants to expand its forecasting capabilities. A solutions architect must identify a highly available cloud storage solution that can handle large amounts of sustained throughput. Files that are stored in the solution should be accessible to thousands of compute instances that will simultaneously access and process the entire dataset. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre scratch file systems.
B. Use Amazon FSx for Lustre persistent file systems.
C. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Bursting Throughput mode.
D. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Provisioned Throughput mode.
optionExplanations: ✗ FSx for Lustre scratch file systems deliver sub-millisecond latency and very high throughput for HPC, but they are NOT highly available or durable: data is not replicated and is lost if a file server fails. This fails the explicit 'highly available' requirement, making it suited only to short-term, fault-tolerant processing.

✓ FSx for Lustre persistent file systems are purpose-built for HPC and machine learning, providing sub-millisecond latencies, hundreds of GB/s of sustained throughput, and concurrent access by thousands of compute instances, while replicating data within an AZ for high availability and durability. This matches every requirement.

✗ EFS is a general-purpose NFS file system optimized for shared access, but it does not deliver the sub-millisecond latency or the massive sustained HPC throughput required; Bursting Throughput mode scales with stored size and can throttle once burst credits are exhausted, making it unsuitable for thousands of instances processing the full dataset.

✗ EFS Provisioned Throughput mode lets you set throughput independent of size, but EFS still cannot match the sub-millisecond latency and the extreme sustained parallel throughput that Lustre provides for HPC workloads accessed by thousands of instances simultaneously.

text: An ecommerce company runs a PostgreSQL database on premises. The database stores data by using high IOPS Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) block storage. The daily peak I/O transactions per second do not exceed 15,000 IOPS. The company wants to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and provision disk IOPS performance independent of disk storage capacity. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
B. Configure the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
C. Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
D. Configure the EBS magnetic volume type to achieve maximum IOPS.
optionExplanations: ✗ gp2 ties IOPS to volume size (3 IOPS/GB) and cannot independently provision 15,000 IOPS without over-provisioning capacity, so it does not decouple IOPS from storage.
✗ io1 can provision 15,000 IOPS independently of capacity but Provisioned IOPS SSD is significantly more expensive than gp3 for the same performance, so it is not the most cost-effective.
✓ gp3 lets you provision IOPS (up to 16,000) independently of storage capacity at a much lower cost than io1, meeting the 15,000 IOPS requirement most cost-effectively.
✗ Magnetic (standard) volumes deliver only ~100-200 IOPS and cannot approach 15,000 IOPS, making them unsuitable for this high-IOPS workload.

text: A company wants to migrate its on-premises Microsoft SQL Server Enterprise edition database to AWS. The company's online application uses the database to process transactions. The data analysis team uses the same production database to run reports for analytical processing. The company wants to reduce operational overhead by moving to managed services wherever possible. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Migrate to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SOL Server. Use read replicas for reporting purposes
B. Migrate to Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2. Use Always On read replicas for reporting purposes
C. Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB. Use DynamoDB on-demand replicas for reporting purposes
D. Migrate to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Use Aurora read replicas for reporting purposes
optionExplanations: ✓ Amazon RDS for SQL Server is a managed service with the least operational overhead, and read replicas offload analytical reporting from the production OLTP workload.
✗ SQL Server on EC2 with Always On requires self-managing the OS, patching, and replication, which is far more operational overhead than a managed service.
✗ DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store, not a relational SQL Server engine, and migrating relational transactional workloads to it is impractical and incompatible.
✗ Aurora MySQL is a different engine (MySQL) than SQL Server, so migrating an Enterprise SQL Server database to it requires major schema/code conversion, not the least overhead.

text: A company stores a large volume of image files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The images need to be readily available for the first 180 days. The images are infrequently accessed for the next 180 days. After 360 days, the images need to be archived but must be available instantly upon request. After 5 years, only auditors can access the images. The auditors must be able to retrieve the images within 12 hours. The images cannot be lost during this process. A developer will use S3 Standard storage for the first 180 days. The developer needs to configure an S3 Lifecycle rule. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 180 days. S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
B. Transition the objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 180 days. S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
C. Transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
D. Transition the objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 180 days, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 360 days, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 5 years.
optionExplanations: ✗ One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, so a loss of that AZ could lose images; the requirement that images cannot be lost rules this out despite Glacier Instant Retrieval being correct for the 360-day tier.
✗ One Zone-IA risks data loss in a single AZ, and Glacier Flexible Retrieval does not provide instant retrieval required at 360 days, so two parts are wrong.

✓ Standard-IA provides multi-AZ durability for the 180-360 day infrequent tier, Glacier Instant Retrieval gives instant access after 360 days, and Deep Archive (12-hour retrieval) is the cheapest tier for the 5-year auditor access, fully meeting all requirements.

✗ Glacier Flexible Retrieval does not provide the required instant availability at 360 days (retrievals take minutes to hours), so this fails the instant-access requirement even though Standard-IA is durable.

text: A company has a large data workload that runs for 6 hours each day. The company cannot lose any data while the process is running. A solutions architect is designing an Amazon EMR cluster configuration to support this critical data workload. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Configure a long-running cluster that runs the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
B. Configure a transient cluster that runs the primary node and core nodes on On-Demand Instances and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
C. Configure a transient cluster that runs the primary node on an On-Demand Instance and the core nodes and task nodes on Spot Instances.
D. Configure a long-running cluster that runs the primary node on an On-Demand Instance, the core nodes on Spot Instances, and the task nodes on Spot Instances.
optionExplanations: ✗ A long-running cluster keeps paying for the primary and core nodes during the 18 idle hours each day, which is not cost-effective for a 6-hour daily job.

✓ A transient cluster terminates after the 6-hour job (saving cost), runs primary and core nodes (which hold HDFS data) on reliable On-Demand to prevent data loss, and uses Spot only for stateless task nodes, meeting all requirements most cost-effectively.
✗ Running core nodes on Spot risks losing HDFS data when Spot Instances are reclaimed, violating the no-data-loss requirement.
✗ A long-running cluster wastes cost during idle hours and placing core nodes on Spot risks HDFS data loss, failing both cost and durability requirements.

text: A company maintains an Amazon RDS database that maps users to cost centers. The company has accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs a solution that will tag all resources that are created in a specific AWS account in the organization. The solution must tag each resource with the cost center ID of the user who created the resource. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Move the specific AWS account to a new organizational unit (OU) in Organizations from the management account. Create a service control policy (SCP) that requires all existing resources to have the correct cost center tag before the resources are created. Apply the SCP to the new OU.

B. Create an AWS Lambda function to tag the resources after the Lambda function looks up the appropriate cost center from the RDS database. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function.

C. Create an AWS CloudFormation stack to deploy an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to look up the appropriate cost center from the RDS database and to tag resources. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the CloudFormation stack.

D. Create an AWS Lambda function to tag the resources with a default value. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function when a resource is missing the cost center tag.
optionExplanations: ✗ An SCP cannot tag resources or look up cost center IDs from RDS; SCPs only set permission guardrails and cannot 'require existing resources to have a tag before creation,' so this does not meet the requirement.

✓ A CloudTrail event (resource creation) triggers an EventBridge rule that invokes a Lambda function, which identifies the creating user, looks up that user's cost center ID in the RDS database, and applies the cost center tag to the new resource. This is event-driven, automatic, and meets all requirements.

✗ Invoking a CloudFormation stack on an EventBridge schedule is the wrong pattern; scheduled (time-based) runs do not react to individual resource creation events, and EventBridge does not 'invoke a CloudFormation stack' to tag resources per-creation, so the per-user cost center tagging requirement is not met.

✗ Tagging resources with a default value does not satisfy the requirement to tag each resource with the cost center ID of the specific user who created it, since the default value would not reflect the creating user's cost center.

text: A company recently migrated its web application to the AWS Cloud. The company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run multiple processes to host the application. The processes include an Apache web server that serves static content. The Apache web server makes requests to a PHP application that uses a local Redis server for user sessions. The company wants to redesign the architecture to be highly available and to use AWS managed solutions. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to host the static content and the PHP application. Configure Elastic Beanstalk to deploy its EC2 instance into a public subnet. Assign a public IP address.

B. Use AWS Lambda to host the static content and the PHP application. Use an Amazon API Gateway REST API to proxy requests to the Lambda function. Set the API Gateway CORS configuration to respond to the domain name. Configure Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to handle session information.

C. Keep the backend code on the EC2 instance. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster that has Multi-AZ enabled. Configure the ElastiCache for Redis cluster in cluster mode. Copy the frontend resources to Amazon S3. Configure the backend code to reference the EC2 instance.

D. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 endpoint to an S3 bucket that is configured to host the static content. Configure an Application Load Balancer that targets an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service that runs AWS Fargate tasks for the PHP application. Configure the PHP application to use an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster that runs in multiple Availability Zones.
optionExplanations: ✗ Elastic Beanstalk on a single public EC2 instance is not highly available by default and still serves static content from EC2 rather than a managed/scalable solution, falling short of the HA managed-service goal.
✗ Lambda cannot run an Apache web server or serve static content the way described, and hosting a stateful PHP/Apache app this way is a poor fit compared to using S3/CloudFront for static content.
✗ Keeping the backend on a single EC2 instance leaves a single point of failure (the EC2 instance is not highly available), so the architecture is not highly available.

✓ CloudFront with S3 serves static content at scale, an ALB fronting ECS Fargate provides a highly available managed PHP tier, and multi-AZ ElastiCache for Redis provides resilient session storage, fully meeting HA and managed-service requirements.

text: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that has a target group. The company designed the application to work with session afinity (sticky sessions) for a better user experience. The application must be available publicly over the internet as an endpoint. A WAF must be applied to the endpoint for additional security. Session afinity (sticky sessions) must be configured on the endpoint. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: A. Create a public Network Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
B. Create a Gateway Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
C. Create a public Application Load Balancer. Specify the application target group.
D. Create a second target group. Add Elastic IP addresses to the EC2 instances.
E. Create a web ACL in AWS WAF. Associate the web ACL with the endpoint
optionExplanations: ✗ A Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and does not support cookie-based sticky sessions in the way required, nor can AWS WAF be associated with an NLB.
✗ A Gateway Load Balancer is for inserting third-party virtual appliances (firewalls/IDS), not for publicly serving web application traffic with sticky sessions.

✓ A public Application Load Balancer supports HTTP/HTTPS sticky sessions (cookie-based session affinity) on its target group and can be associated with AWS WAF, meeting both the public endpoint and stickiness requirements.
✗ Creating a second target group with Elastic IPs on the instances does not provide session affinity or a WAF-protected endpoint and is unnecessary.
✓ Creating a web ACL in AWS WAF and associating it with the ALB endpoint provides the required WAF protection on the public endpoint.

text: A company runs a website that stores images of historical events. Website users need the ability to search and view images based on the year that the event in the image occurred. On average, users request each image only once or twice a year. The company wants a highly available solution to store and deliver the images to users. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Store images in Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
B. Store images in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
C. Store images in Amazon S3 Standard. Use S3 Standard to directly deliver images by using a static website.
D. Store images in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use S3 Standard-IA to directly deliver images by using a static website.
optionExplanations: ✗ Amazon EBS is single-AZ block storage attached to one EC2 instance, so it is not highly available on its own and adds EC2 web server cost and operational overhead; wrong.
✗ Amazon EFS plus EC2 provides shared file storage but is far more expensive than object storage for this use case and requires running and managing EC2 web servers; wrong.

✗ Amazon S3 Standard with static website hosting is highly available and serverless, but Standard pricing is meant for frequently accessed data, making it more expensive than necessary for images read only once or twice a year; not the MOST cost-effective.

✓ Amazon S3 Standard-IA delivers the same multi-AZ high availability and serverless static website hosting at lower storage cost, which is ideal for images accessed only once or twice per year; correct and most cost-effective.

text: A company has multiple AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations that different business units use. The company has multiple ofices around the world. The company needs to update security group rules to allow new ofice CIDR ranges or to remove old CIDR ranges across the organization. The company wants to centralize the management of security group rules to minimize the administrative overhead that updating CIDR ranges requires. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Create VPC security groups in the organization's management account. Update the security groups when a CIDR range update is necessary.

B. Create a VPC customer managed prefix list that contains the list of CIDRs. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the prefix list across the organization. Use the prefix list in the security groups across the organization.

C. Create an AWS managed prefix list. Use an AWS Security Hub policy to enforce the security group update across the organization. Use an AWS Lambda function to update the prefix list automatically when the CIDR ranges change.

D. Create security groups in a central administrative AWS account. Create an AWS Firewall Manager common security group policy for the whole organization. Select the previously created security groups as primary groups in the policy.
optionExplanations: ✗ Creating security groups in the management account does not let them be referenced by VPCs in other accounts, and manually updating them does not centralize management across the organization.

✓ A customer-managed prefix list holds the CIDR ranges centrally, AWS RAM shares it across all organization accounts, and security groups reference the prefix list so a single update propagates everywhere with minimal overhead and no extra service cost.
✗ AWS Security Hub does not enforce security group rule updates via policy, and AWS managed prefix lists cannot contain arbitrary custom office CIDRs, so this approach does not work as described.

✗ AWS Firewall Manager common security group policies replicate security groups but Firewall Manager carries additional cost and complexity, making it less cost-effective than a shared prefix list for simply managing CIDR ranges.

text: A company uses an on-premises network-attached storage (NAS) system to provide file shares to its high performance computing (HPC) workloads. The company wants to migrate its latency-sensitive HPC workloads and its storage to the AWS Cloud. The company must be able to provide NFS and SMB multi-protocol access from the file system. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST latency? (Choose two.)
options: A. Deploy compute optimized EC2 instances into a cluster placement group.
B. Deploy compute optimized EC2 instances into a partition placement group.
C. Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
D. Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system.
E. Attach the EC2 instances to an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system.
optionExplanations: ✓ A cluster placement group packs EC2 instances close together within a single Availability Zone on the same high-bisection-bandwidth, low-latency network segment, which is the optimal choice for tightly coupled, latency-sensitive HPC workloads.

✗ A partition placement group spreads instances across distinct hardware partitions to reduce correlated failures for large distributed/replicated workloads (e.g., Hadoop, Cassandra); it does not minimize inter-node latency the way a cluster placement group does.

✗ Amazon FSx for Lustre delivers very high throughput/IOPS for HPC, but it presents a POSIX/Lustre file system and does not provide native SMB multi-protocol access, so it fails the NFS+SMB requirement.
✗ Amazon FSx for OpenZFS supports the NFS protocol but does not offer SMB access, so it cannot satisfy the requirement for simultaneous NFS and SMB multi-protocol access.

✓ Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP natively supports multi-protocol access over both NFS and SMB from the same file system and offers low-latency, high-performance storage suitable for the migrated HPC workloads.

text: A company is relocating its data center and wants to securely transfer 50 TB of data to AWS within 2 weeks. The existing data center has a Site-to- Site VPN connection to AWS that is 90% utilized. Which AWS service should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?
options: A. AWS DataSync with a VPC endpoint
B. AWS Direct Connect
C. AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized
D. AWS Storage Gateway
optionExplanations: ✗ DataSync over the existing VPN would compete for the already 90%-utilized link, making it too slow to move 50 TB within 2 weeks.
✗ Provisioning a new Direct Connect circuit typically takes weeks to months, so it cannot meet the 2-week deadline.
✓ Snowball Edge Storage Optimized physically ships a device to transfer 50 TB offline, avoiding the saturated VPN and reliably completing the transfer within 2 weeks.
✗ Storage Gateway transfers data over the network and would also contend with the saturated VPN, making it unable to move 50 TB in time.

text: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances in an Auto Scaling group. Application peak hours occur at the same time each day. Application users report slow application performance at the start of peak hours. The application performs normally 2-3 hours after peak hours begin. The company wants to ensure that the application works properly at the start of peak hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure an Application Load Balancer to distribute trafic properly to the instances.
B. Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on memory utilization.
C. Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on CPU utilization.
D. Configure a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances before peak hours.
optionExplanations: ✗ An Application Load Balancer distributes traffic but does not add capacity; with too few instances at peak start, distributing traffic alone does not resolve the slow performance.

✗ Dynamic scaling on memory utilization is reactive and triggers only after load builds, so it still lags behind the known peak start and does not pre-provision capacity (and EC2 does not natively report memory without the CloudWatch agent).
✗ Dynamic scaling on CPU utilization is also reactive, scaling out only after CPU rises during the peak, which leaves the application under-provisioned at the very start of peak hours.
✓ A scheduled scaling policy launches additional instances at a fixed time before the predictable daily peak, ensuring capacity is ready when peak hours begin, which directly meets the requirement.

text: A company runs applications on AWS that connect to the company's Amazon RDS database. The applications scale on weekends and at peak times of the year. The company wants to scale the database more effectively for its applications that connect to the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon DynamoDB with connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the DynamoDB endpoint.
B. Use Amazon RDS Proxy with a target group for the database. Change the applications to use the RDS Proxy endpoint.
C. Use a custom proxy that runs on Amazon EC2 as an intermediary to the database. Change the applications to use the custom proxy endpoint.
D. Use an AWS Lambda function to provide connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the Lambda function.
optionExplanations: ✗ DynamoDB is a NoSQL service, not a connection pooler for RDS; you cannot point RDS-dependent applications at a DynamoDB endpoint, so this does not solve RDS connection scaling.

✓ Amazon RDS Proxy is a fully managed, highly available database proxy that pools and shares connections to RDS, improving scalability during spikes with minimal operational overhead and just an endpoint change.
✗ A custom proxy on EC2 would provide connection pooling but requires you to build, patch, scale, and maintain the EC2 fleet, which is far more operational overhead than the managed RDS Proxy.

✗ Lambda cannot serve as a persistent connection pool for a database the way RDS Proxy does; Lambda invocations are ephemeral and would actually worsen connection storms, plus building it is high overhead.

text: A company uses AWS Cost Explorer to monitor its AWS costs. The company notices that Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage and snapshot costs increase every month. However, the company does not purchase additional EBS storage every month. The company wants to optimize monthly costs for its current storage usage. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs to monitor the storage utilization of Amazon EBS. Use Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes to reduce the size of the EBS volumes.
B. Use a custom script to monitor space usage. Use Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes to reduce the size of the EBS volumes.
C. Delete all expired and unused snapshots to reduce snapshot costs.
D. Delete all nonessential snapshots. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to create and manage the snapshots according to the company's snapshot policy requirements.
optionExplanations: ✗ CloudWatch Logs monitors application/system logs, not native EBS volume free space, and resizing volumes addresses provisioned storage but does nothing about the growing snapshot costs that are part of the problem.
✗ A custom script to monitor space is more operational overhead and, like option A, only shrinks volumes while ignoring the snapshot cost growth.
✗ Deleting expired and unused snapshots reduces cost but is a manual one-time action with no ongoing governance, so snapshot costs will simply grow again over time.

✓ Deleting nonessential snapshots and using Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager to automatically create, retain, and expire snapshots per policy directly stops the recurring snapshot cost growth with the least ongoing operational overhead.

text: A company is developing a new application on AWS. The application consists of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster, an Amazon S3 bucket that contains assets for the application, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL database that contains the dataset for the application. The dataset contains sensitive information. The company wants to ensure that only the ECS cluster can access the data in the RDS for MySQL database and the data in the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key to encrypt both the S3 bucket and the RDS for MySQL database. Ensure that the KMS key policy includes encrypt and decrypt permissions for the ECS task execution role.

B. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key to encrypt both the S3 bucket and the RDS for MySQL database. Ensure that the S3 bucket policy specifies the ECS task execution role as a user.

C. Create an S3 bucket policy that restricts bucket access to the ECS task execution role. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon RDS for MySQL. Update the RDS for MySQL security group to allow access from only the subnets that the ECS cluster will generate tasks in.

D. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon RDS for MySQL. Update the RDS for MySQL security group to allow access from only the subnets that the ECS cluster will generate tasks in. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from only the S3 VPC endpoint.
optionExplanations: ✗ A KMS customer managed key encrypts data at rest but does not restrict network or principal access to the RDS database; any client with network connectivity and DB credentials can still query MySQL, so encryption alone does not ensure only the ECS cluster can access the data.

✗ An AWS managed KMS key cannot be used in a custom key policy granting a specific role, and S3 bucket policies do not control RDS access; encryption does not restrict who can connect to either resource, so this does not meet the requirement.

✗ The S3 bucket policy correctly restricts the bucket to the ECS task execution role, but there is no native VPC interface endpoint service for RDS for MySQL itself, and this option leaves an incomplete network restriction approach compared to a full endpoint-plus-policy design.

✓ Restricting the RDS security group to only the ECS task subnets enforces network-level access control to MySQL, and creating an S3 gateway VPC endpoint plus a bucket policy that allows access only from that VPC endpoint (aws:sourceVpce condition) ensures S3 is reachable only from within the ECS VPC, fully limiting both resources to the ECS cluster.

text: A company has a web application that runs on premises. The application experiences latency issues during peak hours. The latency issues occur twice each month. At the start of a latency issue, the application's CPU utilization immediately increases to 10 times its normal amount. The company wants to migrate the application to AWS to improve latency. The company also wants to scale the application automatically when application demand increases. The company will use AWS Elastic Beanstalk for application deployment. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
B. Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale based on requests.
C. Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use compute optimized instances. Configure the environment to scale on a schedule.
D. Configure an Elastic Beanstalk environment to use burstable performance instances in unlimited mode. Configure the environment to scale on predictive metrics.
optionExplanations: ✗ Burstable (T-family) instances in unlimited mode can sustain high CPU by spending credits, but a sustained 10x CPU spike is poorly served by burstable instances which are designed for low-to-moderate baseline usage with occasional bursts; compute optimized instances are a better fit for sudden high-CPU workloads.

✓ Compute optimized (C-family) instances handle the immediate 10x CPU surge well, and scaling based on requests reacts dynamically to the increased demand during the unpredictable twice-monthly latency events. This is the correct, responsive, cost-appropriate choice.

✗ Compute optimized instances suit the CPU spike, but scaling on a schedule is wrong because the latency issues are unpredictable (twice a month at no fixed time), so a schedule cannot anticipate them.

✗ Burstable unlimited instances are not ideal for sustained 10x CPU, and predictive scaling relies on recurring historical patterns; twice-monthly unpredictable spikes provide no reliable pattern for prediction, so it would fail to scale in time.

text: A company has customers located across the world. The company wants to use automation to secure its systems and network infrastructure. The company's security team must be able to track and audit all incremental changes to the infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
B. Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Config to track changes.
C. Use AWS Organizations to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
D. Use AWS CloudFormation to set up the infrastructure. Use AWS Service Catalog to track changes.
optionExplanations: ✗ AWS Organizations manages multiple accounts and policies but does not provision infrastructure as code, so it does not satisfy the automation-to-set-up-infrastructure requirement.
✓ AWS CloudFormation automates and secures infrastructure provisioning as code, and AWS Config records and tracks all incremental configuration changes for audit, meeting both requirements.
✗ Organizations does not provision infrastructure, and AWS Service Catalog manages approved product portfolios rather than tracking and auditing incremental change history.
✗ CloudFormation correctly provisions infrastructure, but AWS Service Catalog distributes approved templates/products and does not provide change tracking and auditing the way AWS Config does.

text: A startup company is hosting a website for its customers on an Amazon EC2 instance. The website consists of a stateless Python application and a MySQL database. The website serves only a small amount of trafic. The company is concerned about the reliability of the instance and needs to migrate to a highly available architecture. The company cannot modify the application code. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to achieve high availability for the website? (Choose two.)
options: A. Provision an internet gateway in each Availability Zone in use.
B. Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance.
C. Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB, and enable DynamoDB auto scaling.
D. Use AWS DataSync to synchronize the database data across multiple EC2 instances.
E. Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute trafic to an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances that are distributed across two Availability Zones.
optionExplanations: ✗ Internet gateways are regional (one per VPC), not per Availability Zone, and provisioning them does not provide application or database high availability.
✓ Migrating to Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ provides a synchronously replicated standby with automatic failover, giving the database high availability without changing application code.
✗ Migrating to DynamoDB would require rewriting the application from MySQL/SQL access, which violates the constraint that the application code cannot be modified.
✗ AWS DataSync transfers files between storage systems and is not a database replication mechanism, so it cannot keep a MySQL database consistent across EC2 instances.
✓ An Application Load Balancer fronting an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances across two Availability Zones makes the stateless web tier highly available and self-healing without code changes.

text: A company is moving its data and applications to AWS during a multiyear migration project. The company wants to securely access data on Amazon S3 from the company's AWS Region and from the company's on-premises location. The data must not traverse the internet. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection between its Region and its on-premises location. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create gateway endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the gateway endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
B. Create a gateway in AWS Transit Gateway to access Amazon S3 securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
C. Create interface endpoints for Amazon S3. Use the interface endpoints to securely access the data from the Region and the on-premises location.
D. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key to access the data securely from the Region and the on-premises location.
optionExplanations: ✗ S3 gateway endpoints route traffic privately only from within the VPC and are not accessible from on-premises networks over Direct Connect, so they cannot serve the on-premises access requirement.
✗ Transit Gateway connects VPCs and on-premises networks but does not itself provide a private S3 access path; you still need an interface endpoint to reach S3 privately, so this alone is incorrect.

✓ S3 interface endpoints (powered by PrivateLink) expose private IPs in the VPC that can be reached from on-premises over Direct Connect, allowing both the Region and on-premises to access S3 privately without using the internet.
✗ AWS KMS provides encryption key management, not network connectivity or a private path to S3, so it does not meet the requirement.

text: A company created a new organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has multiple accounts for the company's development teams. The development team members use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access the accounts. For each of the company's applications, the development teams must use a predefined application name to tag resources that are created. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that gives the development team the ability to create resources only if the application name tag has an approved value. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specified for resources to be created.
B. Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.
C. Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in all accounts.
D. Create a tag policy in Organizations that has a list of allowed application names.
optionExplanations: ✗ An IAM group with a conditional allow could enforce that a tag is present, but it would not constrain the tag value to an approved list and must be replicated and maintained across every account, increasing overhead and not centrally governing allowed values.
✗ A cross-account role with a Deny on resources having the application name tag would block tagged resources entirely, which is the opposite of the requirement.
✗ AWS Resource Groups only group and view resources by tags; it cannot validate or enforce that resources are created with approved tag values.
✓ A tag policy in AWS Organizations centrally defines compliant tag keys and an allowed list of values across all accounts, enforcing that resources use only approved application name tag values.

text: A company runs its databases on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company wants a secure solution to manage the master user password by rotating the password every 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a custom AWS Lambda function to rotate the password every 30 days.
B. Use the modify-db-instance command in the AWS CLI to change the password.
C. Integrate AWS Secrets Manager with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
D. Integrate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
